project.description: A local, AI-first project orchestrator that provides a web interface for managing multi-project workflows with Claude Code as the execution engine. It covers the full project lifecycle: ideation, specification, kanban-based planning, automated code generation via Claude Code CLI, real-time agent monitoring, and release management.
project.spec:
# Arij

**Your AI-powered project manager that actually writes the code.**

## 1. Project overview
Arij is an MIT-licensed, local-first project orchestrator for planning, building, reviewing, and releasing software with AI coding agents. It combines a multi-project dashboard, specification editor, Kanban board, chat workspace, agent monitoring, Git automation, QA reports, project memory, and release management in one Next.js application.
Claude Code is the default execution engine. Named agents can instead use OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, Mistral Vibe, Qwen Code, OpenCode, DeepSeek, Kimi, Zai, Pi, or Oh My Pi. An OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint provides a direct, low-latency chat path; it is not a build, review, QA, or merge provider.
Arij has no hosted service, Arij account, cloud synchronization, or telemetry. Its database, documents, logs, clones, worktrees, and runtime artifacts remain on the local machine. Configured AI CLIs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, Git remotes, and GitHub APIs may still communicate with their respective external services.
The package manifest reports version `0.1.0`. The only recorded product release and Git tag are `0.0.1` and `v0.0.1`; the main branch contains substantial completed work beyond that release.

### 1.1 Current implementation state
The GitHub import lifecycle is complete. Arij can:
- Attach a project to an existing local directory.
- Import a GitHub repository from a supported URL or `owner/repo` shorthand.
- Clone into an app-managed workspace and safely reuse a healthy matching clone.
- Analyze a repository or short-circuit from an existing `arji.json`.
- Populate GitHub ownership, clean remote URL, and detected default branch.
- Delete a clone only when database provenance, path containment, and an on-disk ownership marker all prove that Arij created it.

The current main branch also includes:
- Guarded epic and story transitions with explicit activity records for both accepted and refused moves.
- Manual and chat-driven epic creation, bug tickets, stories, dependencies, comments, screenshots, and review findings.
- A redesigned ticket detail surface with a hierarchical sticky header, mobile-safe layout, and compact, scannable activity feed.
- Isolated epic branches and Git worktrees for code-producing agents.
- Single-ticket pipelines, dependency-aware batch builds, night runs, Team Mode, and Full Auto Mode.
- Simplified named-agent creation based on a name and CLI, with optional model overrides and advanced role/runtime configuration.
- Agent reliability badges and opt-in reliability-based Full Auto dispatch.
- Manual and release-triggered specification rewrites.
- Per-session memory distillation and cross-session Dreaming.
- GitHub pull requests, issues, releases, push/pull status, and synchronization logs.
- Persisted session chunks, outcome classification, usage reporting, full failure notifications, and stalled-session detection.
- Project-scoped Server-Sent Events with polling fallback.
- An opt-in red-to-green regression gate for bug tickets: bug-specific prompts, a mechanical regression checker that runs the configured test command on the branch and on the merge-base, a pipeline gate between the code stage and review, a fix cycle carrying the exact red-to-green verdict, a persisted regression report per run, and a review/merge block while the gate fails.
- Structured review verdicts: the overall verdict of `submit_findings` is persisted on the originating review session and is the authoritative input to the guarded transitions; the legacy prose scan is retained only as a fallback for providers that cannot call MCP tools.
- Structured acceptance-criteria grading: an opt-in pipeline grading stage (default off), a `submit_grading` MCP tool, persisted grading reports, and per-criterion badges in the ticket detail and on kanban cards.
- Visual session artifacts: an `attach_artifact` MCP tool, opt-in visual-proof generation, and artifacts persisted under the session's data directory and viewable during review.
- Scheduled routines: an internal daily scheduler for night runs, Dreaming, GitHub issue synchronization, and CI watch, with persisted restart-safe state and opt-in CI autofix with limits.
- Agent friction reports: a `report_friction` MCP tool, a project-scoped friction register with occurrence counts and triage states, and a path to convert a friction into a ticket.
- Agent-created bug tickets: a `create_bug` MCP tool exposed to build/review agents, attributed to the originating session, duplicate-rejecting, and rate-limited per session.
- Model economy: per-agent-type model mapping (mechanical sessions such as title generation and import analysis route to a lightweight named agent when configured), opt-in same-provider effort escalation as a retry-ladder rung, and an opt-in second opinion before Full Auto merge.
- Recurring-failure digests (Telescope-lite) that cluster terminal outcomes, forensic reports, and critical findings over a sliding window and can be converted into tickets.
- A Sessions view sortable by last activity as well as creation time.

### 1.2 Development boundary
The following work is under review on a feature branch and is not part of stable main-branch behavior:
- A generic, deterministic `verify` pipeline stage in which Arij itself executes configured `test`/`lint`/`build` commands (`verify_commands` / `verify_timeout_ms` tri-state settings), persists `verify_reports`, and inserts a verify stage between build and grading/review with Full Auto merge gating, a manual verify route, and ticket-detail verification reports. The epic is in active review (multiple review rounds, ongoing fix cycles) and is not merged; the only mechanical gate on main today is the bug-ticket red-to-green regression check.

Principal backlog items include:
- A unified execution order: `position` as the single source of truth for the board and Full Auto dispatch (the supervisor currently sorts by priority/position and ignores `ticket_dependencies` outside wave builds).
- Board readability: execution-queue ranking, blocked-ticket state, and readiness indicators.
- A divided Review column with a "ready to merge" section.
- Agent refinement re-passes over Backlog and To do.
- A persistent Chat CLI with a warm process per conversation.
- Estimating the token volume sent to agents at build/review dispatch.
- Per-CLI named-agent options and persona pre-prompts.
- Open bug tickets: Oh My Pi sessions losing their MCP token (401s), a review gate vacuously satisfied when findings cannot be filed, merges that do not cascade epic-to-story statuses, and a 500 instead of 409 on conflicting merges.

These items must not be described as current product behavior until they are merged.

## 2. Objectives
1. **Unify the software lifecycle.** Let a user move from an idea or imported repository to a specification, actionable tickets, agent execution, review, merge, and release without switching project-management systems.
2. **Keep the application local-first.** Store project state, credentials, logs, documents, clones, worktrees, and runtime artifacts locally without requiring an Arij account or hosted backend.
3. **Support multiple execution providers.** Use Claude Code as the built-in default while allowing named agents backed by other supported CLIs and a separate OpenAI-compatible direct-chat mode.
4. **Protect repositories during autonomous work.** Isolate code changes in worktrees, serialize conflicting work, honor the repository's real base branch, and refuse destructive filesystem actions without explicit ownership evidence.
5. **Make automation observable and interruptible.** Persist session state and output, classify terminal outcomes, surface failures and questions, expose live activity, support cancellation, and retain an audit trail for automated decisions.
6. **Automate without bypassing workflow rules.** Route manual actions, MCP requests, imports, pipelines, approval, release, and Full Auto through the same transition service. Completion must come from approval or a guarded merge, never an ordinary status write.
7. **Preserve project context.** Inject the project specification, learned memory, relevant tickets, user-authored comments, screenshots, and explicitly mentioned documents into the prompts that need them.
8. **Improve dispatch quality from evidence.** Show per-agent reliability and duration statistics and optionally select the strongest sufficiently sampled agent when the user has not made an explicit choice.
9. **Replace prose-only confidence with mechanical evidence.** Execute deterministic gates (red-to-green regression check, opt-in acceptance grading, opt-in second opinion) and persist structured verdicts, grading reports, and review artifacts so that agent assertions are never treated as proof.

## 3. Product principles and constraints

### 3.1 Local execution and access
- Arij is a single local Next.js application backed by SQLite.
- API access is restricted to localhost host/origin values by default. Additional origins require explicit `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` configuration.
- There is no multi-user authentication, cloud synchronization, external queue, worker service, or event broker.
- Long-running agents are local child processes. Authentication and provider-specific configuration belong to their respective CLIs.
- Scheduler queues, launch closures, active pipeline registries, live night-run state, Full Auto runtime locks, MCP tokens, and SSE subscriptions live in the server process.
- Agent session rows, chunks, settings, documents, tickets, releases, and batch tags are durable.
- On restart:
- queued sessions whose launch closures were lost are cancelled as orphaned;
- running sessions are failed and any unverifiable mid-run review promotion is pulled back when possible;
- active pipelines and waves are not resumed;
- night-run summaries can be partially reconstructed from tagged session rows;
- Full Auto restarts from its persisted settings;
- scheduled routines resume from their persisted `last_run_at`, which is the restart-safe half of the anti-double-run guard.
- GitHub clone and repository analysis requests are synchronous and do not have a background cancellation service.

### 3.2 Database and migrations
- SQLite runs with WAL mode and foreign keys enabled.
- Drizzle migrations are applied at server startup.
- Migrations are hand-written under `lib/db/migrations/`.
- `npx drizzle-kit generate` must not be run. Snapshot files stop at `0013`, while the migration journal now reaches index `39` and migration `0039_named_agent_escalation`.
- A new relational change requires:
- a numbered SQL migration;
- a new monotonically increasing entry in `lib/db/migrations/meta/_journal.json`;
- a `when` value greater than every previously applied migration.
- Settings keys, document kinds, and session agent types are free-form text and need no migration unless the relational schema changes.
- Legacy databases without migration bookkeeping are baseline-stamped and then advanced through the runtime migration path.

### 3.3 Git and repository safety
- `simple-git` remains the Git integration library. GitHub API operations use `@octokit/rest`; the `gh` CLI is not part of the architecture.
- GitHub imports are full clones. `--depth` and `--single-branch` are forbidden because worktrees, merge-base computation, branch integration, and releases require complete history.
- Code-producing work runs in an epic-specific branch and worktree, not directly in the project's base checkout.
- Stories within one epic share the epic branch. Work on multiple stories of the same epic is serialized.
- Worktrees are created in the repository's sibling `.arij-worktrees` directory. Worktrees outside the expected managed directory are treated as user-owned.
- The stored or repository-derived default branch is authoritative. `main` and `master` are fallbacks, not assumptions.
- Existing directories are never silently overwritten.
- A matching healthy clone may be fetched and reused. A mismatching or unowned destination is a conflict.
- Local repositories supplied by the user are never deleted by Arij.
- Clone deletion requires all of the following:
- `projects.clone_source = "github"`;
- the resolved directory remains inside the current projects root;
- the repository contains a valid `.git/arij-clone.json` marker.
- Registered worktrees are removed during managed-clone cleanup only when they are inside the expected `.arij-worktrees` and projects roots.

### 3.4 Credentials and external communication
- The GitHub PAT is stored in the local `settings` table under `github_pat`.
- `GITHUB_TOKEN` is not read by the application.
- Clone and reuse-fetch operations first try anonymously. Authentication is retried only for credential-related failures.
- Authenticated Git uses a one-command `http.extraHeader`; the PAT is not embedded in the remote URL or persisted in `.git/config`.
- Clone errors are redacted for authorization headers, URL user information, bearer tokens, GitHub token patterns, and the exact supplied secret.
- GitHub API operations use the stored PAT through Octokit.
- Ordinary push, pull, and tag-push operations still rely on the machine's Git credential configuration. A private repository imported with a PAT may need a credential helper for later Git transport.
- OpenAI-compatible credentials are stored locally but are sent to the configured endpoint when that chat mode is used.
- AI CLI providers may transmit prompts, code, and project context according to their own configuration and service terms.

### 3.5 Workflow integrity
- Existing epic and story status writes go through `lib/workflow/transition-service.ts` and the workflow engine.
- Successful moves are logged. Guard refusals create explicit same-state activity entries.
- A build moves its target-and, for story work, the parent epic-to `in_progress` before its queued session row is created.
- A queued or running code-producing session owns its target's `in_progress` state.
- Other users, agents, and system actions cannot move that target out of `in_progress` while the code session owns it.
- The sole owning code session may move its own target only from `in_progress` to `review`. It cannot demote the ticket, approve it, move it to Done, or move a story's parent epic directly.
- If an owning session promotes work and then fails, asks a question, or otherwise does not deliver, terminal handling attempts to return the target to `in_progress`.
- Successful epic builds move the epic and the stories that were part of the build to `review`.
- Successful story builds move the story to `review`; the parent epic advances only after every sibling is in `review` or `done`.
- Failed, silent, refused, or question-ending builds remain or return to an appropriate held state with an explicit reason.
- A negative review returns the affected scope to `in_progress`.
- `review -> done` requires an approval or merge source, a completed review where required, and no open blocking findings.
- The structured review verdict persisted by `submit_findings` is the authoritative input to that guard; open `[critical]`/`[major]` findings block completion even under an approving verdict; providers without MCP tool support fall back to the legacy prose scan.
- Explicit human story approval acts as the review decision for that story but does not resolve epic-scoped findings.
- `released` is terminal and may only be entered by the system during release creation.
- Agent sessions cannot approve their own work through ordinary status updates.
- `arji.json` imports reconcile content transactionally and route existing status changes through the same guards. Refused statuses are reported and skipped.

### 3.6 Testing and delivery
- Unit, integration, and component tests live primarily in `__tests__/` and run with Vitest.
- Browser tests live in `e2e/` and run with Playwright.
- Vitest excludes dependencies, build output, app-managed clones, `.claude` worktrees, and runtime data artifacts.
- CI uses Node.js 22 and runs the complete Vitest suite on pushes and pull requests.
- Type checking, linting, production builds, and relevant Playwright tests remain expected verification steps but are not all enforced by the current CI workflow.
- Bug fixes are expected to include a regression test with a demonstrated failing state (red to green). For Arij's own bug tickets the mechanical red-to-green gate can enforce this; the test must fail before the fix and pass after it.

## 4. Technical stack
| Technology | Role
|---|---|
| Runtime | Node.js 20, 24 or newer |
| Application | Next.js 16.1 |
| App Router, TypeScript 5.9 | |
| UI | React 19.2, Tailwind CSS v4, shadcn/Radix components |
| Kanban drag-and-drop | dnd-kit |
| Database | SQLite through better-sqlite3, WAL mode, foreign keys enabled |
| ORM and validation | Drizzle ORM and Zod |
| Git | Git CLI through `simple-git` |
| GitHub | `@octokit/rest` |
| Agent execution | Local CLI child processes behind a common provider interface |
| Agent tool protocol | Model Context Protocol (`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`) |
| Direct chat | API-compatible HTTP chat completions endpoint |
| Real-time UI | Server-Sent Events with reconnect and polling fallback |
| Markdown | `react-markdown` and `remark-gfm` |
| Documents | `mammoth` for DOCX and `pdf-parse` for PDF |
| IDs | SANO IDs |
| Tests | Vitest, Test Library, jspm, and Playwright |
| Packaging | npm package with the `arij` CLI wrapper |

## 5. Implemented product surface

### 5.1 Projects and repository import
A project can be created against an existing local directory or imported from a GitHub codebase. The import flow supports:
- A local filesystem path validated as an existing directory.
- GitHub HTTPS, SSH-shaped, `git://`, or `owner/repo` shorthand, with strict owner/repository segment validation and clone-path containment.
- Separate "Cloning" and "Analyzing" progress states.
- An editable preview before creating the project and its tickets.
- An existing `arji.json` short-circuit that avoids agent analysis.
- Automatic creation of epics and stories followed by an `arji.json` export.
- A deterministic clone destination under the configured projects root.
- Reuse of a healthy matching clone.
- Replacement only of broken clone directories carrying Arij's marker for the same repository.
- Replacement of a clone only when the database provenance, path containment, and `.git/arij-clone.json` ownership marker all agree.
- Project deletion with optional, provenance-guarded clone cleanup.
- Arij imports normalize the remote to a clean HTTPS URL and populate `gitRemoteUrl`, `githubOwnerRepo`, and `defaultBranch`.

### 5.2 Planning and Kanban
Each project provides:
- Backlog, To Do, In Progress, Review, Done, and Released columns.
- Feature epics and red bug tickets with readable IDs.
- User stories, descriptions, acceptance criteria, priorities, dependencies, and activity history.
- Manual drag-and-drop and API/MCP moves through the shared workflow engine.
- Direct manual epic creation with inline stories.
- Chat-driven epic refinement and creation.
- Bug creation with clipboard paste, drag-and-drop, or file-picker screenshots.
- Batch selection with parallel, sequential, and dependency-aware execution, and Team Mode.
- Project-scoped SSE updates, move animations, and live agent indicators, with polling fallback.
- A ticket detail panel with prioritized information and actions, a sticky header, responsive layout, and a compact chronological activity feed.
- A friction register: agent-submitted frictions are listed with occurrence counts and state (`new`, `triaged`, `converted`, `dismissed`) and can be converted into tickets or dismissed.

#### 5.2.3 Bug tickets
Bugs have a simplified creation flow - a direct form (title, description, images) with no mandatory chat step. They can optionally link to an existing epic. A "Create and Resolve" action creates the bug and immediately dispatches a selected agent through the existing provider/agent selection and build pipeline. Bugs have a simplified creation flow - a direct form (title, description, images) with no mandatory chat step. They can optionally link to an existing epic. A 'Create and Resolve' action creates the bug and immediately dispatches a selected agent (via the existing provider/agent selection) to reproduce and fix it. When `bug_regression_check` is enabled, the branch additionally must carry a test that is green on the branch and red on the merge-base (RoboBun rule). Build/review agents can also file attributed bug tickets through the `create_bug` MCP tool.

### 5.3 Chat, specifications, documents, and memory
The unified chat workspace provides tabbed conversations. Persisted history, provider or named-agent selection, attachments for supported CLI modes, and streamed responses.
Regular chat conversations can use board tools to:
- List and inspect tickets.
- Create and edit tickets.
- Request guarded status changes.
- Post comments.
- Inspect agent status.
- Start builds.
The board-tool channel is available to the OpenAI-compatible path and to supported CLI chat providers when MCP tools are enabled.
Structured brainstorm and epic-creation conversations keep their output contracts isolated from board tools. The OpenAI-compatible mode stores a base URL, optional API key, model, and reasoning settings. It supports connection testing and token-by-token streaming. It can run isolated, brainstorm, and epic-creation conversations, but structured conversations receive no board tools. Image attachments are rejected in this mode.
Project context can include:
- Project name and description.
- The stored specification.
- Learned project memory.
- Ticket and story details.
- User-authored comments and review findings.
- Bug screenshots.
- Explicitly mentioned project documents.
The specification can be:
- Edited manually.
- Initially generated by an agent.
- Rewritten by a session after a release when the opt-in setting is enabled. Agent-driven specification output replaces the saved specification only after a successful run with usable content. Successful specification writes re-export `arji.json`.
Documents support:
- Manual upload of PDF, DOCX, Markdown, plain text, and images.
- Markdown conversion for supported text formats.
- Local storage and display of image documents.
- `@file` and `#file` references.
- Repository scanning for text, Markdown, DOCX, and DOCX candidates.
- User approval before import.
- Idempotent, case-insensitive duplicate handling.
- Per-file import failures without aborting the entire batch.
- Legacy `.doc` files can be discovered but must be converted to `.docx`.
- Repository scanning skips symlinks, dependencies, VCS internals, worktrees, caches, and build output.

#### 5.4 Learned memory and Dreaming
Each project has one capped Markdown memory document that is injected into relevant prompts.
- Per-session memory distillation can run manually.
- Auto-distillation is off by default and skips failed, silent, or question-ending sessions.
- Memory writes are serialized, and concurrent memory rewrites are detected.
- Dreaming is the cross-session memory pass. It:
- Collects recent completed build and review evidence across multiple tickets.
- Includes successful, failed, silent, and question-ending outcomes where applicable.
- Incorporates final-response tails, major findings, review conclusions, errors, and forensic diagnostics.
- Reads at most 30 eligible terminal sessions from a rolling window of up to 14 days bounded by the last successful collection cutoff.
- Can be started manually or after a night run when enabled.
- Rewrites memory into four required sections: `Codebase pitfalls`, `Recurring agent mistakes`, `Strategies that work`, and `Build instructions`.
- Serial Dreaming and per-session distillation through one memory-writer lock.
- Refuses to overwrite a manual memory edit made while the agent was running.
- Preserves one pre-Dreaming snapshot for recovery.
- Emits an activity trace and notification after a successful rewrite.
The default creation path requires only a name and CLI. Availability indicators show whether each CLI is detected.
- An optional model override; an empty value uses the CLI's default.
- Advanced configuration exposes:
- Per-role prompts.
- Global and project-scoped prompts.
- Custom review agents.
- Reviewer/provider segregation.
- Runtime concurrency and watchdog settings.
- Reliability and duration statistics.
- Provider authentication and low-level configuration remain each CLI's responsibility.
- Agent resolution follows this precedence:
1. Explicit named-agent choice.
2. Project-scoped role assignment.
3. Global role assignment.
4. Built-in Claude Code fallback.
- For reviews, optional provider segregation may choose an installed provider different from the last successful builder, but never overrides an explicit choice.
- Agent configuration:
- Lifecycle status.
- Provider, model, named-agent identity, and task type.
- Project, epic, and story scope.
- Prompt, CLI command display, branch, worktree, and logs path.
- Ordered output chunks.
- Terminal outcome and full error information.
- Start, completion, and activity timestamps.
- Token and reported-cost usage.
- Batch or night-run attribution.
- Provider session identity where available.
- Sessions can be queued, monitored, cancelled, inspected, and resumed for providers whose CLI exposes usable continuity.
- A per-project in-process scheduler applies an optional concurrency cap. The built-in default is unlimited; a stored value of `0` also means unlimited.
- Positive values create a FIFO queue.

### 5.5 Automation modes
Arij provides three automation scopes:

#### 5.5.1 Single-ticket autonomous pipeline
The pipeline runs: `build -> [red-to-green regression gate, bug tickets only, when enabled] -> [acceptance grading, when enabled] -> review -> optional fix -> re-review`. It includes:
- Per-stage retry ladder:
- Attempt 1 uses the run's as-configured resolution (the original named agent for code stages; reviewer segregation for review).
- Attempt 2 resumes the failed attempt's session when the machinery allows, otherwise starts fresh on the same provider.
- Attempt 3 starts fresh on the named agent's configured same-provider escalation target when one exists (`named_agents.escalates_to`); without that opt-in edge this is the legacy provider-escalation attempt.
- Attempt 3 and beyond escalate to an alternative provider when no model escalation occupied attempt 3.
- Optional provider escalation on late failures.
- A configurable fix-cycle limit.
- A hard limit of 12 sessions per run.
- Cancellation, question, target-conflict, and exhaustion policies.
- A forensic diagnostic after exhausted stage attempts.
- A clean result leaves the ticket in Review awaiting approval or merge.
- The pipeline does not approve its own work.
- Mechanical gates and stages:
- Regression gate (bug tickets only, opt-in, default off): after a successful build or fix stage, the branch must carry a test file that is green on the branch and red on the merge-base. A failed gate short-circuits review: the runner enters a fix cycle with the exact failure reason injected. Every gate run - passed or failed - is persisted as a ticket comment so the regression block survives restarts. Gate rejection after the fix budget parks the ticket back to `in_progress` with an explicit failure.
- Acceptance grading (opt-in, default off): a plan-mode grader session evaluates the story's acceptance criteria one by one and persists a structured report through `submit_grading`. A rubric-free target is a journalled no-op. Missed criteria trigger a fix cycle with the exact criterion and its evidence injected. The ticket detail shows per-criterion badges and an aggregate on the kanban card, refreshed by SSE.
- Second opinion before merge (Full Auto, opt-in, default off): before merging a cleanly reviewed epic, an independent read-only MCP-capable session from a provider different from both builder and reviewer re-examines the final diff. Its structured verdict is mandatory; a negative verdict or any open finding parks the epic with a deep-link notification and the merge never happens. The gate counts against the Full Auto review budget. When no MCP-capable eligible provider exists, the merge is held with an explicit trace rather than a false rejection.

#### 5.5.2 Night runs
A night run processes selected epics through dependency-ordered waves. Each launched epic runs the complete autonomous pipeline. Night runs support:
- To do tickets and optionally selected Backlog work.
- Dependency blocking.
- Continue-or-stop failure policies.
- A configurable consecutive-failure circuit breaker.
- A reported-cost cap.
- Explicit user stopping.
- Notifications and detailed morning summaries.
- Reconstruction of interrupted history from session batch tags.
- Optional Dreaming after the run terminates.

#### 5.5.3 Full Auto Mode
Full Auto is a standing per-project supervisor. It repeatedly:
1. Reconciles its in-flight state.
2. Merges eligible cleanly reviewed epics.
3. Dispatches reviews within the review budget.
4. Dispatches builds within the build budget.
It considers buildable Backlog, To Do, and unoccupied In Progress work while skipping tickets that are busy, awaiting a user reply, blocked by dependencies, owned by another pipeline or night run, or parked after repeated failures.
Full Auto provides:
- Separate build and review concurrency budgets.
- Explicit build and review agent choices.
- Opt-in smart dispatch.
- Activity entries for automatic choices and skips.
- A fresh-review requirement before merge.
- Blocking-finding checks.
- An optional second opinion before merge (see 5.5.1).
- Soft parking after three consecutive failures.
- Hard parking after unresolved merge conflicts.
Smart dispatch is off by default. When enabled and no role-specific agent is explicitly selected, it chooses the highest-success named agent over the previous 30 days among agents with at least five terminal runs for that role. Ties are deterministic, and the choice is recorded in the ticket activity log.
A clean merge uses the normal Git and workflow logic. On a genuine content conflict, Full Auto may dispatch one merge-resolution agent and retry once. An unresolved conflict parks the epic and notifies the user.

#### 5.5.4 Scheduled routines and CI watch
Arij provides an internal, process-local scheduler for durable, project-scoped routines. There is no external cron, webhook receiver, or job queue:
- Kinds: `night_run`, `dreaming`, `github_issue_sync`, and `ci_watch`.
- One routine of a given kind per project (uniqueness enforced by migration).
- A daily `HH:MM` time-of-day and an enable flag.
- The scheduler claims a run by writing `last_run_at` before launching the action; that timestamp is the restart-safe half of the anti-double-run guard.
- `ci_watch` polls the CI status of open pull requests. An opt-in autofix mode (disabled by default) dispatches a fix build for failing PRs, with per-run limits and a concurrency guard so two watches cannot claim the same PR head.

### 5.6 Reviews, QA, and releases
Built-in reviews cover:
- Security.
- Code quality.
- Compliance.
- Feature completeness.
- Custom reviews.
Custom reviews can add their own instructions.
Review findings are stored with file and line anchors and may be linked to the session that filed them. Open findings block guarded completion.
The overall verdict of a review is the structured `submit_findings` verdict, persisted on the originating review session (`agent_sessions.review_verdict`). It is the authoritative input to the transition service: an approving verdict still blocks while open `[critical]` or `[major]` findings remain; a `changes_requested` verdict returns the scope to `in_progress`. Providers that cannot call MCP tools fall back to the historical prose scan of the reviewer's output.
- QA supports:
- Technology checks.
- E2E test sessions.
- Custom prompts.
- Named-agent selection.
- Persisted reports and report history.
- Creating feature or bug epics from report findings.
- Recurring-failure digests: a sliding-window collector clusters terminal session outcomes, forensic reports, and critical findings and produces a digest that can be turned into tickets.
- Friction reports: agent-submitted frictions (broken tooling, misleading docs, flaky tests, unclear conventions, other) are registered per project with occurrence counts and triage state, and can be converted into tickets.
- QA checks are agent-driven. Project documents are not injected automatically merely because a QA job was started. Arij executes the red-to-green regression gate and the opt-in acceptance-grading stage independently of the agents' assertions; a generic `test`/`lint`/`build` verification stage remains under review.
- Release creation:
- Accepts completed, unreleased epics.
- Generates a structured changelog or falls back to ticket titles.
- Creates or reuses a `<version>` branch.
- Writes and commits `CHANGELOG.md`.
- Creates a `<version>` Git tag targeting the release commit.
- Optionally pushes the tag and creates a draft GitHub release.
- Moves included epics from Done to Released.
- Emits project events and an optional webhook.
- May trigger the opt-in automatic specification rewrite.

### 5.7 GitHub integration
Once `githubOwnerRepo` and a PAT are configured, Arij supports:
- Detecting and connecting repository remotes.
- Branch ahead/behind status.
- Guarded push and pull operations with conflict reporting.
- Synchronizing open GitHub issues.
- Filtering and triaging issues.
- Mapping GitHub issue labels to feature or bug ticket types.
- Importing selected issues as Arij tickets.
- Creating draft GitHub pull requests.
- Creating GitHub releases and publishing them.
- Recording Git operations in `git_sync_log`.

## 6. Architecture

### 6.1 Runtime overview
`Browser <-> HTTP + Server-Sent Events -> Next.js API routes <-> SQLite / Drizzle <-> in-process scheduler, watchdog, event bus, pipelines, routines, and supervisors <-> AI CLI child processes + OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoints + Git CLI through simple-git + GitHub API through Octokit`
Arij is intentionally a single-process local application. The database is the durable state source; in-process registries coordinate active work but are not a durable job queue.

### 6.2 Filesystem layout
`arij/ data/arij.db sessions/<session-id>/ documents/<project-id>/ uploads/<project-id>/ ...lib/db/migrations/ projects/<owner>/<repo>.git/arij-clone.json .arij-worktrees/`
Session artifacts (visual proofs and attached screenshots) are copied under `data/sessions/<session-id>/artifacts/`; the database stores only the generated basename, never an agent-controlled source path. The managed projects root defaults to `~/projects` and can be overridden with the absolute `projects_root` setting. Generated and runtime artifacts are excluded from source control.

### 6.3 GitHub import flow
`POST /api/projects/clone -- parse and validate owner/repo -- resolve destination inside projects_root -- serialize access to destination -- reuse and fetch a healthy matching clone -- or clone into a private staging directory -- stamp the ownership marker -- atomically rename into place`
`POST /api/projects/import -- validate the local directory -- read existing arji.json -- or run repository analysis -- Editable preview -- Project and ticket creation`
Clone and analysis remain separate synchronous requests. This preserves the established progress model without introducing another job system.

### 6.4 Build lifecycle
`Build request -- validate project, target, workflow and concurrency -- resolve the named agent and provider -- create or attach the epic worktree and branch -- move target and parent to In Progress -- create the queued session -- provider child process -- persist chunks and activity -- hold scoped Arij MCP actions where supported -- delivered success -> mechanical regression gate (bug tickets, when enabled) -> optional grading stage -> review -- failure/question/refusal -> hold or return to In Progress -- support events, comments, notifications and automation hooks`
Build start and completion workflow handlers share the same workflow helpers across manual dispatch, pipelines, batches, night runs, and Full Auto.
The autonomous pipeline's retry ladder, regression gate, grading stage, and second-opinion gate are described in 5.5.1. The gate and grading reports are persisted so they survive restarts and are visible in the ticket activity feed.

### 6.5 Workflow guards
Activity log rows provide write-provenance. Project-scoped SSE events drive UI. Automation engines select work and dispatch stages; they do not have a separate status-writing path.

### 6.6 Provider layer and MCP channel
`lib/providers/` defines a shared interface for spawning, streaming, selecting, resuming, and checking CLI availability.
Shared child-process behavior includes:
- Bounded output handling.
- CLI session ID extraction where available.
- Ordered chunk persistence.
- Usage extraction.
- Command display with prompt and secret redaction.
- SIGTERM-to-SIGKILL cancellation for process-backed providers.
- Claude Code and Codex provider per-spawn MCP configuration. Their agent toolset currently exposes: `get_ticket`, `update_ticket_status`, `post_comment`, `report_friction`, `attach_artifact`, `create_bug`, `ask_question`, `submit_findings`, and `submit_grading`. Each MCP token is short-lived and scoped to a session, project, epic, story, and agent type. Tokens are revoked when the process ends. Claude Code receives its MCP configuration through a per-spawn 0700 temporary file that is deleted after the session. Codex receives process-level configuration overrides; the real command line therefore has residual token exposure to local process inspection, although the persisted display command is redacted.
- Providers without per-spawn MCP injection still receive structured prompt context but cannot use Arij's structured agent tools. MCP tool injection is capability-gated to the Claude Code and Codex providers.
- The regular chat toolset (CLI chat conversations and the OpenAI-compatible fast path) exposes: `list_tickets`, `get_ticket`, `create_ticket`, `update_ticket`, `update_ticket_status`, `post_comment`, `get_agent_status`, and `start_build`. Chat tokens are rejected by the agent-only routes.

### 6.7 Durable state, events, and observability
SQLite stores:
- Projects, epics, bugs, stories, dependencies, and activity.
- Conversations, messages, attachments, documents, and project memory.
- Agent sessions, ordered chunks, prompts, named agents, and role assignments.
- Review comments, grading reports, and persisted review verdicts.
- QA reports, releases, pull requests, and GitHub issues.
- Session artifacts (visual proofs).
- Scheduled routines and their persisted run state.
- Friction reports.
- Git synchronization logs, notifications, read cursors, and provider usage snapshots.
- Free-form global and project-scoped settings.
The server emits project-scoped SSE events for ticket, session, release, and routine changes. Clients reconnect with exponential backoff and use polling fallback when disconnected. This is an in-process event bus, not a durable event stream.
The watchdog periodically checks running sessions against their last persisted output. It creates one stalled notification and activity entry per stall but never kills the agent automatically. Terminal failures retain the full readable error in the session and notification, with a deep link to the affected session.

### 6.8 Specification and memory writers
Specification rewrites and memory rewrites share one memory-writer exclusion rule:
- Agent-level plan-mode sessions.
- Agent output replaces durable content only after a successful run.
- Dreaming and distillation compare the current memory with the version used to build the prompt before committing a replacement.
- Successful specification writes re-export `arji.json`.
- Successful Dreaming writes archive the immediately previous memory and advance the collection cutoff atomically.

### 6.9 `arji.json` synchronization
`arji.json` is the repository-facing export of a project's epics, stories, and comments.
The board writes trigger best-effort export. Users can also request export or guarded import. Import behavior:
- Reconciles project and ticket content.
- Creates or updates tickets by stable ID.
- Removes rows absent from the file through the synchronization path.
- Sends existing epic and story status changes through the workflow service.
- Reports and skips refused status changes.
- Emits move events only after the database transaction commits.
- Keeps installation simple and puts every project under the user's control.
- CLI commits instead of a single vendor API.

## 7. Key decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|
| Local, Next.js, and SQLite | Installation simplicity and puts project data under the user's control |
| Multiple CLIs | Arij stores provider and model choices without duplicating every CLI's authentication and runtime settings |
| OpenAI-compatible HTTP as chat-only | Provides low-latency conversation without pretending a stateless chat endpoint is a build or review runner |
| Named agents separate identity from task role | Users can configure understandable agents once and assign them globally, per project, per role, or per dispatch |
| Explicit agent choices beat automation | A user's selection always wins over smart dispatch |
| Worktrees and branches per epic | Supports parallel work across epics while keeping one integration unit for stories, review, and merge |
| Central transition service | Manual actions, API calls, MCP actions, imports, approval, release, pipelines, and Full Auto share the same guards and audit trail |
| Owning-session promotion | A build can deliver its own target to Review without unlocking unrelated moves or self-approval |
| SSE with polling fallback | Responsive local updates without a Websocket server or external broker |
| In-process scheduling | Fits the single-process deployment while optional concurrency limits and FIFO admission |
| Separate pipelines, night runs, and Full Auto modes | Each automation scope has a clear lifecycle, budget, and termination model |
| Smart dispatch is opt-in and deterministic | Reliability data can improve unattended work without silently changing established agent choices |
| Full Auto conflict resolution is explicit and opt-in | It enables automated work while making the risk of merging an agent-resolved conflict explicit |
| Structured MCP channels are capability-gated | Claude Code and Codex receive scoped tools without writing shared provider configuration into repository files |
| Ownership marker plus database provenance | Location, remote URL, or a request flag alone is insufficient authority to delete source code |
| PAT supplied through one-command Git configuration | Private clone and reuse-fetch operations work without persisting credentials in repository configuration |
| Clone into staging, then rename atomically | A failed or interrupted download cannot leave a half-valid destination |
| Clones into a deterministic root | Worktrees, tags, retry, and safe cleanup need consistent and predictable paths |
| Agents' durable documents commit only after a successful run | Failed, silent, cancelled, question-ending, or concurrent rewrites cannot corrupt saved context |
| Per-session distillation and cross-session Dreaming remain distinct | One captures a fresh local lesson; the other extracts recurring patterns across many outcomes |
| Mechanical gates, structured verdicts, and persisted artifacts | Agent prose and AI review are not substitutes for mechanically executed checks; the red-to-green regression gate, structured review verdicts, acceptance grading, and session artifacts are executed or persisted by Arij |
| Full Auto merge gating (including the opt-in second opinion) | Unattended merge paths carry explicit mechanical evidence before touching the base branch |

## 8. Current limitations and exclusions
- GitHub is the only supported clone host. GitLab, Bitbucket, and self-hosted Git services are not implemented.
- SSH-shaped GitHub inputs are normalized to HTTPS; SSH-key-based private cloning is not a supported credential path.
- Monorepo subdirectory imports are not supported.
- Clone and analysis requests are synchronous and do not have a background cancellation service beyond the UI phases.
- Scheduler queues, active pipelines, wave registries, runtime locks, MCP tokens, and live event subscriptions do not survive a server restart.
- Full Auto configuration survives restart, but its in-flight and parking state does not.
- Arij is a single-user local application, not a collaborative hosted service.
- Team Mode is limited to Claude Code.
- OpenAI-compatible mode is chat-only and does not support image attachments.
- Providers other than Claude Code and Codex do not receive per-session MCP tools; their sessions cannot call `submit_findings`, `submit_grading`, `create_bug`, `report_friction`, or `attach_artifact`, and review decisions for them retain the prose fallback.
- The generic deterministic `verify` stage (Arij-executed `test`/`lint`/`build` commands with `verify_commands` settings and persisted `verify_reports`) is not yet merged; it is under active review. The only mechanical gate on main today is the bug-ticket red-to-green regression check, which is off by default.
- Pipeline verification outside that gate remains agent-instructed rather than independently executed by Arij.
- Legacy `.doc` documents require conversion to `.docx`.
- Git push, pull, and tag transport may require an external credential helper for private repositories.
- Unbounded table growth (reports, logs, artifacts) is not pruned automatically; retention is a review finding waiting to happen.
- The Sessions page last-activity sort is implemented; Full Auto's execution order (priority/position vs. `position`-only with dependency awareness) and board readability improvements remain backlog items.

epics.title: Branche d'intégration `arjj` : socle git main→arjj + PR `arjj`→défaut dans GitHub sync
epics.description:
## Contexte

Aujourd'hui le socle git d'Arij est la **branche par défaut** du dépôt (§3.3, §5.7) : les branches/worktrees d'épic partent de là, le merge (manuel + Full Auto) y retombe, et les releases `release/vX` + tag `vX` en découlent.

**Changement radical proposé :** Arij adopte sa propre branche longue-vie **`arjj`** comme tronc de travail. La branche par défaut (`main`/défaut) reste la **vérité amont** ; `arjj` est le **tronc Arij** où tout est intégré, et on shippe vers l'amont via une **PR `arjj` → défaut** proposée depuis l'écran GitHub sync (§5.8).

### Modèle cible

```text
main / défaut   (amont — source de vérité, inchangée §3.3)
  ^  PR `arjj` → défaut   (proposée dans GitHub sync, draft par défaut)
  |  sync guardé défaut → arjj   (pour rester mergeable)
arjj            (tronc Arij — longue-vie, Arij-owned)
  |  les branches épic forkent d'arjj ; le merge retombe sur arjj
  +-- epic-xxx (worktree isolé par epic, stories partagées)
```

### Conséquences (câblées dans les stories)
- Base des worktrees/branches d'épic → `arjj` (fallback défaut si mode off).
- Cible de merge (manuel + Full Auto) → `arjj` ; gardes de workflow inchangées, autre cible.
- Releases `release/vX` + tag `vX` découlent de `arjj`.
- Nouvelle action GitHub sync : **proposer une PR `arjj` → défaut** (Octokit, trackée, journalisée).
- Sécurité : `arjj` est un **artifact Arij** — jamais de force-push, jamais de suppression de la branche par défaut, preuve de provenance explicite (discipline du marqueur de clone §3.3).
- **Amendement du spec** : §3.3 (la branche par défaut reste l'amont ; `arjj` devient le tronc d'intégration Arij) et §5.7 (cibles de merge et de release) seront mis à jour avec l'implé.

### Décisions à trancher (à confirmer avant implé)
1. **Nom exact** de la branche (`arjj` par défaut, configurable par projet ?) — *spelling à valider*.
2. **Bascule dure ou opt-in** par projet (toggle `git_use_integration_branch`) ; défaut sur les nouveaux projets ?
3. PR `arjj` → défaut : **draft par défaut** (non destructif) ou régulière ?
4. Les **releases découlent de `arjj`** (vs de la PR mergée) — à valider.
5. Le **sync amont→`arjj`** est-il une op à la demande seulement, ou automatique avant chaque PR ?

user_stories.title: Socle : réglages + bootstrap de la branche d'intégration
user_stories.description: Ajouter `git_integration_branch` (défaut `arjj`) et `git_use_integration_branch` (bool) en settings (free-form, pas de migration). Au premier dispatch sur un projet avec le mode actif, créer `arjj` depuis la branche par défaut du dépôt et le mémoriser ; idempotent. `main`/défaut restent la vérité amont (§3.3 inchangée).
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- Les 2 clés se round-trip via l'API de settings.
- `arjj` est créée une seule fois depuis la branche par défaut, idempotent (pas de re-branche si elle existe).
- Si le toggle est off, comportement = aujourd'hui (base = défaut).
- Aucune écriture destructrice sur la branche par défaut.

user_stories.title: Worktrees/branches + merge retargetés sur `arjj`
user_stories.description: La création de branche/worktree d'épic part de `arjj` (fallback défaut si mode off/absent). Le merge manuel et Full Auto (épiques clean reviewés) retombent sur `arjj`. Toutes les gardes existantes (merge clean, résolution de conflit par agent + une retry, blocage sur findings ouverts, revue fraîche) s'appliquent désormais contre `arjj` : mêmes règles, autre cible.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- Une branche épic fork d'`arjj` (pas du défaut) quand le mode est actif.
- Le merge (manuel + Full Auto) atterrit sur `arjj`.
- La résolution de conflit Full Auto (un agent, une retry) cible `arjj`.
- Les gardes de workflow (provenance, revue, findings, ownership de session) restent identiques en forme.

user_stories.title: Garder `arjj` en sync avec l'amont (reste mergeable)
user_stories.description: Opération guardée « sync `arjj` avec l'amont » : merge/pull de la branche par défaut dans `arjj`, avec reporting de conflits et résolution par agent optionnelle. Dispo à la demande et/ou avant de proposer la PR. Journalisée dans `git_sync_log`.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- `arjj` peut être amenée à jour de l'amont sans perte.
- Les conflits sont surfacés (jamais de drop silencieux), résolvables par agent si opt-in.
- Chaque op de sync est journalisée dans `git_sync_log`.

user_stories.title: GitHub sync : proposer une PR `arjj` → défaut
user_stories.description: Nouvelle action dans l'écran GitHub sync : détecter la divergence (ahead/behind `arjj` vs défaut), créer ou mettre à jour une PR (head=`arjj`, base=défaut) via Octokit, draft par défaut, trackée dans `pull_requests`, journalisée dans `git_sync_log`, avec lien projet et statut live (SSE).
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- Un clic crée / met à jour la PR (une seule ouverte à la fois pour le même head/base).
- La divergence est affichée avant création.
- Draft par défaut ; bascule vers PR régulière possible.
- Le statut PR (open/merged/closed) est persisté et mis à jour en live via SSE ; entrées dans `git_sync_log`.

user_stories.title: Flux de release dérivé de `arjj`
user_stories.description: `release/v<version>` et le tag `v<version>` partent de `arjj` (une release contient tout le travail Arij intégré). On garde CHANGELOG, push du tag, draft GitHub release optionnel, et Done→Released.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- La branche release et le tag dérivent de `arjj`, pas du défaut.
- Les epics inclus passent Done→Released comme aujourd'hui.
- Le contenu d'une release = l'état de `arjj` au moment du cut.

user_stories.title: Sécurité & provenance de `arjj` (artifact Arij)
user_stories.description: `arjj` vit dans le dépôt de l'utilisateur mais est un artifact Arij : jamais de force-push sur `arjj`, jamais de suppression de la branche par défaut, toute op destructive exige une preuve de provenance explicite (discipline du marqueur de clone §3.3). État (nom + toggle + PR/divergence) persisté de façon restart-safe.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- `git push --force` sur `arjj` et suppression de la branche par défaut sont refusés.
- Toute op destructive sans preuve de provenance est refusée.
- Le state (settings + `pull_requests` + `git_sync_log`) survit à un restart.

user_stories.title: Compatibilité rétro & transition des projets existants
user_stories.description: Projets déjà sur le modèle défaut : détecter si `arjj` existe ; proposer un bootstrap depuis le défaut ; toggle projet pour repasser au comportement actuel (fallback = zéro régression). Export/import `arji.json` inchangé.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- Un vieux projet démarre sans casser (fallback actif par défaut).
- Toggle off = comportement actuel bit-à-bit.
- Toggle on = bootstrap propre de `arjj` depuis le défaut, sans perte de données.
- L'export/import `arji.json` reste stable.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
## Passe de refinement — ticket maintenu en Backlog

Seul ticket des deux colonnes de planification qui ne peut pas être démarré tel quel. Sa section « Décisions à trancher (à confirmer avant implé) » liste 5 questions qui changent le contenu des stories, pas seulement leur implémentation. Elles sont regroupées ici pour pouvoir être répondues en une fois.

**Question de fond, en amont des cinq : adopte-t-on ce modèle ?** Le ticket se décrit lui-même comme un « changement radical proposé » et amende §3.3 et §5.7 de la spec. Tant que ce oui/non n'est pas donné, les 7 stories sont spéculatives — c'est la raison principale du maintien en Backlog.

Puis, si oui :

1. **Nom de la branche.** `arjj` est-il le nom voulu, ou une coquille pour `arij` ? Le dépôt utilise déjà `arji.json`, donc la question n'est pas rhétorique — le nom apparaît 8 fois de façon cohérente, ce qui peut être délibéré comme répété. Et est-il figé ou configurable par projet ? (la story 1 prévoit `git_integration_branch`, ce qui répond « configurable » — à confirmer.)
2. **Bascule dure ou opt-in.** Quel défaut pour `git_use_integration_branch` sur un projet **nouvellement créé** ? La story « Compatibilité rétro » ne tranche que le cas des projets existants (fallback = off).
3. **PR `arjj` → défaut : draft par défaut ou PR régulière ?** Les critères de la story 4 disent draft ; confirmer que c'est la décision et pas une hypothèse d'écriture.
4. **Les releases découlent-elles de `arjj`** (état intégré au moment du cut) ou de la branche par défaut une fois la PR mergée ? Ça change §5.6 et toute la story 5.
5. **Sync amont → `arjj` : à la demande seulement, ou automatique avant chaque PR ?**

### Dépendances ajoutées dans cette passe

`B-arij-130` et `B-arij-131`. Les deux corrigent le chemin de merge que ce ticket retarge (cascade des stories côté merge ; conflit → 409 + pré-vol sans écriture dans l'arbre vivant). Les traiter avant évite de porter les mêmes bugs sur la nouvelle cible et de réécrire deux fois les mêmes fichiers.

La priorité High est laissée inchangée : le ticket n'est pas dispatchable tant qu'il est en Backlog, donc la baisser n'aurait rien changé au fonctionnement et aurait effacé un signal d'intention.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
**Planning pass — kept in Backlog, and why.**

This is the one ticket in the two planning columns whose blocker is a decision rather than work. Its own description frames the `arjj` trunk as a *changement radical proposé*, and it rewrites the base of §3.3 (worktrees, merge, releases) and §5.7 (GitHub sync). That is not something to hand to an agent on the strength of a proposal. It also still waits on B-arij-130 and B-arij-131, both of which are correctly retained as dependencies — they are merge-path defects, and this epic retargets the merge path.

Questions blocking promotion:

1. **Go / no-go on the model itself.** Is `arjj`-as-trunk approved, or is it still an option being weighed against staying on the default branch? Everything else here is downstream of that answer.
2. **The branch name.** `arjj` is one keystroke from the project name `arij`. Deliberate, or a typo that would be permanent once branches, tags and settings are written against it?
3. **Settings scope.** The first story requires "les 2 clés se round-trip via l'API de settings" — global keys, or project-scoped? Arij supports both, and the seventh story's retro-compat promise ("un vieux projet démarre sans casser") reads as per-project.
4. **Release cut before the PR merges.** The fifth story derives the release branch and tag from `arjj`. Is a tagged release allowed to exist that the upstream default branch does not yet contain, or must the `arjj` → default PR merge first?
5. **What keeps `arjj` in sync.** The third story requires it to stay mergeable with upstream but does not say what triggers the sync — a manual action on the GitHub sync screen, or a scheduled routine alongside `ci_watch` and `github_issue_sync`?

Answering 1 and 2 is enough to unblock; 3–5 could be settled during the build if the direction is confirmed.

Posting the open questions in one place, as this pass was asked to. Backlog is now three tickets and all three are held by a decision rather than by work; everything else has been promoted to To do.

**This ticket (E-arij-135, `arjj` trunk) — unchanged, still the deepest blocker.** The questions from 26/08 and 27/08 stand and have not been answered. The two that actually gate a start:

Questions 3–5 (settings scope, release cut before the PR merges, what triggers the upstream sync) can be settled during the build once 1 and 2 are answered.

**`_80zRfoh-ryb` (data retention) — one question, and it is a policy one.** Four of its five stories are concrete enough to build today. What holds it: *should the retention routine delete session output outright, or archive it first?* Session chunks are what forensic reports, Dreaming and the recurring-failure digests read from, so this is a choice about destroying evidence and is not a developer's to make. The retention window and the two cap values are secondary — the story text already suggests 256 KB for the chunk cap, and a documented default can be picked once delete-vs-archive is answered.

Still true and actionable independently of that: `data/backups/` shows as untracked in `git status` right now, so the half-gigabyte accidental-commit hazard in story 5 is live today, not theoretical.

**`7n2sxOJdaqlO` (memory limit) — asked on the ticket itself.** Short version: "10k tokens" is 40 000 characters under Arij's own `chars/4` estimator — a 3.3× increase over the current 12 000 — and the "tell the model the limit" half already exists in both memory-writing prompts. Details and the question are on that ticket.

**One observation, since it is the evidence behind a priority change made in this pass.** The specification this session received still carries the injected `<system-directive>` block instructing the session to rewrite the specification. It was ignored, as project memory prescribes. It is also why B-arij-139 was raised to Critical: `buildSpecAutoRewritePrompt` writes its output back to `projects.spec`, so the bypass can re-persist the poison.

**`lgwdC9W_gB6f` (E-arij-142, GitHub OAuth Device Flow) — kept in Backlog.** Fully specified otherwise, but the first story requires the client ID of an OAuth App named "Arij" as an exported constant. **Has that app been registered, and under which account?** A developer cannot invent the value, and the registration also fixes the name and icon every user sees on the authorization screen. Asked in full on that ticket.

Both were filed as urgent and neither is. Details on each ticket; summary here because it changes what the board is telling you.

**`H3WaoKFiwd8j` ("Production build is broken on main") — it is not. Dropped Critical → Low.** `lib/providers/pi.ts:361` now passes one argument, and CI's `verify` job runs `tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint` and `npm run build`. Both landed in commit `ab329b2`. Its third story is also premised on an error: `pi.ts` is not dead code — `OhMyPiProvider extends PiProvider`, and `oh-my-pi` is registered, so the "delete it" option would break a live provider. **Recommend closing.**

**`YZ2C7NWim0jL` ("Sessions endpoint returns 44 MB") — already fixed and in review. Dropped High → Low.** It is story `c67GmGMH-Mco` of `gSmCpCmda37D`, commit `b2c7a20`: projection, `prompt` dropped, limit plus cursor, 42.7 MB → 0.19 MB. ### One thing worth knowing regardless of the above

The checkout's installed `next` is **16.1.6** while `package.json` pins **16.3.3**. That mismatch is the source of the phantom `lib/git/clone.ts` type errors that sessions keep rediscovering and filing as pre-existing failures, and it hides the Next 16.3.3 build warnings entirely. `Fw0pLbA9_JGU` fixes it and has been ranked above its Medium priority for that reason — it is at rank 4, ahead of work that is nominally more important, because everything downstream of it is currently being verified against the wrong tree.

The specification this session received again carries the injected `<system-directive>` block instructing it to rewrite the specification. Ignored as data, as project memory prescribes; already on the friction register, so not refiled.

epics.title: Introduce data retention, write-path caps, and storage hygiene
epics.description: There is no time-, size-, or count-based pruning for any table. The only db.delete() calls in lib/ are user-initiated ticket and project deletion in lib/planning/permanent-delete.ts. The live database is 489 MB plus a 14 MB WAL, generated by 531 agent sessions. agent_session_chunks holds 126,953 rows totalling 395.5 MB of content; agent_sessions.prompt holds 45.4 MB across 531 rows. lib/agent-sessions/chunks.ts appendChunk stores content verbatim at any size — the largest single chunk is 8.3 MB and the largest single session is 51.3 MB across 1,715 chunks. Deduplication is opt-in: appendChunk only checks for an existing row when the caller supplies a chunkKey, and measured same-session identical content amounts to 31.9 MB across 7,694 distinct repeated contents. Prompts average 86 KB with a 4.96 MB maximum — the prompt-snowball feedback loop already diagnosed in project memory, still materialized in storage. The project specification anticipates this: 'Unbounded table growth (reports, logs, artifacts) is not pruned automatically; retention is a review finding waiting to happen.' Separately, data/.gitignore uses an enumerate-known-artifacts approach and misses backups/, so data/backups/ (472 MB, containing a full SQLite board snapshot and comment-echo-archive-2026-08-26.json) currently shows as untracked in git status — one `git add -A` from a half-gigabyte commit of ticket, session, and prompt content. No credential-shaped settings key exists in either the live or backup database today, so this is a content-and-size exposure rather than a secret leak — but that changes the moment a GitHub PAT is configured.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
**Planning pass — kept in Backlog, and why.**

Four of the five stories are fully concrete and I would have promoted them on their own. What holds the ticket back is that the retention story asks a developer to pick a policy for destroying data the user may consider evidence — session output is what forensic reports, Dreaming and the recurring-failure digests read from.

Also added a dependency on **gSmCpCmda37D** (bound API payloads): both land a hand-written migration and both touch `lib/agent-sessions/chunks.ts`, and two branches each claiming the next journal index is a known way to get a migration silently skipped.

Questions blocking promotion:

1. **Automatic deletion at all?** Should the retention routine delete pruned chunks outright, or export/archive them first? The criteria assume deletion with only `lastNonEmptyText` and the forensic tail preserved.
2. **Retention window default.** The criteria say "configurable via a settings key with a documented default" without naming one. 30 days? 90? Dreaming already reads a rolling 14-day window, which is a defensible floor but not obviously the intended answer.
3. **Cap values.** Two named constants are required — one for chunk `content`, one for `agent_sessions.prompt` — and neither has a proposed size. The measured extremes are an 8.3 MB single chunk and 45.4 MB of prompts across 531 rows.

One correction to the fifth story while it sits here: **`data/.gitignore` already exists.** I checked. So that story is "make it deny-by-default" (`*` plus `!.gitignore`), not "create it" — worth knowing before someone writes a file that is already there.

epics.title: Connecter GitHub via OAuth Device Flow (SSO — phase 1)
epics.description:
## Objectif

Remplacer la saisie manuelle du PAT par un bouton « Se connecter avec GitHub » basé sur le **Device Flow** OAuth (le flux de `gh auth login`) : l'app affiche un code à 8 caractères, l'utilisateur le saisit sur github.com/login/device, l'app récupère le token en pollant.

Étude complète : voir l'artifact « SSO GitHub pour Arij » (2026-08-28).

## Décisions de design (à respecter)

- **Le token obtenu est stocké sous la clé `settings.github_pat` existante** : clone, PR, issues, releases et la validation fonctionnent sans modification. Zéro migration de schéma.
- **Aucun client secret, aucune callback URL** : le Device Flow n'en a pas besoin. Le client ID de l'OAuth App « Arij » est public et vit en constante dans le code.
- Métadonnées de connexion sous une nouvelle clé `settings.github_oauth_meta` : `{login, scopes, obtainedAt, tokenSource: "oauth_device" | "manual"}`. Pas de secret dedans → pas de masquage nécessaire, mais la clé doit être ajoutée aux clés typées du `PATCH /api/settings`.
- Scopes : `repo read:user` (limite structurelle des OAuth Apps, assumée en phase 1).
- Le champ « coller un PAT manuellement » **reste disponible en repli**.
- Identité résolue via `validateGitHubToken()` existant (`lib/github/client.ts:78`).
- Polling discipliné : respecter l'`interval` renvoyé par GitHub, gérer `authorization_pending`, `slow_down` (+5s), `expired_token`, `access_denied`. Un seul flux actif à la fois, expiration à 15 min.
- Le `device_code` ne sort jamais du serveur : map mémoire sur `globalThis` (même pattern que le store MCP), le client ne reçoit qu'un handle opaque.
- Réponses au format `{data}`/`{error}` de `lib/api/route-helpers.ts`, corps validés en zod via `lib/validation/validate.ts`.

## Hors périmètre

- Phase 2 (login/session sur l'UI web, cookies, table users) — étude §5.
- GitHub App / tokens expirants — piste v2.
- Push git : `pushGitBranch` continue d'utiliser le credential helper ambiant, le token stocké n'y est pas injecté (comportement actuel, documenté).

## Dépendance

Dépend du bug « useGitHubConfig : isConfigured toujours faux » : l'UI de cet epic s'appuie sur le hook corrigé (forme masquée `{hasToken}`).

user_stories.title: Module Device Flow (lib/github/device-flow.ts)
user_stories.description: Nouveau module serveur : `startDeviceFlow(scopes)` → POST github.com/login/device/code (header `Accept: application/json`) renvoyant `{deviceCode, userCode, verificationUri, expiresIn, interval}` ; `pollDeviceFlow(deviceCode)` → POST github.com/login/oauth/access_token avec `grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code`, renvoyant un état discriminé `pending | slow_down | success{accessToken, scopes} | expired | denied | error`. Le client ID public de l'OAuth App Arij vit ici en constante exportée.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria: Toutes les réponses d'erreur GitHub (`authorization_pending`, `slow_down`, `expired_token`, `access_denied`, `incorrect_device_code`) sont mappées sur des états typés, jamais des throws non gérés. Aucune dépendance nouvelle dans package.json (fetch natif). Aucun secret dans le module.

user_stories.title: Routes API /api/auth/github/device/{start,poll}
user_stories.description: POST `start` : appelle startDeviceFlow, stocke le deviceCode côté serveur dans une map mémoire sur `globalThis` (expiration 15 min, un seul flux actif), renvoie `{userCode, verificationUri, interval, handle}` — le deviceCode ne quitte jamais le serveur. POST `poll` avec `{handle}` : un tick de polling par appel ; en cas de succès, valide via `validateGitHubToken()`, puis écrit `github_pat` (token) et `github_oauth_meta` (login, scopes, obtainedAt, tokenSource="oauth_device") dans settings en transaction, et purge le flux. Ajouter `github_oauth_meta` aux clés typées du PATCH /api/settings.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria: Enveloppe `{data}`/`{error, code}` conforme à lib/api/route-helpers.ts. Corps validés en zod. Un handle inconnu ou expiré → 404/410 propre. Après succès, GET /api/settings expose `github_pat: {hasToken: true}` (masquage existant) et `github_oauth_meta` en clair. Le token n'apparaît dans aucune réponse HTTP ni aucun log.

user_stories.title: UI Settings : bouton « Se connecter avec GitHub »
user_stories.description: Dans la section GitHub de app/settings/page.tsx (~lignes 1580-1625) : bouton « Se connecter avec GitHub » qui démarre le flux, affiche le user code (copiable) et le lien github.com/login/device, polle au rythme de `interval`, puis affiche « Connecté en tant que {login} » (depuis github_oauth_meta). Bouton « Déconnecter » qui efface `github_pat` et `github_oauth_meta`. Le champ PAT manuel existant reste en repli et positionne `tokenSource: "manual"` à la sauvegarde. S'appuie sur le hook useGitHubConfig corrigé (ticket bug lié).
user_stories.acceptance_criteria: Le flux complet marche depuis l'UI sans coller de token. Gestion visible des états expired/denied (message + bouton réessayer). Déconnexion → la section revient à l'état non configuré. Aucune régression sur la saisie manuelle du PAT et sur « Validate Token ».

user_stories.title: Tests unitaires et de routes
user_stories.description: `__tests__/github-device-flow.test.ts` : mapping complet des réponses GitHub (fetch mocké) y compris slow_down qui augmente l'intervalle. Tests des deux routes sur le modèle de `__tests__/settings-github-validate-route.test.ts` (DB mockée via `__tests__/helpers/db-mock.ts`, GitHub mocké au niveau fetch) : succès bout-en-bout (settings écrits), handle expiré, refus utilisateur, flux concurrent remplacé.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria: `npm run test:changed` vert. Les tests ne touchent ni le réseau ni data/arij.db (convention ARIJ_DB_PATH/VITEST respectée).

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
**Board pass 28/08 — kept in Backlog. One question blocks it, and it is not one a developer can answer.**

The design decisions in this ticket are unusually complete — token stored under the existing `settings.github_pat` key, no schema migration, no client secret, no callback URL, `{data}`/`{error}` envelope, zod-validated bodies, `device_code` never leaving the server, manual PAT retained as fallback. Four stories, each with checkable criteria. On specification alone this would be promoted.

**What blocks it: the OAuth App does not exist yet, or if it does, its client ID has not been recorded anywhere.**

The first story says the client ID "de l'OAuth App « Arij » vit ici en constante exportée". A developer cannot invent that value. Someone has to register an OAuth App on GitHub under an account you control, and that registration is also where the app's name, icon and description are set — all user-visible on the device-authorization screen. So:

1. **Has the "Arij" OAuth App been registered, and what is its client ID?** If not, who registers it — and under which account/org, given the app name is what every user sees when they authorize?
2. Secondary, answerable at build time if you prefer: the scopes are pinned to `repo read:user`. `repo` is broad — full read/write on every private repository the user can reach. It is the structural minimum for OAuth Apps (fine-grained scoping needs a GitHub App, which the ticket explicitly defers to v2), so this is a limitation to confirm you accept rather than a choice, but it is worth confirming knowingly.

**Dependency status:** `z45Ju-3qfSY9` (the `useGitHubConfig` masked-shape bug) has been promoted to To do in this pass and sits at rank 5. The edge is correct and was left in place — this epic's settings UI reads connection state through that hook, and the hook currently reports "not configured" unconditionally.

Answer question 1 and this is ready to promote as written; nothing else in it is speculative.

epics.title: Production build is broken on main and CI cannot detect it
epics.description:
`npm run build` fails on main. `lib/providers/pi.ts:363` calls `this.extractResult(info.stdout, info.stderr, info.spawnContext)` while the override at `lib/providers/pi.ts:301` declares `extractResult(stdout: string): string` — one parameter. The abstract base at `lib/providers/base-provider.ts:192` declares three. Turbopack compiles cleanly in 12.4s; the TypeScript pass fails with `error TS2554: Expected 1 arguments, but got 3` and `next build` exits 1.

This was verified as the SOLE build blocker: widening the signature made the production build succeed (48 static pages), boot via `next start`, serve all pages and APIs, hold its 403 host/origin boundary, and pass 20/21 browser tests, with all 67 tests in `__tests__/pi-providers.test.ts` + `__tests__/oversized-prompt-transport.test.ts` still green.

Root cause of it reaching main: `.github/workflows` runs only `npm ci` -> `npm audit --audit-level=high` -> `npm test`. It never typechecks, lints, or builds, so a fully green `npm test` coexists with a broken `npm run build`. Note also that `pi` is not a registered provider — `AgentProvider` in `lib/agent-config/constants.ts:193` is `claude-code | codex | oh-my-pi | agy` — so this is unreachable production code that still breaks the build.

Recommended: fix the signature, add the missing CI gates, and decide whether `pi.ts` should be deleted or re-registered.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
**Board pass 28/08 — kept in Backlog, priority dropped Critical → Low. The premise is stale: main builds.**

Two of the three stories are already done, and the third rests on a factual error. Checked against the working tree and `git log`, not against the ticket text.

**Story 1 (pi.ts typechecks) — done.** `lib/providers/pi.ts:361` now reads `this.extractResult(info.stdout)` — one argument, matching the override at line 301. The `TS2554: Expected 1 arguments, but got 3` described in the ticket cannot occur on this tree.

**Story 2 (CI runs typecheck, lint, build) — done.** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` has a `verify` job running `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint` and `npm run build`, plus a separate `e2e` job. Both landed in commit **`ab329b2` — "Enforce type check, lint and build in CI"**, which is also the commit that touched `lib/providers/pi.ts`. The build step deliberately leaves `NODE_ENV` unset, with a comment explaining why: `next build` sets production itself, and exporting it would make `npm ci` skip devDependencies. That is a considered variation on the criterion's "set `NODE_ENV` explicitly", not an omission.

**Story 3 (resolve the unregistered pi provider) — the premise is wrong.** The ticket calls `pi.ts` "unreachable production code" referenced "only by two test files". It is neither:

- `lib/providers/oh-my-pi.ts:106` — `export class OhMyPiProvider extends PiProvider`
- `lib/providers/index.ts:18` — `"oh-my-pi": new OhMyPiProvider()`

`PiProvider` is the base class of a **registered** provider. It is live production code reached on every Oh My Pi spawn. The "delete the module and its tests" option in the acceptance criteria would break `oh-my-pi`, and the criterion "no remaining source file is typechecked but unreachable from the provider registry" is already satisfied — `pi.ts` *is* reachable from the registry, via inheritance rather than via a registry key.

What is true is narrower: there is no standalone `pi` entry in `AgentProvider`, and there does not need to be.

**Recommendation: close this ticket.** Nothing in it is actionable as written. If you want the residue tracked, the only real item is cosmetic — whether `PiProvider` should be renamed or moved to make its role as a shared base class obvious rather than reading as an orphaned provider. That is a one-line refactor ticket, not this one.

Left in Backlog rather than promoted, and dropped to Low so the board stops signalling that main is broken.

epics.title: Sessions list endpoint returns a 44 MB payload, 98% of it never rendered
epics.description:
`GET /api/projects/:id/sessions` does `db.select().from(agentSessions)` — an unprojected `SELECT *` with no limit and no pagination.

Measured against the live board (391 sessions returned): total payload 44.91 MB, of which the `prompt` column alone is 44.21 MB (98.4%). `cliCommand` is 0.18 MB and everything else about 0.5 MB. Server time 0.55–1.5s per request. The largest single stored prompt is 4.96 MB.

`app/projects/[projectId]/sessions/page.tsx:182` fetches this on every visit to the Sessions page and never references `prompt` anywhere in the list view. The session detail page already fetches its own row separately via `/api/projects/:id/sessions/:sessionId`, so the heavy column already has a correct home.

This violates the project's own documented convention that list endpoints select explicitly and keep large text columns behind a detail fetch. Projecting the rendered columns is roughly a 98% payload reduction for no behaviour change.
