epics.title: Full Auto Mode: Standing Build / Review / Merge Supervisor
epics.description:
## Contexte

Arij dispose déjà de deux modes autonomes, mais ce sont tous les deux des rafales one-shot :
- `lib/pipeline/` fait passer *un* ticket par build → review → auto-fix puis s'arrête.
- `lib/night/` fait *une* passe DAG sur un lot d'epics puis se termine.

Aucun ne surveille le board en continu. Le mode Full Auto est le chaînon manquant : un superviseur permanent, activé par projet, avec des budgets de concurrence indépendants pour la build et la review.

Une fois activé, Arij en continu :
- build tout ce qui est en `todo`, plus tout ce qui est en `in_progress` sans agent dessus (ticket revenu d'une review négative) ;
- review tout ce qui est en `review` ;
- merge un ticket dès que sa review est propre.

## Décisions validées avec l'utilisateur

| Question | Réponse |
|---|---|
| Périmètre des tickets | Tous les tickets — epics, bugs et user stories |
| Merge après une review propre | Oui, le mode auto merge |
| Portée d'activation | Par projet |
| Si build+review > budget scheduler | Avertir seulement — ne jamais le remonter silencieusement |

## Réutilisation (ne rien réécrire)

| Besoin | Existant | Chemin |
|---|---|---|
| Dispatch build/review programmatique | `createPipelineStageDriver(...).launchStage({stage})` — « réplique les closures des routes au byte près pour que le board ne puisse pas distinguer une étape de pipeline d'un dispatch humain ». Supporte `scope: 'epic' \| 'story'`. | `lib/pipeline/stages.ts:140` |
| Primitive de merge | `mergeWorktree(gitRepoPath, branchName, worktreePath)` → `{merged, commitHash, error}` | `lib/git/manager.ts` |
| Porte « la review est OK » | Les gardes `→ done` du moteur de workflow | `lib/workflow/engine.ts:49-97` |
| Transition validée + event + log | `applyTransition({... source:'merge'})` | `lib/workflow/transition-service.ts:47` |
| « Un agent est-il déjà sur ce ticket ? » | `getRunningSessionForTarget(target)` — compte `queued` + `running` | `lib/agents/concurrency.ts:94` |
| « Ce ticket attend-il un humain ? » | `isAwaitingReply(signal)` — pur, client-safe | `lib/kanban/awaiting-reply.ts:30` |
| Budget de slots + file FIFO | `agentScheduler.submit(projectId, sessionId, launch)` | `lib/agents/scheduler.ts:124` |
| Patron de boucle permanente | Watchdog : singleton globalThis, `start()` idempotent, interval `unref()`, `sweep(now)` pur pour les tests | `lib/agents/watchdog.ts` |
| Patron de registre mémoire | `NightRunRegistry` — map active + ring récent, pas de table | `lib/night/registry.ts` |
| Convention constantes client-safe | clé + fn clé par projet + défaut + `parseX` renvoyant `null` pour tomber au niveau suivant | `lib/agents/scheduler-constants.ts` |
| Wiring au boot | `register()` dans `instrumentation.ts` (démarre déjà le watchdog) | `instrumentation.ts` |
| UI sélecteur agent + concurrence | `NightRunDialog` compose déjà `NamedAgentSelect` + `Input` de concurrence + `OptionRow` | `components/night/NightRunDialog.tsx` |

## La machine à états boucle déjà toute seule

Vérifié dans `lib/pipeline/stages.ts` :
- lancement build → epic `→ in_progress`, branche créée (`:585`)
- build réussie → epic `→ review` (`:745`)
- verdict de review négatif → epic `→ in_progress` (`:916`), sans agent dessus
- verdict positif → l'epic reste en `review`

Le superviseur ne fait que dispatcher ; c'est le driver qui déplace les tickets. Un ticket rejeté retombe en `in_progress` sans agent et est naturellement repris au sweep suivant.

## Granularité : « tous les tickets » face à une branche par epic

Git est la contrainte. Il y a un worktree et une branche par epic — la route de build story écrit `epics.branchName` et réutilise le worktree de l'epic, et `getRunningSessionForTarget` en scope story matche aussi les sessions de l'epic parent (`lib/agents/concurrency.ts:65-70`), donc deux stories du même epic ne peuvent jamais tourner en parallèle. Cette garde existe déjà ; le mode auto en hérite gratuitement.

Règle retenue :
- Build → scope story quand l'epic a des stories (une à la fois par epic, plein d'epics en parallèle) ; scope epic sinon. La route de build story promeut déjà l'epic en `review` quand toutes les stories sœurs sont review/done (`stories/[storyId]/build/route.ts:303-330`).
- Review et merge → toujours au scope epic. La branche est l'unité d'intégration et `epic.branchName` est ce qui se merge. Reviewer chaque story *puis* l'epic doublerait le coût en tokens pour le même diff.

## Les quatre pièges à traiter

1. Re-review infinie. Une review qui passe laisse l'epic en `review`. Un balayage naïf le re-reviewerait sans fin. → Un epic en `review` n'est candidat que s'il n'a aucune session de review terminale plus récente que sa dernière session de code terminale. Délibérément temporel, pas basé sur le verdict : le verdict est une heuristique de sous-chaîne sur le markdown de l'agent (`epics/[epicId]/review/route.ts:337`), sans champ structuré.

2. Écraser une question d'agent. Un agent finissant en `asked_question` laisse le ticket maintenu en `in_progress` par `handleAskedQuestionOutcome` (`lib/workflow/agent-question.ts:42`) — indiscernable de « revient de review » pour un sélecteur naïf. → Exclure tout ticket où `isAwaitingReply(...)` est vrai ; il redevient éligible dès que l'utilisateur répond par un commentaire.

3. Merger quelque chose qui n'est pas réellement approuvé. « Review OK » n'existe comme booléen nulle part. → Ne pas en inventer un. `applyTransition(→ done, source:'merge')` refuse déjà tant que `hasCompletedReview` est faux *ou* que `hasOpenReviewComments` est vrai (`lib/workflow/engine.ts:51-63`). Le mode auto tente la transition et traite un refus comme « pas prêt, on passe ». Sa propre porte est *plus stricte* que celle du moteur, car la fraîcheur du piège 1 compense le fait que `hasCompletedReview` est laxiste (`lib/workflow/context.ts:32-51`). → Ne surtout pas réutiliser `POST .../approve` : il résout en masse tous les commentaires de review ouverts (`approve/route.ts:30-38`), écrasant exactement les findings bloquants qui doivent empêcher un merge auto.

4. Double comptage des budgets. Build (N) + review (M) vivent *au-dessus* du budget `agent_max_concurrent` par projet (`lib/agents/scheduler.ts:81`, défaut 3). Si N+M le dépasse, le mode admet du travail qui s'empile dans la file FIFO — et comme `getRunningSessionForTarget` compte les `queued`, le board paraît occupé sans rien exécuter. → Admission control sur ses propres sessions en vol, et avertissement dans le dialog quand N+M dépasse le budget (décision utilisateur : avertir seulement).

## Plan d'implémentation

Aucune migration. Toute la config vit dans la table clé/valeur `settings` existante et chaque session dispatchée est une ligne `agent_sessions` ordinaire.

1. `lib/auto-mode/constants.ts` (client-safe, sans import `db`) — clés par projet avec repli global : `auto_mode_enabled:<projectId>`, `auto_mode_build_agent:<projectId>`, `auto_mode_build_concurrency:<projectId>`, `auto_mode_review_agent:<projectId>`, `auto_mode_review_concurrency:<projectId>`. Plus `DEFAULT_AUTO_BUILD_CONCURRENCY = 2`, `DEFAULT_AUTO_REVIEW_CONCURRENCY = 1`, `AUTO_MODE_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS = 15_000`, parsers renvoyant `null`, `resolveAutoModeConfig(settingsMap, projectId)` pour l'UI, chaînes de raison d'activity-log préfixées `"Auto mode "`, et `AUTO_RUN_ID_PREFIX = "auto_"` pour tamponner `batchRunId`.
2. `lib/auto-mode/config.ts` — résolveur serveur par projet → global → défaut, copie de `resolveMaxConcurrentForProject`.
3. `lib/auto-mode/select.ts` — les trois sélecteurs (build, review, merge) avec toutes les exclusions.
4. `lib/auto-mode/registry.ts` — état mémoire globalThis + map de parking.
5. `lib/auto-mode/merge.ts` — `tryAutoMerge(projectId, epicId)`.
6. `lib/auto-mode/engine.ts` — le sweep avec mutex par projet.
7. Extension du driver : ajouter `reviewNamedAgentId` optionnel à `PipelineStageDriverInit`.
8. `instrumentation.ts` — `startAutoMode()` + chaînage du hook terminal.
9. `app/api/projects/[projectId]/auto-mode/route.ts` — GET/PUT.
10. `components/auto-mode/AutoModeDialog.tsx` + toggle dans la toolbar du board.

## Hors périmètre

Reviews par story (les stories sont des unités de travail, les epics des unités d'intégration), switch global multi-projets, table persistée pour l'état du mode, planification horaire (le mode est ON/OFF, pas « de 22h à 6h »).

user_stories.title: As a developer, I want auto-mode configuration stored in the settings table with a client-safe constants module, so that I can enable the mode per project and tune agents and concurrency without a schema migration
user_stories.description: Create `lib/auto-mode/constants.ts` following the exact convention established by `lib/agents/scheduler-constants.ts` and `lib/pipeline/constants.ts`: a header comment explaining why the file is split, the global setting key, a `<key>:<projectId>` per-project override function, defaults with an inclusive clamp range, and a `parseX` returning `null` for "not configured" so callers fall through the chain. The five keys are `auto_mode_enabled`, `auto_mode_build_agent`, `auto_mode_build_concurrency`, `auto_mode_review_agent`, `auto_mode_review_concurrency`. Also export `AUTO_MODE_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS = 15_000`, `AUTO_RUN_ID_PREFIX = "auto_"`, an `AUTO_MODE_REASONS` object mirroring `PIPELINE_REASONS`, and a client-side `resolveAutoModeConfig(settingsMap, projectId)` for the dialog. Add the server-side resolver in `lib/auto-mode/config.ts` as a direct copy of `resolveMaxConcurrentForProject` (`lib/agents/scheduler.ts:81`), re-read on every sweep so config changes apply without a restart. Because `PATCH /api/settings` always `JSON.stringify`s values (`app/api/settings/route.ts:71`), every parser must tolerate both raw and JSON-encoded forms — copy the `coerceNumber` body from `lib/night/constants.ts:81`.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `lib/auto-mode/constants.ts` exists, imports nothing from `lib/db`, and is safely importable from a client component
- [ ] The five setting keys are exported with a global constant plus a `<key>:<projectId>` per-project override function
- [ ] `DEFAULT_AUTO_BUILD_CONCURRENCY = 2` and `DEFAULT_AUTO_REVIEW_CONCURRENCY = 1`; concurrency is clamped to 0..10 with 0 meaning "do not dispatch this kind"
- [ ] Every parser returns `null` for unconfigured/invalid input and accepts raw values, numeric strings, and JSON-encoded strings
- [ ] `AUTO_MODE_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS = 15_000` and `AUTO_RUN_ID_PREFIX = "auto_"` are exported; the prefix does not collide with `isNightRunId`'s `night_`
- [ ] `lib/auto-mode/config.ts` resolves per-project key → global key → built-in default, and is re-read on each call
- [ ] No database migration is added; `lib/db/migrations/` is untouched
- [ ] Unit tests cover the parser fall-through chain and the clamp boundaries

user_stories.title: As a developer, I want candidate selectors that identify buildable, reviewable and mergeable tickets, so that the supervisor never dispatches onto a ticket that is busy, waiting on a human, or already reviewed
user_stories.description: Create `lib/auto-mode/select.ts` with `selectBuildCandidates`, `selectReviewCandidates` and `selectMergeCandidates`. All three exclude tickets that have an active (`queued`/`running`) session via `getRunningSessionForTarget`, are owned by a live pipeline run (`pipelineRegistry`), DAG batch (`dagBatchRegistry`) or night run (`nightRunRegistry`) — the same three conflicts the batch route already refuses on (`app/api/projects/[projectId]/build/route.ts:742-775`) — are `isAwaitingReply`, or are parked. Build candidates follow the granularity rule: stories (status `todo` or `in_progress`) when the epic has stories, else the epic itself; skip anything whose epic is `done`/`released`; order by epic `priority DESC, position ASC` then story `position ASC`. Review candidates are epics in `review` passing the freshness guard. Merge candidates are epics in `review` with a non-null `branchName`, already reviewed since their last code change, and zero open `review_comments`. Use one batched query per sweep — follow `loadEpicStatuses` (`lib/dependencies/validation.ts:228`) and the LEFT-JOIN-IS-NULL idiom — never N per-ticket lookups. The module lives in `lib/auto-mode/` (not `lib/kanban/`, which is by convention client-safe and DB-free) but may import the pure `isAwaitingReply` predicate from it.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] An epic in `review` whose newest terminal review session is newer than its newest terminal code session is NOT a review candidate (infinite re-review guard)
- [ ] An epic in `review` whose newest terminal session is a build IS a review candidate
- [ ] A ticket in `in_progress` whose latest session outcome is `asked_question` with no newer user comment is NOT a build candidate, and becomes one after the user comments
- [ ] A ticket with a `queued` or `running` session is excluded from all three selectors
- [ ] Tickets owned by a live pipeline run, DAG batch or night run are excluded from all three selectors
- [ ] An epic with user stories yields story-scoped build candidates; an epic without yields itself as an epic-scoped candidate
- [ ] An epic with at least one open `review_comment` is NOT a merge candidate
- [ ] Tickets whose epic is `done` or `released` are never candidates
- [ ] Each selector issues a bounded number of queries independent of ticket count (no N+1)
- [ ] `__tests__/auto-mode-select.test.ts` covers every bullet above using `createTestDb()

user_stories.title: As a developer, I want a standing sweep engine with independent build and review budgets, so that the board drains itself continuously without ever exceeding the concurrency I configured
user_stories.description: Create `lib/auto-mode/registry.ts` (globalThis-backed, modeled on `NightRunRegistry`: enabled flag, in-flight build and review session id sets, last sweep timestamp, rolling recent-dispatch list, and a parked map of `ticketId → consecutive failure count`) and `lib/auto-mode/engine.ts` (the sweep, guarded by a per-project mutex so two ticks never overlap). Sweep order: read config and bail if disabled; reconcile in-flight ids whose session rows are terminal; merge every merge candidate (cheap, no slot) to free the `review` column first; then dispatch reviews while `inFlightReviews < M`; then builds while `inFlightBuilds < N`. Every action is logged via `logTransition` (actor `system`, `"Auto mode "`-prefixed reason) so the ticket activity feed explains why an agent appeared unprompted. Dispatch reuses `createPipelineStageDriver({projectId, scope, epicId, userStoryId, buildNamedAgentId, reviewNamedAgentId, batchRunId: 'auto_<projectId>'}).launchStage({stage, attempt: 1, fixCycle: 0, previousAttemptSessionId: null, lastCodeSessionId: null})`, calling the driver's own `checkGuards(ownSessionIds)` (`lib/pipeline/stages.ts:205`) immediately before each dispatch as the last-moment race check. Three consecutive failures parks a ticket. Start/stop mirror the watchdog: idempotent `startAutoMode()`/`stopAutoMode()`, globalThis-backed `Symbol.for("arij.auto-mode")` interval, `.unref()`'d, with a pure `sweep(now)` exported for tests. Add `startAutoMode()` to `instrumentation.ts` next to `startSessionWatchdog()`, and chain an auto-mode kick into the session terminal hook — note `setSessionTerminalHook` is a single slot, so register one composed callback calling both `maybeAutoDistillAfterSessionTerminal` and the kick rather than overwriting it; the timer sweep stays as the backstop.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `startAutoMode()` is idempotent, survives dev hot reloads via a `globalThis` symbol, and its interval is `.unref()`'d so it never keeps the process alive
- [ ] A pure `sweep(now)` is exported and can be driven directly by tests with fake timers
- [ ] A per-project mutex guarantees two sweeps never overlap for the same project
- [ ] The engine never exceeds N in-flight builds or M in-flight reviews of its own dispatch
- [ ] Setting build or review concurrency to 0 disables that dispatch kind without disabling the other
- [ ] Dispatch goes through `createPipelineStageDriver(...).launchStage(...)` — not through HTTP routes, and not by duplicating the batch route's `launchEpic` closure
- [ ] Every dispatched session carries `batchRunId = auto_<projectId>` and is visible in the sessions viewer
- [ ] Every dispatch and skip writes a `logTransition` entry with actor `system` and an `"Auto mode "`-prefixed reason
- [ ] A ticket that fails 3 consecutive times is parked and skipped until the mode is toggled or the ticket is touched
- [ ] `instrumentation.ts` starts the mode and registers a composed terminal hook that preserves `maybeAutoDistillAfterSessionTerminal`
- [ ] Disabling the mode clears registry state and stops all further dispatch
- [ ] `__tests__/auto-mode-engine.test.ts` asserts the N/M caps, the mutex, and parking after 3 failures using an injected fake dispatcher and config resolver

user_stories.title: As a user, I want a clean review to merge the ticket automatically, so that finished work lands on main without me clicking Approve on every epic
user_stories.description: Create `lib/auto-mode/merge.ts` exposing `tryAutoMerge(projectId, epicId)`. Step 1: call `mergeWorktree(project.gitRepoPath, epic.branchName, worktreePath)` — plain git, no agent, no scheduler slot. Step 2 on success: call `applyTransition({fromStatus: 'review', toStatus: 'done', actor: 'agent', source: 'merge', reason: 'Auto mode: review clean, merged'})`, then update the epic to `status: 'done', branchName: null` and call `tryExportArjiJson(projectId)` — mirroring `merge/route.ts:77-102`. A guard refusal from `applyTransition` is logged and the epic is skipped, NOT parked, so it retries once its review comments are resolved. Step 3 on conflict: dispatch a merge-fix agent (`agentType: 'merge'`, prompt from `merge/route.ts:129-140`) counted against the build budget, then retry the merge once; a second failure parks the epic and raises a notification. The critical design constraint: the engine's `→ done` guards ARE the "review is OK" gate — `applyTransition` already refuses unless `hasCompletedReview` is true and `hasOpenReviewComments` is false (`lib/workflow/engine.ts:51-63`), so no new boolean is invented. `POST .../approve` must NOT be reused: it bulk-resolves every open review comment before transitioning (`approve/route.ts:30-38`), which would steamroll exactly the blocking findings that should stop an auto-merge.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A conflict-free merge runs as pure git: no agent session is created and no scheduler slot is consumed
- [ ] On success the epic moves to `done`, `branchName` is cleared, and `tryExportArjiJson` is called
- [ ] The transition goes through `applyTransition` with `source: 'merge'` so events and activity logs are emitted
- [ ] An epic with at least one open `review_comment` is never merged; the guard refusal is logged and the epic is skipped, not parked
- [ ] An epic with no completed review is never merged
- [ ] `POST .../approve` is not called anywhere in the auto-mode code path
- [ ] On merge conflict a merge-fix agent is dispatched, counted against the build budget, and the merge is retried once after it completes
- [ ] A second merge failure parks the epic and raises a notification instead of looping

comments.content:
**Code Review**

# Code Review Report

Note: I could not file structured Arij MCP findings because the MCP call was rejected by the current approval policy (`never`). Review was performed from the working tree, with delegated read-only subreviews.

## Findings

### 1. Critical
**Location:** `instrumentation.ts:58`  
**Description:** The terminal hook kicks auto-mode synchronously from `markSessionTerminal`, before pipeline/merge closures finish their ticket updates. A successful build can be picked up again before it moves to `review`; a negative review can be merged before `finalizeReviewSession` moves it back to `in_progress`.  
**Recommendation:** Trigger auto-mode only after the full session finalization path completes, or defer the kick from an explicit post-finalize hook.

### 2. Major
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/merge.ts:266`  
**Description:** Merge-conflict recovery dispatches an agent into `worktreePath`, but `mergeWorktree` removes that worktree before attempting the merge (`lib/git/manager.ts:95`). The merge-fix agent can start in a missing cwd.  
**Recommendation:** Keep/recreate the worktree before dispatching the merge-fix agent, or use a helper that leaves the conflicted worktree intact.

### 3. Major
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/engine.ts:370`  
**Description:** Merge-fix sessions are dispatched before checking build-budget capacity, then “charged” afterward. With `buildConcurrency = 0`, or multiple merge conflicts, auto-mode can exceed its own build cap.  
**Recommendation:** Gate conflict-agent dispatch on available build capacity before launching it.

### 4. Major
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/select.ts:505`  
**Description:** `needsReview` treats failed/cancelled review sessions as fresh terminal reviews. A failed review leaves the epic in `review`, but then it is neither reviewed again nor mergeable, so parking never triggers.  
**Recommendation:** Let failed/cancelled review sessions remain review candidates until they complete successfully or hit the parking threshold.

### 5. Major
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/select.ts:518`  
**Description:** Merge freshness accepts any completed review session, including `asked_question` or `silent`. After the user answers a review question, the epic can become mergeable without a clean review verdict.  
**Recommendation:** Require an acceptable structured outcome, or introduce a real clean-review signal before auto-merge.

### 6. Major
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/select.ts:276`  
**Description:** Epic review facts aggregate story-scoped review sessions because they group only by `epicId`. A completed story review can satisfy the epic-level merge gate, despite the design requiring review/merge to be epic-scoped.  
**Recommendation:** Exclude `userStoryId IS NOT NULL` from epic review facts; keep story sessions only for code-change freshness where appropriate.

### 7. Major
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/select.ts:310`  
**Description:** Epic awaiting-reply facts also rank story-scoped sessions, but compare only epic-level user comments. A story question can keep the parent epic blocked even after the user replies on the story.  
**Recommendation:** Build epic awaiting facts from epic-scoped sessions only, or match story questions to story replies.

### 8. Major
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/merge.ts:461`  
**Description:** A merge-fix session that succeeds but whose retry fails parks the epic, but the completed session remains in auto-mode’s in-flight map. The next reconcile can clear the failure streak and unpark it.  
**Recommendation:** Remove merge-fix sessions from in-flight before parking, or preserve unresolved merge-conflict parks during reconcile.

### 9. Minor
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/config.ts:81`  
**Description:** `resolveAutoModeConfigForProject` can return `enabled: true` from the global key, while `listAutoModeEnabledProjectIds` only sweeps per-project enabled keys. UI/API can say enabled while the supervisor never runs.  
**Recommendation:** Make enabled strictly per-project or make sweep discovery honor the same fallback semantics.

### 10. Minor
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/constants.ts:283`  
**Description:** `AUTO_MODE_REASONS.merged` is `"Auto mode: ..."`, which does not match `AUTO_MODE_REASON_PREFIX = "Auto mode "`. `isAutoModeActivityReason` misses successful auto-merge activity.  
**Recommendation:** Align the reason prefix or update the predicate/tests to cover this expected string.

### 11. Minor
**Location:** `app/api/projects/[projectId]/auto-mode/route.ts:187`  
**Description:** PUT returns status before `kickAutoMode`, so runtime fields like `running`, `inFlight`, and `lastSweepAt` can be stale immediately after enable/disable.  
**Recommendation:** Mirror registry enablement before building the response, or return status after a synchronous state update.

### 12. Minor
**Location:** `components/auto-mode/AutoModeDialog.tsx:131`  
**Description:** The dialog load path does not check `res.ok`; a 404/500 JSON error can leave default/stale state with Save enabled.  
**Recommendation:** Treat non-2xx or missing `data` as a load error and disable save until valid status is loaded.

## Checklist Coverage

- **Readability:** No issues found.
- **DRY Principle:** No issues found.
- **Error Handling:** Findings 1, 2, 8, 12.
- **Performance:** No issues found.
- **Naming Conventions:** Finding 10.
- **Type Safety:** No issues found.
- **Testing:** Missing coverage for Findings 1-8, especially real merge-conflict worktree behavior and failed review retries.
- **API Design:** Findings 9, 11, 12.

## Summary

Critical: 1  
Major: 7  
Minor: 4  
Suggestion: 0

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

**Review findings fixed — all 12, one commit (`65f5830`). 2737 tests passing.**

I verified each finding against the code before changing anything; all 12 were real.

**[critical] Terminal-hook race.** Confirmed and worse than described. `markSessionTerminal` fires the hook synchronously, and `sweepProject` runs its board load + merge selection synchronously too — so the sweep ran entirely *before* `finalizeReviewSession`. An epic whose review had just come back negative still looked clean (in `review`, completed reviewer newer than the build, zero open findings) and got **merged into main**. Kicks are now debounced 250 ms onto a later macrotask. `__tests__/auto-mode-e2e.test.ts` reproduces the exact `markSessionTerminal` → revert ordering; I confirmed it fails when I temporarily restore the synchronous kick.

**[major] Merge-fix worktree.** Confirmed — `mergeWorktree` removes the worktree at `manager.ts:95` before merging, and the conflict path aborts without restoring it, so the agent got a deleted cwd. The branch survives (deletion only happens after a successful merge), so the conflict path now re-attaches with `createWorktree`.

**[major] Conflict-agent budget.** Now gated: the engine passes `dispatchConflictAgent` from free build capacity; `buildConcurrency: 0` dispatches none.

**[major] Failed reviews.** Confirmed a hard deadlock — a failed review was neither re-reviewable nor mergeable, and couldn't even reach the parking threshold. Only *completed* reviews count as an attempt now.

**[major] `asked_question` / `silent` satisfying the merge gate.** Split into two signals: `lastReviewAttemptAt` (blocks re-review) and `lastCleanReviewAt` (satisfies merge). `silent` blocks re-review but never approves — re-dispatching a reviewer that says nothing would just burn tokens.

**[major] Story sessions at epic level** (findings 6 + 7). Review and awaiting-reply facts are epic-scoped now. Story *builds* still count as code changes (same branch). A story question is answered by a comment on either thread, since the notification deep-links to the epic.

**[major] Un-parking a merge conflict.** Confirmed: the merge-fix agent completes *successfully* before its retry fails, so reconcile credited it and cleared the park → infinite loop. Merge-conflict parks are now **hard** — immune to `clearFailures`, reversed only by `unpark` or toggling the mode.

**Minors 9–12** all fixed: discovery honours the resolver's fallback chain; `isAutoModeActivityReason` matches the colon form (`Auto mode: review clean, merged` was being dropped from the feed); PUT mirrors the flag into the registry before responding; the dialog checks `res.ok` and disables Save on a failed load.

Also hardened beyond the findings: `finalizeMergedEpic` re-reads the epic status after the merge instead of validating against a snapshot taken seconds earlier — `mergeWorktree` is slow enough for a human to act during it.

**Second review round fixed — all 14, one commit (`ec4b6b4`). 2764 tests passing (269 files).**

**[major] Every failure treated as a conflict.** Failures now carry `reason: 'conflict' | 'branch-missing' | 'error'`; only a real conflict earns an agent.

**Code Review**

# Code Review Report

Note: Arij MCP `submit_findings` was attempted, but rejected by the current approval policy (`never`), so findings were not filed structurally. This was a source review; I did not rerun the full test suite.

## Findings

### 1. Critical
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/merge.ts:718`  
**Description:** The merge-conflict retry path calls `mergeWorktree` without the preflight/checkpoint/rollback protection used by the clean merge path. If the retry lands on `main` and `finalizeMergedEpic` then refuses, `main` stays changed while the ticket is parked outside `done`.  
**Recommendation:** Preflight again before retry, capture a retry checkpoint, and roll back/restoring the branch on post-retry guard refusal.

### 2. Critical
**Location:** `lib/git/manager.ts:173`  
**Description:** `rollbackMerge` resets the integration branch to the captured `mainHead` unconditionally. If `main` advanced after the checkpoint, rollback can discard unrelated commits.  
**Recommendation:** Serialize repo-level merge/rollback work, or verify current `HEAD` is exactly the auto-merge commit being undone before resetting.

### 3. Major
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/merge.ts:351`  
**Description:** Auto mode proceeds even when `captureMergeCheckpoint` returns `null`. If the post-merge guard refuses, there is no undo path.  
**Recommendation:** Treat missing checkpoint capture as a pre-merge skip/failure for unattended auto-merge.

### 4. Major
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/merge.ts:356`  
**Description:** `tryAutoMerge` does not do a last-moment active-session/status recheck before `mergeWorktree` removes the worktree and checks out `main`. A stale merge candidate can race with manual work.  
**Recommendation:** Re-read target status and `getRunningSessionForTarget` immediately before mutating git.

### 5. Major
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/merge.ts:569`  
**Description:** The merge lock is released only after `retryMergeAfterFix`. If the scheduled launch closure throws before that point, the scheduler marks the session failed while the auto-mode merge lock remains forever.  
**Recommendation:** Wrap the entire scheduled launch closure in `try/finally` and always call `endMergeWork`.

### 6. Major
**Location:** `lib/git/manager.ts:237`  
**Description:** Every `git merge` rejection is classified as `reason: "conflict"`. Non-conflict errors can incorrectly dispatch a merge-fix agent.  
**Recommendation:** Inspect `git status().conflicted`; return `reason: "error"` when no real conflict exists.

### 7. Major
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/registry.ts:147`  
**Description:** `setEnabled(projectId, false)` deletes all project state, including sweep and merge locks. Disable/re-enable during in-flight work can erase the mutex and allow overlapping sweeps/merges.  
**Recommendation:** Preserve active locks with a disabled/generation marker, then clear runtime state after active work releases.

### 8. Major
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/engine.ts:168`  
**Description:** Auto-mode review dispatch allows `targetStatus === "done"`. A stale review candidate can still dispatch after a human approves it, and review finalization may move the completed ticket back to `in_progress`.  
**Recommendation:** Require `targetStatus === "review"` for auto-mode review dispatch.

### 9. Major
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/engine.ts:673`  
**Description:** After `await deps.dispatch(...)`, the engine records the session in-flight without checking whether auto mode was disabled during the await.  
**Recommendation:** Re-check enabled state or a registry generation before mutating registry state.

### 10. Major
**Location:** `app/api/projects/[projectId]/auto-mode/route.ts:158`  
**Description:** `buildAgent` / `reviewAgent` accept arbitrary or deleted string IDs, so status can report an agent that dispatch later does not honor.  
**Recommendation:** Validate string IDs against `named_agents`; reject invalid non-null IDs.

### 11. Major
**Location:** `components/auto-mode/AutoModeDialog.tsx:156`  
**Description:** Invalid or empty concurrency input is coerced to defaults before save, so clearing the field can overwrite stored budgets with `2` / `1`.  
**Recommendation:** Treat `null` parse results as invalid UI state and disable Save.

### 12. Minor
**Location:** `lib/auto-mode/select.ts:462`  
**Description:** `storyRows.find(...)` runs once per latest story session, making board loading O(stories × storySessions).  
**Recommendation:** Build a `Map<storyId, story>` while processing `storyRows`.

## Checklist Coverage

- **Readability:** No issues found.
- **DRY Principle:** No issues found.
- **Error Handling:** Findings 1-7, 9.
- **Performance:** Finding 12.
- **Naming Conventions:** No issues found.
- **Type Safety:** No issues found.
- **Testing:** Missing coverage for findings 1-9 and the invalid UI/API inputs in findings 10-11.
- **API Design:** Finding 10.

## Summary

Critical: 2  
Major: 9  
Minor: 1  
Suggestion: 0

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

### Summary of Delivered Work: Full Auto Mode

We have implemented **Full Auto Mode: Standing Build / Review / Merge Supervisor** in full accordance with the epic specification and all user stories.

---

### Implementation Details by User Story

#### 1. Configuration & Constants (`lib/auto-mode/constants.ts`, `lib/auto-mode/config.ts`)
- Client-safe `lib/auto-mode/constants.ts` importing nothing from `lib/db`, defining global settings keys and per-project key helpers (`autoModeEnabledSettingKey`, `autoModeBuildAgentSettingKey`, `autoModeBuildConcurrencySettingKey`, `autoModeReviewAgentSettingKey`, `autoModeReviewConcurrencySettingKey`).
- Coercion parsers (`parseAutoModeEnabled`, `parseAutoModeConcurrency`, `parseAutoModeAgent`) tolerating raw, string, and JSON-encoded forms, clamping concurrency to $0..10$, and returning `null` for unconfigured values to allow fall-through.
- `lib/auto-mode/config.ts` resolving per-project key $\rightarrow$ global key $\rightarrow$ built-in default, discovering enabled projects via `listAutoModeEnabledProjectIds()`.
- **No schema migration added.**

#### 2. Review Agent Support in Pipeline Stage Driver (`lib/pipeline/stages.ts`)
- Added optional `reviewNamedAgentId?: string | null` to `PipelineStageDriverInit`.
- When set, review stage dispatch resolves the named agent (`init.reviewNamedAgentId`); when `null` or omitted, defaults to previous resolution behavior with reviewer provider segregation.

#### 3. Candidate Selectors (`lib/auto-mode/select.ts`)
- `selectBuildCandidates`: story-scoped candidates when epic has stories, epic-scoped otherwise; ordered by epic `priority DESC, position ASC` then story `position ASC`.
- `selectReviewCandidates`: epics in `review` with freshness temporal guard (newest terminal review newer than newest terminal code session excluded from re-review).
- `selectMergeCandidates`: epics in `review` with non-null `branchName`, fresh clean review, and 0 open review comments.
- Batched query architecture (`loadAutoModeBoard`) without N+1 queries.
- Exclusions for tickets with `queued`/`running` sessions (`getRunningSessionForTarget`), active pipeline runs, DAG batches, night runs, `isAwaitingReply`, and parked tickets.

#### 4. Auto-Merge on Clean Review (`lib/auto-mode/merge.ts`)
- Pure git merge via `mergeWorktree(repoPath, branchName, worktreePath)` without consuming scheduler slots or agent sessions for clean merges.
- Transitions through `applyTransition({ fromStatus, toStatus: 'done', actor: 'agent', source: 'merge' })`, clears `epics.branchName`, and calls `tryExportArjiJson`.
- On merge conflict: dispatches a `merge` fix agent charged to the build budget, with worktree re-attached to the exact surviving branch, and retries the merge once. A second failure parks the ticket with a hard flag and triggers `createAutoModeMergeParkedNotification`.
- Guard refusal or human intervention rolls back `main` and restores the branch via `rollbackMerge`.
- `POST .../approve` is strictly avoided to preserve blocking review comments.

#### 5. Standing Sweep Engine & Lifecycle (`lib/auto-mode/registry.ts`, `lib/auto-mode/engine.ts`, `instrumentation.ts`)
- GlobalThis-backed `autoModeRegistry` tracking enabled state, in-flight build/review sessions, sweep mutex, failure tallies, and recent dispatches.
- Mutual exclusion per project ensuring two sweeps never overlap.
- Reconciles terminal sessions, merges candidates first to drain the `review` column, then dispatches reviews ($< M$) and builds ($< N$) via `createPipelineStageDriver`.
- Timer loop at `AUTO_MODE_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS = 15_000` (`unref()`'d).
- `instrumentation.ts` starts auto mode on server boot and chains the session terminal hook (`kickAutoModeForSession` composed with `maybeAutoDistillAfterSessionTerminal`).

#### 6. Auto Mode API & Board UI (`app/api/projects/[projectId]/auto-mode/route.ts`, `components/auto-mode/`)
- `GET /api/projects/[projectId]/auto-mode`: returns status, in-flight counts, candidate counts, parked tickets, and recent activity.
- `PUT /api/projects/[projectId]/auto-mode`: validates and persists settings, updates registry, and triggers an immediate sweep.
- `AutoModeDialog.tsx`: enable switch, build and review named agent selects, concurrency inputs ($0..10$), candidate indicators, and scheduler budget overload warning.
- `AutoModeToggle.tsx`: board toolbar toggle with active running badge (`N building · M reviewing`).

#### 7. Safety Verification & Documentation
- Verified safety guards: infinite re-review prevention, agent question guard (`isAwaitingReply`), coexistence with manual/night/DAG runs, and story serialization.
- Documented in `README.md` and `docs/architecture/full-auto-mode.md`.

# Epic Implementation: Impossible d'utiliser l'API pour chat

## Root Cause Analysis
1. **Dual Conflicting Dropdowns:** `ChatWorkspaceHeader.tsx` was rendering two distinct dropdowns side-by-side: `ChatProviderSelect` and `NamedAgentSelect`. When a named agent was associated with the active conversation (standard default in Arij), `ChatProviderSelect` was disabled (`disabled={... || Boolean(activeConversation?.namedAgentId)}`).
2. **Missing Direct API in Active Selector:** The active dropdown `NamedAgentSelect` only listed Named Agents from the database (CLI providers) and had no option for the direct API ("OpenAI-compatible").
3. **Artificial Conversation Type Block:** `isOpenAiIneligibleConversationAgentType` blocked `brainstorm` and `epic_creation` conversation types from using OpenAI-compatible mode, making it impossible to use the direct API across the app.

---

## Changes Made

### 1. Unified Single Dropdown Selector
- **`components/chat/ChatProviderSelect.tsx`:** Refactored into a single unified selector component that offers:
  - **Direct API:** `OpenAI-compatible`
  - **Named Agents:** All user-configured Named Agents (e.g. Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, etc.)
- **`components/chat/ChatWorkspaceHeader.tsx`:** Removed the secondary redundant dropdown. The header now renders exactly one interactive selector.
- **`components/chat/UnifiedChatPanel.tsx`:** Added `handleSelectAgentOrProvider` to update both `namedAgentId` and `provider` when switching between Named Agents and Direct API.

### 2. Conversation & Chat Stream Updates
- **`lib/chat/conversation-agent.ts` & `app/api/projects/[projectId]/chat/stream/route.ts`:** Lifted the artificial conversation type restriction so OpenAI-compatible fast mode can be selected and used across chat conversations.
- **`app/api/projects/[projectId]/conversations/[conversationId]/route.ts`:** Updated the conversation update PATCH route to cleanly set `provider = "openai-compatible"` and clear `namedAgentId` when direct API is selected.

### 3. Verification & Testing
- **`__tests__/chat-unified-agent-api-select.test.tsx`:** Added dedicated unit tests verifying:
  - Exactly one dropdown is rendered in the chat header (no secondary disabled dropdown).
  - Direct API ("OpenAI-compatible") and all configured Named Agents are available options.
  - Proper payload dispatching when switching between Direct API and Named Agents.
  - Gating behavior on active vs busy/has-messages conversations.
- **`__tests__/chat-provider-select.test.tsx`**, **`__tests__/chat-provider-toggle.test.tsx`**, and **`__tests__/chat-stream-route-openai.test.ts`:** Updated mocks and assertions to match the unified selector and direct API support.
- **Full Test Suite:** All 267 test files and 2,660 tests pass.

comments.content:
**Code Review**

I can't call `mcp__arij__submit_findings` — the session is in plan mode, which blocks it, and no `ExitPlanMode` tool is available to leave. The full report is below and is also saved at `/home/orosius/.claude/plans/project-arij-federated-fern.md`. Exit plan mode (shift+tab) and say "file the findings" and I'll submit them as anchored review comments.

---

# Code Review — Bug fix: « Impossible d'utiliser l'API pour chat »

**Scope:** commit `307144a` only (10 files). Earlier branch commits that introduced the OpenAI-compatible provider were reviewed in prior passes.

**Verification performed:** read every touched file plus the surrounding call graph (`hooks/useConversations.ts`, `hooks/useEpicCreate.ts`, `lib/db/init.ts`, `lib/agent-config/constants.ts`, `app/api/projects/[projectId]/generate-spec/route.ts`); ran `npx eslint` on the changed files; ran `npx vitest run` on the five touched test files — 42 tests, all green.

The reported bug is genuinely fixed: one selector renders, it is no longer disabled when `namedAgentId` is set, and "OpenAI-compatible" is present. Two blocking problems remain.

---

## 1. Critical — one selection fires three concurrent PATCHes, and the last one unlinks the named agent

**`components/chat/ChatProviderSelect.tsx:109`** (wired at `ChatWorkspaceHeader.tsx:66-68`, `UnifiedChatPanel.tsx:363-365`)

`handleValueChange` invokes **all three** callbacks for a single choice:

```ts
onSelect?.({ namedAgentId: nextValue, provider }); // -> handleSelectAgentOrProvider
onAgentChange?.(nextValue);                        // -> handleAgentChange
onProviderChange?.(provider);                      // -> handleProviderChange
```

The header passes all three, and `UnifiedChatPanel` maps each to its own `updateConversation()` — three independent `PATCH /conversations/:id` requests in the same tick, no ordering guarantee.

The third is the damaging one. Its body is `{ provider: "codex" }` with **no** `namedAgentId` key; `updateConversationSchema` uses zod `.nullish()`, which drops absent keys, so `hasOwnProperty(body, "namedAgentId")` is false and it lands in the legacy branch at `conversations/[conversationId]/route.ts:152-161`, which does `updates.namedAgentId = null`.

**Failure scenario:** user picks "Codex (GPT-5)". PATCH#1 sets `namedAgentId = agent-2`; PATCH#3 clears it. Last write wins. When #3 wins, the conversation runs on the *default* chat agent with only the provider overridden (`chat/stream/route.ts:124-127`), silently losing the selected agent's model — and local state is overwritten by whichever response resolves last, so the dropdown can snap back to a different agent. The direct-API path duplicates too (2 PATCHes), idempotent but wasteful.

**Recommendation:** emit exactly one event. Keep `onSelect` as the sole callback and drop `onAgentChange`/`onProviderChange` from this component and the header's wiring — `ChatWorkspaceHeader.handleSelect` already implements the correct mutually-exclusive fallback one level up.

## 2. Major — Direct API on an epic-creation conversation silently degrades to plain chat

**`app/api/projects/[projectId]/chat/stream/route.ts:274`**

Removing the gate (lines 130-149) makes fast mode *selectable* for `epic_creation`, but the fast-mode branch returns at line 274 — before the block at 410-441 that builds `buildEpicRefinementPrompt` / `buildEpicFinalizationPrompt`. In fast mode the `finalize` flag parsed at line 102 is never read, and the model gets the generic chat system prompt.

**Failure scenario:** epic-creation conversation → switch to OpenAI-compatible → discuss → "Create Epic & Generate Stories". `useEpicCreate` (`hooks/useEpicCreate.ts:58-82`) sends two finalization prompts, gets prose back (nothing instructs a fenced JSON block), `parseEpicFromConversation` finds nothing, user sees *"I couldn't extract a full epic yet."* with no hint the provider is the cause.

`brainstorm` is genuinely fine — the CLI path also uses `buildChatPrompt` for it, and "Generate Spec & Plan" posts to `/generate-spec`, which ignores the body's `provider` and resolves the `spec_generation` agent independently. Only `epic_creation` regresses.

**Recommendation:** move the `isEpicCreationConversationAgentType` prompt block above line 274 and feed it in as the fast-mode system message, or keep `epic_creation` ineligible and lift the gate only for `brainstorm`/`chat`.

**Test gap:** `__tests__/chat-stream-route-openai.test.ts:282` asserts only `status === 200` + "fetch was called" — it passes identically whether the epic prompt is wired or not.

## 3. Major — CLI providers without a named agent are no longer selectable

**`components/chat/ChatProviderSelect.tsx:142`**

The old select rendered `PROVIDER_OPTIONS` (11 CLI providers). The unified one lists only Direct API + `named_agents` rows. A fresh DB seeds exactly one named agent — "Claude Code" (`lib/db/init.ts:15-17`) — so out of the box a conversation can run on Claude Code or the direct API and nothing else. Codex, Gemini CLI, Pi… become unreachable from chat until the user creates a named agent for each, while the API layer still accepts them. `normalizeProvider()` at `chat/stream/route.ts:39-50` carries a doc comment explicitly warning against exactly this narrowing.

**Recommendation:** add a third `SelectGroup` ("Providers") listing `PROVIDER_OPTIONS`. If the narrowing is intentional, say so and remove the now-unreachable provider-only PATCH branches.

## 4. Minor — dead function

**`lib/chat/conversation-agent.ts:45`** — `isOpenAiIneligibleConversationAgentType` unconditionally returns `false`, ignores `_type`, and has zero callers (grepped across `app/`, `components/`, `lib/`, `hooks/`, `__tests__/`). Delete it.

## 5. Minor — unused import flagged by lint

**`components/chat/ChatProviderSelect.tsx:16`** — `PROVIDER_OPTIONS` was dropped but `type ChatModeProvider` was left unused:

```
16:8  warning  'ChatModeProvider' is defined but never used  @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars
```

(The one eslint *error*, `UnifiedChatPanel.tsx:252`, is pre-existing from `4bfd1e6` — unrelated.)

## 6. Minor — over-broad, partly dead props contract

**`components/chat/ChatProviderSelect.tsx:25-37`** — eight optional props with overlapping meaning. `value`/`onChange` are legacy shims no caller passes; `conversationType` is declared but not destructured, so it's silently ignored; `ChatAgentSelection.provider` is `string` where `ChatModeProvider` (`constants.ts:103`) is precise. Narrowing to `{ activeConversation, activeProvider, onSelect, disabled, className }` also fixes #1 structurally rather than by convention.

## 7. Minor — hardcoded provider fallback

**`components/chat/ChatProviderSelect.tsx:104`** — `?? "claude-code"` where `FALLBACK_PROVIDER` exists (`lib/agent-config/agent-resolution.ts:38`). Also unreachable by construction, so it hides the impossible case rather than handling it.

## 8. Minor — the select can display an agent the conversation isn't using

**`components/chat/ChatProviderSelect.tsx:85-89`** — with no `namedAgentId` and no provider match, the fallback is `agents[0]?.id`. A conversation on `provider: "pi"` with no Pi agent renders "Claude Code" as selected; with several agents sharing a provider, `find()` picks an arbitrary one. Since the select disables once messages exist, the user can't correct it. Prefer an empty value (placeholder shows) or a synthetic "Default (<label>)" entry.

## 9. Minor (DRY) — redundant PATCH branch

**`app/api/projects/[projectId]/conversations/[conversationId]/route.ts:104`** — this leading branch and the nested one at 136-143, both added in this commit, produce identical `updates` for the payload the UI actually sends (`{ provider: "openai-compatible", namedAgentId: null }`): `namedAgentIdInput` is `""`, so the nested `else if` runs, and `isChatProvider("openai-compatible")` is `true`. The only input it changes behaviour for is `{ namedAgentId: "<id>", provider: "openai-compatible" }`, which no caller sends.

## 10. Suggestion — the regression test cannot catch #1

**`__tests__/chat-provider-toggle.test.tsx:257`** — `toHaveBeenCalledWith` passes when *any* call matches, so the three-PATCH storm is invisible; the test is green today despite the bug. `expect(mockFetch).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` turns it into a real guard. Related: `chat-unified-agent-api-select.test.tsx` exercises the component in isolation with one `onSelect` spy — the failing paths only appear once header, panel and route are wired together, which no test covers.

---

## Checklist verdicts

| Criterion | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Readability | Issues — #4, #5, #6, #7 |
| DRY | Issues — #1 (three code paths for one action), #9 |
| Error handling | No issues found |
| Performance | Issue — #1 (3× write amplification per selection) |
| Naming conventions | No issues found |
| Type safety | Issues — #6; no `any` introduced |
| Testing | Issues — #2 (test asserts nothing meaningful), #10 |
| API design | Issue — #9; status codes and `{data}`/`{error}` shape consistent |

## Summary

**Critical:** 1 · **Major:** 2 · **Minor:** 6 · **Suggestion:** 1

The two-dropdown and disabled-selector problems are genuinely fixed and the direct API is now reachable. But the unified component fans a single selection out to three conflicting write paths that can undo the user's choice, and lifting the epic-creation gate exposes a mode that silently cannot finalize an epic.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

**Code Review**

# Code Review — Bug fix: « Impossible d'utiliser l'API pour chat »

**Scope:** commits `307144a` + `a681bae` (12 files). Report also saved at `/home/orosius/.claude/plans/project-arij-greedy-crystal.md`.

**Verification performed:** `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npx eslint` on all 8 changed source files; full `npx vitest run` — **267 files / 2662 tests, all passing**. Read every touched file plus the call graph (`useConversations.ts`, `useEpicCreate.ts`, `prompt-builder.ts`, `prompt-sections.ts`, `constants.ts`, `chat-schemas.ts`).

## The reported bug is fixed

`ChatWorkspaceHeader.tsx:60-65` renders exactly one selector, no longer disabled when `namedAgentId` is set, and "OpenAI-compatible" is a first-class option. The end-to-end path holds: select → single PATCH `{provider:"openai-compatible", namedAgentId:null}` → new branch at `conversations/[conversationId]/route.ts:128` → `chat/stream/route.ts:123-127` → fast-mode branch. All four previously-blocking findings are genuinely resolved: one PATCH per selection (asserted by `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)`), epic prompts wired into fast mode with real assertions replacing the old `status === 200` check, CLI providers restored, dead helper deleted.

---

## 1. Major — epic-creation fast mode sends the entire conversation twice
**`app/api/projects/[projectId]/chat/stream/route.ts:340`**

Line 319 sets `fastModeSystemPrompt = isEpicCreation ? prompt : chatSystemPrompt`. `buildEpicRefinementPrompt`/`buildEpicFinalizationPrompt` both call `chatHistorySection(messages)` with `fullHistory` (`prompt-builder.ts:499`, `:538`) — the system message already contains every turn. Lines 340-349 then push all of `messageHistory` (up to 20 rows) plus `userContent` again as chat messages.

**Failure scenario:** epic conversation with ~15 exchanges, fast mode against a local endpoint (the primary use case — small context windows). "Create Epic & Generate Stories" fires two finalization requests (`useEpicCreate.ts:58-82`), each carrying spec + existing epics + the conversation *twice*. Upstream rejects on context length; the catch at line 400 saves the error as the assistant message, `parseEpicFromConversation` finds no JSON, user sees *"I couldn't extract a full epic yet."* When it does fit, every epic turn costs ~2× the tokens.

**Recommendation:** for `isEpicCreation`, the prompt is self-contained — send it as the single message and skip the history append.

## 2. Minor — `buildChatPrompt` computed and discarded in fast mode
**`route.ts:310`** — hoisting the block above the branch means 309-310 always run, but fast mode reads only `chatSystemPrompt` and returns at 446. `buildChatPrompt` calls `withProjectMemory()` → `getProjectMemoryContent()`, then serialises spec + docs + history into a discarded string.

## 3. Minor — unused import (only new lint diagnostic)
**`conversations/[conversationId]/route.ts:6`** — `OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_PROVIDER` added in `307144a`, superseded by the generic `isChatProvider()` test. The `UnifiedChatPanel.tsx:252` error and `agent-resolution.ts:79` warning both predate `307144a`.

## 4. Minor — dead legacy props keeping a divergent dispatch path alive
**`ChatWorkspaceHeader.tsx:19`** — `onAgentChange`/`onProviderChange` survive only in two test files. The fallback at 40-44 is lossy where the primary path is not: a named agent discards `selection.provider`; a CLI provider discards the `namedAgentId: null` needed to reach route.ts:128. Any future caller wiring them reintroduces the split write path.

## 5. Minor — "Claude Code" appears twice in one dropdown
**`ChatProviderSelect.tsx:159`** — a fresh DB seeds one named agent "Claude Code" and `PROVIDER_OPTIONS[0]` is `"claude-code"` labelled "Claude Code". Identical text, different behaviour (agent model/prompt vs. cleared `namedAgentId` + default agent's model). The select disables once messages exist, so a wrong pick can't be corrected. Invisible before — the old header used two separate dropdowns.

## 6. Minor — redundant disjunct that contradicts the server
**`ChatProviderSelect.tsx:74`** — `activeProvider` *is* `activeConversation?.provider || "claude-code"` (`UnifiedChatPanel.tsx:145`). Where the two could differ, this ranks openai-compatible above `namedAgentId` while `route.ts:124-127` ranks `namedAgentId` first.

## 7. Minor — handler re-widens `provider` to `string`
**`UnifiedChatPanel.tsx:303`** — `ChatAgentSelection` now types `provider: ChatModeProvider`; the inline re-declaration loses the exhaustive discriminator at line 308.

## 8. Info — the two provider PATCH branches are still byte-identical
**`conversations/[conversationId]/route.ts:144`** — all three production callers always send the `namedAgentId` key, so the outer branch serves only legacy clients. Legitimate but duplicated.

## 9. Info — test gap for finding #1
**`chat-stream-route-openai.test.ts:298`** — both assertions check `messages[0]` only, and the builder is mocked to a constant, so the duplication is invisible by construction.

---

| Criterion | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Readability | Issues — #3, #4, #5, #6 |
| DRY | Issues — #2, #8 |
| Error handling | No issues found |
| Performance | Issues — #1, #2 |

## The reported bug is fixed

`ChatWorkspaceHeader.tsx:45-50` renders exactly one selector, no longer disabled when `namedAgentId` is set, with "OpenAI-compatible" as a first-class option. End-to-end verified: select → **one** PATCH → `conversations/[conversationId]/route.ts:128-135` → `chat/stream/route.ts:123-130` → fast-mode branch. All prior findings (triple PATCH, epic prompts, dead helper, duplicate history) are genuinely closed.

## 1. Major — `npx tsc --noEmit` fails; the project no longer type-checks

`__tests__/chat-unified-agent-api-select.test.tsx:127, 142, 217, 228`

`38131f4` made `onSelectAgentOrProvider` required on `ChatWorkspaceHeaderProps` and updated only **one** of the five `<ChatWorkspaceHeader>` renders in this file (line 86).

```
error TS2741: Property 'onSelectAgentOrProvider' is missing in type
'{ activeConversation: Conversation; activeProvider: string; hasMessages: false; isBusy: false; }'
but required in type 'ChatWorkspaceHeaderProps'.
```

Vitest strips types, so the suite stays green and hides it. `tsconfig.json` includes `**/*.tsx` with no `__tests__` exclusion and `next.config.ts` does not set `typescript.ignoreBuildErrors`, so the same diagnostics gate `next build`. **Fix:** add `onSelectAgentOrProvider={noop}` to the four remaining renders.

## 2. Major — Direct API chat runs with no project context (fresh install: no system prompt at all)

`chat/stream/route.ts:308-310`, `:344-358`, `:457-459`

For non-epic conversations the fast-mode system prompt is `resolveAgentPrompt("chat", projectId)` — a raw configured string. `BUILTIN_AGENT_PROMPTS.chat` is `""` and nothing is seeded, so by default `fastModeSystemPrompt.trim()` is falsy and **no system message is sent**: the request is the last 20 raw turns and nothing else. The CLI branch one `if` below calls `buildChatPrompt()`, which adds `projectContextSections()` (spec, memory, documents) plus the "answer considering the full project context above" instructions. `38131f4` moved that call *below* the fast-mode return, making the asymmetry structural.

**Failure scenario:** user switches a chat to "OpenAI-compatible" and asks "what's left on the auth epic?". Claude Code / Codex in the same dropdown answer from the project spec; the direct API answers as a generic assistant with no idea what the project is. `307144a` widens this: lifting the gate routes `brainstorm` — the type whose whole purpose is discussing *this* project — down the same context-free path. Epic creation is unaffected (its builder embeds everything).

**Recommendation:** `buildChatPrompt(project, [], [], chatSystemPrompt)` with empty history (history already travels in `openAiMessages`), or export `projectContextSections()` and prepend it.

## 3. Major — picking a CLI provider spawns that CLI with another provider's model

`chat/stream/route.ts:123-127` + `ChatProviderSelect.tsx:150-163`

The "CLI Providers" group (added in `a681bae`) PATCHes `{provider, namedAgentId: null}`. The route then keeps the *default chat agent's* model and overrides only the provider:

```ts
resolvedAgent = conversationProvider && !conversation?.namedAgentId
  ? { ...resolvedByNamedAgent, provider: conversationProvider }   // model untouched
  : resolvedByNamedAgent;
```

`resolveAgentByNamedId("chat", projectId, null)` → the seeded default agent, `claude-code` / `claude-opus-4-6` (`lib/db/init.ts:16-17`). The model passes through unnormalized (`lib/providers/types.ts:69`) and codex renders it verbatim: `args.push("-m", model)` (`lib/providers/codex.ts:133`, `:168`).

**Failure scenario:** fresh install → pick "Codex (CLI)" → send → `codex exec … -m claude-opus-4-6` → CLI rejects the model, user sees `Error: <codex stderr>`. Newly reachable: `main` exposed only `NamedAgentSelect`, and the branch's earlier select was disabled whenever a `namedAgentId` existed — i.e. the bug being fixed. **Recommendation:** drop the model when the provider differs from the resolved agent's, or resolve a per-provider default.

## 4. Minor — epic fast mode still sends the latest user message twice
`chat/stream/route.ts:336-343` — `fullHistory` includes the just-saved message and the epic builders embed it via `chatHistorySection()`; it is pushed again as the `user` turn. Much smaller than before (one message), and a user turn is needed by most endpoints — but the system prompt could carry history minus the current message.

## 5. Minor (DRY) — the two branches differ by one loop
`chat/stream/route.ts:335-358` — the system push and trailing user push are written twice; only the `messageHistory` loop is conditional.

## 6. Minor — dead fallback branch and a now-redundant prop
`ChatProviderSelect.tsx:79-83` — that arm only runs when `activeConversation` is null, and the sole caller disables the select in exactly that case (`ChatWorkspaceHeader.tsx:49`). `activeProvider` is derived from `activeConversation?.provider` (`UnifiedChatPanel.tsx:146`), so it carries no new information.

## 7. Minor — a deleted named agent renders an empty selector
`ChatProviderSelect.tsx:72-73` — `selectedValue` takes `namedAgentId` without checking it exists in `safeAgents`; if deleted, Radix shows the placeholder while the conversation runs on the resolved default.

## 8. Minor (API design) — named-agent PATCH carries a `provider` the server ignores
`UnifiedChatPanel.tsx:312` sends `{namedAgentId, provider}`; `conversations/[conversationId]/route.ts:122-123` re-derives it from the agent row. `chat-provider-toggle.test.tsx:264` asserts the exact body, locking the redundant field into the contract.

- No test drives header → panel → PATCH for **Direct API** or a **CLI provider**; only the named-agent case is covered end-to-end. Findings #3 and #8 live in that gap.
- `chat-stream-route-openai.test.ts` mocks the prompt builders to constants, so #2 is invisible by construction — the non-epic assertions never inspect the system message.
- `lib/agent-config/agent-resolution.ts:39-40` — double blank line left where `FALLBACK_PROVIDER` moved out; the constant now has a single consumer, back in the file it came from.

|---|---|

| DRY | Issues — #5, #8 |
| Error handling | No issues found — fast-mode abort/mid-stream/cancel paths complete; `useChat` surfaces `payload.error` for the 400s |

**Summary:** Major 3 · Minor 5 · Suggestion 1

The dual-dropdown and disabled-selector defects are properly fixed and the direct API is reachable from every conversation type — the ticket's actual complaint is resolved. epics.title: Échec de build silencieux : « Agent error » sans message d'erreur ni notification
epics.description:
## Problème

Sur un deuxième projet, la tentative de build d'un ticket échoue avec uniquement un message **« Agent error »** en tout petit en bas de l'interface. Aucune indication sur la nature de l'erreur n'est affichée, ni dans l'UI ni via une notification.

## Comportement attendu

Quand un build (ou toute session d'agent) échoue :

1. **Notification** : une notification du système de notifications global doit être émise, avec le **message d'erreur complet** (stderr / sortie de l'agent / raison de l'échec), pas seulement un libellé générique.
2. **Visibilité dans l'UI** : l'erreur doit être visible et lisible sur la carte / le ticket — pas un texte minuscule tronqué. Un clic doit permettre de voir le détail complet (par exemple via la modale de notifications ou la vue session).
3. **Traçabilité** : l'erreur complète doit rester consultable après coup (log de session), pas seulement au moment de l'échec.

## Contexte

- Le système de notifications global existe déjà (E-arij-009, done) — il faut le brancher sur les échecs de session/build.
- Un bug proche a déjà été traité : B-arij-108 (« Le badge "Session failed" réapparaît après un retry réussi ») et E-arij-010 (« trop de cas de "(no textual output)" ») — vérifier que la cause n'est pas liée (sortie vide de l'agent → message générique au lieu de l'erreur réelle).
- Piste probable : quand la sortie de l'agent est vide ou que le process meurt sans stderr, l'UI retombe sur le libellé « Agent error » sans surface pour afficher la raison.

## Critères d'acceptation

- Un build qui échoue déclenche une notification contenant le message d'erreur complet (ou, si l'agent n'a produit aucune sortie, un message explicite le disant + où trouver les logs).
- Le message « Agent error » seul, en tout petit, n'est plus le seul signal : le détail est accessible en un clic.
- L'erreur reste consultable après coup dans l'historique de la session.
- Cas vide/no-output couvert explicitement (cf. leçon E-arij-010).

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
**Forensic diagnostic**

**Probable root cause** — The run never started. Arij's pi adapter passes the configured model verbatim as `--model qwen3.8-27b` and never emits a `--provider` flag (`lib/providers/pi.ts:203-207`, `buildArgs`). Two authenticated pi providers (`ninfer` and `vllm`) both serve that model name, so the pi CLI refused to disambiguate and exited during argument/model resolution — before emitting its `session` header or any `message_end` event. Because the failure is a startup error on stderr rather than a stream event, nothing reached the output stream and no assistant text was produced, so the pipeline surfaced only the generic "Agent error" with no message. This is a configuration defect (an under-qualified model identifier), not a defect in the ticket's code or prompt; retrying was futile, which is why both `build` attempts failed identically.

**Evidence**

- The recorded error is a pi CLI resolution failure, not a task failure: `Error: Model "qwen3.8-27b" is ambiguous across providers: ninfer/qwen3.8-27b, vllm/qwen3.8-27b. More than one matching provider is authenticated. Use --provider or provider/model.`
- The run produced nothing: *Output stream (tail): (none)* and *Last text produced: (none)* — consistent with an exit before pi's `--mode json` stream opened, which is what leaves the UI with an empty "Agent error".
- The raw stream tail contains that single error line and nothing else — no `{"type":"session"…}` header, no tool calls — confirming the process died at startup rather than mid-task.

**Recommended next action**

- Requalify the model in the agent/pipeline config for this ticket from the bare `qwen3.8-27b` to a provider-qualified `vllm/qwen3.8-27b` (or `ninfer/qwen3.8-27b`, whichever endpoint is intended) — pi's own message accepts the `provider/model` form, and Arij forwards the string unchanged to `--model`, so this needs no code change — then re-run the `build` stage. If both providers should stay authenticated long-term, follow up separately by teaching `PiProvider.buildArgs` to emit `--provider`, since bare model names will keep colliding.

Fittingly, that's the exact failure class this epic fixes — pi *did* write a real stderr line, so with this branch merged that message now reaches the notification and the card instead of a bare label.

**The branch was 50 commits behind `main`**, which had landed overlapping work: B-arij-108's badge rework (`latest-failure.ts`, with its own Retry / "View log" buttons) and `recordSessionTransitionRefusal()` in the very same `lifecycle.ts`. Left unmerged, this epic wasn't mergeable.

## What I did

Merged `main` in (`d6c6646`). One conflict, in `lib/agent-sessions/lifecycle.ts`, and only on the import line — `main` widened the drizzle import to `{ and, eq }` while this branch added `fs`/`path`. Both needed; kept both. The feature regions are disjoint. `EpicCard.tsx` auto-merged coherently: this epic's clickable clamped error line now sits above main's Retry / View log row. Migrations append cleanly (main stops at `0030`/idx 29, this branch adds `0031` at idx 30) — no `drizzle-kit generate` run.

**Verified on the merged tree:** `tsc --noEmit` clean, and `npm test` — exactly what CI runs — **356 test files / 4088 tests passed**, including main's `latest-failure` suite alongside this epic's suites.

One detail worth recording: the literal string `"Agent error"` never existed in the UI. The reported tiny red text was the card's `Session failed · <error>` line rendering an **empty** error. Guaranteeing a non-empty error at the lifecycle choke point is what actually removes the symptom — which is what `failure-message.ts` does.

## Not done

`update_ticket_status → review` was **rejected**: `Cannot move an in-progress ticket while an agent session is queued or running` — my own session blocks it. The ticket is still **`in_progress`** and needs moving to `review` once this session ends. My full report is posted as a comment (`zf8EVsp-UbqV`), so the conclusion survives regardless.

I did not touch `PiProvider.buildArgs` to emit `--provider`. It's a real latent issue — bare model names will keep colliding while both providers are authenticated — but it's a separate config-layer fix, outside this epic's acceptance criteria.

epics.title: Pipeline : étage `verify` déterministe (tests/lint/build exécutés par Arij)
epics.description:
## Contexte
Arij ne vérifie jamais programmatiquement le travail des agents : « run the tests and commit » n'existe que comme consigne de prose dans les prompts (`lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts`). Le pipeline autonome (`lib/pipeline/runner.ts` + `lib/pipeline/stages.ts`) enchaîne build → review → fix sans aucune étape déterministe : un ticket passe en `review` sur la seule foi de l'agent. Enseignement central de Code with Claude 2026 : la vérification est le goulot, pas l'écriture du code.

## À construire
1. **Settings** : `verify_commands` (JSON, tableau de `{ name, command }`, ex. `[{"name":"test","command":"npm test"},{"name":"lint","command":"npm run lint"}]`) et `verify_timeout_ms` (défaut 600000), résolus en tri-state projet → global → défaut comme les autres clés (voir `lib/settings/`). Constantes dans un fichier `verify-constants.ts` client-safe (convention du repo). Clé absente = verify désactivé, aucun changement de comportement.
2. **Runner** `lib/verify/runner.ts` : exécute chaque commande séquentiellement dans le worktree de l'epic (`cwd = worktreePath`), capture stdout/stderr borné (~64 Ko par commande, garder la FIN de la sortie), exit code, durée. Timeout dur par commande avec kill du process group (SIGTERM puis SIGKILL, même échelle que `lib/providers/base-provider.ts`). Zéro LLM dans ce module. Arrêt à la première commande en échec.
3. **Persistance** : nouvelle table `verify_reports` (id, projectId, epicId, agentSessionId nullable, status pass|fail, startedAt, finishedAt, `commands` JSON `[{name, command, exitCode, durationMs, tail}]`). Migration SQL écrite à la main : fichier numéroté dans `lib/db/migrations/` + entrée ajoutée dans `meta/_journal.json` (ne JAMAIS lancer `drizzle-kit generate`, cf. CLAUDE.md — les snapshots sont figés à 0013).
4. **Câblage pipeline** (`lib/pipeline/stages.ts`) : après un stage build réussi (outcome `answered`) et avant le stage review, exécuter verify si configuré. Échec → consommer un fix cycle existant (`pipeline_max_fix_cycles`) avec un prompt de fix enrichi du tail de la sortie d'erreur (nouvelle section dans `prompt-builder.ts`) ; succès → injecter un résumé une-ligne-par-commande dans le prompt du reviewer. Le run verify n'est PAS une session agent : il ne compte ni dans le plafond de 12 sessions/run ni dans les budgets ; il est journalisé dans `ticket_activity_log` (actor `system`).
5. **Déclenchement manuel** : `POST /api/projects/:projectId/epics/:epicId/verify` (réponse d'erreur lisible si aucun worktree), et affichage du dernier rapport dans le détail du ticket (statut par commande + tail dépliable).

## Contraintes
- N'exécuter que dans le worktree de l'epic, jamais dans le repo principal ni sur main.
- Les commandes viennent exclusivement des settings (saisies par l'humain) — un agent ne doit jamais pouvoir écrire `verify_commands`.
- Full Auto et night run héritent du comportement via le pipeline : aucune logique spécifique chez eux.
- Tests vitest : runner (child_process mocké : succès, échec, timeout, troncature) et câblage stages (échec → fix cycle, succès → review, non configuré → passthrough bit-à-bit identique).

## Hors scope
La règle « test de régression obligatoire pour les bugs » — ticket séparé qui dépend de celui-ci.
