I've completed the review. Verification I ran myself in the worktree: all 9 touched test files pass (310 tests), `npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false` is clean, and ESLint on every changed file is clean — the claims in the comment history hold.

---

# Code Review — Pipeline: étage `verify` déterministe

**Scope:** `269e399..96acc8c` (4 commits, 24 files, +2674/−8), covering all four user stories.

## Summary of what was built

The epic is implemented end to end and the architecture is sound: a client-safe constants module, a tri-state resolver over SQLite, an LLM-free sequential runner with byte-bounded output capture and process-group kill escalation, a hand-written migration (`0033`, journal `idx: 32`, `when` strictly increasing — no `drizzle-kit generate`), pipeline wiring that consumes the *existing* fix-cycle budget without touching the 12-session ceiling, `actor: "system"` activity traces, a manual `GET`/`POST` route with worktree containment, and an `EpicDetail` panel. The passthrough path is proven bit-identical by comparing two harness runs' `requests`/`traces`/`summary` — a genuinely strong test.

---

## 1. Readability

No issues found. Comments explain *why* (the `detached`/negative-pid rationale at `lib/verify/runner.ts:66-71`, the "empty array is deliberately valid" note at `verify-constants.ts:112-118`, the "there is deliberately no repository-path fallback" contract at `runner.ts:27`) rather than restating the code. Naming is precise and consistent with the surrounding pipeline vocabulary.

## 2. DRY Principle

**Minor — `lib/verify/verify-constants.ts:177`** — `resolveVerifyConfig` is a complete second implementation of the precedence logic in `resolveVerifyConfigForProject` (`lib/verify/config.ts:24`), and it has **no production caller** — `grep` finds it only in `__tests__/verify-settings.test.ts`. The "client-safe resolver" rationale in its doc comment never pays off because no client consumes it (see finding 8.1).
*Recommendation:* either wire it into the settings UI or delete it and keep one resolver.

**Minor — `app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/[epicId]/verify/route.ts:35`** — `parseCommandResults` re-implements, field for field, the per-command validation already in `isVerificationReport` (`verify-constants.ts:63-73`).
*Recommendation:* export an `isVerifyCommandResult` predicate from `verify-constants.ts` and call it from both.

## 3. Error Handling

**Major — `app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/[epicId]/verify/route.ts:161` and `lib/pipeline/stages.ts:266`** — nothing serialises verification against concurrent work in the same worktree. The POST route runs regardless of whether a build, fix, review or Full Auto merge-fix session is live on that epic, and neither call site takes a per-worktree lock.
*Failure scenario:* a night run's pipeline is executing `npm run build` in epic E's worktree when the user opens the ticket and clicks **Run verification**. Two `next build` processes write `.next/` in the same directory; both reports are garbage, and the pipeline consumes a fix cycle — dispatching a real agent — against a phantom failure. Same class of corruption when the manual run races an agent that is mid-edit.
*Recommendation:* the ingredients already exist — `getRunningSessionForTarget` is imported at `lib/pipeline/stages.ts:15`; use it to refuse the POST with a 409 while a session owns the epic, and add an in-process per-worktree mutex around `runVerification` so pipeline and manual runs cannot interleave.

**Minor — `lib/verify/runner.ts:148`** — `runCommand` resolves only on `close`, which requires both process exit *and* every inherited stdio pipe closing. A descendant that escapes the group kill (`setsid`) while holding stdout leaves the promise pending forever: after SIGKILL there is no absolute deadline. `lib/pipeline/runner.ts:556` awaits this inline, and the stalled-session watchdog cannot help because a verify run is deliberately not an agent session — so the pipeline run stalls with no terminal state and no notification.
*Recommendation:* after the SIGKILL escalation, arm one final timer that calls `finish(null)` unconditionally (or settle on `exit` with a bounded grace for `close`).

**Suggestion — `lib/verify/runner.ts:196`** — with an empty `commands` array, `commandResults.length === input.commands.length` holds and `[].every(...)` is `true`, so the function persists a `status: "pass"` report having executed nothing. Both current callers pre-check `config.enabled`, so it is unreachable today, but `runVerification` is exported and the whole point of the table is that a `pass` row means something was mechanically proven.

## 4. Performance

**Minor — `hooks/useEpicDetail.ts:52`** — the verify `GET` was added to `fetchData`, which is also the 5-second poll callback (`hooks/useEpicDetail.ts:98`). Each tick re-downloads the full report, whose `commands` blob carries up to 64 KiB of `tail` **per command** (`VERIFY_OUTPUT_LIMIT_BYTES`). A two-command config means ~128 KiB every 5 s for a payload that changes only when a run finishes.
*Recommendation:* serve tails lazily (`?tails=1`, or a per-command endpoint), or refetch the report on the `ticket:updated` event and after a manual run instead of on every tick.

Otherwise fine: the `verify_reports_epic_finished_idx` index matches the GET's `WHERE epic_id … ORDER BY finished_at DESC`, and `OutputTail` is correctly O(limit) rather than accumulating unbounded output.

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found. `verify_reports` / `verifyReports`, `verify-constants.ts` (mirrors the existing `regression-constants.ts` / `workspace-constants.ts` client-safe convention), `VerificationReportSection.tsx` under `components/kanban/epic-detail/` — all consistent.

## 6. Type Safety

No issues found. No `any`; `unknown` is narrowed through real predicates; `VerifyCommandResult`/`VerificationReport` are shared across server, route and client from one client-safe module; the `PromptVerificationCommand` structural projection in `prompt-builder.ts` correctly avoids dragging a server type into the prompt layer.

## 7. Testing

**Minor — `__tests__/pipeline-deterministic-verification.test.ts:132`** — the two highest-consequence new branches have no coverage:
- exhaustion (`lib/pipeline/runner.ts:589-611`) — emits `failedDeterministicVerification`, calls `parkRejectedTicket` to pull the ticket back out of Review, and terminates the run;
- crash (`lib/pipeline/runner.ts:627-648`) — same park + terminate on any throw from the driver, including the two `throw`s in `runPipelineVerification` (`stages.ts:246`, `stages.ts:261`).

`grep` confirms no test references `failedDeterministicVerification` or either park reason. The suite covers pass / fail→fix→pass / disabled, which is the happy topology; the paths that move a ticket backwards are the ones a regression would hurt most. Also untested: the "not configured" 409 in `POST` (`route.ts:150-159`) and the runner's spawn-error branch (`runner.ts:140-143`).

Positives worth noting: the `maxSessions: 2` test is exactly the right way to prove the session-ceiling criterion, and the disabled-path equality assertion is stronger than the acceptance criterion asked for.

## 8. API Design

**Major — `lib/verify/verify-constants.ts:177` / `app/settings/page.tsx`** — there is no way for a user to configure `verify_commands` or `verify_timeout_ms` anywhere in the product. `app/settings/page.tsx` imports `@/lib/verify/regression-constants` (the sibling epic wired `BUG_REGRESSION_COMMAND_SETTING_KEY` and `TEST_FILE_PATTERNS_SETTING_KEY` into it at lines 28-30/329-366), but nothing from `verify-constants.ts`; `grep` for the verify keys across `app/` and `components/` returns only `lib/` and tests.
*Failure scenario:* a user opens a ticket, sees the new **Verification** panel, clicks **Run verification**, and gets `409 "Verification is not configured for this project. Add at least one verify command in Settings."` — pointing at a Settings page with no such field. The only way to enable the epic's entire feature is to hand-craft a `PATCH /api/settings` call or edit SQLite. Meanwhile the pipeline stage sits permanently on the disabled passthrough path, and `resolveVerifyConfig` — the client resolver written for precisely this UI — stays dead.
I acknowledge story 1's literal acceptance criteria are all about resolution semantics and say nothing about a control, so this may have been consciously deferred. But the epic states the commands are "saisies par l'humain", and as shipped no human can enter them, which makes stories 2–4 unreachable in the product.
*Recommendation:* add the two controls to `app/settings/page.tsx` mirroring the regression-command/test-patterns block, reusing `parseVerifyCommands`, `parseVerifyTimeoutMs` and `resolveVerifyConfig`. If the UI is genuinely a follow-up ticket, then hide `VerificationReportSection` when no commands resolve, so the product does not advertise a button that cannot work.

**Minor — `lib/pipeline/stages.ts:260`** — the pipeline path trusts `agentSessions.worktreePath` verbatim, while the manual route validates the same value with `containsPathOnDisk(candidate, worktreesRootFor(repoPath))` (`route.ts:90-102`). The epic's hard constraint — never execute in the main checkout or on `main` — is therefore enforced at one of the two call sites. Sessions carrying `worktreePath = project.gitRepoPath` do exist (`app/api/projects/[projectId]/git/pull/route.ts:170`, `app/api/projects/[projectId]/releases/route.ts:228`); they happen to have no `epicId`, so the `projectId + epicId + sessionId` lookup cannot reach them today — but the invariant rests on that accident rather than on a check.

# Code Review — Pipeline: étage `verify` déterministe (re-review)

## Summary of what changed since the last review

`920602e` added the **Deterministic verification** card to global Settings (JSON command list + per-command timeout), wired through the same client-safe parsers, and made `resolveVerifyConfig` a shared resolver instead of dead code — closing prior Major #1. `f81a7e9` added `lib/verify/worktree.ts` (containment enforced at *both* call sites now, not just the route), `lib/verify/execution-lock.ts` (per-worktree serialisation), and an agent-active 409 in the POST route — closing prior Major #2. Prior Minors #2 (duplicate command validation), #3 (`close`-only settle), #4 (poll payload) and the empty-commands suggestion were not addressed.

---

## 1. Readability

No issues found. The comments carry the *why*: the negative-pid rationale (`lib/verify/runner.ts:70-71`), "empty array is deliberately valid" (`lib/verify/verify-constants.ts:112-118`), "there is deliberately no repository-path fallback" (`lib/verify/runner.ts:27`), and the lock's fail-fast-vs-queue split (`lib/verify/execution-lock.ts:3-10`). `verificationOutputFence` (`lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts:113`) and the "untrusted command output" framing in the fix section are a thoughtful touch — agent-visible output is fenced so a failing test's stdout can't impersonate instructions.

## 2. DRY Principle

**Minor — `app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/[epicId]/verify/route.ts:35`** — `parseCommandResults` still re-implements, field for field, the per-command validation in `isVerificationReport` (`lib/verify/verify-constants.ts:63-73`). Unchanged since the last review. The two copies also disagree semantically: the route silently drops malformed entries and returns a partial report, while the client predicate rejects the whole report — so a half-corrupt row renders as a *shorter* passing report instead of an error.
*Recommendation:* export an `isVerifyCommandResult` predicate from `verify-constants.ts` and call it from both.

## 3. Error Handling

**Major — `lib/verify/runner.ts:148`** — `runCommand` settles only on `close` (or `error`). The timeout path at `:150-158` *only signals*; it never settles the promise. `close` requires both process exit **and** every inherited stdio pipe closing, so any descendant that outlives the process group while holding stdout leaves the promise pending forever — and the timeout cannot rescue it, because the timeout has no terminal settle of its own.

I reproduced both halves of this against the exact spawn options the runner uses (`shell: true, detached, stdio: ["ignore","pipe","pipe"]`):

```
# escapee + group kill (the timeout path)
exit fired at 1001 ms
SIGKILL err ESRCH
after group SIGKILL -> exited: true  closed: false   <-- never settles

# clean exit, background descendant holding stdout
stdout: "done\n"
exit 0 at 3 ms
still not closed after 4s
CLOSE 0 at 8006 ms                                   <-- settle deferred to the descendant
```

*Failure scenario:* a project configures `{"name":"e2e","command":"npm run test:e2e"}`. A run leaves a stray dev server / watcher / `setsid` descendant holding the inherited pipe. `runCommand` never resolves → `runVerification` never returns → and because `f81a7e9` now wraps both call sites in `withVerificationWorktreeLock`, the `finally` at `execution-lock.ts:49-52` never runs. The lock key is poisoned for the lifetime of the server process: the pipeline (`wait` defaulted to true) queues behind it **forever** on every subsequent run for that epic, and the manual POST (`wait: false`) returns 409 forever. The originating pipeline run has no terminal state, emits no notification, and the stalled-session watchdog cannot see it because a verify run is deliberately not an agent session. On Windows this is not a corner case but the guaranteed timeout behaviour: `detached` is false, so `signalProcessGroup` falls through to `child.kill()`, which reaches only `cmd.exe` while the grandchild keeps the pipes open.

The lock is the right fix for the concurrency Major — it just converted a single hung command into a permanent per-worktree deadlock, which is why I'm raising this from the Minor it was last time.

*Recommendation:* give `finish` an unconditional deadline. Simplest form: settle on `exit` with a short grace window for `close` to flush, and arm one final `setTimeout(() => finish(null), VERIFY_KILL_GRACE_MS)` when escalating to SIGKILL. Secondary benefit: `durationMs` is currently measured to `close` (8 006 ms in the trace above for a command that exited in 3 ms), so the persisted duration is wrong whenever a descendant lingers.

**Minor — `lib/pipeline/stages.ts:248, 264, 275, 277`** — `runPipelineVerification` throws on every *applicability* fault (no code session, no recorded worktree, no `gitRepoPath`, non-managed path), and the runner's crash handler (`lib/pipeline/runner.ts:627-648`) responds by calling `parkRejectedTicket` — pulling the ticket back out of Review — and terminating the run as `failed`. The sibling regression gate deliberately does the opposite and documents why at `lib/pipeline/verify.ts:179-185`: *"the gate is TOTAL: a transient database error must resolve to 'did not apply', never to a thrown gate. The runner's crash path would otherwise fail the run and park a ticket … for a fault that says nothing about the branch."*
*Failure scenario:* the most reachable one is inside `runVerification` itself — all commands pass, then `database.insert(verifyReports).values(...).run()` (`lib/verify/runner.ts:207-213`) throws (FK, disk, lock). The exception propagates into the crash path, so a fully green branch is parked back to `in_progress` and the run is reported failed, with the only diagnostic a `console.warn`.
*Recommendation:* mirror the gate's split — wrap the applicability reads and the persistence in a total path that returns `{ ran: false }`, and reserve the crash/park path for "commands ran and told us something".

**Minor — `app/api/.../verify/route.ts:142` vs `lib/pipeline/stages.ts` stage dispatch** — the new exclusion covers verification-vs-verification only. The agent-active check at `:142` is a point-in-time read, and nothing on the dispatch side consults the verification lock. A manual run started while the epic is idle can therefore overlap a fix or review agent that the pipeline dispatches into the same worktree seconds later. The blast radius is now much smaller than before (a misleading manual report, not a spent fix cycle), which is why this is Minor rather than a repeat Major.

**Suggestion — `lib/verify/runner.ts:196-200`** — with an empty `commands` array, `[].every(...)` is `true`, so the function persists `status: "pass"` having executed nothing. Both callers pre-check `config.enabled`, so it's unreachable today, but `runVerification` is exported and the point of the table is that a `pass` row means something was mechanically proven.

**Suggestion — `lib/verify/runner.ts:133`** — `env: process.env` inherits the Arij server's environment, including `NODE_ENV`. This epic's own comment history records a `npm run build` failing under an inherited non-standard `NODE_ENV` and passing under `env -u NODE_ENV`. A `build` verify command run from the dev server will inherit `NODE_ENV=development`. Worth either scrubbing `NODE_ENV` or documenting it next to the Settings field.

## 4. Performance

**Minor — `hooks/useEpicDetail.ts:57`** — the verify `GET` was added to `fetchData`, which is also the 5-second poll callback (`hooks/useEpicDetail.ts:99`). Each tick re-downloads the full report, whose `commands` blob carries up to `VERIFY_OUTPUT_LIMIT_BYTES` (64 KiB) of `tail` **per command**. Polling is gated on `isRunning` (`components/kanban/EpicDetail.tsx:221`), so this is bounded to "an agent is working on this ticket and the panel is open" — but that is exactly the window a user watches. Unchanged since the last review.
There is also a small ordering race: a poll `GET` issued before a manual run finishes can resolve *after* `onReportChange`, reverting the panel to the stale report for one tick.
*Recommendation:* serve tails lazily (`?tails=1` or a per-command endpoint), or refetch on `ticket:updated` plus after a manual run rather than every tick.

Otherwise sound: `verify_reports_epic_finished_idx` matches the GET's `WHERE epic_id … ORDER BY finished_at DESC`, `OutputTail` is O(limit) rather than accumulating, and `resolveVerifyConfigForProject` fetches all four keys in one `inArray` read.

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found. `verify-constants.ts` mirrors the existing `regression-constants.ts` / `workspace-constants.ts` client-safe convention, `verify_reports` / `verifyReports` follow the schema's snake/camel split, and `VerificationReportSection.tsx` sits with its siblings under `components/kanban/epic-detail/`.

## 6. Type Safety

No issues found. No `any`; `unknown` is narrowed through real predicates; `VerifyCommand` / `VerifyCommandResult` / `VerificationReport` are shared from one client-safe module across server, route and client; `PromptVerificationCommand` is a structural projection that keeps a server type out of the prompt layer. `VerifyConfig.enabled` being *derived* from `commands.length` rather than stored is the right call — it makes "configured but empty" unrepresentable.

## 7. Testing

**Minor — `__tests__/pipeline-deterministic-verification.test.ts:132`** — the two branches that move a ticket *backwards* remain the only uncovered ones, unchanged since the last review. `grep` finds no test referencing `failedDeterministicVerification`, `failedDeterministicVerificationCrashed`, or a `parkRejectedTicket` spy in this file (the harness at `:62-127` never passes one):
- exhaustion — `lib/pipeline/runner.ts:589-611`: park + terminate;
- crash — `lib/pipeline/runner.ts:627-648`: park + terminate on any throw from the driver, including the four `throw`s at `stages.ts:248/264/275/277`.

Also untested: the "not configured" 409 in `POST` (`route.ts:170-179`) and the runner's spawn-error branch (`runner.ts:140-143`).

**Minor — `lib/pipeline/runner.ts:460-462`** — `handleStageFailure` now forwards `currentRequest.verifyFailure` to retried stages; before this branch it forwarded nothing (confirmed against the merge-base). That changes the *regression gate's* retried-fix prompt for bug tickets even when `verify_commands` is unset, so "verify non configuré → comportement strictement identique" holds only for projects without the regression gate enabled. The new behaviour is almost certainly the better one — a retried fix should keep its failure context — but it is an undeclared, untested change to a neighbouring feature riding inside a commit that claims strict passthrough.
*Recommendation:* add a retry-carries-`verifyFailure` case to `__tests__/pipeline-regression-gate.test.ts`, or split the line out of this epic.

Positives worth keeping: the disabled-path test comparing two full harness runs' `requests`/`traces`/`summary` (`:133-148`) is a stronger proof than the acceptance criterion asked for; `maxSessions: 2` (`:189`) is exactly the right way to prove the session-ceiling criterion; and `pipeline-stages-dispatch.test.ts` now proves the driver *refuses* a session-recorded main checkout, which is the epic's hard constraint tested rather than assumed.

## 8. API Design

No blocking issues. `{ data }` / `{ error }` throughout, `getProjectOr404` / `getEpicOr404` for 404s, 409 for all three refusal modes (no worktree, agent active, not configured) with the standard `createAgentAlreadyRunningPayload` shape reused for the agent case, `errorResponse` for 500, and `emitTicketUpdated` reused instead of a verify-only SSE event.

One design note, not a defect: the Settings card writes the **global** keys only. Per-project overrides are resolvable (`verifyCommandsSettingKey`) and are cleaned up on project delete (`lib/projects/project-settings-keys.ts:40-41`), but a user cannot set them from the UI — so a single global command list applies to every project until someone hand-crafts a PATCH. That matches how `bug_regression_command` behaves today, so it's consistent, and the story's criteria are about resolution semantics; worth a follow-up ticket rather than a change here.

Also correct and worth calling out: `POST` never creates a worktree and never falls back to `gitRepoPath`, `findExistingWorktree` walks older sessions when a recorded worktree has been pruned, and `verify_commands` is reachable only through `/api/settings` — no MCP tool can write it, satisfying the "saisies par l'humain" constraint.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 1 |
| Minor | 6 |
| Suggestion | 2 |

The two Majors from the previous review are properly closed, and the additions in `f81a7e9` are the right shape — containment lifted into `lib/verify/worktree.ts` and applied at both call sites, a process-local lock rather than a lock file. The one blocker is that the lock exposed a pre-existing gap: `runCommand` has no unconditional settle, so a hung command now permanently poisons its worktree's lock and strands the pipeline run with no terminal state. I reproduced it above; the fix is a few lines in `lib/verify/runner.ts`. Everything else here I would approve.

**Note on this session:** the harness has this session in read-only plan mode, which forbids non-read-only tool calls, so I could not file these through `mcp__arij__submit_findings` — no finding rows exist to block approval, and the Major needs to be tracked manually or re-filed from a normal session.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

**Code Review**

# Code Review — Pipeline: étage `verify` déterministe (third pass)

**Scope:** `269e399..715a8b8` — 7 commits, 32 files, +3443/−14, covering all four user stories.

Verification I ran myself in this worktree: the 12 touched test files pass (**347 tests**), `npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false` is clean, ESLint on every changed `.ts`/`.tsx` file is clean, `git diff --check` is clean, and the worktree has no uncommitted changes. The comment history's claims hold.

The two Majors from review #1 (no Settings surface; no worktree exclusion) and the Major from review #2 (`runCommand` had no unconditional settle, poisoning the lock) are all genuinely closed. I re-read `lib/verify/runner.ts:169-199`: `exit` now arms a bounded close-grace, the SIGKILL escalation arms an absolute deadline, and `durationMs` is measured at exit — the deadlock is gone, and both halves are covered by tests at `__tests__/verify-runner.test.ts:219` and `:243`.

---

## 1. Readability

No issues found. The comments carry the *why* consistently: the negative-pid rationale (`lib/verify/runner.ts:85-86`), the close-grace rationale (`runner.ts:20-26`), "there is deliberately no repository-path fallback" (`runner.ts:42`), "empty array is deliberately valid" (`verify-constants.ts:119-125`), the lock's fail-fast-vs-queue split (`execution-lock.ts:3-10`), and the totality argument in `runPipelineVerification` (`lib/pipeline/stages.ts:237-244`) that cites its own precedent. `verificationOutputFence` + the "untrusted command output" framing (`prompt-builder.ts:112-118`, `:148`) is the right instinct — a failing test's stdout can't impersonate instructions.

## 2. DRY Principle

No blocking issues. `isVerifyCommandResult` is now exported once from `verify-constants.ts:46` and consumed by both the route parser and the report guard, closing the prior duplicate. `resolveVerifyConfig` is a single resolver shared by the Settings UI and `resolveVerifyConfigForProject`. See the Suggestion in §3 for the one behavioural difference that survived the deduplication.

## 3. Error Handling

**Major — `hooks/useEpicDetail.ts:117-123`** — the comment claims *"Pipeline and manual runs announce finished reports via `ticket:updated`"*. Only the manual run does. `grep` for `emitTicketUpdated` across `lib/` and `app/` returns exactly two production call sites: the epic `PATCH` route (`app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/[epicId]/route.ts:76`) and the new verify `POST` (`verify/route.ts:203`). The pipeline path never emits it — `runPipelineVerification` (`lib/pipeline/stages.ts:245-315`) emits nothing, and the pipeline's own `trace()` (`lib/pipeline/index.ts:165-188`) only calls `logTransition`, which writes a row and returns.

This is a regression introduced by `715a8b8`. Before it, the verify `GET` was part of `fetchData` (confirmed at `git show 96acc8c:hooks/useEpicDetail.ts:50-58`), so it rode the 5-second poll that `EpicDetail.tsx:221` enables whenever `isRunning`. `715a8b8` removed it from the poll — correctly, to kill the ~128 KiB/tick payload I flagged last time — and replaced it with a `ticket:updated` subscription that the pipeline never fires.

*Failure scenario:* a user opens a ticket and starts an autonomous build. Arij runs `npm test` in the worktree, it fails, a fix cycle is spent, a fix agent is dispatched, verification runs again. Throughout the entire run — potentially an hour — the Verification panel shows "No verification report yet". `EpicDetail` never remounts (`epicId` is stable), the effect deps `[loadData, fetchVerification]` are stable `useCallback`s, and **Run verification** returns 409 while an agent is active (`verify/route.ts:136-145`). The only way to see the mechanical evidence is to close and reopen the panel. This is precisely the observability the epic exists to add, silently absent from the primary path.

*Recommendation:* emit from the pipeline too — `emitTicketUpdated(init.projectId, init.epicId, { verifyReportId, verifyStatus })` after `executeVerification` resolves in `runPipelineVerification`. That also gives the board the same refresh signal the manual route already provides, and makes the hook's comment true.

**Minor — `lib/verify/runner.ts:141-149` / `lib/pipeline/runner.ts:571-608`** — `VerifyCommandResult` cannot distinguish *"could not start"* from *"timed out"* from *"ran and failed"*: `finish` collapses the first two into `exitCode: null`, and the spawn-error flag is not carried into the result. The pipeline consequently treats all three as a fixable code defect and spends a fix cycle. The regression gate in the *same function* deliberately does the opposite and documents why at `lib/pipeline/runner.ts:688-691`: *"An agent in a fix cycle cannot fix an environment fault — fail immediately rather than burning the fix budget."*

*Failure scenario:* a project configures `{"name":"test","command":"npm test"}` and that script defaults to watch mode. Every invocation hangs to the 10-minute default timeout. Night run, per epic: verify (10 min) → fix cycle → real agent session → verify (10 min) → exhausted → park + failed run. Roughly 20–30 minutes and one-to-two agent sessions burned per ticket on a fault no agent can repair, repeated across every epic in the wave.

*Recommendation:* add a discriminator to `VerifyCommandResult` (`outcome: "exited" | "timeout" | "spawn_error"`), and fast-fail the `spawn_error` case in the runner the way `gate.result.reason === "command_error"` already does.

**Minor — `lib/pipeline/stages.ts:245-315`** — making the stage total was the right call, but every applicability fault now resolves to `{ ran: false }` with only a `console.warn`: no `onTrace`, therefore no `ticket_activity_log` entry, therefore no user-visible signal. That includes `assertManagedEpicWorktreePath` throwing (`:296`) — the epic's hard constraint firing — and a pruned worktree.

*Failure scenario:* a project has verification configured. The epic's worktree is pruned after a merge; the next pipeline run's session row still records the stale path, `spawn` never happens, and the ticket lands in Review with no verification and nothing in the activity feed to say so. The operator reasonably reads "reached Review" as "the configured checks passed". `{ ran: false }` is currently indistinguishable from *"verify_commands is not configured"*, which is the one case where silence is correct.

*Recommendation:* return a reason with `{ ran: false }` and emit a `PIPELINE_REASONS.deterministicVerificationSkipped(reason)` trace for everything except the genuinely-disabled path. `trace()` already writes an `actor: "system"` activity row, so this is a one-line addition per branch.

**Minor — `hooks/useEpicDetail.ts:85-87` vs `:198-204`** — the stale-response guard's comment names two writers (*"a manual run or a later fetch"*), but `setVerificationReport` never touches `verifyRequestSeq`. A `fetchVerification` issued before a manual run and resolving after it therefore installs the older report over the manual result. The window is real: `fetchVerification` fires on every `ticket:updated` for the epic, the `POST` holds the request open for the full command duration, and the server is CPU-loaded by the very commands being verified.
*Recommendation:* `++verifyRequestSeq.current` inside `setVerificationReport`.

**Suggestion — `app/api/.../verify/route.ts:36-45`** — `parseCommandResults` now shares `isVerifyCommandResult`, but the two guards still disagree on what to do with a malformed entry: the route `.filter()`s it out and returns a *shorter* report, while `isVerificationReport` rejects the whole thing. A row whose failing command entry is corrupt renders as "Checks failed" with only passing commands listed. Rejecting the row (returning `null`, as the "never verified" case already does) is the safer default for evidence.

**Suggestion — `lib/verify/runner.ts:166-167`** — after settling via the close-grace or the absolute deadline, the `stdout`/`stderr` listeners stay attached and the pipes are never destroyed or `unref`'d. The escaped descendant the grace exists for keeps writing into a stream nobody drains. Memory is bounded by `OutputTail`, but the handles are not released for the server's lifetime. Consider `child.stdout?.destroy()` / `child.stderr?.destroy()` inside `finish`.

**Suggestion — `app/settings/page.tsx:341-370`** — `handleSaveVerifySettings` passes `() => {}` as the revert callback, unlike every sibling handler. It also normalises the two fields *before* awaiting the PATCH, so a failed save leaves the textarea showing reformatted JSON that was never persisted, next to "Failed to save the pipeline settings."

## 4. Performance

**Suggestion — `app/settings/page.tsx:341-370`** — `handleSaveVerifySettings` passes `() => {}` as the revert callback, unlike every sibling handler, and normalises both fields *before* awaiting the PATCH. `8f63da6` makes `tryAutoMerge` refuse when verification is configured and the epic has no fresh passing report. But **nothing in Full Auto ever produces one.** I traced every producer:

6. Nothing in steps 3–5 changed any selector input. Next sweep — `AUTO_MODE_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS = 15_000` (`lib/auto-mode/constants.ts:52`) — repeats it identically.

The epic never completes, and `logTransition` (`lib/workflow/log.ts:24-40`) inserts unconditionally with no dedup: **240 `ticket_activity_log` rows per hour per stuck epic, ~5,760/day**, which floods the ticket's activity feed — the same feed the epic added `actor: system` verify traces to. The user gets no notification, because a skip is not a failure.

Before this commit the gap was *silent*: Full Auto merged without evidence. After it, Full Auto with verification configured **cannot merge at all**. The only escape is for a human to open each ticket and click **Run verification** — which contradicts both the epic's constraint (*"Full Auto et night run héritent du comportement via le pipeline : aucune logique spécifique chez eux"*) and the mode's purpose.

Worth noting the codebase already knows this shape: `lib/auto-mode/select.ts:550-557` documents "the infinite-re-review guard" for precisely the analogous case. The new gate has no equivalent.

*Recommendation:* run the checks where the mode owns the lifecycle — in `reconcileInFlight`, when a `build`/`fix` in-flight session goes terminal, call `createPipelineStageDriver(...).runDeterministicVerification(sessionId)` (the driver is already constructed on the dispatch path; the call creates no session, so it touches neither budget). If that is genuinely a follow-up, then the refusal must at minimum become bounded — see the Minor below — and the ticket must say Full Auto requires a pipeline-built or manually verified epic.

### Major — `lib/auto-mode/merge.ts:794-809` and `:334` — the merge-conflict retry bypasses the gate it just added

`retryMergeAfterFix` calls `mergeWorktree` directly; it never re-enters `runAutoMerge`, so `verificationGateReason` is not consulted. Compounding it, the gate's own "last code session" query filters `inArray(agentSessions.agentType, ["build", "fix"])` (`merge.ts:334`) — and the merge-fix session is created with `agentType: "merge"` (`merge.ts:637`). Even if the gate *were* re-run, it would not see the session that edited the code.

*Failure scenario:* a night run builds and verifies epic E — a genuine passing report exists. Full Auto later picks E up, the gate passes, `mergeWorktree` conflicts. A merge-fix agent is dispatched, edits the conflicted files, commits, and `retryMergeAfterFix` merges to the default branch. The passing report describes the pre-conflict tree; the agent's conflict resolution is merged with zero mechanical evidence and no second review. That is the exact scenario spec §8 already flags as the mode's known risk — and it is the one path the new gate was supposed to cover but doesn't.

*Recommendation:* add `"merge"` to the `agentType` filter and call `verificationGateReason` again immediately before the retry's `mergeWorktree`; on a block, keep the branch and skip rather than merge.

### Minor — `lib/auto-mode/merge.ts:386-396` — a repeating refusal has no backoff, no dedup, and no notification

The mechanism behind the Major's log flood is independent of it: even once Full Auto runs verification, a *failing* report yields `"the latest deterministic verification did not pass"` on every sweep, forever, with the same unbounded write and no user-visible escalation. The conflict path already models the fix (`autoModeRegistry.deferMerge(..., AUTO_MERGE_CONFLICT_BACKOFF_MS)` at `merge.ts:515-529`).

*Recommendation:* defer the merge with a backoff on a verification refusal, log once per deferral window, and notify after N consecutive refusals.

### Minor — `lib/auto-mode/merge.ts:341-344` / `lib/verify/runner.ts:153-161` — the evidence is not bound to a commit

The gate's freshness test is `latestReport.finishedAt < codeEndedAt` — a timestamp proxy for "this report describes the tree that will be merged". Two ways it is wrong:

- The runner executes in the **worktree** (`cwd: input.worktreePath`), while `mergeWorktree` merges the **branch**. Changes the agent left uncommitted are verified but never merged; commits made after verification are merged but never verified.
- Anything that touches the worktree between the report and the merge — a human edit, a subsequent `arji.json` write — is invisible to the gate.

Round #4 flagged commit-SHA binding as a follow-up *"if verification is ever to gate merges"*. `8f63da6` made it gate merges, so the follow-up is now load-bearing.

*Recommendation:* record the verified `HEAD` SHA on `verify_reports` and compare it to the branch head at merge time.

### Suggestion — `lib/auto-mode/merge.ts:341`

`codeEndedAt = lastCodeSession.endedAt ?? lastCodeSession.createdAt`. `finishedAt` is always `new Date().toISOString()` (`T`-separated), whereas a `createdAt` falling back to the schema default is SQLite `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` (space-separated, `lib/db/schema.ts:579`). Lexically `'T'` (0x54) > `' '` (0x20), so any ISO report compares *newer* than any same-day default-format session — the staleness check fails open. Every current build/fix creator passes an explicit ISO `createdAt`, so this is latent rather than live, but the comparison should normalise rather than rely on that.

### Suggestion — `app/api/.../verify/route.ts:36-45` (carried over, unaddressed)

`parseCommandResults` `.filter()`s malformed entries and returns a *shorter* report; `isVerificationReport` rejects the whole value. A row whose failing entry is corrupt renders as "Checks failed" listing only the passing commands. Returning `null` is the safer default for evidence.

### Suggestion — `app/settings/page.tsx:341-370` (carried over, unaddressed)

`handleSaveVerifySettings` passes `() => {}` as the revert callback, unlike every sibling handler, and normalises both fields *before* awaiting the PATCH — a failed save leaves reformatted JSON on screen next to "Failed to save the pipeline settings".

## 4. Performance

**Minor** — the activity-log growth in §3's Major is the significant one: an unbounded insert stream on a 15-second timer, into a table the ticket detail reads in full.

Otherwise sound and unchanged: the 64 KiB-per-command tails are off the 5-second poll, `verify_reports_epic_finished_idx` matches both the GET's and the gate's `WHERE epic_id … ORDER BY finished_at DESC`, `OutputTail` is O(limit), and `resolveVerifyConfigForProject` reads all four keys in one `inArray`. Still open from earlier rounds: the hook's second `EventSource` (`hooks/useEpicDetail.ts:119`) duplicating the page's, and `verify_reports` having no retention policy.

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found.

## 6. Type Safety

No issues found. No `any`; `unknown` narrowed through real predicates; the client-safe module is the single source of `VerifyCommand` / `VerifyCommandResult` / `VerificationReport`; `VerifyConfig.enabled` derived from `commands.length` keeps "configured but empty" unrepresentable. `tsc --noEmit --incremental false` is clean.

## 7. Testing

Coverage of the runner, stage and route is genuinely strong — both park paths, the skip trace, the disabled-path bit-identity comparison, the `maxSessions: 2` ceiling proof, the exit-grace and SIGKILL-deadline settlements, the `NODE_ENV` scrub, the empty-commands guard, tolerant persistence, the spawn-error branch, all five route refusal/success paths, and the pruned-worktree skip added in `8f63da6`.

**Minor — `__tests__/auto-mode-merge.test.ts:762-845`** — round #4 asked that the Full Auto behaviour be pinned *"whichever way §3's Major is resolved"*. Only half of it was: the five new cases all call `tryAutoMerge` **directly**, so they prove the gate's decision logic but say nothing about whether the mode can ever satisfy it. No test touches `sweepProject` with verification configured (`grep` for `verify_commands` across `__tests__/` finds no auto-mode-engine or auto-mode-e2e hit), which is exactly why the livelock in §3 passes CI. A sweep-level test — configured verification, one epic through build → review → merge — would have caught it.

**Minor — `__tests__/auto-mode-merge.test.ts:722-730`** — the new block opens with a `/* The deterministic-verification gate */` banner at column 0 and then registers an `afterEach` and five `it()`s at two-space indentation with **no enclosing `describe`** (line 720 closed `describe("tryAutoMerge — merge conflict")`). They are top-level tests wearing a nested test's indentation, and the `afterEach` is consequently file-global: `db.delete(settings).run()` and `db.delete(verifyReports).run()` now run after *every* test in the file. Harmless today (nothing else in the file uses `settings`), but it is an unintended global hook and the indentation actively misleads.

## 8. API Design

**Minor — `app/settings/page.tsx:1157-1214`** — the card writes only the **global** keys. That was a reasonable follow-up when verification affected only the pipeline; `8f63da6` changed the blast radius. Setting `verify_commands` for one project now blocks unattended merges in **every** Full Auto project on the machine, none of which has a way to opt out from the UI (the per-project keys are resolvable and cleaned up on delete, but not settable). Per-project controls move from "nice to have" to "needed alongside the gate".

**Suggestion — `components/kanban/EpicDetail.tsx:659`** — `VerificationReportSection` renders for every epic regardless of configuration, so with verification off the **Run verification** button always 409s with "Add at least one verify command in Settings". Round #1 suggested hiding it; now that a Settings control exists this is cosmetic, but the panel could read the resolved config.

Everything else in the REST surface remains correct: `{ data }` / `{ error }`, `getProjectOr404` / `getEpicOr404`, 409 for all four refusal modes reusing `createAgentAlreadyRunningPayload`, `errorResponse` for 500, `emitTicketUpdated` at both call sites. The migration is correct — `0033_verify_reports.sql` hand-written with `IF NOT EXISTS`, FKs cascading on project/epic and `set null` on session, `_journal.json` at `idx: 32` with a strictly increasing `when`, no `drizzle-kit generate`. `verify_commands` is reachable only through `/api/settings`, which no MCP tool writes, so the "saisies par l'humain" constraint holds.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 2 |
| Minor | 5 |
| Suggestion | 4 |

The engineering core continues to be strong, and I would approve the runner, the settings contract, the migration, the pipeline wiring and the manual route on their own — the settlement contract is airtight, containment is enforced at both call sites, the stage is total, and the passthrough-identity and session-ceiling proofs exceed what the acceptance criteria asked for.

The blockers are both in `8f63da6`, the commit that answered round #4. Choosing a merge gate over actually running the checks left Full Auto unable to produce the evidence the gate demands, converting a silent gap into a livelock that writes an activity row every fifteen seconds and never completes an epic — and the gate skips the one path where an agent edits code and merges it, the conflict retry. Neither is visible to the suite, because the new tests exercise `tryAutoMerge` in isolation rather than a sweep. Both fixes are contained: a `runDeterministicVerification` call in `reconcileInFlight`, a re-check plus `"merge"` in the `agentType` filter before the retry, and a `deferMerge` backoff on refusal.

**Note on this session:** the harness has this session in read-only plan mode, which forbids non-read-only tool calls, so I could not file these through `mcp__arij__submit_findings` and could not open a `create_bug` follow-up. No finding rows exist to block approval — the two Majors need to be tracked manually or re-filed from a normal session. I have written a remediation plan to `/home/orosius/.claude/plans/project-arij-glimmering-badger.md`.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

**Forensic diagnostic**
<!-- arij:dead-session=D-tvwjBurmSm -->

**Probable root cause** — The build never ran. `spawn E2BIG` is an `execve()` failure raised by the kernel before the child process exists, which is why all three evidence streams are empty. The `oh-my-pi` provider passes the entire build prompt as a single positional argv element (`omp --mode json … -p <PROMPT>`, `lib/providers/oh-my-pi.ts:12-15`), and Linux caps one argv string at 128 KiB (`MAX_ARG_STRLEN`). The ticket-code prompt embeds "the full comment history" verbatim (`lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts:1179`, `1220-1231`) with no byte budget — only the CI-fix path has one (`CI_FIX_MAX_SPEC_BYTES = 16_000`, `prompt-builder.ts:1087`). A `verify`-stage ticket on the workflow engine accumulates exactly the kind of bulk that overflows this: pasted review findings, diffs, test logs. This is deterministic, not transient — the retry produced the identical error, and each pass appends more comments.

**Evidence**
- `spawn E2BIG` with `Raw stream (tail): (none)`, `Output stream (tail): (none)`, `Last text produced: (none)` — no child output at all, so the failure is at spawn, not in the build.
- `lib/providers/oh-my-pi.ts:12`: `omp --mode json [--tools …] [--model <M>] -p <PROMPT>` — the prompt is one argv element, subject to the 128 KiB per-string cap.
- `Attempts before giving up: 2` with an identical recorded error both times, consistent with a size limit rather than a flaky provider or model (`openrouter/stealth/ox-alpha` never received the request).

**Recommended next action**
- Relaunch this ticket on the `claude` provider (which does not pass the prompt through argv) after pruning the accumulated comment thread — trim or summarize the oversized review/log comments on the ticket first, since re-running on `oh-my-pi` at the same size will fail identically. Durable fix, still open: give the ticket-code prompt the same byte budget the CI-fix path already has, and feed argv-based providers via stdin or a temp file.

**Forensic diagnostic**
<!-- arij:dead-session=jCKghqZab4mR -->

**Probable root cause** — The `omp` process never started: `spawn E2BIG` is the kernel refusing `execve` because the argument vector exceeded `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` (128 KB per argv element on Linux). Arij's Oh My Pi provider passes the entire session prompt as a *positional argv element* (`lib/providers/oh-my-pi.ts:13-15`), and the build-stage ticket prompt inlines the full comment history with no byte budget (`lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts:1220-1231`). This ticket ("étage `verify` déterministe") sits on a pipeline epic with a long, repeatedly-retried comment thread, so the assembled prompt crossed the cap. The failure is deterministic in the prompt size, which is why both attempts died identically with zero output — retrying the same stage rebuilds the same oversized argv. Note the codebase already guards this exact limit for CI-fix prompts only (`CI_FIX_MAX_SPEC_BYTES`, `prompt-builder.ts:1085-1116`); the normal build prompt has no equivalent cap. Nothing here indicates a problem with the ticket's code, the model, or the `verify` stage logic itself.

**Evidence**
- `spawn E2BIG` — an `execve` errno, raised by Node before the child runs; it is not an agent-side or model-side error.
- "Raw stream (tail) (none)" / "Output stream (tail) (none)" / "Last text produced (none)" — the process produced no bytes at all, confirming it died at spawn rather than during the build.
- `lib/providers/oh-my-pi.ts:13-15`: "`omp --mode json … -p <PROMPT>` … omp's `-p` is a boolean `--print` flag with the prompt as a positional argument" — the whole prompt travels through argv, where the 128 KB per-element cap applies; contrast `prompt-builder.ts:1107-1109`, "an uncapped spec could still push the prompt past MAX_ARG_STRLEN on argv-based providers."

**Recommended next action**
- Relaunch this ticket's build stage on the `claude` provider (Claude Code CLI passes the prompt via stdin, not argv, so it is immune to this cap) — and, as the durable fix, open a follow-up to byte-budget the comment history in `buildTicketPrompt` the way `CI_FIX_MAX_SPEC_BYTES` already budgets the CI-fix spec, or switch `OhMyPiProvider` to feed the prompt over stdin.

Fifth-review fixes committed in `d9afcf2` (12 files, +1162/−22).

**Major #1 fixed — Full Auto could not satisfy the gate it was given.** `8f63da6` answered round #4 with a merge gate, but `runDeterministicVerification` was still wired only into `startPipelineRun`, and Full Auto never enters `runPipeline`. No epic the mode built could ever produce a `verify_reports` row, so the gate refused forever — an activity row every 15s per stuck epic and no path to `done`.

The engine now runs the checks itself in `reconcileInFlight`, right after a delivered code session — the same point in the lifecycle the pipeline uses. Verification is not an agent session: no slot, neither budget. A pass is traced; a skip is traced *separately* so it cannot read as a pass; a crash leaves the ticket untouched (a fault in the checks says nothing about the branch). A **failure returns the ticket to In Progress** through the negative-review transition and posts the failing command's bounded tail to the ticket — the mode has no fix-cycle ladder, so making the ticket buildable again with the evidence attached is how it repairs a red branch. The failure is charged to the parking ladder, which bounds build → red → build.

**Major #2 fixed — the merge-conflict retry bypassed the gate.** `retryMergeAfterFix` called `mergeWorktree` directly, so a merge-fix agent could edit, commit and land on the default branch with no mechanical check and no second review. It now runs the checks against the resolved tree and re-asks the gate, failing closed (park + notify) when the evidence is missing. `verificationGateReason` counts `merge` sessions as code sessions, so the merge-fix session's own fresh report is what unblocks the retry.

**Minors/suggestions also closed:**
- A refused merge now `deferMerge`s with a 10-minute backoff and notifies once after three consecutive refusals, instead of one activity row per sweep forever.
- `verificationGateReason` normalises SQLite's space-separated timestamps against ISO ones — lexically `'T' > ' '` made the staleness check fail open.
- The verify `GET` rejects a report whose command rows are malformed instead of returning a shorter, misleadingly-passing one.
- `handleSaveVerifySettings` restores the typed value when the PATCH fails.
- The verification-gate tests were top-level with no enclosing `describe`, which made their `afterEach` file-global.

**Tests:** sweep-level coverage of build → verify → review → merge with verification configured (both directions), the failed-checks bounce and its park, skip/crash traces, story scope, the conflict-retry gate both ways, the refusal backoff and notification, the corrupt-report GET, and the settings revert. Live Full Auto behaviour remains pending merge — the orchestrator runs `main`.

# Code Review — Pipeline : étage `verify` déterministe (sixth pass)

**Scope:** `269e399..d9afcf2` — 10 commits, 40 files, +4936/−20, all four user stories.

Round #5's two Majors are genuinely closed, and closed the *right* way. `lib/auto-mode/engine.ts:443-448` now runs the checks in `reconcileInFlight` rather than only gating on them, so the mode can satisfy its own gate; `__tests__/auto-mode-e2e.test.ts:530-660` proves the loop closes end to end through a real sweep, which is exactly the test whose absence let the livelock pass CI. `retryMergeAfterFix` verifies the resolved tree and re-asks the gate (`lib/auto-mode/merge.ts:909-918`), with `"merge"` added to the code-session filter (`merge.ts:343`) so the merge-fix session's own report is what unblocks it — and it fails closed, pinned both ways at `__tests__/auto-mode-merge.test.ts:184` and `:220`. The refusal backoff, the `normalizeInstant` fix, the all-or-nothing report parse, the Settings revert callback and the stray top-level `describe` are all done.

This round's findings are all in the new engine path.

---

## 1. Readability

No issues found. The new comments carry the *why* and are unusually precise about lifecycle: the `isMergeInFlight` guard explains the closure-vs-sweep race it prevents (`engine.ts:517-522`), the "run the checks BEFORE crediting the session" note explains the ordering constraint rather than restating it (`engine.ts:439-442`), `refuseUnverifiedMerge`'s doc quantifies the log flood it exists to stop (`merge.ts:373-386`), and `normalizeInstant` states the `'T' > ' '` collation fact directly (`merge.ts:360-367`).

## 2. DRY Principle

No issues found. `createAutoModeMergeNotification` factors the parked/blocked pair without inventing a second notification shape, and `verifyDeliveredCode` reuses `buildDeterministicVerificationFixSection` so the untrusted-output framing is identical to the pipeline's fix prompt. See §3.1 for the one place the *convention* was not reused.

## 3. Error Handling

### Major — `lib/auto-mode/engine.ts:629-644` — a story's verification evidence is filed on the epic, so neither the rebuilt story nor the user ever sees it

`postVerificationFailureComment` always inserts `{ epicId }`. Every other comment writer in this codebase branches on scope — `lib/pipeline/stages.ts:948-951` and `:983-986` both use `scope === "story" && userStoryId ? { userStoryId } : { epicId }` — and the function ten lines below it, `returnTicketToInProgress` (`engine.ts:666`), already distinguishes the two cases via `entry.ticketId !== entry.epicId`. Full Auto does dispatch story builds: `addInFlight` records `ticketId: candidate.ticketId` (`engine.ts:1010-1014`), which is the story id for story-scoped candidates.

The consumers both filter by story id:
- the next build's prompt — `lib/pipeline/stages.ts:602-608`, `scope === "story" && userStoryId ? eq(ticketComments.userStoryId, userStoryId) : eq(ticketComments.epicId, epicId)`;
- the story's comment panel — `app/api/projects/[projectId]/stories/[storyId]/comments/route.ts:23`, `eq(ticketComments.userStoryId, storyId)`.

*Failure scenario:* Full Auto builds story `s1` of epic `e1`. `npm test` goes red. The engine traces the failure, files the tail on `e1`, and returns `s1` to In Progress. The next sweep dispatches a story build for `s1`; `buildTicketPrompt` loads comments `WHERE user_story_id = 's1'` and finds nothing about the failure, so the agent rebuilds blind and produces the same red tree. Three rounds later the ticket parks — three agent sessions and three full test runs spent, with the evidence sitting on a thread nobody in that loop reads. The user opening `s1` sees no failure comment either. This is precisely the mechanism the commit message names as the mode's substitute for a fix-cycle ladder ("posts the failing command's bounded tail to the ticket, so the next build sees why"), and in story scope it doesn't work.

*Recommendation:* pass `entry.ticketId`/`entry.epicId` through and use the same `scope === "story"` ternary as `stages.ts:948`.

### Major — `lib/auto-mode/engine.ts:438-448` — verification fires on any `completed` build, including `asked_question` and `silent`, unlike the pipeline

The guard is `status === "completed" && !silentReview && !transitionRefused`, and `silentReview` is scoped to `entry.kind === "review"` (`engine.ts:430-433`). A build session that ends by asking a question, or that delivers nothing, has `status: "completed"` with outcome `asked_question` / `silent` — `lib/workflow/automatic-transitions.ts:676` (`opts.success && opts.outcome !== "asked_question"`) and `lib/auto-mode/select.ts:41-42` ("an `asked_question` session leaves the ticket in `in_progress`") both confirm the shape. So `verifyDeliveredCode` runs on code that was never delivered.

The pipeline deliberately does not: `lib/pipeline/runner.ts:539-545` returns `paused_question` *before* reaching the verification block at `:557-563`, so the checks only ever run on `result.success && outcome !== "asked_question"`. `readSessionOutcome` is already read three lines above the call site, so the engine has everything it needs to match.

*Failure scenario:* a build agent stops mid-edit and calls `ask_question`. The ticket is held in `in_progress` awaiting the user. Full Auto then runs `npm test` on the half-finished worktree — up to `verify_timeout_ms` per command with the sweep mutex held (see the Minor below) — gets a red, and:
1. traces `Auto mode: deterministic verification failed at "test" — returned to In Progress` (`constants.ts:365-366`) into the ticket feed, which is false: `returnTicketToInProgress` sees status `in_progress`, not `review`/`done`, and returns without moving anything (`engine.ts:673`, `:691`);
2. posts a failing-test comment into the exact thread where the user is being asked to answer the agent's question;
3. charges a failure to the parking ladder (`engine.ts:596-601`) for a session that ended correctly by asking.

*Recommendation:* gate on delivery — `sessionOutcome === "answered"` (or at minimum `!== "asked_question" && !== "silent"`) — mirroring `runner.ts:539`.

### Minor — `lib/auto-mode/engine.ts:586-594` — the failure trace asserts a transition that may not have happened

`AUTO_MODE_REASONS.verificationFailed(label)` ends in `— returned to In Progress` and is written *before* `returnTicketToInProgress`, which has three silent no-op exits (ticket row missing, status not `review`/`done`) plus a `try/catch` that swallows a refused transition into a `console.warn` (`engine.ts:699-704`). The comment at `:584-585` explains the ordering as feed readability, which is fair, but the string states an outcome the next call may not produce.

*Failure scenario:* an epic in `review` has one story already `released`. `transitionReviewRejected` (`lib/workflow/automatic-transitions.ts:438-453`) pre-validates every non-`in_progress` story; `released` is terminal, `requireValid` throws, nothing moves. The feed says the ticket was returned to In Progress; the board shows it still in Review; the failure streak advanced anyway.

*Recommendation:* have `returnTicketToInProgress` return whether it moved, and trace the outcome (moved / held) after the fact — the codebase already has this pattern in `pullTicketBackIfPromoted`, which returns "the status the ticket is held at afterwards … so the caller's hold entry stays truthful instead of hard-coding in_progress" (`automatic-transitions.ts:495-497`).

### Minor — `lib/auto-mode/engine.ts:767-772` — the per-project sweep mutex is now held across child-process execution

`reconcileInFlight` is awaited inside the `tryLock`/`unlock` critical section, and it awaits verification *sequentially per in-flight entry*. With the epic's own worked example (`test`, `lint`, `build`) at the default `DEFAULT_VERIFY_TIMEOUT_MS = 10 * 60_000` (`verify-constants.ts:17`), one delivered build can hold the lock for up to 30 minutes; with `buildConcurrency: 3` delivering together, up to 90. Nothing else for that project progresses in that window — no review dispatch, no merge, no build on any other epic — and every 15-second tick (`constants.ts:52`) returns `"locked"` and is dropped rather than queued. The driver's lock also defaults to `wait: true`, so a user's manual **Run verification** on the same worktree extends the hold rather than being refused.

The comment at `:767-771` acknowledges the hold and argues it is bounded, which is true, but "bounded by 30 minutes" is a different claim from "safe for a 15-second supervisor loop". The pipeline does not have this problem because each run is its own async lifetime.

*Recommendation:* run the checks outside the sweep's critical section — e.g. kick them from the terminal hook and let the next sweep read the persisted report (the merge gate already reads `verify_reports` rather than a return value, so the two are decoupled) — or at minimum cap what one sweep will verify per tick and log the deferral.

### Suggestion — `lib/auto-mode/merge.ts:825-843` — `verifyResolvedConflict` discards `skipReason`

The engine goes out of its way to trace skips separately so they cannot read as a pass (`engine.ts:548-561`). The merge path does the opposite: it awaits `runDeterministicVerification`, ignores the returned outcome entirely, and lets the gate speak. When the run *skipped* (pruned worktree, unmanaged path), the epic parks with `deterministic verification blocked the merge: the passing verification predates the most recent code session` — true but two steps removed from the actual cause the skip already knew. `__tests__/auto-mode-merge.test.ts:226-230` sets up exactly this case and asserts only the park.

### Suggestion — `lib/verify/runner.ts:254-271` — tolerant persistence now has a second-order effect on the gate

A `pass` whose row fails to insert is warned and returned anyway. That was the right call when only the pipeline consumed the return value. Now `verifyDeliveredCode` traces `deterministic verification passed` from that in-memory report while `verificationGateReason` reads the table, finds nothing, and returns `"deterministic verification has never run for this epic"` — forever, until someone clicks **Run verification**. Consider treating a failed persist as a traced skip so the two halves cannot disagree.

## 4. Performance

The sweep-mutex hold in §3 is the significant one this round.

Otherwise the new code is cheap and the earlier fixes hold: the refusal backoff replaces ~5,700 activity rows/day/epic with one per 10-minute window, `verify_reports_epic_finished_idx` serves both the GET and the gate's `WHERE epic_id … ORDER BY finished_at DESC`, `VERIFICATION_COMMENT_TAIL_LIMIT = 4_000` (`engine.ts:483`) correctly bounds what gets copied into a thread that every subsequent prompt embeds verbatim, and the 64 KiB tails remain off the 5-second poll.

Still open from earlier rounds, unchanged: `hooks/useEpicDetail.ts:119` opens a second `EventSource` for a project the page already subscribes to, and `verify_reports` has no retention policy.

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found.

## 6. Type Safety

No issues found. `runDeterministicVerification` is typed as an optional dep returning the shared `PipelineDeterministicVerificationOutcome` rather than a bespoke shape, `AutoModeInFlightEntry` is imported as a type, no `any` anywhere in the new code, and `tsc --noEmit --incremental false` is clean.

## 7. Testing

The sweep-level coverage added this round is the right fix for round #5's testing gap — `__tests__/auto-mode-e2e.test.ts:530-660` runs build → verify → review → merge with `verify_commands` actually set in `settings`, in both directions, and its header comment states precisely why the two halves must be tested together. The `describe` nesting fix landed, and the conflict-retry gate is pinned both ways.

**Minor — `__tests__/auto-mode-engine.test.ts:1162`** — `it("returns a story — not its epic — to In Progress when its checks fail")` asserts only `userStories.status === "in_progress"`. The name's negative claim is not asserted, and it is wrong: `transitionReviewRejected` applies an unconditional epic transition to `in_progress` in story scope too (`lib/workflow/automatic-transitions.ts:455-466`). Either assert the epic's real status and rename, or make the behaviour match the name.

**Minor — no test covers where the failure comment is filed in story scope.** The epic-scope test asserts comment content (`:1050-1067`); the story test asserts none. That is the gap behind §3's first Major — a single `expect(comment?.userStoryId).toBe("s1")` would have caught it.

Also untested: the `asked_question` / `silent` build outcomes reaching verification (§3's second Major — `__tests__/auto-mode-engine.test.ts` proves reviews are excluded at `:1141` but never probes a non-delivering build), and `returnTicketToInProgress`'s refused-transition branch.

## 8. API Design

No new issues. `createAutoModeMergeBlockedNotification` reuses the extracted helper and the `status: "failed"` alarm-styling convention the file already documents for non-failure notifications (`lib/notifications/create.ts:386`, `:471`). `toResponseReport` returning `null` for a corrupt row is the right call and matches `isVerificationReport`. The migration remains correct: `0033_verify_reports.sql` hand-written, `_journal.json` at `idx: 32` with a strictly increasing `when`, no `drizzle-kit generate`. `verify_commands` is still reachable only through `/api/settings`, so "saisies par l'humain" holds.

Carried forward unchanged, previously triaged as follow-ups: per-project verify settings have no UI while the global keys now gate unattended merges for every project on the machine; `verify_reports` records no commit SHA, so the gate's freshness test remains a timestamp proxy for "this report describes the tree that will be merged"; `VerifyCommandResult` still cannot distinguish spawn-error from timeout from ran-and-failed.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 2 |
| Minor | 4 |
| Suggestion | 2 |

Round #5's blockers are properly closed, and the resolution is better than the option the review proposed — running the checks where the mode owns the lifecycle, with a sweep-level test that would have caught the livelock. The runner, the settings contract, the migration, the pipeline wiring, the manual route and the conflict-retry gate are all in good shape, and I ran typecheck, lint and the relevant suites myself.

Both blockers are in the new `verifyDeliveredCode` path and both are contained. The evidence comment ignores story scope, so for story-scoped work the repair loop the commit describes — rebuild with the failure attached — degrades into three blind rebuilds and a park; the fix is the same `scope === "story"` ternary `lib/pipeline/stages.ts:948` already uses. And the trigger condition is broader than the pipeline's, so a build that ended by asking the user a question gets its half-finished worktree tested, a false "returned to In Progress" written to the feed, and a failure charged against it; `readSessionOutcome` is already in hand three lines above the call.

**Note on this session:** the harness has this session in read-only plan mode, which forbids non-read-only tool calls, so I could not file these through `mcp__arij__submit_findings` and could not open a `create_bug` follow-up. No finding rows exist to block approval — the two Majors need to be tracked manually or re-filed from a normal session.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**
