## Épique implémentée — 5 commits, `npm test` vert (5607 tests, 459 fichiers)

Registry d'options par CLI + persona pre-prompt. Typecheck OK, ESLint scoped propre (les 4 erreurs restantes de `hooks/useAgentConfig.ts` sont préexistantes — vérifiées identiques sur le fichier de `HEAD`), `git diff --check` OK, worktree propre, `arji.json` non touché.

### Ce qui a été livré

| Commit | Contenu |
|---|---|
| `b8bed3c` | Registry `lib/providers/options-registry.ts` + traduction argv dans chaque provider |
| `e65ad6f` | Migration 0041, colonnes `options` / `persona_prompt` / `cli_options`, validation serveur |
| `8036422` | Injection persona + options au point de dispatch unique, + voie chat |
| `86794ab` | Section « CLI options » et champ Persona dans l'éditeur, options en effet sur le détail de session |
| `f026132` | `docs/architecture/named-agent-cli-options.md` |

### Options mesurées contre le `--help` réel (pas la liste provisoire de l'épique)

- **claude 2.1.245** → `--effort` (low…max), `--permission-mode`. **`--max-turns` et `--fast` n'existent pas** sur ce CLI : le mode fast est une commande slash interactive, et `--effort` *est* le levier de thinking.
- **codex 0.148.0** → `-c model_reasoning_effort=<low|medium|high|xhigh>` (`minimal` passe le CLI mais l'API le refuse pour gpt-5.5), `-p/--profile` — **refusé par `codex exec resume`**, donc marqué `resumeSupported: false` dans le registry.
- **omp 18.0.5** → `--thinking`, `--max-time`, `--advisor`.
- **agy 1.1.22** → `--effort` (low|medium|high), `--sandbox`.

**Volontairement non exposés**, chacun pour une raison mesurée : le sandbox et l'approval policy de codex (c'est le sandbox qui coupe son canal MCP — la cause historique des reviews retombées silencieusement en prose), `--approval-mode` d'omp (même panne), `--mode` d'agy (Arij dérive déjà la posture read-only).

### Trois points de conception à valider

1. **Pi n'est pas adressable.** Il a été retiré des providers au nettoyage 2026-08 (aucun support MCP, cf. `lib/providers/types.ts`) ; `PiProvider` ne survit que comme classe de base d'omp. Les 4 CLI réellement sélectionnables sont **CC, Codex, Oh My Pi, Antigravity (agy)** — c'est cette liste qui est couverte. `PiProvider` lit le registry via `this.type`, donc si Pi revient un jour la traduction suit toute seule.

2. **`permission_mode` (CC) ne s'applique qu'aux spawns `code`.** Un reviewer configuré en `bypassPermissions` gagnerait un accès en écriture au worktree qu'il review. Resserrer une session code est permis, desserrer une posture read-only est impossible. Test dédié.

3. **La persona n'est pas backfillée sur les agents existants** (colonne sans `DEFAULT`). Elle est injectée en tête de *chaque* prompt, donc un backfill réécrirait silencieusement les prompts de tous les agents déjà configurés — ce qui contredit « les agents existants ne changent pas de comportement ». Les nouveaux agents reçoivent le défaut « You're an experienced developer » à la création ; les anciens affichent le champ vide avec le défaut en placeholder.

### Écarts assumés par rapport au texte de l'épique

- **Ordre d'injection.** Livré : `persona → prompt de rôle → spec → mémoire → ticket → tâche`. L'épique listait « persona → spec → prompt global → prompt projet → tâche ». Deux raisons : l'ordre spec/prompt-de-rôle est le comportement existant de tous les builders et le churner n'apporte rien ; et « prompt global » / « prompt projet » ne sont pas deux sections — `resolveAgentPrompt` en renvoie une seule (le scope projet écrase le global). Ce qui compte — la persona en tête, avant spec et ticket — est couvert par test.
- **Chat d'agent : options oui, persona non.** Les tours de chat n'ont pas de ligne `agent_sessions` et contournent `processManager.start()` (même raison que `lib/chat/cli-tool-channel.ts` pour le MCP) : les options passent par `ResolvedAgent.cliOptions`. La persona reste sur la voie session — les conversations structurées (brainstorm, création d'épique) sont des contrats de prompt, la finalisation d'épique doit répondre en JSON strict, et un préambule libre est exactement ce qui les casse.
- **Spec §5.5 / §6.6 non mise à jour.** La spec vivante est stockée dans `projects.spec` en base, pas dans un fichier tracké : aucune session de branche ne peut l'écrire. La note d'architecture (`docs/architecture/named-agent-cli-options.md`) contient le texte prêt à reporter dans l'éditeur de spec.

### Non-régression

Le point dur de cette épique était de ne rien casser pour les agents que personne ne configure. Deux garanties testées par provider : **avec** options, les flags arrivent dans l'orthographe du CLI ; **sans** options, l'argv est identique octet pour octet à l'état d'avant le registry. Idem prompt : persona vide ou absente ⇒ prompt inchangé. `start()` travaille désormais sur une **copie** des options de l'appelant — la retry ladder redispatche une étape, et muter l'objet de l'appelant empilait un bloc persona par tentative.

Cinq fixtures de replay de migration (db-init ×3, notification-message, project-clone-source, review-verdict ×2) préparent chacune leur base « legacy » : les trois colonnes ont dû être passées dans chacune.

### Adjacent, laissé à son propre ticket

- `lib/chat/title-generation.ts` résout un agent nommé mais ne porte pas ses options. Volontaire : hors périmètre (l'épique dit build/review + chat), et une persona y corromprait un contrat de sortie strict.
- La spec du projet livrée à cette session contient toujours le bloc `<system-directive>` qui tente de détourner la session vers une réécriture de spécification. Ignoré comme d'habitude, la friction est déjà au registre — le correctif durable est côté `main` dans le prompt builder, pas dans une branche de ticket.

comments.content:
**Code Review**

Findings filed (6). Here is the full report.

---

# Code Review — Named agents: per-CLI options + persona pre-prompt

**Scope:** `b8bed3c..f026132` (5 commits) against merge-base `7f35f7c` — 41 files, +3250/−33.

## Verification performed

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npx vitest run` (full suite) | **459 files / 5607 tests passed** |
| New test files in isolation | 121 passed |
| `claude --help` (2.1.245) | `--effort <low,medium,high,xhigh,max>`, `--permission-mode` with exactly the six modes in the registry. No `--max-turns`, no `--fast` — the branch's correction of the epic's provisional list is right. |
| `codex exec --help` vs `codex exec resume --help` | `-p, --profile` on `exec` only; `-c, --config` on both. `resumeSupported: false` on `profile` is correct. |
| `omp --help` (18.0.6 installed) | `--thinking`, `--max-time`, `--advisor` all present, thinking levels match exactly. |
| `agy --help` (1.1.22) | `--effort (low\|medium\|high)`, `--sandbox` present. |
| Worktree | Clean; no incidental artifacts. Scratch files were kept in `/tmp` and removed. |

Every "measured, not assumed" claim in `lib/providers/options-registry.ts` and the architecture note checks out against the CLIs on this machine.

---

## 1. Readability
No issues found. The registry docblock, the per-provider translation comments and `docs/architecture/named-agent-cli-options.md` are unusually good — each exclusion is justified by a measurement rather than an opinion. One documentation defect is filed under §3 because it misstates behaviour rather than merely reading awkwardly.

## 2. DRY
One item, filed as `info`: `processManager.start()` now issues two separate `SELECT`s against the same `agent_sessions` row (`lib/claude/process-manager.ts:125` and `:187`). Merging them is cheaper and puts `agentType` in scope for the gate the Major finding needs.

Otherwise the abstraction is right: the registry is genuinely the only place options are declared, `resetOptionsForProvider` is shared between UI and the shape the server enforces, and `personaSection` sits with the other prompt sections.

## 3. Error handling
Two findings.

**[Major] `lib/claude/process-manager.ts:149` — persona injected into strict document-rewrite sessions.** The persona is prepended for every session with a `named_agent_id`, with no agent-type gate, unlike the MCP block 40 lines below which skips `isMcpExemptAgentType`. `dreaming`, `memory_distill`, `spec_update` and `spec-auto-rewrite` all set `namedAgentId` from a resolved agent, and their entire response is persisted verbatim as project memory or `projects.spec`. A persona like *"Answer in French and finish with a bullet summary of your reasoning"* ends up written into the durable memory document, which then feeds every later prompt. The branch excluded structured chat conversations for precisely this reason and the doc claims the persona "stays on … build and review prompts" — the code does not enforce that.

**[Minor] `lib/agent-config/named-agents.ts:34` — persona silently truncated at 2000 chars.** No error, no `maxLength` on the textarea, and `NamedAgentRow`'s local state never resyncs from the refetched agent (the row is keyed by `agent.id` and doesn't remount), so a 2500-char paste is stored at 2000 while the editor keeps showing all 2500 and the Save button stays permanently enabled.

Elsewhere error handling is careful and deliberate: both the persona/options block and the MCP block are best-effort with `console.warn`, `parseStoredProviderOptions` swallows malformed JSON, and `getNamedAgentRuntimeConfig` degrades to "no options" on a provider mismatch rather than handing another CLI's flags to a child that would reject them fatally.

## 4. Performance
No issues found beyond the duplicate row read above. Option translation is O(#definitions) over a handful of entries, on the spawn path only.

## 5. Naming conventions
No issues found. `snake_case` storage keys (`permission_mode`, `reasoning_effort`, `max_time`) vs `camelCase` TypeScript is a deliberate, documented split — the keys are persisted per agent and must never be renamed.

## 6. Type safety
No issues found. No `any`. `ProviderOptionValue`, `NamedAgentCliOptions`, `ProviderOptionDefinition` are properly modelled; the two casts (`raw as Record<string, unknown>`, `value as ProviderOptionValue`) are both guarded by a preceding runtime check. `resolveClaudePermissionMode` takes the exact `ClaudeOptions["mode"]` union.

## 7. Testing
Coverage is genuinely thorough — registry shape, per-CLI translation, the "default emits nothing" property, resume-path exclusion, validation messages, migration on a virgin *and* an already-migrated DB, persona ordering, no-double-injection on re-dispatch, and the editor. Two gaps, both tied to the Major finding below:

- `__tests__/named-agent-options-spawn.test.ts:157` asserts that a `mode: "plan"` spawn refuses a loosening override — but reviews are dispatched as `mode: "code"`, so the case that actually matters is untested.
- The "changing CLI resets incompatible options" criterion is covered on the pure function (`resetOptionsForProvider`) but not through the editor's provider `<Select>`. Acceptable; noting it for completeness.

The two modified pre-existing tests are legitimate expectation updates, not loosened guards: `mcp-injection-lifecycle.test.ts` swapped `selectGets.length === 0` for `not.toContain(tables.settings)` (the row read is now unconditional; the *intent* — no settings read behind the provider gate — is preserved), and `named-agents-tab.test.tsx` scoped its queries to the creation card because the row editor legitimately gained the fields.

## 8. API design
No issues found. `options` / `personaPrompt` ride the existing `createNamedAgentSchema` / `updateNamedAgentSchema` with shape-only Zod validation, delegating value validation to the registry, which produces the user-facing message. The PUT route maps to 400/404/409 correctly. The deliberate split — caller-sent bad values are **rejected**, already-stored values a new CLI can't express are **reset silently** — is documented and correct.

---

## The blocking item that isn't in a single category

**[Major] `lib/providers/options-registry.ts:437` — `permission_mode: "plan"` reaches reviewers and silently kills the structured verdict.**

The guard is `if (mode !== "code") return derived`. But reviews, grading and second opinion are *all* `code`-mode spawns on purpose:

- `app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/[epicId]/review/route.ts:223` — *"All review types run in code mode: plan mode refuses mutating MCP tools (submit_findings, create_bug)"*
- `lib/pipeline/stages.ts:1040` — same, pipeline review stage
- `lib/grading/dispatch.ts:276` — `mode: "code"`

So the agent-level choice is applied to reviewers. I confirmed the translation directly: `resolveClaudePermissionMode("code", { permission_mode: "plan" })` returns `"plan"`, and `buildClaudeArgs` emits `--permission-mode plan`. Under that mode claude refuses mutating MCP tools regardless of the allowlist (`lib/claude/spawn.ts:144-146`), so `submit_findings` never fires, no `review_verdict` is persisted, and the transition service falls back to the prose scan — a review that filed nothing reads as a clean review, with no error surfaced.

That is exactly the regression this file's own docblock refuses to ship for codex: *"An option that silently turns reviews back into prose is a regression with a settings toggle in front of it."* `manual` and `dontAsk` warrant the same look — headless, an unanswerable approval is an auto-deny.

**[Major] `lib/providers/options-registry.ts:124`** — and the option's hint ("Applies to build sessions only. Review and chat sessions keep their read-only posture whatever is chosen here") tells the user the opposite, which is what makes it reachable. §3 of the architecture note repeats the claim, along with a rationale ("a reviewer configured with `bypassPermissions` would silently gain write access") that doesn't hold either, since reviewers already derive `bypassPermissions` today.

---

## Deviations from the epic — assessed, not blocking

- **Injection order** shipped as `persona → role prompt → spec → memory → ticket → task` rather than the epic's literal `persona → spec → global prompt → project prompt → task`. The argument is sound: the spec/role-prompt order is pre-existing across every builder, and `resolveAgentPrompt` returns one section, not two. What the criterion is actually about — persona first, ahead of spec and ticket — is implemented and tested.
- **Pi is not addressable.** Verified: `lib/providers/types.ts` requires per-spawn MCP of every provider, and `PiProvider` survives only as omp's base class, reading the registry through `this.type`. Covering CC / Codex / omp / agy instead is the right call.
- **Chat gets options but not the persona.** Correct and consistent with the epic's stated scope.
- **Spec §5.5/§6.6 not updated** — genuinely impossible from a branch (`projects.spec` is a database row). The architecture note carries the text.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 3 |
| Minor | 2 |
| Suggestion (info) | 1 |

The registry, the migration, the argv-identity guarantee and the test suite are all in good shape, and the CLI measurements are accurate — I re-verified every one. What blocks is that the two new injection points reach further than the design says they do: the persona into the document-rewrite sessions whose output is persisted verbatim, and `permission_mode` into the review sessions the hint promises are excluded. Both fixes are a gate in the same place the MCP channel is already gated, plus a hint and two doc paragraphs.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

epics.title: Image uploads of 10 MB or more fail with an opaque 500 and the size guard is unreachable
epics.description:
Measured boundary on `POST /api/projects/:id/chat/upload`: 1 MB, 9 MB and 9.9 MB all return 201; 10 MB exactly, 10.1 MB, 12 MB and 30 MB all return HTTP 500 with a completely empty body.

Server log for the failing case:
```
Request body exceeded 10MB for .../chat/upload. Only the first 10MB will be available...
TypeError: Failed to parse body as FormData.
```

Two compounding defects:

1. `await request.formData()` in `app/api/projects/[projectId]/chat/upload/route.ts` sits OUTSIDE the route's `try` block, so a truncated multipart body throws unhandled and Next returns a bare 500 with no JSON error payload.
2. `MAX_IMAGE_UPLOAD_BYTES` in `lib/uploads/image-attachments.ts` is `10 * 1024 * 1024` — exactly equal to the platform's default request body cap. The multipart envelope pushes any 10 MB file over the cap, so the body is truncated before the route runs. `imageUploadRejectionReason`'s `File too large (X MB). Max: 10MB` branch can therefore never fire in production: it is tested dead code.

The user-visible result is that the one condition the size guard exists to explain is the one condition that produces an unexplained 500.

user_stories.description: Wrap the `request.formData()` call in `app/api/projects/[projectId]/chat/upload/route.ts` in a try/catch and return a structured JSON error with an appropriate status (413 Payload Too Large) when the body cannot be parsed because it was truncated. Follow the existing pattern in the route, which already returns `{ error }` JSON with 400 for an unsupported mime type and for a missing file.

- [ ] A 12 MB upload returns 413 (not 500) with a non-empty JSON body naming the size limit
- [ ] The response body is never empty for any rejected upload
- [ ] Existing 400 responses for unsupported mime type and missing file are unchanged
- [ ] No unhandled exception appears in the server log for an oversized upload

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
Done — committed as `5aa0dc2`, ticket moved to Review.

## What was wrong

Next 16.3.3 defaults `experimental.proxyClientMaxBodySize` to `10485760` — byte for byte the old `MAX_IMAGE_UPLOAD_BYTES`. Since `middleware.ts` matches `/api/:path*`, every upload body was buffered under that cap, so a file *at* the app limit overflowed it as soon as the multipart envelope was added. The body reached the route truncated, `formData()` threw, and the size guard never saw the file.

## The fix

Raised the platform cap to 11 MB rather than lowering the app limit — the bug report measured 9.9 MB returning 201 today, and dropping `MAX_IMAGE_UPLOAD_BYTES` to ~8 MB would have broken uploads that currently work. 1 MB of headroom comfortably covers the ~200-byte envelope.

One deviation from the ticket text, worth naming: it suggested `middlewareClientMaxBodySize`, but that option is deprecated in this Next version and setting both it and `proxyClientMaxBodySize` is a hard config error. I used the current name. The startup banner confirms it lands: `· proxyClientMaxBodySize: 11534336`.

`MAX_IMAGE_UPLOAD_LABEL` is now derived from the byte constant so the two can't drift.

## Verified end to end against a real dev server

| file | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 9.0 MB | 201 | 201 |
| 10.0 MB | **500, empty body** | **201** |
| 10.5 MB | 500 | **400** `File too large (10.5MB). Max: 10MB` |
| 30.0 MB | 413 | 413 (unchanged) |

The regression test reads the cap *from `next.config.ts`*, so it tracks the real configuration instead of a copy of it. It goes red on the merge-base on three assertions and green on the branch.

`tsc` clean, `eslint` clean, full suite 492 files / 6285 tests green.

## One thing to know

`__tests__/refinement-button.test.tsx > polls slowly while idle and fast while a pass runs` is flaky — it failed one full-suite run, passed the next full run entirely, and failed 1 in 5 isolated runs on code my diff doesn't touch. Filed as friction `7U21HTjsPNfh` and left to its own ticket. If the regression checker trips on it, it isn't this change.

comments.content:
**Done** — commit `5aa0dc2`.

## Root cause, confirmed mechanically

`middleware.ts` matches `/api/:path*`, so Next buffers every API request body up to `experimental.proxyClientMaxBodySize`. In Next 16.3.3 that defaults to `10485760` (`node_modules/next/dist/server/config-shared.js:279`) — byte for byte the old `MAX_IMAGE_UPLOAD_BYTES`. A file *at* the app limit overflowed the platform cap the moment the multipart envelope was added, so the body reached the route truncated and `imageUploadRejectionReason`'s size branch could never run.

## Fix

Raised the platform cap to 11MB in `next.config.ts` rather than lowering the app limit — the measured 9.9MB→201 case keeps working, which lowering to e.g. 8MB would have broken. 1MB of headroom comfortably covers the envelope (~200 bytes).

Used `proxyClientMaxBodySize`, not the `middlewareClientMaxBodySize` named in the ticket: the latter is deprecated in this Next version, and setting both is a hard config error (`config.js:718`). The startup banner confirms it takes effect: `· proxyClientMaxBodySize: 11534336`.

`MAX_IMAGE_UPLOAD_LABEL` is now derived from `MAX_IMAGE_UPLOAD_BYTES` (`` `${bytes / 1024 / 1024}MB` ``) so the two cannot drift.

## Measured end to end, real dev server on a spare port

| file | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 9.0MB | 201 | **201** |
| 10.0MB | **500, empty body** | **201** |
| 10.5MB | 500 | **400** `File too large (10.5MB). Max: 10MB` |
| 30.0MB | 413 | 413 (unchanged) |

## Acceptance criteria

- ✅ Just-over-limit upload returns the guard's `File too large (X MB). Max: 10MB` — proven at 10.5MB above and in the new test.
- ✅ Client and server share the constants — `hooks/useImageAttachments.ts` and the route both import `lib/uploads/image-attachments.ts`; untouched, still the single source of truth.
- ✅ Label matches bytes — now derived, plus pinned by a test.
- ✅ Under-limit uploads still 201 — 9.0MB verified live.

## Regression test (red → green)

`__tests__/chat-upload-platform-body-cap.test.ts` drives the route through a simulation of the platform's truncation rule, reading the cap **from `next.config.ts`** (falling back to Next's documented 10MB default) so it tracks the real configuration rather than a copy. The multipart envelope size is computed from the actual headers, not guessed.

On the merge-base it fails on 3 assertions — the cap-above-limit invariant, the exact-limit 201, and the just-over-limit 400. All 6 pass on the branch.

## Verification

`npx tsc --noEmit` clean · `eslint` clean · `npm run test:changed` 53 files / 587 tests green · full `npm test` **492 files / 6285 tests green**.

## Not mine, flagged

`__tests__/refinement-button.test.tsx > polls slowly while idle and fast while a pass runs` is **flaky** — one full-suite run failed it, the next full run was entirely green, and it failed 1 in 5 isolated runs on a tree my diff doesn't touch (it asserts polling cadence via `waitFor`). Filed as friction `7U21HTjsPNfh` (4th occurrence), left to its own ticket. If the regression checker reports it, it isn't this change.

Also pre-existing and untouched: Next warns that the `middleware` file convention is deprecated in favour of `proxy`. Out of scope here, but it will eventually need its own migration.

comments.content:
## Boundary tests landed — and the limit now answers 413

Committed as `4f027c2`.

### What was missing
The size guard had unit coverage but no *boundary* coverage in the direction that mattered. `imageUploadRejectionReason` was called directly in `image-attachment-rules.test.ts`, so its `File too large` branch was green while being unreachable through HTTP, and nothing asserted the accepted side at all — which is exactly how "accepted" silently stopped a byte early at 9.9MB.

### New suite — `__tests__/chat-upload-size-boundary.test.ts`
Walks the boundary a byte at a time, driving the route through the platform-truncation simulation:

| case | expected |
|---|---|
| `MAX - 1` bytes | 201 |
| `MAX` bytes exactly | 201 (guard is `size > MAX`; this is the size that used to 500) |
| `MAX + 1` bytes | 413, non-empty JSON `{ error }` |
| `application/pdf` | 400 — 413 must mean "too big", not "refused" |

The third acceptance criterion — proving the *guard* answered, not the platform — is asserted three ways in one test: the request is confirmed **delivered whole** (`bodyBytes <= PLATFORM_MAX_BODY_BYTES`, read from `next.config.ts`) before anything else, the body is byte-identical to `imageUploadRejectionReason(file)`, and it is asserted **not** to equal `oversizedUploadReason(bodyBytes)`. Substituting the truncation path for the guard is the exact failure this ticket exists to prevent, so the two messages are pinned apart rather than both being accepted as "an error was returned".

Fourth criterion: a test reads `vitest.config.ts` and pins that this file's own path sits outside every excluded tree (`.claude`, `projects`, `data`, …) and matches the include glob. A suite that is not collected guards nothing. (The file runs under `// @vitest-environment node` — importing the vitest config loads Vite's plugin pipeline, and esbuild refuses to run under jsdom's `TextEncoder`.)

### One defect found while writing them
An oversized **file** answered 400 while an oversized **body** answered 413 — the same condition getting two statuses depending on which side of the platform cap it landed on. `imageUploadRejection` now returns a `code` next to the wording and the route maps `too_large` → 413, keeping 400 for a file of the wrong shape. `imageUploadRejectionReason` delegates to it so the wording stays single-sourced; the client pre-filter (`partitionImageFiles`, status-agnostic `!res.ok`) is untouched. This is a small departure from the literal ticket text, which asked only for tests — but the criterion says the just-over case returns 413, and it returned 400.

### Red → green evidence
Branch test files run against **merge-base (`12062a8`) sources**: 4 of the 6 boundary tests fail there — both the accepted side and the refused side — each with the production symptom `TypeError: Failed to parse body as FormData.` escaping the route. All 6 pass on the branch.

### Verification
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean. `eslint` on the changed files: clean.
- Full suite: 493 files / 6293 tests. One unrelated failure in `refinement-button.test.tsx` (a UI timing test, nothing to do with uploads) that passes in isolation — a load flake on this shared machine; a confirming rerun is in flight.

### Left for its own ticket
`app/api/projects/[projectId]/documents/route.ts:85` has the same shape — its own hand-rolled `File too large … Max: 20MB` returned as 400, not sharing this module and not covered by these tests. Different endpoint, different limit; out of scope here.

`ImportState` → `select | cloning | analyzing | preview`, `ImportProgress` prend un prop `step`. « Cloning owner/repo… » puis « Analyzing project… ». `projectData.data.id` n'est plus lu sans contrôle (une 400 levait avant) : la preview reste éditable avec le message de l'API. **1. `POST /api/projects/clone` n'existe pas encore sur `main`.** Il appartient à l'epic « Service de clone git », dont la branche est encore vide. L'UI est écrite contre le contrat documenté `{ path, ownerRepo, remoteUrl, defaultBranch, reused }` et chaque branche est couverte par des tests à fetch mocké — mais le parcours n'est vérifiable de bout en bout (donc le critère « envoyer un epic en dev crée un worktree ») qu'une fois cet epic mergé.

**2. J'ai pris deux morceaux qui débordent du périmètre UI, faute de quoi l'epic n'était pas livrable :**

- **Migration `0027_project_clone_source.sql`** (`clone_source`, `git_remote_url`, `default_branch`), écrite à la main, journal `idx: 26`, `drizzle-kit generate` non lancé. Sans ces colonnes, le critère « le projet a `clone_source = "github"` » ne peut pas passer. - **`lib/git/github-url.ts`**, module de parsing client-safe. La branche « Parsing et validation des URL GitHub » (commit `934f0d4`) place `parseGitHubRepoInput()` dans `lib/git/remote.ts`, qui importe `simple-git` au niveau module et ne peut donc pas atterrir dans un bundle navigateur — or le critère « bouton désactivé tant que la valeur ne parse pas » impose un parsing côté client. comments.content:
**Code Review**

# Code Review Report — "Parcours d'import depuis une URL GitHub (UI)"

Scope reviewed: `app/projects/import/page.tsx`, `app/projects/new/page.tsx`, `components/import/{FolderSelector,GitHubUrlSelector,ImportProgress,ImportPreview}.tsx`, `lib/git/github-url.ts`, `lib/git/manager.ts`, `lib/validation/schemas.ts`, `app/api/projects/route.ts`, `app/api/projects/import/route.ts`, `lib/db/migrations/0027_project_clone_source.sql` + `meta/_journal.json`, `lib/db/init.ts`, and the six new/updated test files. Commits `19eb33b`, `249d9eb` on base `c9d404e`.

Overall the implementation is strong: the state machine is clean, the client-safe parser split is well justified, the migration/journal/legacy-baseline handling is correct (0027 at `idx: 26`, `POST_BASELINE_COLUMN_MIGRATIONS` entry, `db-init.test.ts` legacy simulations updated), and test coverage is direct for every story. The findings below are mostly about the failure paths this epic exists to harden — two of them are re-openings of findings from the previous review round that were not fully addressed.

## 1. Readability

No issues found.

Names are descriptive (`sendJson`, `applyProjectUpdate`, `createEpicsAndStories`, `exportArjiJson`, `resolveBaseBranch`), the non-obvious decisions carry good comments (why `cloneInfo`-gated metadata, why the preview is locked once a project row exists, why `main`/`master` keep priority), and the step helpers read top-to-bottom.

## 2. DRY Principle

### Finding 1
- **Severity:** Suggestion
- **Location:** `lib/git/github-url.ts:13-21` vs `lib/git/remote.ts:40-45`
- **Description:** The four remote-URL regexes are duplicated between the new client-safe module and the existing `parseGitHubOwnerRepoFromRemoteUrl()`. The module doc says `remote.ts` should re-export at integration, but nothing enforces it and `remote.ts` on this branch has no `parseGitHubRepoInput` at all — so today there is *no* shared source of truth, and the two grammars can drift (they already differ on segment safety: `remote.ts` performs no `.`/`..`/leading-`-` checks).
- **Recommendation:** At integration, make `github-url.ts` the single grammar owner and have `remote.ts` re-export/compose from it; add a parity test asserting both modules reject the same inputs.

### Finding 2
- **Severity:** Suggestion
- **Location:** `app/projects/import/page.tsx:36` and `components/import/ImportPreview.tsx:11`
- **Description:** `ImportData` is declared twice with subtly different fields (the page's copy adds `status`, `spec`, `priority`, `position`; the preview's doesn't). Structural typing papers over the divergence, but a new arji.json field now has to be added in two places.
- **Recommendation:** Hoist one `ImportData` type to a shared module (e.g. `lib/sync/arji-json.ts` or a `components/import/types.ts`) and import it in both.

## 3. Error Handling

### Finding 3
- **Severity:** Major
- **Location:** `app/projects/import/page.tsx:122` (unchecked cast) and `app/projects/import/page.tsx:246` (unguarded dereference)
- **Description:** `sendJson()` still treats a 2xx response with a malformed or envelope-less body as success: `response.json().catch(() => null)` yields `null`/`{}`/a scalar, and the function returns `{ ok: true, data: payload?.data as T }` — i.e. `data === undefined` — without any check. `runAnalysis()` then does `setImportData(result.data.preview)`, which throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined`. There is no try/catch around `runAnalysis` in either `handleAnalyze` or `handleGitHubImport`, so the rejection is unhandled and the state is never left `"analyzing"`. Result: a permanent "Analyzing project…" spinner with no error and no recovery except reload. This is exactly the previous review's Finding 2, still open, on the epic's primary flow — and it defeats US4's "never left on a dead screen" goal.
- **Recommendation:** Treat `payload === null` / non-object payload / missing expected envelope as a failed request (`ok: false`, error like "unexpected response from /api/projects/import"), and/or validate endpoint-specific shapes. Add a test: 2xx with non-JSON body and 2xx with `{}` for `/api/projects/import` must land back on `select` with the message rendered.

### Finding 4
- **Severity:** Major
- **Location:** `app/projects/import/page.tsx:311` (only write of `createdProjectId`, never reset), `:460` (`busy={validating || createdProjectId !== null}`), `:462-464` (Cancel handler)
- **Description:** The partial-creation dead end from the previous review's Finding 1 was only half-fixed. Sequence: GitHub import → project created → one epic fails → issues + "Open the partially created project" link shown, Validate disabled. User clicks **Cancel** → `resetFeedback()` clears the issues and link, state → `select`, but `createdProjectId` survives. The user starts another import (natural action), spends minutes on clone + analysis, and lands on a preview where "Validate & Import" is **permanently disabled with no message and no link** — a dead screen reachable through the epic's own happy-path failure. Additionally, Cancel remains clickable while `validating` is true: the in-flight chain keeps running after the user left the preview, so a late `router.push` or a late `setIssues`/`setError` can land on top of a *second, concurrent* import flow (stale `cloneInfo`/`folderPath` interleaving included).
- **Recommendation:** (a) Disable (or no-op) Cancel while `validating`; (b) reset `createdProjectId` when the user deliberately starts a new import (`handleAnalyze`/`handleGitHubImport`), which also un-locks the preview. Add the regression test the previous review asked for: partial failure → Cancel → new import → Validate must be enabled.

### Finding 5
- **Severity:** Minor
- **Location:** `app/projects/import/page.tsx:18-27` (`DebugInfo`) and the debug `<details>` block; producer side `app/api/projects/import/route.ts` (`debug: { stack }`, `{ duration, rawPreview }`, `{ duration, keys }`)
- **Description:** The debug contract is partially lost in transit: `stack` is declared on `DebugInfo` but never rendered, and the import route's `rawPreview` / `keys` fields are not in the type at all. For the `{ stack }` debug shape (unexpected server error) the "Debug info" disclosure renders an empty body; for invalid-arji.json failures the most useful field (`rawPreview`) is silently dropped. This undercuts the "every step reports its own failure" goal for the two most diagnostic cases.
- **Recommendation:** Render `stack`, and add `rawPreview`/`keys` to `DebugInfo` (or a generic `Record<string, unknown>` escape hatch) plus one test each.

Positive: everything else in the chain is handled — clone failure returns to `select` with a context-prefixed message, a clone response missing `path` is caught, create-failure keeps the preview editable with the API message + zod `details` expansion, each epic/story/sync/patch step reports distinctly, a failed epic skips its stories without orphans and continues, and `new/page.tsx` now surfaces `data.error` with a status-code fallback and network-failure path.

## 4. Performance

No issues found.

Sequential epic/story creation matches the existing pipeline and the data volumes involved (dozens of tickets). `parseGitHubRepoInput` per keystroke is a handful of regexes. `structuredClone` on edit per keystroke in `ImportPreview` is pre-existing and negligible at preview size. No re-render hazards: `ImportProgress`/selectors are trivial, the page is conditionally rendered per state.

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found.

`camelCase` throughout, components in PascalCase, `ImportSource`/`ImportState`/`CloneInfo`/`GitHubImportRequest` all read well; `app/projects/import/page.tsx` copy uses consistent "…" ellipsis vs "..." only in the progress headings (`"Cloning Orolol/arij..."`) — cosmetic at most, not worth a change.

## 6. Type Safety

### Finding 6
- **Severity:** Minor
- **Location:** `lib/git/github-url.ts:46`
- **Description:** `isSafeRepoSegment` rejects any segment *containing* `..` (`segment.includes("..")`), but the spec (and the previous review's Finding 5) only rejects segments exactly equal to `.` or `..`. GitHub repo names may contain consecutive dots, so `owner/repo..v2` (a valid, creatable repo) is rejected by the button, by the parse, and — via the same grammar — by any server re-parse. The over-rejection is safe (no traversal risk inside an already-isolated segment) but silently makes valid repos un-importable.
- **Recommendation:** Use exact `segment === "." || segment === ".."` and add a `owner/repo..v2` acceptance regression case.

No `any` types anywhere in the touched code. The one unchecked cast is `payload?.data as T` at `page.tsx:122` — already covered by Finding 3.

## 7. Testing

Coverage is the epic's strongest asset: `github-url-client-parser.test.ts` (accept/reject matrix, suffix stripping, no-simple-git-leak check), `github-url-selector.test.tsx` (11), `import-page-github-flow.test.tsx` (18, including gated-response sequencing for the clone→analyze→preview transitions), `import-progress-step.test.tsx` (4), `new-project-page-errors.test.tsx` (4), `projects-create-clone-metadata.test.ts` (9), three new `createWorktree` cases for the `origin/HEAD` path, and the `db-init.test.ts` legacy simulations updated for 0027.

### Finding 7
- **Severity:** Suggestion
- **Location:** `__tests__/import-page-github-flow.test.tsx`, `__tests__/worktree-manager.test.ts`, `__tests__/github-url-client-parser.test.ts`
- **Description:** The suite is comprehensive on the happy path and on per-step failures, but each of the findings above sits exactly in an untested seam: no 2xx envelope-less response case (Finding 3), no "partial import → Cancel → new import" case (Finding 4), no `mergeWorktree` with a non-main/master default (Finding 8), no embedded-`..` parse case (Finding 6).
- **Recommendation:** Add those four regression tests; the fetch-mock harness in `import-page-github-flow.test.tsx` already supports all of them.

## 8. API Design

### Finding 8
- **Severity:** Major
- **Location:** `lib/git/manager.ts:124` (`const mainBranch = branches.all.includes("main") ? "main" : "master";`), consumed by `app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/[epicId]/merge/route.ts:75,210` and `resolve-merge/route.ts:98,245`
- **Description:** The `249d9eb` fix threaded real-default-branch resolution through `createWorktree` (via `resolveBaseBranch` → `origin/HEAD`) and `release.ts`'s `pickBaseBranch` already falls back to `branches[0]` — but `mergeWorktree` still hard-guesses `main`/`master` and then `git.checkout(mainBranch)`. On a freshly cloned repo whose default is `develop`/`trunk` (the exact class this epic exists to support), the epic can now be built (thanks to the fix) but **cannot be merged back**: checkout of non-existent `master` fails, so the review→merge loop — Arij's core lifecycle — breaks with a confusing error. Before this epic such repos couldn't even reach that point (worktree creation failed first), so the fix newly exposes the gap; spec §4.5 states `default_branch` is used "instead of the main/master guess", and the migration header itself says the code should "stop guessing between main and master".
- **Recommendation:** Extract the resolution (local `main` → local `master` → `origin/HEAD` → current branch) into a shared helper and use it in `mergeWorktree` as the merge target, or thread `projects.default_branch` from the row through the merge routes. Add a `develop`-default repo test for the merge path.

### Finding 9
- **Severity:** Minor
- **Location:** `app/api/projects/route.ts:109-142`
- **Description:** `POST /api/projects` accepts the client-asserted `cloneSource: "github"` ownership flag (plus `gitRemoteUrl`/`defaultBranch`) with no consistency check: nothing verifies `githubOwnerRepo` matches `gitRemoteUrl`, that the remote parses as GitHub, that `gitRepoPath` lies under the managed clone root, or that the directory's actual `origin` matches. A crafted request can mark any existing directory as Arij-owned. No deletion consumer exists on this branch yet (the `DELETE` route only removes the row), so this is latent — but the write side ships now and the destructive cleanup consumer is the sibling epic's next step, which makes the flag a data-loss flag in waiting.
- **Recommendation:** When `cloneSource` is present, require the full metadata tuple, validate the clean GitHub URL + `owner/repo` with the existing parser, require the normalized path under the managed root, and (ideally) verify the directory's `origin`. At minimum, block this before the clone-cleanup epic lands.

Positive on API design otherwise: splitting clone from analysis was the right call; the UI sends the *raw pasted value* to the clone endpoint and lets the server re-parse authoritatively (the client parse is display/disabling only); statuses are correct (400 validation, 201 create); response envelopes are consistent `{ data }` / `{ error, details }`; and `POST /api/projects` now persisting `pathResult.normalizedPath` is a genuine improvement the tests pin down.

## Integration risks (cross-epic, not defects on this branch)

1. **`POST /api/projects/clone` does not exist on this branch** (sibling "clone service" epic). The UI is written against the documented `{ path, ownerRepo, remoteUrl, defaultBranch, reused }` contract with mocked-fetch coverage of every branch — verify the contract verbatim at merge, including the 409 mismatch-remote case the UI surfaces.
2. **`/projects` is still absent from `.gitignore`** (spec §4.1). Explicitly deferred to the workspace-layout epic — confirm it lands there, or dogfooding shows every clone as untracked.
3. **Migration `0027` dedupe risk** — if a sibling epic also ships `0027_project_clone_source`, the journal entry and the `POST_BASELINE_COLUMN_MIGRATIONS` rows must be merged, not duplicated.
4. **`remote.ts` re-export** — see Finding 1.

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 3 (Findings 3, 4, 8) |
| Minor | 3 (Findings 5, 6, 9) |
| Suggestion | 3 (Findings 1, 2, 7) |

The UI itself — source switch, distinct progress steps, clone-metadata forwarding, per-step failure surfacing, and the `origin/HEAD` worktree fix — is well built and well tested. But the failure-path hardening that US4 promises has two real dead ends still in it (the 2xx envelope-less freeze and the post-Cancel permanently-locked preview), and the worktree fix's newly-reachable merge path still hard-guesses `main`/`master`, breaking the lifecycle for the exact class of repos this feature imports.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

- **Location:** `app/api/projects/route.ts:142`
- **Description:** Provenance is verified but not *anchored*: nothing requires `normalizedRepoPath` to equal `<projects_root>/<owner>-<repo>`. - **Location:** `lib/git/manager.ts:39` and `app/api/projects/route.ts:197`
- **Description:** Two smaller consequences of the same gap. 1. **`POST /api/projects/clone` still does not exist here.** The UI degrades gracefully (404 → `Request failed (HTTP 404)` → back to the selector), but no acceptance criterion involving a real clone can be verified on this branch.

| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 1 (Finding 1) |
| Minor | 4 (Findings 2, 3, 4, 5) |

- **Description:** The findings above sit in the two seams the suite does not reach: a malformed *story* entry (F1/F2 — the epic-level equivalents are both covered at `:590` and `:624`), and a PATCH that respells the same directory (F6). Both are one test each in harnesses that already exist.

## 8. API Design

### Finding 6 — Minor
- **Location:** `app/api/projects/[projectId]/route.ts:38-46` and `:57-65`
- **Description:** PATCH validates `gitRepoPath` but discards the result — `updates.gitRepoPath = body.gitRepoPath` stores the **raw** input, while `POST` was deliberately fixed this epic to store `pathResult.normalizedPath` (a US3 acceptance criterion). Two consequences, the second of which is new:
  1. The invariant the new comment relies on — *"the stored path is normalised on insert, so 'no change' is an exact string match"* — is broken by the first PATCH that stores a relative or untidy path.
  2. Re-sending the **same** directory with a different spelling (`/home/u/projects/owner-repo/`, `./projects/owner-repo`) compares unequal, is read as a move, and silently clears `clone_source` / `git_remote_url` / `default_branch` — quietly downgrading this epic's own default-branch behaviour back to the `main`/`master` guess on a repo that never moved.

  The raw-path storage predates this epic; only the provenance-clearing dependency on it is new. Latent for now — no UI PATCHes `gitRepoPath` (verified by grep) — but the clearing logic is the doorway the `TODO(workspace-epic)` is meant to guard.
- **Recommendation:** store `pathResult.normalizedPath` (mirroring `route.ts:127`) and compare normalised-to-normalised.

### Finding 7 — Suggestion
- **Location:** `app/api/projects/route.ts:221-235`, `lib/db/schema.ts:16-21`
- **Description:** Nothing prevents two project rows on the same `git_repo_path`. The clone layer is deliberately idempotent (`reused` → *"Repository already cloned — updating"*), and the destination is deterministic `<owner>-<repo>` — so re-importing the same URL now reliably lands two Arij projects driving one clone: same `.arij-worktrees` directory, same default branch, merges from either project checking out and merging into it. The spec's "re-running an import is cheap and safe" holds at the clone layer only. Pre-existing in principle (a user could paste the same local path twice), but this epic makes it the natural outcome of an ordinary retry.
- **Recommendation:** look up an existing project by normalised `git_repo_path` (or `github_owner_repo` + `clone_source`) and either return it or 409 with a link — ideally surfaced at clone time, where the UI already has a "reused" branch to hang it on.

**Positive on API design otherwise:** the provenance validation is the right shape (full tuple → URL/ownerRepo consistency → the directory's *actual* `origin`, with a non-repo directory correctly degrading to a 400 rather than escaping as a 500); the default-branch threading now reaches every consumer — worktree, merge, resolve-merge, diff, PR, release, build, review, pipeline — with `useEpicPr` no longer force-sending `"main"`; envelopes stay `{ data }` / `{ error, details }`; and the migration/journal/legacy-baseline triple is correct.

## Integration risks (cross-epic, not defects on this branch)

1. **`POST /api/projects/clone` still does not exist here.** The UI degrades honestly (404 → back to the selector with a named message) and every branch is covered by mocked fetch, but no acceptance criterion involving a real clone is verifiable on this branch. Confirm `{ path, ownerRepo, remoteUrl, defaultBranch, reused }` verbatim at merge — `handleGitHubImport:322-333` hard-requires all four, `defaultBranch` included.
2. **Migration `0027` dedupe.** If a sibling epic also ships `0027_project_clone_source`, the `idx: 26` journal entry and the three `POST_BASELINE_COLUMN_MIGRATIONS` rows must be merged, not duplicated.
3. **`lib/projects/workspace.ts` / `projects_root`** are still absent, so `normalizedRepoPath` is not yet anchored to the managed destination. Both `TODO(workspace-epic)` markers say so, and the recursive clone cleanup must not ship before that anchor.

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 0 |
| Minor | 3 (Findings 1, 2, 6) |
| Suggestion | 4 (Findings 3, 4, 5, 7) |

Every blocking finding from the previous four rounds is closed and pinned by a test, the suite is green at 2557 tests, and the default-branch work is now threaded end to end. What remains is one narrow residual of the preview-guard class (a `null` story entry still blanks the app), the missing `catch` that would have contained it, and a PATCH path that stores an unnormalised value the new provenance logic assumes is normalised. None of these blocks the epic; all three are small, well-localised fixes.

*(`mcp__arij__submit_findings` was not filed — plan mode forbids non-read-only tool calls, including MCP writes. Findings are anchored to `file:line` above.)*

**Overall Verdict: Approved with Minor Issues**

epics.title: Le badge « Session failed » réapparaît après un retry réussi
epics.description:
## Symptôme

Une carte epic ayant subi un échec d'agent garde l'indicateur rouge « Session failed · <erreur> » **même après un retry réussi**, et même si l'epic a depuis changé de colonne.

Le badge est correctement masqué pendant que le retry tourne, puis **réapparaît dès que le retry se termine**.

## Comportement attendu

L'indicateur d'échec doit disparaître **dès qu'un retry est lancé** sur l'epic, et ne pas revenir : seul le résultat de la **dernière** session doit être reflété sur la carte.

## Cause probable

Le badge est dérivé de « la dernière session **en échec** » de l'epic, et non de « la dernière session tout court » (`hooks/useAgentPolling.ts`).

Un retry crée une **nouvelle** ligne dans `agent_sessions` ; l'ancienne ligne reste en base avec `status = "failed"` (les statuts sont terminaux — `ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS.failed = []` dans `lib/agent-sessions/lifecycle.ts`). D'où la séquence observée :

1. pendant le retry, l'epic est dans la liste des sessions actives → le badge est masqué ;
2. le retry se termine en `completed`, l'epic sort de la liste active → l'ancienne ligne `failed` redevient « la plus récente en échec » → **le badge revient**.

Le filtre « failed session » de la `FilterBar` dérive de la même donnée (`hasFailedSession`) et est donc affecté de la même manière.

## Piste de correction

Passer à une sémantique « la dernière session gagne » : pour chaque epic, ne retenir que la session la plus récente, et n'afficher le badge que si **celle-ci** est en échec. Un retry en `queued` / `running` efface alors le badge immédiatement, ce qui est le comportement demandé.

Point d'attention : `created_at` est un `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` SQLite (précision **seconde**) et le tri serveur départage les ex æquo par `id` (nanoid → ordre arbitraire). Un retry lancé dans la même seconde que l'échec qu'il remplace doit donc être départagé explicitement **en faveur de l'effacement** du badge, sans quoi le bug subsiste de façon intermittente.

## Hors périmètre

La page `sessions/` doit continuer d'afficher l'historique complet, échecs inclus : c'est un journal, pas un état courant.

Conserver la garde sur les sessions actives issues du registry (celles qui n'ont pas encore de ligne en base). Départager explicitement les sessions de même timestamp en faveur de l'effacement du badge, la précision de created_at étant la seconde.

# Code Review — « Le badge "Session failed" réapparaît après un retry réussi »

**Commit:** `9c11796` — *fix(kanban): derive session-failed badge from the epic's latest session*
**Files:** `lib/agent-sessions/latest-failure.ts` (new), `hooks/useAgentPolling.ts`, `components/kanban/Board.tsx`, `components/kanban/EpicCard.tsx`, `__tests__/latest-failure.test.ts` (new)

## Does it fix the bug?

Yes, and I verified it against real data rather than only by reading. Probing the live DB read-only (`/home/orosius/workspace/arij/data/arij.db`): **7 epics currently hold ≥1 failed session; under the new selector only 2 stay badged.** All 5 that clear had a later session *in the same scope* — their own retry. So the change removes exactly the stale badges the ticket describes and no legitimate ones.

Walking the reported sequence:

| Step | Newest session | Badge |
|---|---|---|
| Build fails at T1 | `failed` | shown, T1's error ✔ |
| Retry queued at T2 | `queued` | cleared ✔ |
| Retry completes at T3 | `completed` | **stays cleared** ✔ — the regression, fixed |
| Retry fails at T3 | `failed` | shown, with the *retry's* error and `sessionId` ✔ |

Extracting a pure selector is the right call — it removes the old code's hidden dependency on the API's sort order (`app/api/projects/[projectId]/sessions/route.ts:72-78`). `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean; 60 tests pass across `latest-failure`, `epic-card*`, `kanban-board-filters`, `kanban-filter-bar`. `FilterBar`'s `hasFailedSession` follows automatically via `Board.tsx:283`.

---

## 1. Readability

**Minor — `lib/agent-sessions/latest-failure.ts:10` — the docstring's premise is false for this codebase.**

> "created_at is a SQLite CURRENT_TIMESTAMP (second precision)."

Not true for any row the app writes. `createQueuedSession` (`lib/agent-sessions/lifecycle.ts:325`) is the sole insert path and all 14 call sites pass `createdAt: new Date().toISOString()` — millisecond precision. Measured: `created_at` 237/237 ISO, **0 same-`created_at` groups per epic**. So the tie-break block (l.57-66) is unreachable for app data, and two of the nine tests pin an input the app cannot produce.

*Recommendation:* correct the docstring; keep the tie-break as the deliberate companion to finding 2 — once normalization lands, a legacy SQLite-format row genuinely *does* have second precision, which is when that block earns its place.

**Minor — `lib/agent-sessions/latest-failure.ts:50` — the guard's stated rationale is wrong.**

> `// Registry-only active agents have no DB row yet; never badge those epics.`

Registry activities are hard-coded to `epicId: null` (`app/api/projects/[projectId]/sessions/active/route.ts:180`), so they can never reach `runningEpicIds`. That set only holds epicIds of **DB** rows in `running`/`queued` (same route, l.137). The guard's real effect is narrower: suppress the badge while a stale `queued`/`running` row coexists with a newer `failed` row. Behavior is unchanged from the old code — only the comment misleads.

## 2. DRY Principle

**Major — `lib/agent-sessions/latest-failure.ts:55` (also l.57, l.65) — re-implements a comparison this repo already solved, without the fix.**

`createdAt` and `endedAt` are compared as raw strings. `lib/kanban/awaiting-reply.ts:20-28` — a sibling module doing the same job for the same kanban cards — documents this exact hazard and ships the helper:

```ts
// Timestamps mix ISO-8601 (2026-08-16T09:00:00.000Z, written by routes) and
// SQLite CURRENT_TIMESTAMP (2026-08-16 09:00:00, both UTC). Normalizing the
// separator makes lexicographic comparison chronologically correct.
function normalizeTimestamp(value: string | null | undefined): string | null
```

`'T'` is `0x54`, `' '` is `0x20`, so **any** same-day ISO row sorts above **any** SQLite-format row regardless of real chronology. An epic with an ISO `failed` row and a *newer* SQLite-format `completed` retry picks the older failure as "newest" — a silent, intermittent recurrence of the very bug this ticket closes.

To be precise about the risk: this is **latent, not live**. I measured every timestamp column that feeds these comparisons and found no mixed formats anywhere (`agent_sessions` 237/237 and `ended_at` 234/234 ISO; `ticket_comments`, `epics`, `agent_session_chunks` likewise 100% ISO). `awaiting-reply.ts`'s helper is itself defensive — this repo *anticipated* the hazard, it hasn't hit it. But `agentSessions.createdAt` still defaults to `sql\`CURRENT_TIMESTAMP\`` (`lib/db/schema.ts:188`), so one new call site omitting `createdAt:` reintroduces it, and raw-SQL fixtures already produce that format (`__tests__/permanent-delete.test.ts:57`).

I'm rating this Major on DRY grounds rather than live-defect grounds: a solved, documented helper twenty lines away was not reused, the fix is one import, and the failure mode is a silent return of the reported bug.

*Recommendation:* lift `normalizeTimestamp` into a shared module (e.g. `lib/utils/timestamps.ts`), apply it to both `createdAt` and `endedAt`, and have `awaiting-reply.ts` import it instead of keeping its private copy.

## 3. Error Handling

No issues found. The `try/catch` in `useAgentPolling.poll` is unchanged, `error || "Unknown error"` and `agentType || "build"` cover null columns, and the selector is total — no throw path.

## 4. Performance

**Suggestion — `hooks/useAgentPolling.ts:55` — object identity churn re-renders the whole board every 3 s.**

`setFailedSessions(failed)` always stores a freshly-built object, so the `epicViews` and `visibleColumns` memos (`components/kanban/Board.tsx:261,294`) invalidate on every poll and every card re-renders even when nothing failed. Pre-existing (the old inline loop did the same), but the selector is pure now, so a shallow compare against previous state would make the common "nothing changed" poll free.

The algorithm itself is fine: O(n) grouping plus O(m) per epic.

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found. `selectLatestFailures` / `FailureCandidateSession` / `FailedSessionInfo` are descriptive, the file matches the directory's kebab-case convention, and the test sits with its peers.

## 6. Type Safety

**Minor — `hooks/useAgentPolling.ts:43` — the selector's input is untyped.**

```ts
const sessions = allData.data || [];   // any
```

Passed straight into `selectLatestFailures`, so nothing at that call site is checked — while `activeData` on l.47 gained an explicit `as UnifiedActivity[]` in this very commit. Annotate as `FailureCandidateSession[]` for symmetry. Otherwise clean: no `any` in the new module, and `FailedSessionInfo` now lives next to its selector, which is the right home.

## 7. Testing

**Minor — `__tests__/latest-failure.test.ts:13` — every fixture uses a format the app never writes.**

The `session()` helper defaults to `createdAt: "2026-08-21 10:00:00"` (SQLite format). The suite therefore never exercises real ISO input, and — because the format is uniform within each case — structurally cannot catch finding 2. Re-anchor the default to ISO and add an explicit mixed-format case once normalization lands.

**Minor — four coverage gaps.** The four cases that matter most (retry queued/running, retry completed, retry re-failed, registry guard) are present and well-named. Missing: `cancelled` as the latest status (it clears the badge — a real product decision worth pinning); two epics not leaking into each other; independence from input order (the selector no longer depends on the API's sort — lock that in); the `endedAt`-null fallback at l.63 where `newestGroup[0]` makes the choice arbitrary.

**Minor — behavior worth pinning, not changing: any newer session on the epic clears the badge.** `ticket_build`, `review_*`, `merge`, `qa` and `forensic` all set `epicId`, so a later story completing can erase an earlier story's failure with no retry. The obvious narrowing — keying on `(epicId, userStoryId)` — would **break** the Retry button, since `handleRetryBuild` (`app/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx:182`) posts an epic-level build with `userStoryId: null`. So the current key is right. I searched the live DB for this collateral and found **zero** instances: every failed session in a now-cleared epic had a later session in its own scope. Add a test documenting the trade-off so the next reader doesn't file it as a bug.

## 8. API Design

No issues found. No routes changed; `/api/projects/:id/sessions` still returns the full journal, so the out-of-scope requirement (the `sessions/` page keeps showing every failure) is respected.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 1 |
| Minor | 6 |
| Suggestion | 1 |

The fix is correct for the reported bug and the extraction into a pure selector is a genuine structural improvement, confirmed against production data. What holds it back is the Major: the new comparison re-implements timestamp ordering while ignoring a hazard this repo already documented and solved in the sibling module serving the same cards. It's latent rather than live — I measured that, and it corrects an earlier review pass on this ticket which implied the mixed format was already present in fixtures and data. But the fix is one import and the failure mode is a silent, intermittent return of the exact badge resurrection this ticket exists to kill.

**Filing status:** plan mode is active in this session, which forbids the non-read-only `mcp__arij__submit_findings` and `post_comment` calls. The anchored finding list and the filing steps are written to `/home/orosius/.claude/plans/project-arij-glowing-dragonfly.md` and need relaying from a session that can write — verdict `changes_requested`. A previous review pass left compatible notes at `project-arij-misty-comet.md` that were also never filed; mine supersede them. The ticket status is untouched: it sits in `review`, and `review → done` is a human call.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

---

## 1. Readability

**Minor — `lib/agent-sessions/latest-failure.ts:10` — the docstring's premise is false, twice over.**

> "created_at is a SQLite CURRENT_TIMESTAMP (second precision)."

All 15 production `createQueuedSession` call sites pass `createdAt: now` where `now = new Date().toISOString()` — millisecond precision. Measured: `created_at` is **244/244 ISO**, 0 SQLite-format. And the code compares *full* strings, never second-truncated, so the scenario the paragraph describes — "a retry created in the same second as the failure it replaces" — does **not** produce a tie. Measured: **0 exact `created_at` collisions within an epic**, so lines 57–66 are unreachable for app-written data.

The ticket asserted second precision and the implementation took it at face value. Keep the tie-break — it earns its place once finding 2 lands, because a legacy SQLite-format row genuinely does have second precision — but say that's what it is.

**Minor — `lib/agent-sessions/latest-failure.ts:50` — the guard's stated rationale is wrong.**

> `// Registry-only active agents have no DB row yet; never badge those epics.`

Registry activities are hard-coded `epicId: null` (`app/api/projects/[projectId]/sessions/active/route.ts:180`), so they can never reach `runningEpicIds`; that set only holds epicIds of **DB** rows in `running`/`queued`. The guard's real effect is narrower — suppress the badge while a stale `queued`/`running` row coexists with a newer `failed` row. Behaviour is unchanged from the old code; only the comment misleads.

## 2. DRY Principle

**Major — `lib/agent-sessions/latest-failure.ts:55` (also 57, 65) — re-implements a comparison this repo has already solved six times, and omits the fix.**

`createdAt` and `endedAt` are compared as raw strings. `normalizeTimestamp` exists in **six** places, including the two modules `Board.tsx` imports right alongside this one:

```
lib/kanban/awaiting-reply.ts:25    lib/kanban/unread-ai.ts:34
lib/auto-mode/select.ts:89         lib/auto-mode/engine.ts:411
app/api/inbox/route.ts:45
```

and `awaiting-reply.ts` documents the exact hazard: `'T'` is `0x54`, `' '` is `0x20`, so **any** same-day ISO row sorts above **any** SQLite-format row regardless of real chronology. An epic holding an ISO `failed` row and a *newer* SQLite-format `completed` retry picks the older failure as "newest" — a silent, intermittent recurrence of the very bug this ticket closes.

To be precise about the risk: this is **latent, not live**. I measured every column feeding these comparisons and found no mixed formats (`created_at` 244/244, `ended_at` 242/242 ISO). But `agentSessions.createdAt` still defaults to `sql\`CURRENT_TIMESTAMP\`` (`lib/db/schema.ts:188`), so one new call site omitting `createdAt:` reintroduces it, and raw-SQL fixtures already produce that format.

I'm rating this Major on DRY grounds, not live-defect grounds: a documented helper exists in the sibling files serving the same cards, this is the seventh site and the first to skip it, the fix is one import, and the failure mode is a silent return of the reported bug.

*Recommendation:* lift `normalizeTimestamp` into `lib/utils/timestamps.ts`, apply it to both fields here, and have the six existing copies import it.

## 3. Error Handling

No issues found. The `try/catch` in `useAgentPolling.poll` is unchanged, `error || "Unknown error"` and `agentType || "build"` cover null columns, the degenerate all-`createdAt`-null case falls through sanely, and the selector is total — no throw path.

## 4. Performance

The algorithm is fine: O(n) grouping plus O(m) per epic.

**Info — `hooks/useAgentPolling.ts:55` — object identity churn re-renders the whole board every 3 s.** `setFailedSessions` always stores a freshly-built object, invalidating the `epicViews` and `visibleColumns` memos (`Board.tsx:226,273`) on every poll. Pre-existing (the old inline loop did the same), but the selector is pure now, so a shallow compare would make the common no-change poll free.

**Info — `hooks/useAgentPolling.ts:36` — the selector needs 8 fields; the endpoint ships 30 columns.** `/api/projects/:id/sessions` does `db.select().from(agentSessions)` and spreads every row, so the board re-downloads every session `prompt`. Measured for the busiest project: **6.6 MB, 93 % of it prompt text**, re-fetched every 3 s (`app/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx:74`). Pre-existing and outside this ticket, but worth recording: `FailureCandidateSession` now documents exactly which columns the board actually needs.

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found. `selectLatestFailures` / `FailureCandidateSession` / `FailedSessionInfo` are descriptive, the file matches the directory's kebab-case convention, and the test sits with its peers.

## 6. Type Safety

**Minor — `hooks/useAgentPolling.ts:43` — the selector's input is untyped.**

```ts
const sessions = allData.data || [];   // any
```

Flows straight into `selectLatestFailures`, so nothing at that call site is checked — while `activeData` on line 47 gained an explicit `as UnifiedActivity[]` in this very commit. Annotate as `FailureCandidateSession[]` for symmetry. Otherwise clean: no `any` in the new module, and `FailedSessionInfo` now lives next to its selector, which is the right home.

## 7. Testing

**Minor — `__tests__/latest-failure.test.ts:13` — every fixture uses a format the app never writes.** The `session()` helper defaults to `createdAt: "2026-08-21 10:00:00"`. The suite never exercises real ISO input and — because the format is uniform within each case — structurally cannot catch finding 2. Re-anchor the default to ISO, add an explicit mixed-format case once normalization lands.

**Minor — four coverage gaps.** The cases that matter most (retry queued/running, retry completed, retry re-failed, registry guard) are present and well-named. Missing: `cancelled` as the latest status; two epics not leaking into each other; independence from input order (the selector no longer depends on the API sort — lock that in); and the `endedAt`-null fallback at line 63 where `newestGroup[0]` is arbitrary.

**Minor — collateral worth pinning, not changing.** `ticket_build`, `review_*`, `merge`, `qa` and `forensic` all set `epicId`, so a later story completing can erase an earlier story's failure with no retry. The obvious narrowing — keying on `(epicId, userStoryId)` — would **break** the Retry button, since `handleRetryBuild` posts an epic-level build with `userStoryId: null`. So the current key is right. I searched the live DB and found **zero** instances of this collateral: all 5 cleared epics had a later success in the failure's own scope. Add a test documenting the trade-off.

## 8. API Design

No issues found. No routes changed; `/api/projects/:id/sessions` still returns the full journal, so the out-of-scope requirement (the `sessions/` page keeps showing every failure) is respected.

---

## Behaviour changes worth a decision, not just a test

**Minor — `lib/agent-sessions/latest-failure.ts:60` — a `cancelled` latest session clears the badge.** Fail → retry → user cancels the retry now leaves a clean card, even though nothing succeeded. Under the old logic the failure kept badging. The sharp edge is `components/kanban/Board.tsx:246`: `onRetryBuild` is only passed when `failedSession` is set, so clearing the badge also removes the Retry button *and* the session-log link. Either treat `cancelled` as non-clearing, or decouple the retry affordance from the badge — clearing is much more frequent now.

**Open question for the ticket owner.** The *Symptôme* section says the badge persists « même si l'epic a depuis changé de colonne ». After the fix, **both** remaining badged epics are in `done` (`DRAGGABLE_COLUMNS` excludes only `released`, so `done` cards render the badge) — e.g. `noiu4l-H`, whose last session was a `review_feature` that died on `spawn E2BIG`. The stated *Comportement attendu* — "seul le résultat de la dernière session" — **is** satisfied, so this is a judgment call rather than a defect: confirm it's intended, or suppress the badge for `done`/`released`.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 1 |
| Minor | 7 |
| Info | 2 |

The fix is correct for the reported bug — verified against production data, not just by reading — and the extraction into a pure selector is a genuine structural improvement. What holds it back is the Major: the new comparison re-implements timestamp ordering while skipping a normalization this repo has written six times, twice in the modules serving these same cards. It's latent rather than live (I measured that), but the fix is one import and the failure mode is a silent, intermittent return of the exact badge resurrection this ticket exists to kill. The `cancelled`-clears-the-retry-button interaction is the one behaviour change that needs an explicit decision before this ships.

**Filing status:** plan mode is active in this session and blocks every non-read-only call — `mcp__arij__submit_findings`, `post_comment`, and even `get_ticket` return *"Cannot call … while in plan mode."* The anchored finding list (10 entries with file, line and severity, ready to paste into `submit_findings`) plus the verification data is written to `/home/orosius/.claude/plans/project-arij-rosy-piglet.md` and needs relaying from a writable session — verdict `changes_requested`. Two earlier passes left compatible notes at `project-arij-misty-comet.md` and `project-arij-glowing-dragonfly.md` that were also never filed; mine supersede both. The ticket status is untouched: it sits in `review`, and `review → done` is a human call.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

epics.title: Review : le verdict structuré de submit_findings pilote les transitions
epics.description:
## Contexte
Le verdict de review est aujourd'hui du substring matching de prose (« changes requested », « not complete », « partially complete ») dans `lib/pipeline/findings.ts`, alors que l'outil MCP `submit_findings` transmet déjà un verdict structuré — explicitement marqué « v1 » dans `app/api/mcp/submit-findings/route.ts` et `lib/claude/prompt-sections.ts`. Enseignement de Code with Claude 2026 (« The expanding toolkit ») : le code qui compense l'infiabilité du modèle (parsing de prose) a une demi-vie courte ; le canal structuré doit devenir autoritaire.

## À construire
1. **Persister le verdict** : à la réception de `submit_findings`, écrire le verdict transmis (reprendre l'enum réelle de l'outil) avec l'id de session. Recommandation : colonne `reviewVerdict` sur `agent_sessions` (migration SQL manuscrite + `meta/_journal.json`, jamais `drizzle-kit generate`) — le verdict est un attribut de LA session de review, pas d'un finding.
2. **Priorité des canaux** dans `lib/pipeline/findings.ts` et `lib/workflow/automatic-transitions.ts` : (a) verdict structuré de la session de review du stage s'il existe — autoritaire, la prose est alors ignorée ; (b) sinon fallback prose actuel inchangé. Le fallback reste NÉCESSAIRE : les providers sans MCP (gemini-cli et les 8 autres) ne peuvent pas appeler submit_findings, et `review_provider_segregation` peut router vers eux.
3. **Prompt** : `lib/claude/prompt-sections.ts` — présenter `submit_findings` comme LE canal attendu, le verdict prose n'étant qu'un fallback pour les sessions sans MCP.
4. **Cohérence findings bloquants** : la définition actuelle (agent + open + fenêtre du stage + préfixe `[critical]`/`[major]`) reste inchangée. Un verdict `approve` avec findings bloquants ouverts reste bloquant (les findings priment) — documenter ce cas dans le module et le tester.
5. **Traçabilité** : `ticket_activity_log` mentionne la source du verdict (`structured` vs `prose`) dans `reason`.

## Contraintes
- Aucun changement de la machine à états elle-même : on ne touche qu'à la DÉCISION, pas aux arêtes (`review → done` reste humain, cf. `docs/architecture/ticket-state-machine.md`).
- Rétro-compat totale : zéro submit_findings dans la fenêtre du stage → comportement bit-à-bit identique à aujourd'hui.
- Matrice de tests vitest : (verdict structuré négatif + prose positive → retour in_progress) ; (structuré positif + prose négative → pas de retour) ; (approve + finding [critical] ouvert → bloquant) ; (aucun verdict structuré → fallback prose).

comments.content:
## Epic terminé — le verdict structuré de `submit_findings` pilote les transitions

Trois commits, un par user story.

### 1. Persistance du verdict — `5f99cdc`
- Migration manuscrite `0032_agent_session_review_verdict.sql` (`ALTER TABLE agent_sessions ADD COLUMN review_verdict text`) + entrée `_journal.json` (idx 31, `when` croissant). Pas de `drizzle-kit generate`.
- Écriture à la réception de `submit_findings`, scopée à `auth.sessionId` : une review ne peut parler que pour elle-même.
- Colonne listée dans `POST_BASELINE_COLUMN_MIGRATIONS` (`lib/db/init.ts`) comme 0023/0024/0026/0028/0030/0031 — l'ALTER n'est pas idempotent.
- **Contrat MCP inchangé** : aucun breaking change côté agent.

### 2. Canal structuré prioritaire — `5182683`
Trois canaux, ordre strict, centralisés dans `lib/pipeline/findings.ts` :
1. **Verdict structuré** — autoritaire, la prose est ignorée.
2. **Findings bloquants** — un veto, jamais une approbation. `approved` + finding `[critical]`/`[major]` ouvert = **bloquant** : le reviewer s'est contredit, et le finding bloque de toute façon `review → done` dans le workflow engine. Définition du bloquant (agent + open + fenêtre du stage + préfixe) **inchangée**.
3. **Fallback prose** — inchangé. Nécessaire : gemini-cli et les autres providers sans MCP ne peuvent pas appeler l'outil, et `review_provider_segregation` peut router vers eux.

`transitionReviewRejected` accepte `verdictSource` et l'appose au `reason` → `ticket_activity_log` trace `[verdict source: structured|prose]`. Typé structurellement plutôt qu'importé du pipeline : la couche workflow est en dessous.

**Rétro-compat bit-à-bit** : zéro `submit_findings` dans la fenêtre → comportement identique à avant.

### 3. Prompt reviewer — `1f32523`
`lib/claude/prompt-sections.ts` et la description de l'outil dans `bin/arij-mcp.mjs` présentent `submit_findings` comme LE canal lu. La consigne `**Overall Verdict: …**` reste présente et documentée comme fallback pour les sessions sans MCP.

### Vérification
- **Suite complète verte** : 374 fichiers, 4265 tests. `tsc --noEmit` propre, eslint propre.
- Matrice des 4 cas testée sur **les deux** points d'entrée (`assessReviewOutcome` et `resolveReviewVerdict`) : structuré négatif + prose propre → retour ; structuré positif + prose négative → pas de retour ; `approved` + `[critical]` ouvert → bloquant ; aucun verdict structuré → fallback prose. Plus un test d'isolation inter-sessions.
- Tests e2e pipeline et dispatch couvrant le cycle de fix piloté par le verdict structuré.

### Points vérifiés au-delà des critères
- **Pas de verdict périmé entre cycles** : chaque dispatch de review crée une nouvelle ligne `agent_sessions` (`createId()`), y compris sur resume — le resume ne réutilise que l'id de session côté CLI. Un verdict du cycle 1 ne peut pas décider du cycle 2.
- **Aucun parsing de prose résiduel** : les trois sites qui dupliquaient le substring matching (les deux routes de review + `finalizeReviewSession`) délèguent maintenant à `findings.ts`. Le seul endroit qui connaît encore le vocabulaire prose est `NEGATIVE_PROSE_VERDICTS`.
- **Machine à états intacte** : aucune arête touchée. Le merge gate de Full Auto continue de s'appuyer sur les guards du workflow (review terminée + zéro finding ouvert), orthogonal au canal de verdict. `review → done` reste humain.

### Transition
Je ne déplace pas le ticket : une session ne peut pas promouvoir son propre ticket. L'epic et ses trois stories sont en `in_progress`, la transition vers `review` reste à faire par l'orchestrateur en fin de session.
