## 3. Error handling / 9. Blocking finding

**[Major] `hooks/useBoardMerge.ts:53` — the "Ready to merge" section makes two cards mergeable into the same working copy at once, and nothing serializes `mergeWorktree` at the repository level.**

`inFlightRef` is a Set keyed by epic, deliberately: *"the board can have several ready cards and each one merges on its own"* (line 16). Nothing greys out the other Merge buttons, and the server-side lock is per-epic too (`beginMergeWork(projectId, epicId)`, `approve/route.ts:160`). Two ready cards clicked a moment apart run two `mergeWorktree` calls concurrently, and `mergeWorktree` does `git checkout <default>` then `git merge --no-ff` in the **shared main checkout** (`lib/git/manager.ts:422-433`).

I reproduced the git half in a scratch repo rather than assuming it, replaying Arij's exact sequence (checkout → merge → `git merge --abort` on failure):

- one merge lands; the other exits 128 (`Unable to create '.git/index.lock'`, or `update_ref failed for ref 'HEAD'`);
- `--abort` does **not** always clean up — `git status` was left with `D a.txt`, a **staged deletion of the file the winning merge had just landed**, plus `A b.txt` from the aborted merge;
- from there a later `git checkout` refuses (*"Please move or remove them"*) and a later commit in the main checkout carries the staged deletion.

The card-visible consequence needs no corruption at all: the loser throws inside the merge try/catch, so `mergeWorktree` reports `reason: "conflict"` for a branch with no conflict. `approve/route.ts:214` sets `isConflict`, logs `buildApprovalMergeBlockedReason`, the LIKE prefixes match it — and per the *accepted* "no conflict-cleared event" deferral, that `merge_conflict` blocker sticks until a terminal code session runs. One mistimed pair of clicks permanently mislabels a healthy epic as conflicted.

Auto-mode already treats this as an invariant: its merges run under the per-project sweep mutex. The HTTP path has no equivalent.

**Fix:** make the board guard project-wide (one in-flight epic id, other Merge/Resolve buttons disabled while held) and/or take a project-level merge lock in the approve route.

**On fairness:** the missing repo-level lock predates this epic — the ticket-detail Approve, the story Approve and resolve-merge all reach `mergeWorktree` the same way. What's new is that this feature puts N Merge buttons on screen simultaneously, one click apart with no navigation between them, and explicitly opts out of a shared guard to do it. The narrowing also created the mirror gap: an approve-path `conflict-markers` failure now logs a reason matching **no** prefix, so no blocker is persisted at all — the card stays in "Ready to merge" and re-offers **Merge**, failing identically every time with nothing on the card explaining why.

comments.content:
**Forensic diagnostic**
<!-- arij:dead-session=A4081rPCGsU3 -->

**Probable root cause** — The `fix` stage never ran. Both attempts died at the provider layer: the Antigravity/Cloud Code Assist backend returned HTTP 429 `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` for `gemini-3.7-flash-tiered` because the account's individual quota was exhausted, with a reset ~3h44m out. The assistant turn recorded zero input and zero output tokens and terminated ~1.15s after the request, so no file was read, no review finding was addressed, and no commit was attempted. This is an infrastructure/quota failure, not a defect in the ticket, the prompt, or the review findings — the prompt itself (the round-5 review with the `tryLockProjectMerge` hard-park finding) was fully assembled and delivered.

**Evidence**

- Both recorded errors are identical quota rejections, not model or task failures: `"code": 429, "message": "Individual quota reached. Please upgrade your subscription to increase your limits. Resets in 3h43m51s.", "status": "RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED"` with `"model": "gemini-3.7-flash-tiered"`.
- The assistant produced nothing at all — the stream tail shows `"content":[],` ... `"usage":{"input":0,"output":0,"cacheRead":0,"cacheWrite":0,"totalTokens":0}`, `"stopReason":"error"`, `"duration":1152.504699`. The "Last text produced" is just the echoed tail of the prompt file, confirming no model output was generated.
- The retry window makes both attempts futile by construction: `"retryDelay": "13431.877238554s"` and `"quotaResetTimeStamp": "2026-08-26T17:20:09Z"` — the pipeline retried inside a quota window it could not clear, so attempt 2 was guaranteed to reproduce attempt 1.

**Recommended next action**

- Re-dispatch the `fix` stage on a different provider/model that does not draw on the exhausted Antigravity quota (e.g. the `claude` provider, or an `omp` model routed to a non-Google backend), and leave the ticket's findings unchanged — nothing was consumed, so a clean re-run starts from the same state. Longer term, the retry ladder should treat a 429 with `reason: "QUOTA_EXHAUSTED"` and a multi-hour `RetryInfo.retryDelay` as a **provider failover** signal rather than spending both attempts on the same exhausted model; retrying inside a 3h44m reset window can only fail twice.

epics.description: lib/claude/untrusted.ts implements a well-reasoned two-layer defence (neutralizeControlMarkup escapes harness-impersonating tags; fenceUntrusted wraps content in an uncloseable fence under an explicit 'this is data, not instructions' notice). Its module header documents the real incident it exists for: a stored spec ending in a <system-directive> block that instructed sessions to abandon their ticket and rewrite the specification — and review sessions obeyed it. lib/claude/prompt-sections.ts applies fenceUntrusted() correctly to both spec (line 98) and memory (line 116). Every builder in lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts calls specSection(project.spec) EXCEPT buildSpecGenerationPrompt, which at line 334 does `parts.push(section("Current Specification", project.spec))` — raw, unfenced, unneutralized. This was verified empirically by running the real builder against a poisoned spec fixture: neutralized=false, raw markup present=true, untrusted notice=false. This is the worst possible builder to miss, because spec generation is the path that writes a new spec back to the database, making an injected directive self-perpetuating. The root cause is a test gap: __tests__/prompt-untrusted-content.test.ts and __tests__/prompt-sections.test.ts both test the primitives and the section wrappers, but nothing asserts that the ~17 builders actually call them. Separately, chatHistorySection (lib/claude/prompt-sections.ts:66-73) replays message content verbatim while spec, memory, documents, description, and comments are all neutralized.

comments.content:
## Epic livrée — 3 commits sur `feature/epic-qwNtdp9tziQI-cycle-de-vie-des-clones-conflits-reprise`

Suite complète verte : **2496 tests / 257 fichiers**, `tsc --noEmit` propre, ESLint sans erreur ni warning sur les fichiers touchés.

### US 1 — suppression du répertoire d'un clone
`DELETE /api/projects/[projectId]?removeDirectory=true`, honoré seulement si **deux** garde-fous passent : `clone_source = "github"` **et** chemin descendant strict de la racine projets courante. Un refus n'est pas une erreur : le projet est supprimé et la réponse dit quel garde-fou a refusé (`not_managed` / `outside_projects_root` / `missing`).
- `git worktree prune`, puis détachement/suppression des worktrees **enregistrés par git** (pas de devinette sur les noms : les worktrees portent le nom de la branche, pas du dépôt) ; le `.arij-worktrees` partagé n'est jamais supprimé.
- Sessions `queued`/`running` annulées (slot de queue puis process) + activités éphémères, **avec ou sans le flag** — la ligne projet cascade vers `agent_sessions`, un process survivant serait orphelin.
- Nettoyage des clés `<key>:<projectId>` (`agent_max_concurrent`, `webhook_url`, pipeline, night) : la table `settings` n'a pas de FK vers `projects`.

### US 2 — reprise après import interrompu
Classification du répertoire de destination : clone sain du même dépôt → `fetch` seul, `reused: true` ; clone d'un **autre** dépôt → 409, jamais écrasé ; débris d'un run interrompu (`.git` présent, HEAD non né) → remplacé, **pas** signalé comme conflit. Un `arji.json` valide court-circuite toujours le LLM.

### US 3 — provenance visible
Bandeau dans l'en-tête projet : chemin absolu + copie en un clic, badge « Arij-managed clone » et lien source pour `clone_source = "github"`. Les projets fournis par l'utilisateur s'affichent inchangés (le badge suit `clone_source`, pas la présence d'un remote).

comments.content:
Epic delivered — 3 commits, full suite green (2496 tests / 257 files), `tsc --noEmit` clean, ESLint clean on every file I touched.

## What I built

**Story 1 — deletion cleanup.** `DELETE /api/projects/[projectId]?removeDirectory=true`, honoured only when two independent gates both pass: `clone_source = "github"` **and** the path is a strict descendant of the current projects root. A refusal isn't an error — the project is deleted either way and the response reports which gate refused. Removal runs `git worktree prune`, then detaches and deletes the worktrees **git has registered** for that clone (worktrees are named after the branch, not the repo, so guessing directory names would hit the wrong clone), then the clone. The shared `.arij-worktrees` is never removed. Sessions and ephemeral activities are cancelled on every delete, and per-project settings rows are swept — `settings` has no FK to `projects`, so they'd otherwise be inherited by a later project reusing the id.

**Story 2 — resume.** Destination classification decides between three outcomes: healthy clone of the same repo → fetch only, `reused: true`; clone of a *different* repo → 409, never overwritten; debris from an interrupted run (`.git` present, HEAD unborn) → replaced, not reported as a conflict. A valid `arji.json` still short-circuits the LLM.

**Story 3 — provenance.** Header strip with the absolute path, one-click copy, and an "Arij-managed clone" badge plus source link. The badge keys off `clone_source`, not the presence of a remote, so a user's own checkout of a GitHub repo isn't mislabelled.

The guard tests run against real git repositories in temp dirs — the story is about which directories vanish from disk, and a mocked `simple-git` can't show that. They cover symlink-escape, root-itself, and shared-prefix cases. One real defect surfaced and was fixed along the way: `simpleGit()` throws *synchronously* from its factory on a missing directory, which sat outside the guarded blocks in `detectDefaultBranch`.

## One thing you need to decide

This epic depends on a clone foundation that **isn't on `main`** — it's being built right now on four sibling branches. I implemented it so this branch compiles and tests standalone, which means `0027_project_clone_source.sql`, `lib/projects/workspace*.ts`, `lib/git/clone.ts` and `parseGitHubRepoInput` exist here *and* on those branches.

Worth knowing before you plan the merge: **the sibling branches already conflict with each other** independently of me. `epic-drG2ZnRFKHeC` adds `0027_git_sync_log_nullable_project.sql` claiming the same journal `idx: 26` as `epic-UY7xsxcNN41T`'s `0027_project_clone_source.sql`. One of them needs renumbering regardless of what happens to my branch.

Recommended order: foundation → parsing → clone service → this one, keeping the sibling implementations for foundation files and taking only `lib/projects/{clone-cleanup,cancel-sessions,project-settings-keys}.ts`, the `DELETE` handler, `ProjectSourceBadge.tsx` and the seven `__tests__/clone-lifecycle-*` files from here. Their nullable `git_sync_log.project_id` is a better fix than my workaround (console-log the clone when no project row exists yet) — prefer theirs.

comments.content:
**Code Review**

# Code Review Report

## Findings

### 1. Critical — Pre-existing directories can be recursively deleted

**Location:** [lib/git/clone.ts:156](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-qwNtdp9tziQI-cycle-de-vie-des-clones-conflits-reprise/lib/git/clone.ts:156)

**Description:** Any non-empty destination without a readable origin is classified as `partial_clone`, including arbitrary directories, files, and valid local repositories without remotes. It is then recursively deleted before cloning. The tests currently codify this unsafe behavior.

**Recommendation:** Treat every existing destination as a conflict unless it is positively identified as the expected clone or carries a trusted Arij-created marker. Only clean up directories created by the current clone attempt.

### 2. Major — Concurrent clone requests can delete each other’s result

**Location:** [lib/git/clone.ts:273](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-qwNtdp9tziQI-cycle-de-vie-des-clones-conflits-reprise/lib/git/clone.ts:273)

**Description:** Classification, cloning, and cleanup are not serialized. Two requests can both observe an absent destination; when one clone subsequently fails because the other created it, its error handler deletes the shared destination.

**Recommendation:** Add a per-destination lock covering classification through completion. Cleanup must only remove a directory proven to have been created by that invocation.

### 3. Major — Clone ownership is client-writable

**Location:** [app/api/projects/[projectId]/route.ts:60](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-qwNtdp9tziQI-cycle-de-vie-des-clones-conflits-reprise/app/api/projects/[projectId]/route.ts:60)

**Description:** The generic PATCH route can set `cloneSource` to `"github"`, while deletion trusts that value as proof of ownership. A user-supplied project inside the projects root can therefore be reclassified and recursively removed. The generic creation route similarly trusts client-supplied provenance.

**Recommendation:** Make provenance immutable through PATCH and establish it through a trusted server-side clone handoff or durable pending-clone record.

### 4. Major — Cleanup can delete non-Arij worktrees

**Location:** [lib/projects/clone-cleanup.ts:158](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-qwNtdp9tziQI-cycle-de-vie-des-clones-conflits-reprise/lib/projects/clone-cleanup.ts:158)

**Description:** Registered worktrees are deleted whenever they are anywhere beneath `projectsRoot`. The acceptance criterion limits removal to the clone’s `.arij-worktrees` entries. A manually created worktree elsewhere under the root, including uncommitted work, would be force-removed.

**Recommendation:** Require strict containment under the shared `.arij-worktrees` directory before either `git worktree remove` or `fs.rm`.

### 5. Major — First-time clones are not written to `git_sync_log`

**Location:** [app/api/projects/clone/route.ts:144](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-qwNtdp9tziQI-cycle-de-vie-des-clones-conflits-reprise/app/api/projects/clone/route.ts:144)

**Description:** A normal import has no project ID yet, so the function returns without creating an audit row. Consequently, almost every first-time clone and clone failure violates the requirement that each clone be recorded.

**Recommendation:** Make `git_sync_log.project_id` nullable and log pre-project operations with `NULL`, as already anticipated in the merge guidance.

### 6. Major — Persisted default branch is never consumed

**Location:** [lib/git/clone.ts:331](/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-qwNtdp9tziQI-cycle-de-vie-des-clones-conflits-reprise/lib/git/clone.ts:331)

**Description:** `defaultBranch` is detected and stored, but no production code reads it. `lib/git/manager.ts` still guesses only `main` or `master`, so repositories using branches such as `develop` will clone successfully but fail during worktree creation or merging.

**Recommendation:** Thread the persisted branch through worktree, merge, and release operations, retaining the old guess only for legacy rows.

## Checklist Assessment

1. **Readability:** No additional issues found.
2. **DRY Principle:** No issues found.
3. **Error Handling:** Findings 1, 2, and 5.
4. **Performance:** No issues found.
5. **Naming Conventions:** No issues found.
6. **Type Safety:** No issues found.
7. **Testing:** Tests are extensive, but currently assert the unsafe behavior in Finding 1 and omit concurrent cloning, manually placed worktrees, and non-`main` default-branch integration.
8. **API Design:** Findings 3 and 5.

## Verification

- TypeScript: passed.
- Targeted ESLint: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Targeted Vitest execution was blocked before collection because the read-only environment prevented Vitest from creating its temporary directory.
- Arij’s structured findings endpoint was invoked, but the connector required approval while this session’s approval policy was `never`; the findings could not be persisted to the ticket.

## Summary

- Critical: 1
- Major: 5
- Minor: 0
- Suggestions: 0

The findings apply to the current checkout. Some overlapping clone-service code may be replaced during the documented sibling-branch merge, but the resolved tree requires another review before approval.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

comments.content:
The epic itself was already implemented; the actual work was the **Changes Requested** review — 1 critical and 5 major findings. All six are fixed in `cae1682`, suite green at 2525 tests / 259 files, typecheck clean.

**The critical finding and the ownership finding were one bug.** Nothing on disk distinguished a clone Arij made from a directory that merely sat where Arij would have put one — classification guessed from `origin`, and `clone_source` (the flag authorising deletion) was a column any PATCH could set. Both now rest on a fact: `.git/arij-clone.json`, written by the clone service into repositories it creates. Inside `.git` deliberately — git never shows it, it can't be committed, and it dies with the repo it vouches for.

For the critical one I didn't just fix the classification. Downloads now run into a staging sibling and land with a single `rename`, so the destination is never observably half-cloned and the whole detect-and-delete-the-debris path is gone. A failed clone can only delete its own staging directory. That also satisfies the story's "interrupted clone is reused, not a conflict" criterion by construction rather than by heuristic.

The rest: a per-destination lock (in-process by design — one local server, and a lock file would add stale-lock recovery to solve a case that can't occur here); provenance derived server-side and absent from both request schemas, with a managed clone's path frozen; worktree cleanup confined to `.arij-worktrees`; `git_sync_log.project_id` nullable via hand-written `0028`; and `resolveBaseBranch` replacing the `main`/`master` guess across all 14 call sites.

Two things worth your attention:

- **The default-branch fix reaches further than the finding did.** `resolveBaseBranch` consults `origin/HEAD`, so `develop`-based repositories now work for *user-supplied* projects too — those never had a recorded branch to read, and were equally broken.
- **Three tests asserted the unsafe behaviour** and now assert the refusal instead. I kept a separate `arij_debris` case so the safe replace path stays pinned. Updating a test to match new behaviour is worth a second look from you, since it's exactly the move that can hide a regression.

The merge caveat from the earlier session is unchanged and still the main risk: this branch carries a clone foundation that isn't on `main`, and two sibling branches still both claim journal `idx: 26` independently of anything I did. Ticket is back in review.

epics.title: Docs : scan du projet pour importer automatiquement les documents (pdf/md/doc/docx…)
epics.description:
## Contexte

La partie **Docs** d'Arij permet d'attacher des documents au projet (utilisés par ex. dans le contexte des sessions agents, cf. E-arij-008). Aujourd'hui, il faut les ajouter un à un manuellement.

Il faut ajouter la possibilité de **scanner le projet** pour récupérer automatiquement tous les fichiers documents (`.pdf`, `.md`, `.doc`, `.docx`, et autres formats lisibles au besoin) et de **demander à l'utilisateur** lesquels il veut rendre accessibles via Arij.

## Comportement souhaité

1. Bouton **« Scanner le projet »** dans la vue Docs.
2. Le scan parcours le répertoire du projet et liste tous les fichiers documents détectés (nom, chemin, taille).
3. L'utilisateur coche les documents qu'il veut importer → confirmation → ils deviennent des documents accessibles via Arij, au même titre que les docs ajoutés manuellement.
4. Les docs déjà importés sont détectés et ne sont **pas dupliqués** au rescan.

## Questions ouvertes

- Formats pris en charge : au minimum pdf/md/doc/docx — on inclut aussi txt/rtf/html ?
- En cas de rescan sur un fichier modifié depuis son import : on met à jour la version Arij, on propose, ou on ignore ?
- Plafond de taille fichier ou de nombre de fichiers à importer (les docs partent dans les prompts agents, cf. E-arij-008) ?
- Ignorer certains répertoires (node_modules, .git, builds) — oui, évidemment, à documenter.

No extra wiring was needed and none is missing.

## 1. Readability — No blocking issues

The code is unusually well-commented, and the comments explain *why* rather than *what* (the iterative-walk rationale at `lib/documents/scan.ts:42`, the symlink policy at `:27`, the `« conserver et signaler »` decision at `ScanProjectDialog.tsx:149`). Open questions from the epic are answered in code with their reasoning attached.

## 2. DRY

**Minor — `app/api/projects/[projectId]/documents/import/route.ts:60`**
Lines 60-74 duplicate `scan/route.ts:20-34` verbatim: stat the repo path, 400 on missing, 400 on not-a-directory.
*Recommendation:* extract `getProjectDirectoryOr400` alongside `getProjectOr404` in `lib/api/route-helpers.ts`.

**Info — `lib/documents/import.ts:90`**
`MIME_BY_EXTENSION` and `DOCUMENT_SCAN_EXTENSIONS` are independent literals that can drift — and the epic explicitly floats adding `.rtf`/`.html`. Adding one to the scanner alone leaves `mimeType` `undefined` at runtime (typed `string`, so the `?? null` is dead code today), surfacing as `Unsupported file type "null"` to the user. ## 3. Error Handling

**Minor — `lib/documents/import.ts:163`**
The bare `catch` around the insert labels *every* failure `"Déjà importé."`. SQLITE_BUSY, disk-full or a future constraint violation all reach the user as a confidently wrong statement.
*Recommendation:* match the error on `UNIQUE`/`SQLITE_CONSTRAINT` and fall through to a generic reason otherwise.

**Minor — `lib/documents/import.ts:94`**
`statSync`/`readFileSync` follow symlinks that `scanProjectDocuments` deliberately refuses (`lib/documents/scan.ts:66`, reason spelled out in its doc comment). The lexical `..`/prefix guard on lines 68-77 does not catch `docs/link-to-outside/passwd`. To be fair on threat model: not reachable from the dialog (the scan never lists a symlink), and cross-origin POST is preflight-blocked — this is defense-in-depth and honoring the module's own documented invariant, not a live hole.
*Recommendation:* `fs.realpathSync` the resolved path and re-check the root prefix, or `lstatSync` and skip.

**Info — `lib/documents/import.ts:62`** — empty/blank paths `continue` with no `skipped` entry, so `imported.length + skipped.length` silently fails to reconcile with the request.

Otherwise the error posture is consistent and good: per-entry failures never abort either the walk or the batch, and every skip carries an actionable reason.

## 4. Performance

**Info — `lib/documents/import.ts:59`** — up to 100 files of up to 20 MB are read and converted **sequentially and synchronously** inside one request; PDF conversion is the slow path. This blocks the Node event loop for the whole orchestrator, and the dialog shows only a spinner. Defensible for a local-first app and the cap is documented, but worth an explicit note.

**Info — `lib/documents/scan.ts:47`** — `truncated` is a false positive when the repo holds exactly 500 documents: after the 500th push, any still-unvisited directory makes the next `while` iteration set the flag even though nothing was dropped.

The per-file duplicate `SELECT` is not an N+1 concern — bounded at 100 and served by the `LOWER(original_filename)` expression index from migration 0014.

## 5. Naming Conventions — No issues found

## 6. Type Safety — No issues found

No `any`. `getProjectOr404`'s `requireGitRepo: true` overload is used correctly to narrow `gitRepoPath` to `string`. The one cast (`relativePaths as string[]`, import route line 80) follows a real runtime validation.

**Info — `lib/documents/import.ts:124` vs `ScanProjectDialog.tsx:135`** — the two dedup layers claim to mirror each other but diverge for non-ASCII: SQLite's `LOWER()` is ASCII-only, JS `toLowerCase()` is Unicode-aware. `RÉSUMÉ.pdf` on disk against `résumé.pdf` in the DB is marked « déjà importé » client-side while the server and the unique index would accept it.

## 7. Testing

**Minor — `lib/documents/scan.ts:37`**
`scanProjectDocuments` has **no test**, and neither does the scan route. Story 1's acceptance criteria are entirely about this walker — ignores `.git`/`node_modules`/`dist`, reports errors clearly — and none of it is asserted anywhere; the ignore list, symlink policy, `truncated` flag and `errors` array are all unverified. It is the only new module without coverage.
*Recommendation:* add `__tests__/documents-scan.test.ts` against a real temp tree, mirroring `documents-import-route.test.ts`.

The two tests that do exist are strong — real filesystem, real components, minimal mocking, and they cover the genuinely tricky cases (path escape, same-basename collision within a batch, imports landing between two scans).

## 8. API Design

Envelope contract (`{ data }` / `{ error }`) and status codes follow `lib/api/route-helpers.ts` correctly. `POST` for a read-only scan is defensible and has precedent in `POST /api/projects/import`.

**Minor — `documents/import/route.ts:49`** — error strings mix French ("Aucun fichier sélectionné.", "Trop de fichiers") with English ("Invalid JSON body.", "relativePaths must be an array of strings."). The sibling upload route is English throughout, and `scan.ts` emits English while `import.ts` emits French — both land in the same dialog. Pick one language for the API layer.

## 9. UX correctness

**Minor — `components/documents/ScanProjectDialog.tsx:307`**
`.doc` rows are listed, selectable, and swept in by « Tout sélectionner » — but `lib/documents/import.ts:84` refuses every one of them. The default happy path (select-all → import) therefore always produces skip noise on any repo holding a legacy `.doc`, and the dialog description at line 257 advertises `doc` as supported.
*Recommendation:* mark `.doc` rows unsupported and non-selectable up front, or drop it from `DOCUMENT_SCAN_EXTENSIONS`.

**Minor — `components/documents/ScanProjectDialog.tsx:155`**
`missingSources` matches on basename only, so every manually-uploaded document with no repo counterpart is permanently reported as "ne correspond à aucun fichier du dépôt". The comment acknowledges this, but it makes the orphan signal noise for any project mixing upload and scan. There is no provenance on `documents` to tell the two apart; a `source`/`source_path` column would make the signal mean what Story 4 asks.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 0 |
| Minor | 6 |
| Suggestion / Info | 6 |

Solid work: the walk is iterative and bounded, path traversal is guarded and tested, dedup matches the existing unique index, one bad file never aborts a batch, and the epic's four open questions are each answered in code with the reasoning recorded. The two things I'd actually fix before merge are the untested scan walker (Story 1's entire AC surface) and the `.doc` extensions being offered but never importable. Nothing here blocks.

**Overall Verdict: Approved with Minor Issues**

epics.title: Enforce MCP toolset segregation on the server rather than in the shim
epics.description: Toolset selection currently happens in bin/arij-mcp.mjs:67 and :709, driven by the ARIJ_MCP_TOOLSET environment variable — client-side code the agent process controls. Server-side, enforcement is asymmetric. Agent-only routes correctly reject chat tokens: create-bug, attach-artifact, submit-findings, ask-question, submit-grading, and report-friction all check `auth.agentType === "chat"` and return 403. But the chat-only board routes (start-build, create-ticket, update-ticket, list-tickets, get-agent-status) all route through createBoardToolRouteHandler in lib/mcp/board-tool-route.ts:53, which calls requireMcpToken(request) and performs no agentType check at all. The token is trivially reachable by the agent: lib/claude/mcp-injection.ts:257 places it in the child's own environment as ARIJ_MCP_TOKEN (the 0700 temp-file config correctly keeps it off the process table, but a process can always read its own env). Any build or review session with shell access can curl /api/mcp/start-build and dispatch agents — a capability outside its declared toolset. This compounds with the prompt-injection epic: injected spec markup could drive an agent to call start_build, spawning a new session that reads the same poisoned spec. The test suite confirms the gap is unintentional — __tests__/mcp-chat-routes.test.ts:427 has `describe("agent-only routes — chat tokens are rejected")` with three cases, but no converse suite exists because no converse check exists.

epics.title: When starting a QA job, docs are automatically sent to the prompt, it shouldn't
Grader : évaluation structurée des critères d'acceptation (Outcomes)
epics.description:
## Contexte
Les `acceptanceCriteria` des user stories sont injectés dans les prompts de build et de review, mais personne ne les évalue jamais un par un. Motif « Outcomes » des Claude Managed Agents (Code with Claude 2026) : un agent évaluateur note le travail contre une rubrique, et le producteur itère jusqu'à satisfaire les critères. Ici la rubrique existe déjà : ce sont les critères d'acceptation.

## À construire
1. **Outil MCP `submit_grading`** (nouveau, toolset agent) : payload `{ gradings: [{ storyId, criterion, status: met|partial|missed, evidence }], summary }`. Route `app/api/mcp/submit-grading/route.ts` sur le modèle de `submit_findings` (auth par token, scope epic, erreurs lisibles par l'agent). Persistance : table `grading_reports` (migration SQL manuscrite + `_journal.json`).
2. **Agent grader** : agentType `grading`, session en mode plan sur le worktree, prompt `buildGradingPrompt` — reçoit les user stories et leurs critères, examine le diff/le worktree, et DOIT appeler submit_grading. Distinct du reviewer : le grader ne juge pas la qualité du code, uniquement « chaque critère est-il satisfait, avec quelle preuve ». Ségrégation de provider souhaitable (réutiliser la logique de `lib/agent-config/review-segregation.ts`).
3. **Déclenchement** : bouton manuel sur le ticket (comme les reviews) + option pipeline `pipeline_grader_enabled` (tri-state, défaut OFF) : s'exécute après verify (si présent) et avant review ; un critère `missed` → fix cycle avec les critères manqués et leurs evidence injectés dans le prompt de fix.
4. **UI** : dans le détail du ticket, badge par critère sur chaque user story (met/partial/missed, evidence au survol) et état agrégé sur la carte kanban.

## Contraintes
- Le grading n'introduit AUCUNE nouvelle transition : il alimente les fix cycles existants et l'affichage ; `review → done` reste humain (cf. `docs/architecture/ticket-state-machine.md`).
- Epic sans user stories ou sans critères → grader sauté (no-op journalisé), jamais un échec.
- Intégrer l'agentType `grading` aux constantes/enums (watchdog, classification) comme pour les autres types.
- Tests vitest : route MCP (validation payload, scope token, storyId hors epic rejeté), câblage pipeline (missed → fix, all met → continue, sans stories → skip), section Arij tools des prompts à jour.

comments.content:
**Code Review**

# Code Review — Grader: évaluation structurée des critères d'acceptation (Outcomes)

**Scope reviewed:** `269e399..7e75278` (3 commits, 62 files, +2972/−99) — MCP tool + persistence, plan-mode grader agent, pipeline wiring and UI badges.

---

## 1. Readability

Strong. Every new module opens with a doc comment that states the *invariant*, not just the mechanism — `submit-grading/route.ts:1-8` explains why story validation precedes the atomic insert, `runner.ts:678-679` explains why grading success is keyed to the exact report id, and `report.ts:1-7` states the "malformed row must never green-light a pipeline" contract. `RUNNING_STATE_BY_STAGE` and `PIPELINE_REASONS` keep the new stage symmetrical with the existing ones.

One readability nit: `lib/pipeline/runner.ts:228-238` now carries two consecutive `/** ... */` blocks for the single `parkRejectedTicket` field (the first, describing the regression-gate use, was left orphaned when the second was added). Harmless, but a reader hits a doc comment that documents nothing.

## 2. DRY Principle

Good reuse throughout: `dispatchGradingSession` is a single implementation shared by the manual route and the pipeline stage (per the project's "manual and automatic paths share one effectful function" convention); provider segregation reuses `pickAlternativeReviewProvider` / `resolveAgentForDispatch` rather than cloning it; `parseAcceptanceCriteria` is shared by prompt display and badge matching.

**Minor — `lib/pipeline/constants.ts:115`** — `resolvePipelineGraderEnabledDefault` is dead code. Its sibling `resolvePipelineEnabledDefault` exists because `AgentActionsBar.tsx:204` needs a client-side effective value for the pipeline checkbox; the grader has no client-side consumer, and the only references to this function in the repository are in `__tests__/pipeline-settings-section.test.tsx`. **Recommendation:** delete the function (and its test), or wire it into the dispatch dialog if the grader is meant to be visible there.

## 3. Error Handling

Well covered. The `settled` promises never reject; the scheduler safety net is correctly relied on for the throw path in `dispatch.ts:384-395`; `assessGrading` throwing is routed into the retry ladder rather than green-lighting; `parkRejectedTicket` calls are individually try/caught so they cannot change how the run terminates. `GradingDispatchError` carrying `status`/`code`/`payload` keeps the route thin without losing the 409 conflict contract.

**Major — `lib/grading/dispatch.ts:333`** — a grading session that ends with `asked_question` is silently swallowed. The terminal block classifies the outcome, computes `success = false` (no report was filed), and calls `emitSessionFailed`. But `createNotificationFromSession` (`lib/notifications/create.ts:299`) *deliberately returns early* for `outcome === "asked_question"`, because that notification is owned by `createAskedQuestionNotificationFromSession`, invoked only through `handleAskedQuestionOutcome`. The grading dispatcher never calls it. The terminal hook (`terminal-notification.ts:32`) hits the same early return.

Net effect: the grader asks the user something → **no notification at all** (neither the question flavour nor the generic failure one) and no held-status activity entry. In the pipeline this is worse than cosmetic: `runner.ts:544-548` returns `paused_question` on the strength of an explicit comment — *"the stage closure already held the ticket, notified, and logged via handleAskedQuestionOutcome"* — which is true for `finalizeReviewSession` (`stages.ts:954`) and `finalizeBuildTerminalOutcome`, and false for grading. The run stops and the only trace is the pipeline activity line. `mcp__arij__ask_question` is in the agent allowlist, so the grader can reach it.

**Recommendation:** in the terminal block, mirror the review stage:
```ts
if (outcome === "asked_question") {
  handleAskedQuestionOutcome({
    projectId: input.projectId,
    epicIds: [input.epicId],
    sessionId,
    ticketStatus: gradingTarget.status ?? "review",
  });
}
```
and add a dispatch test for it — `__tests__/grading-agent-dispatch.test.ts` currently has no `asked_question` case.

**Minor — `app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/[epicId]/grading/route.ts:36`** — a malformed stored report returns HTTP 500. `report.ts:1-7` states the opposite contract ("must render as ungraded"). The client happens to degrade correctly (`useEpicDetail.ts:64` gates on `gradingRes.ok`), so the symptom is only a spurious server error in the network log — but the status code asserts a server fault for what is a data condition. **Recommendation:** return `{ data: null }` (200) and log, matching how `epics/route.ts` handles the same row via `parseGradingEntries` → `null`.

## 4. Performance

The board query is handled well — one `ROW_NUMBER()` subquery joined once, backed by the new `(epic_id, created_at)` index, rather than a per-epic lookup.

**Minor — `lib/grading/report.ts:97` / `EpicUserStoriesSection.tsx:144`** — `findCriterionGrading` re-normalizes every report entry for every criterion, on every render. `normalizeCriterion` is a split + three regex replaces + a lowercase, and the lookup is `O(criteria × entries)`. A 6-story epic with 5 criteria each and a 30-entry report is ~900 normalizations per render, and the detail panel re-renders on a 5 s poll *and* on every project SSE event. **Recommendation:** build the normalized index once per report — `useMemo(() => new Map(gradings.map(g => [`${g.storyId}|${normalizeCriterion(g.criterion)}`, g])), [gradingReport])` — and look up by key.

**Minor — `components/kanban/EpicDetail.tsx:229`** — `if (refreshTrigger > 0) void refresh()` fires three fetches (full epics list + user stories + grading report) on *every* project-scoped SSE event, including `ticket:updated` / `session:started` for unrelated tickets, on top of the existing 5 s poll. The stated goal ("grader completion arrives as `session:completed`") is narrower than the trigger. **Recommendation:** either accept it explicitly in the comment, or have the board pass an epic-scoped trigger so unrelated events don't refetch an open panel.

**Suggestion — `app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/route.ts:202`** — `gradingSummary` (up to 4000 chars) is now returned for every epic on every board load, solely to fill the card tooltip. On a large board that is a meaningful payload increase for a hover affordance; consider truncating server-side.

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found. `grading` as an agent type, `GRADING_AGENT_TYPE`, `PIPELINE_GRADER_ENABLED_SETTING_KEY`, `gradingReports`/`grading_reports`, `buildGradingPrompt`, `GradingStatusBadge` — all consistent with their neighbours. The `grader`(setting)/`grading`(agent type) split reads as intentional and matches the epic's wording.

## 6. Type Safety

No `any`. `GradingStatus` is derived from the `GRADING_STATUSES` tuple and shared by the Zod enum, the DB parse path, and the UI; `DispatchGradingResult` is a discriminated union on `skipped`, so the route cannot read `sessionId` off a skip. `PromptGradingStory extends PromptUserStory` with a required `id` correctly encodes what `submit_grading` needs. `parseGradingEntries` narrows `unknown` through a real type guard rather than a cast.

## 7. Testing

Genuinely good coverage of the contracts the epic named: strict status enum, unknown-key rejection at both levels, mixed-scope `STORY_NOT_IN_EPIC` with a no-partial-write assertion, `ticket_id` rejection, OFF-by-default pipeline flow, `verify → grading → review` ordering, missed → fix with criterion+evidence threading, rubric-free skip, watchdog classification, and the Arij-tools prompt section.

Gaps worth closing:

- **`asked_question` on a grading session** (see §3) — untested, and the missing behaviour is precisely what a test would have caught.
- **Grading-stage failure paths** — `__tests__/pipeline-grading.test.ts` only exercises successful graders. There is no test for the retry ladder on a grader that fails, for `assessGrading` throwing (malformed report → `handleStageFailure`), or for `missed` with `fixCycles >= maxFixCycles` → `parkRejectedTicket` + `failed`. That last one is a user-visible terminal state with a board side effect.
- **Story-scoped grading in the pipeline** — `dispatchPipelineGradingStage` passes `userStoryId` for story runs, but only epic-scoped dispatch is covered.

## 8. API Design

`{ data }` / `{ error }` shape is respected, `STORY_NOT_IN_EPIC` is agent-readable and names the offending id, and the 409 conflict reuses `createAgentAlreadyRunningPayload` so the client's existing `isAgentAlreadyRunningError` handling works unchanged. Validation order (auth → chat rejection → body → ticket scope) mirrors `submit-findings` exactly, as the epic required.

**Minor — `lib/claude/mcp-injection.ts:51-58`** — `submit_grading` is added to `ARIJ_MCP_ALLOWED_TOOL_NAMES`, i.e. every agent session gets it, and the route only rejects `agentType === "chat"`. A `build` or `ticket_build` session can therefore file a grading report on its own epic, and that report becomes the epic's latest — it drives the Kanban aggregate badge and the per-criterion badges. The pipeline is safe (`assessGrading` matches on `agentSessionId`), so this is a display-integrity issue, not a gate bypass. It also directly undercuts the Outcomes premise that the evaluator is independent of the producer. The epic text does say "toolset agent", so this may be deliberate — but the tool description already says "(Grading sessions)". **Recommendation:** if independence is intended, gate the route on `auth.agentType === "grading"` (one line, mirrors the existing chat guard); if not, drop "(Grading sessions)" from the description.

**Suggestion — `app/api/mcp/submit-grading/route.ts:97`** — unlike `submit_findings`, no ticket comment mirrors the summary into the activity feed. After a manual "Grade Criteria" run the only durable user-visible output is a badge tooltip; the feed shows nothing. A one-line summary comment would make manual grading auditable the way reviews are.

**Suggestion — `lib/pipeline/stages.ts:262`** — `dispatchPipelineGradingStage` ignores `request.attempt` and `previousAttemptSessionId`, so the grading stage has no resume-on-attempt-2 and no escalate-on-attempt-3, and always reports `escalatedToProvider: null`. Consequence: a grader on a weaker CLI that never calls `submit_grading` burns the full ladder on the *same* provider, triggers a forensic, and **fails the whole run before review ever executes** — for a stage the module header calls "intentionally observational". Either route grading through `resolveStageAgent`'s ladder, or degrade a grader-infrastructure failure to "skip grading, continue to review" and keep hard failure for `missed` criteria only.

**Suggestion — `components/kanban/EpicCard.tsx:381`** — the aggregate badge has no relation to the code state it graded. A report survives subsequent builds and merges, so a card can show "Criteria met" over code that changed afterwards. `gradingCreatedAt` is already selected, joined, and typed in `KanbanEpic` — but never rendered. Comparing it against the epic's latest code session (or just showing the age in the tooltip) would make the signal honest.

**Suggestion — session budget** — enabling the grader adds one session per cycle against the fixed `PIPELINE_MAX_SESSIONS_PER_RUN = 12`, and missed criteria consume the *same* `maxFixCycles` budget as review findings. With the defaults a grading-driven fix can leave zero budget for blocking review findings, turning a previously-fixable review into an immediate terminal failure. Worth stating in the settings copy (which currently mentions the shared budget but not that it can starve the review stage).

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 1 |
| Minor | 6 |
| Suggestion | 5 |

This is careful, well-tested work that honours the epic's hard constraints: no new transitions, `review → done` untouched, rubric-free epics are journalled no-ops rather than failures, the setting is genuinely OFF by default and the OFF path is proven byte-identical to the previous flow, the migration is hand-written with a monotonic journal entry, and `grading` is threaded through the constants, watchdog, classification, monitor and session views. The one Major finding — silent `asked_question` handling — is a narrow, well-localized gap with an obvious three-line fix and an existing pattern to copy; the rest are polish.

*Note: findings are reported here as prose rather than filed through `submit_findings`, because this session is running under plan mode, which forbids state-changing tool calls.*

**Overall Verdict: Approved with Minor Issues**

epics.title: Bound API payloads and eliminate unbounded query patterns
epics.description: Two routes select unbounded, unprojected rows against a 489 MB database, and because better-sqlite3 is synchronous on one shared memoized connection (lib/db/index.ts:56-61), either request blocks the entire Node event loop — all other API requests, all SSE heartbeats (app/api/projects/[projectId]/events/route.ts:40), and the Full Auto sweep. This makes them global availability problems, not per-request latency problems. (1) app/api/projects/[projectId]/sessions/route.ts:23-27 does `db.select().from(agentSessions).where(...).all()` with no column projection, no limit, no pagination. Measured against the live database: the Arij project returns ~37.8 MB, of which 37.5 MB is the `prompt` column — and the Sessions list page (app/projects/[projectId]/sessions/page.tsx) never references `.prompt`. The adjacent chatConversations query in the same handler is exemplary by contrast, using projected columns and correlated subqueries. (2) app/api/projects/[projectId]/sessions/[sessionId]/route.ts:66-68 returns the full session row including prompt, the entire logs.json parsed into memory, and all three chunk streams via listSessionChunks (which has no LIMIT). Worst measured session: 51.95 MB; 19 of 528 sessions already exceed 5 MB. (3) lib/sync/export.ts:13-70 is an N+1: one epics query, then per-epic a stories query and a comments query, then per-story another comments query — roughly 752 queries for 158 epics and 435 stories — producing a 3.7 MB arji.json rewrite, fired fire-and-forget on every board mutation. (4) Core tables carry only their primary-key autoindex: epics, user_stories, agent_sessions, ticket_comments, projects, releases, git_sync_log, conversations, and messages have no secondary indexes, so every project- or epic-scoped lookup is a full table scan. Newer tables (frictions, grading_reports, session_artifacts, ticket_dependencies, agent_session_chunks) are well-indexed — the discipline arrived after the core tables were built.

## What I did

**Route** (`app/api/projects/[projectId]/sessions/route.ts`): replaced `db.select()` with an explicit projection, and added `?limit=` (default 200, clamped 1–1000) + opaque `?cursor=` keyset pagination returning `nextCursor`. ## Measured against the live board (dev server on a DB copy, project `u1HcvrXnpuvm`)

| | bytes | time |
|---|---|---|
| before | 42,756,192 (40.8 MB) | 1.17 s |
| after, default page | 192,391 (0.18 MB) | 0.28 s |
| after, whole list in one request | 310,323 (0.30 MB) | 0.08 s |

- `coalesce(created_at, '')` on both sides of the keyset — `created_at` is nullable, and a keyset comparing NULL directly drops legacy rows from every page after the first.
- The JS tiebreaker is byte-wise, not `localeCompare`, so it matches SQLite's BINARY collation on mixed-case nanoids. This is a small deliberate change to the existing sort; without it, rows at a same-second page boundary get duplicated or skipped.

## What I found

The ticket's substance had already landed in `71b7548` (a prior session). What remained was an unfinished fix in the working tree, which I completed, corrected, and committed as `199bfd3`.

## The defect

The "oversized chunk is shown in part" notice never cleared. The server sets `contentTruncated` on *every* slice of a split chunk — including the last one — so walking an 8.3 MB chunk to its end with "Load more" left the warning on screen permanently, telling the reader output was missing when the pane held all of it.

The in-flight fix made the count reach-based and per-chunk, which is the right shape. But it compared `chunk.content.length` — UTF-16 units — against `contentLength`, which the server derives from SQLite `length()`, counting code points. `lib/agent-sessions/chunks.ts` already had a `countCharacters` helper written specifically for this hazard; the client didn't use it. Four emoji measure 8 against a stored length of 6, so the notice clears while part of the chunk is genuinely unread — and agent output carries emoji routinely.

I moved `countCharacters` into `lib/agent-sessions/session-detail.ts`, the module both ends already share, and deleted the private copy in `chunks.ts`. The two sides can't drift apart on that rule again.

- **`listSessionChunks` callers unchanged** — verified byte-identical to the merge-base, not just eyeballed.

### The defect fixed this session

The "oversized chunk is shown in part" notice never cleared. The server sets `contentTruncated` on **every** slice of a split chunk — including the last — so walking an 8.3 MB chunk to its end with "Load more" left the warning up, telling the reader output was missing when the pane held all of it.

The count is now per chunk and reach-based: slices of one sequence fold together, and a chunk counts only while its furthest reach is short of the stored `contentLength`.

Reach is measured in **code points, not UTF-16 units**. `contentLength`/`contentOffset` both come from SQLite `length()`/`substr()`, which count code points; a JS `.length` is larger for anything astral, and agent output carries emoji routinely — four emoji measure 8 against a stored length of 6, clearing the notice while part of the chunk is genuinely unread. `countCharacters` moved into `lib/agent-sessions/session-detail.ts` (the module both ends already share) so the two sides cannot drift apart on it again; `chunks.ts` dropped its private copy. The reverse import is type-only, so there is no runtime cycle.

Confirmed by mutation: reverting the predicate to `chunk.content.length` fails the new emoji test **and nothing else** — that case was previously uncovered.

`npm test` 482 files / 5927 tests green · `tsc --noEmit` clean · `next build` clean (with `NODE_ENV` unset — the inherited `development` from the dev server produces a false prerender error) · eslint reports nothing in the touched files (the 71 repo-wide problems are pre-existing, in files outside this diff).

`collectArijActions()` still reads the whole raw stream through the unbounded `listSessionChunks` — ~500 ms for the 112 MB session, the dominant residual in handler time. This ticket asks explicitly for that caller to stay unchanged, so it does.

## All six review findings addressed — commit `4802b4d`

Full suite green (**487 files / 5967 tests**), `tsc --noEmit` clean, ESLint clean on every touched file. Each fix is mutation-checked: reverting it fails the test written for it.

### [major] Detail route still scanned the whole raw stream (`route.ts:302`)

Confirmed and quantified on a copy of the live DB. Replaying what `collectArijActions()` did per poll on session `ZZAP6QWzM-Ss` (3,015 rows / 112.7 MB): **287 ms SELECT + 326 ms parse ≈ 610 ms of blocked event loop, every 3 seconds.**

The combined payload now carries the **durable half only** (`collectDurableArijActions()` — three indexed reads, zero chunk content). The supplement moved to `?view=arij-actions`, a **resumable bounded** scan: ≤ 2 MiB of raw stream per call, cursor + partial-line carry cached per session, so a poll only covers what was appended since.

The carry is why the scan is stateful rather than "read N chunks and parse": page boundaries land mid-line routinely, and a stateless pass over each page would parse two halves and find nothing. Tested, plus a test that the tentative parse of an unterminated tail is never counted twice.

Measured after, same session: detail poll **10–27 ms** / 79,755 B; the full 112.7 MB scan takes 55 background calls of ~40–60 ms (3.3 s); every later poll **6–7 ms** with zero re-read.

The instrumentation test asserts the handler's **actual chunk reads**: `listSessionChunks` called **0** times, `listSessionChunkPage` exactly 3 (the previews), content read ≤ 3 × 64 KiB, against a seeded 3 MB raw stream. Reverting fails it at `wholeStreamCalls 1 ≠ 0`.

### [major] List bounded rows but not bytes (`sessions/route.ts:45`)

- `error` → `substr(error, 1, 400)` + `length(error)`, ellipsis appended only when the stored value really was longer (no spurious `…` at exactly the cap — tested).
- `last_non_empty_text` → reduced **in SQL** to `producedOutput`, the boolean that was the list's only consumer of it (`selectLatestFailures`). The text never leaves the database.

Worth a reviewer's eye: SQLite's one-argument `trim()` strips **spaces only**, where the JS `.trim()` it replaces stripped all whitespace — a last line of a bare newline would have flipped to "spoke". So the set is explicit: `trim(x, char(32,9,10,13,11,12))`.

New `sessions-list-response-budget.test.ts` (real sqlite): 20 sessions each with a 4 MB output line *and* a 4 MB error (~160 MB unprojected) → **< 1 MB**; the finding's one-row case → **< 64 KiB**; the badge still resolves end to end. Restoring either column fails 4 of the 5.

### [major] `arji.json` comment order under MULTI-INDEX OR (`export.ts:72`)

Reproduced exactly: `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` confirms `MULTI-INDEX OR`, and the legacy story query gives `[c-story-only, c-dual]` where the batched one bucketed `[c-dual, c-story-only]`.

Both batched queries now `ORDER BY rowid` — the insertion order a per-parent `WHERE fk = ?` returned under either plan. Added the requested fixture (earlier story-only + later dual-key), asserted on bucket order *and* byte-identity against the legacy oracle already in that file, with a vacuity guard on the plan. Removing the `ORDER BY` fails it with the reviewer's exact `[dual, story-only]`.

I ordered the **stories** query by rowid too: safe today, but relying on the plan for the same reason, with the stable position sort on top of it.

### [minor] Chunk page batch materialisation (`chunks.ts:429`)

Batch size now derives from the remaining byte budget (`ceil(remaining / maxChunkBytes)`). The new test instruments what SQLite *hands back*: 64 chunks at the 256 KiB cap materialise **≤ 1.3 M characters**; the mutation back to the row ceiling reports **16,777,216** — the reviewer's 16 MB to the byte. A companion test pins that an ordinary stream (120 × 5.5 KB) still returns as one full page.

Cost, stated plainly: at the default budget this asks for 4 rows at a time, so a full page of average chunks takes a few dozen small indexed queries instead of four large ones. Copying the page's content dominates either way.

### [minor] Served-logs ceiling counted UTF-16 units (`route.ts:122`)

Now `Buffer.byteLength(..., "utf8")`. Fixture is a legacy array-shaped log of 300,000 CJK characters — under 512 KiB by `.length`, ~900 KB on the wire — asserted from both sides so it cannot go stale, plus a test that a multibyte log which *fits* still comes through whole.

### [minor] `fetchUnifiedSessions` treated 25 pages as success (`session-list.ts:56`)

Replaced by cursor-cycle detection: a repeated cursor throws `UnifiedSessionListIncompleteError` (carrying `partialRowCount`) instead of returning a prefix. The page ceiling stays as a runaway backstop at 10,000 and also throws. The Sessions page renders a visible `sessions-incomplete` notice rather than silently showing truncated totals; the other two callers already discarded on rejection. New contract test: >25 pages (400 rows at limit 10) returns everything; a stuck cursor rejects after 2 requests.

### Renders identically

Against the real board on a DB copy: **415 rows, same set and same order as the route serves**, unchanged under the last-activity sort toggle, error column populated, no page errors, no incomplete banner. The detail page's action list contains `get_ticket` — the lazy endpoint really does populate the chunk-derived half in the browser, not just in tests.

`retry-resume-agent.test.ts` moved off `lastNonEmptyText` to the flag replacing it, and the "whitespace-only is not output" case it owned moved to `sessions-list-response-budget.test.ts` where the trim now happens. Noted because that coverage changed files rather than disappearing.

## Constat

`hooks/useGitHubConfig.ts:41-43` teste :

```ts
typeof settingsData.data?.github_pat === "string" && settingsData.data.github_pat.length > 0
```

mais `GET /api/settings` masque cette clé en `{ hasToken: boolean }` (`app/api/settings/route.ts:23-36`). - Test unitaire du hook avec la forme masquée `{hasToken: true}` / `{hasToken: false}` / clé absente.

## Contexte

Découvert pendant l'étude SSO GitHub (2026-08-28). L'epic « Connecter GitHub via OAuth Device Flow » dépend de ce fix : son UI settings s'appuie sur ce hook pour afficher l'état de connexion.

comments.content:
**Revue traitée** — 5 constats sur 5 corrigés (commit `7f6f448`). Suite verte : `npm test` 2730 tests / 263 fichiers, `npm run test:e2e` 12 tests, `tsc --noEmit` propre.

| # | Constat | Traitement |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fetch de réutilisation non authentifié | corrigé |
| 2 | Fuite des métadonnées de clone vers un import local | corrigé |
| 3 | Propriété du clone décidée par le client | corrigé |
| 4 | Branche par défaut non utilisée | corrigé (voir réserve) |
| 5 | Points consécutifs refusés à tort | corrigé |

**1 — fetch authentifié et borné.** Le PAT est volontairement absent de `.git/config`, donc `fetchGitRemote()` sur le chemin de réutilisation partait sans identifiant : pour un dépôt privé, git demandait des identifiants sans terminal attaché — un blocage, pas une erreur. Le constructeur `-c http.extraHeader` est désormais partagé avec le clone, et le fetch porte le même timeout et `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`.

**2 — provenance liée à l'analyse.** `clone` survivait à une prévisualisation annulée, à une analyse en échec et au retour vers « Local folder ». La provenance voyage maintenant avec le résultat d'analyse et n'est posée que pour la prévisualisation à laquelle elle appartient. Trois tests de non-régression couvrent les trois chemins, plus la contre-épreuve que le cas GitHub légitime enregistre toujours sa provenance.

**3 — propriété vérifiée côté serveur.** `POST /api/projects` recalcule `<projects_root>/<owner>-<repo>` et refuse le drapeau pour tout autre chemin ; `gitRemoteUrl` est ré-analysée (une URL porteuse d'identifiants ne parse pas), stockée normalisée, et la cohérence owner/repo est vérifiée. `defaultBranch` est validée au niveau du schéma contre les formes que git refuse dans une réf.

**4 — branche par défaut.** `resolveRemoteDefaultBranch()` (`origin/HEAD`) est partagée par le service de clone, `manager.ts` et `release.ts` ; la convention `main`/`master` ne sert plus que de repli quand il n'y a pas de distant à interroger. La réponse du distant n'est retenue que si la branche existe localement — `main` seul ne résout pas `refs/remotes/origin/main`, on échangerait un échec contre un autre. Le clone rapporte cette branche plutôt que celle qui se trouve extraite dans un clone réutilisé.

⚠️ **Réserve assumée** : je n'ai pas étendu le transport authentifié à `pushGitBranch()` / `pullGitBranchWithConflictSupport()` / au tag de release, comme le suggérait la recommandation du constat 1. Ces fonctions préexistent à l'import et le débordement touchait l'orchestration git de toute l'application, hors périmètre d'un epic tests+doc. All five review findings are fixed and the ticket is back in review (commit `7f6f448`).

## What the findings actually were

**Three were real defects in code this epic authored:**

- **Reuse fetch had no credentials, timeout, or prompt suppression.** Because the PAT is deliberately kept out of `.git/config`, the fetch on the reuse path was unauthenticated — a private-repo re-import blocked on a credential prompt with no terminal attached, which is a hang rather than an error. - **Clone provenance leaked between imports.** `clone` state survived a cancelled preview, a failed analysis, and a switch back to "Local folder", so the next local import was created carrying the previous repo's `cloneSource`/owner/remote/branch. Provenance now travels with the analysis result.

**One was a pre-existing bug the import surfaced:** `createWorktree`/`mergeWorktree` guessed `main`-else-`master`, so a `trunk` or `develop` repo imported cleanly and then failed at `worktree add`. All call sites now resolve `origin/HEAD` through a shared helper.

**I found a second instance of finding 5.** Fixing the parser to accept `repo..archive` (legal on GitHub; the character class already excludes separators) exposed that `validatePath()` rejected *any* `..` substring — so a clone the parser had just accepted would have failed at import. **I deliberately did not do part of finding 1.** The reviewer recommended a credential-aware transport for push, pull, and tag as well. Those functions predate the import flow and rewiring them touches the whole app's git orchestration — well outside a tests-and-docs epic, with real regression risk. I fixed the reuse fetch, which is the path this epic owns, and documented the remainder as a "Known gap" in `docs/architecture/github-import.md`: a private repo imported this way needs a credential helper to push. comments.content:
**Forensic diagnostic**

**Probable root cause** — The `build` stage never started: `spawn E2BIG` is the kernel's `execve()` "argument list too long" error, surfaced by Node before the child process exists. Arij's Codex provider passes the entire prompt as a single `argv` element (`lib/providers/codex.ts:181`, `args.push(prompt)`), plus a `-c developer_instructions=<JSON>` argument. Linux caps *one* argv string at 128 KiB (`MAX_ARG_STRLEN`) and the whole argv+env block at ~2 MB. The build prompt for this ticket is assembled by concatenation with no size guard — ticket body, all comments, review context, fix instructions, mention enrichment and the Arij tools section (`lib/pipeline/stages.ts:476-552`, `lib/claude/process-manager.ts:135`) — and grows further on each retry. For a docs-and-tests ticket on the GitHub import (which typically carries long pasted diffs/logs in comments), that pushed a single argument past the limit. This is deterministic, not transient, which is exactly why both attempts failed identically.

**Evidence**

- `spawn E2BIG` — Node emits this string only when `execve` fails with `E2BIG`; the failure is at process creation, not inside the build.
- "Raw stream (tail): (none)", "Output stream (tail): (none)", "Last text produced: (none)" — no stdout/stderr at all, confirming the Codex CLI never ran. A build failure or model error would have produced output.
- `lib/providers/codex.ts:181` `args.push(prompt)` combined with `stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"]` (`lib/providers/base-provider.ts:~397`) — stdin is closed, so the prompt can only travel via argv; there is no length check anywhere (`grep -rn "E2BIG\|prompt.length" lib/` returns only logging).

**Recommended next action**

- Re-dispatch this ticket on the `claude` provider (which overrides `spawn()` and does not pass the prompt as a Codex-style argv element), and in parallel have a human trim the ticket's accumulated comments/review context — the oversized inputs are the trigger. The durable fix, once someone picks it up: pass the Codex prompt over stdin or a temp file instead of `argv`, and add a hard prompt-size guard in `lib/pipeline/stages.ts` so this fails with a readable message instead of `E2BIG`.

epics.title: Multi-Provider CLI Integration with Base Class Refactor
epics.description:
Add 6 new CLI providers (Mistral Vibe, Qwen Code, OpenCode, DeepSeek, Kimi/Moonshot, Zai) and refactor the provider layer with a BaseCliProvider abstract class to reduce duplication. Updates the provider registry, named agents UI, and availability checks to support all 9 providers.

New providers:
- Mistral Vibe (`vibe`): --prompt, --agent, --output json, --resume, --max-turns, --max-price
- Qwen Code (`qwen`): -p, --yolo, --model, /resume
- OpenCode (`opencode`): run "...", --format json, --session, --file
- DeepSeek (`deepseek`): -q, --model, --no-stream, SQLite history
- Kimi/Moonshot (`kimi`): --print, --continue, stream-json
- Zai/Zhipu AI (`zai`): API-based via subprocess wrapper, GLM models

Architecture: BaseCliProvider abstract class handles 70% of shared spawn/kill/log/parse logic. Each provider is ~80-120 lines. Existing Claude Code, Codex, Gemini refactored onto base class first.

user_stories.title: As a developer, I want a BaseCliProvider abstract class so that adding new CLI providers requires minimal boilerplate
user_stories.description:
Create lib/providers/base-provider.ts with an abstract class that encapsulates the shared provider lifecycle: child_process.spawn with stdio piping, stdout/stderr buffer collection, SIGTERM then SIGKILL kill logic, session ID extraction via extractCliSessionIdFromOutput, NDJSON session logging, endedWithQuestion detection, duration tracking, display command building, and exit code to success/error mapping.

Abstract methods for subclasses:
- get binaryName(): string
- buildArgs(options: ProviderSpawnOptions): string[]
- extractResult(stdout: string, stderr: string): string
- Optional overrides: parseSessionId(), isAvailable(), buildEnv()

Also support chunk callbacks (onRawChunk, onOutputChunk, onResponseChunk) in the base for providers that stream.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] BaseCliProvider class exists in lib/providers/base-provider.ts
- [ ] Handles spawn, collect, kill, log, extract session ID, detect questions
- [ ] Supports optional chunk callbacks for streaming providers
- [ ] Abstract methods: binaryName, buildArgs, extractResult
- [ ] Default isAvailable() checks `which <binaryName>

user_stories.title: As a developer, I want existing providers refactored onto BaseCliProvider so that the abstraction is proven before adding new providers
user_stories.description:
Refactor ClaudeCodeProvider, CodexProvider, and GeminiCliProvider to extend BaseCliProvider. Each should only implement buildArgs(), extractResult(), and any provider-specific overrides (e.g., Codex overrides isAvailable() for login check, Codex uses temp file output capture). The spawn logic in lib/claude/spawn.ts, lib/codex/spawn.ts, and lib/gemini/spawn.ts should be consolidated where possible.

All existing tests and behavior must remain identical after refactoring.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:

- [ ] CodexProvider extends BaseCliProvider
- [ ] GeminiCliProvider extends BaseCliProvider
- [ ] All existing provider behavior unchanged
- [ ] Spawn files simplified to delegate to base class
- [ ] No regression in session resume, chunk streaming, or kill logic

user_stories.description: Update lib/agent-config/constants.ts to add new provider types: 'mistral-vibe' | 'qwen-code' | 'opencode' | 'deepseek' | 'kimi' | 'zai'. user_stories.title: As a user, I want to use Zai (Zhipu AI) as an agent provider so that I can leverage GLM-4 models with hybrid reasoning
user_stories.description:
Implement ZaiProvider extending BaseCliProvider.

Zai is API-based (no native CLI binary). Implementation wraps LiteLLM or a thin subprocess call to a bundled Python script that calls the Zai API.

CLI wrapper: `python -m arji_zai_bridge --prompt <PROMPT> --model <zai/glm-4.7> --api-key <from env>`

Alternatively, if a `zai` CLI exists at runtime, use it directly. The provider should check for both.
Mode mapping: all modes pass prompt to API. No permission system.
Resume: not supported (stateless API calls).
Output: JSON response from API.
Availability: check for ZHIPU_API_KEY env var OR `which zai`.

39:export function useAgentPolling(projectId: string, intervalMs = 3000, refreshTrigger?: number) {
40:  const [activities, setActivities] = useState<UnifiedActivity[]>([]);

43:  const poll = useCallback(async () => {
44:    try {
45:      const [activeRes, allRes] = await Promise.all([
46:        fetch(`/api/projects/${projectId}/sessions/active`),
47:        fetch(`/api/projects/${projectId}/sessions`),
48:      ]);
49:      const activeData = await activeRes.json();
50:      setActivities(activeData.data || []);
51:
52:      const allData = await allRes.json();
53:      const sessions = allData.data || [];
54:
55:      // Build a set of epicIds that currently have a running agent
56:      const runningEpicIds = new Set<string>(
57:        ((activeData.data || []) as UnifiedActivity[])
58:          .filter((a) => a.epicId)
59:          .map((a) => a.epicId as string)
60:      );
61:
62:      // "Latest session wins": the badge reflects only the most recent
63:      // session per epic, so a retry clears the failure immediately.
64:      const failed = selectLatestFailures(sessions, runningEpicIds);
65:      setFailedSessions(failed);
66:    } catch {
67:      // ignore
68:    }
69:  }, [projectId]);
70:
71:  usePolling(poll, intervalMs);
72:
73:  // Immediate re-poll when SSE triggers a refresh
74:  useEffect(() => {
75:    if (!refreshTrigger) return;
76:    const timeout = window.setTimeout(() => void poll(), 0);
77:    return () => window.clearTimeout(timeout);
78:  }, [refreshTrigger, poll]);
79:
80:  return { activities, failedSessions, refresh: poll };
81:}

1:/**
2: * "Latest session wins" failure indicator for epic cards.
3: *
4: * A retry creates a NEW agent_sessions row and statuses are terminal
5: * (ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS.failed = [] in lifecycle.ts), so an old failed row
6: * stays in the database forever. The badge must therefore reflect only the
7: * most recent session of an epic: a queued/running/completed retry clears
8: * it immediately, and it never comes back unless that retry fails too.
9: *
10: * created_at is a SQLite CURRENT_TIMESTAMP (second precision). When the
11: * newest timestamp is shared by several sessions — e.g. a retry created in
12: * the same second as the failure it replaces — ties break in favor of
13: * CLEARING the badge. Within an all-failed tie group, the session that
14: * ended most recently wins so the badge shows the retry's error.
15: */
16:
17:export interface FailedSessionInfo {
18:  sessionId: string;
19:  error: string;
20:  agentType: string;
21:}
22:
23:/** Minimal shape of a unified session row as returned by /api/projects/:id/sessions. */
24:export interface FailureCandidateSession {
25:  id: string;
26:  kind: string;
27:  status: string;
28:  epicId?: string | null;
29:  error?: string | null;
30:  agentType?: string | null;
31:  createdAt?: string | null;
32:  endedAt?: string | null;
33:}
34:
35:export function selectLatestFailures(
36:  sessions: FailureCandidateSession[],
37:  runningEpicIds: Set<string>
38:): Record<string, FailedSessionInfo> {
39:  const byEpic = new Map<string, FailureCandidateSession[]>();
40:  for (const session of sessions) {
41:    if (session.kind !== "agent_session") continue;
42:    if (!session.epicId) continue;
43:    const list = byEpic.get(session.epicId);
44:    if (list) list.push(session);
45:    else byEpic.set(session.epicId, [session]);
46:  }
47:
48:  const failed: Record<string, FailedSessionInfo> = {};
49:  for (const [epicId, epicSessions] of byEpic) {
50:    // Registry-only active agents have no DB row yet; never badge those epics.
51:    if (runningEpicIds.has(epicId)) continue;
52:
53:    let newest = "";
54:    for (const s of epicSessions) {
55:      if ((s.createdAt ?? "") > newest) newest = s.createdAt ?? "";
56:    }
57:    const newestGroup = epicSessions.filter((s) => (s.createdAt ?? "") === newest);
58:
59:    // Same-second tie with any non-failed session → clear the badge.
60:    if (newestGroup.some((s) => s.status !== "failed")) continue;
61:
62:    // All-failed tie: prefer the session that ended most recently.
63:    let latest = newestGroup[0];
64:    for (const s of newestGroup) {
65:      if ((s.endedAt ?? "") > (latest.endedAt ?? "")) latest = s;
66:    }
67:    failed[epicId] = {
68:      sessionId: latest.id,
69:      error: latest.error || "Unknown error",
70:      agentType: latest.agentType || "build",
71:    };
72:  }
73:  return failed;
74:}

/**
 * "Latest session wins" failure indicator for epic cards.
 *
 * A retry creates a NEW agent_sessions row and statuses are terminal
 * (ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS.failed = [] in lifecycle.ts), so an old failed row
 * stays in the database forever. The badge must therefore reflect only the
 * most recent session of an epic: a queued/running/completed retry clears
 * it immediately, and it never comes back unless that retry fails too.
 *
 * created_at is a SQLite CURRENT_TIMESTAMP (second precision). When the
 * newest timestamp is shared by several sessions — e.g. a retry created in
 * the same second as the failure it replaces — ties break in favor of
 * CLEARING the badge. Within an all-failed tie group, the session that
 * ended most recently wins so the badge shows the retry's error.
 */

export interface FailedSessionInfo {
  sessionId: string;
  error: string;
  agentType: string;
}

/** Minimal shape of a unified session row as returned by /api/projects/:id/sessions. */
export interface FailureCandidateSession {
  id: string;
  kind: string;
  status: string;
  epicId?: string | null;
  error?: string | null;
  agentType?: string | null;
  createdAt?: string | null;
  endedAt?: string | null;
}

export function selectLatestFailures(
  sessions: FailureCandidateSession[],
  runningEpicIds: Set<string>
): Record<string, FailedSessionInfo> {
  const byEpic = new Map<string, FailureCandidateSession[]>();
  for (const session of sessions) {
    if (session.kind !== "agent_session") continue;
    if (!session.epicId) continue;
    const list = byEpic.get(session.epicId);
    if (list) list.push(session);
    else byEpic.set(session.epicId, [session]);
  }

  const failed: Record<string, FailedSessionInfo> = {};
  for (const [epicId, epicSessions] of byEpic) {
    // Registry-only active agents have no DB row yet; never badge those epics.
    if (runningEpicIds.has(epicId)) continue;

    let newest = "";
    for (const s of epicSessions) {
      if ((s.createdAt ?? "") > newest) newest = s.createdAt ?? "";
    }
    const newestGroup = epicSessions.filter((s) => (s.createdAt ?? "") === newest);

    // Same-second tie with any non-failed session → clear the badge.
    if (newestGroup.some((s) => s.status !== "failed")) continue;

    // All-failed tie: prefer the session that ended most recently.
    let latest = newestGroup[0];
    for (const s of newestGroup) {
      if ((s.endedAt ?? "") > (latest.endedAt ?? "")) latest = s;
    }
    failed[epicId] = {
      sessionId: latest.id,
      error: latest.error || "Unknown error",
      agentType: latest.agentType || "build",
    };
  }
  return failed;
}

  for (const [epicId, epicSessions] of byEpic) {
    // Registry-only active agents have no DB row yet; never badge those epics.
    if (runningEpicIds.has(epicId)) continue;

    let newest = "";
    for (const s of epicSessions) {
      if ((s.createdAt ?? "") > newest) newest = s.createdAt ?? "";
    }
    const newestGroup = epicSessions.filter((s) => (s.createdAt ?? "") === newest);

    // Same-second tie with any non-failed session → clear the badge.
    if (newestGroup.some((s) => s.status !== "failed")) continue;

    // All-failed tie: prefer the session that ended most recently.
    let latest = newestGroup[0];
    for (const s of newestGroup) {
      if ((s.endedAt ?? "") > (latest.endedAt ?? "")) latest = s;
    }
    failed[epicId] = {
      sessionId: latest.id,
      error: latest.error || "Unknown error",
      agentType: latest.agentType || "build",
    };
  }
  return failed;
}

/**
 * "Latest session wins" failure indicator for epic cards.
 *
 * A retry creates a NEW agent_sessions row and statuses are terminal
 * (ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS.failed = [] in lifecycle.ts), so an old failed row
 * stays in the database forever. The badge must therefore reflect only the
 * most recent session of an epic: a queued/running/completed retry clears
 * it immediately, and it never comes back unless that retry fails too.
 *
 * created_at is a SQLite CURRENT_TIMESTAMP (second precision). When the
 * newest timestamp is shared by several sessions — e.g. a retry created in
 * the same second as the failure it replaces — ties break in favor of
 * CLEARING the badge. Within an all-failed tie group, the session that
 * ended most recently wins so the badge shows the retry's error.
 */

export interface FailedSessionInfo {
  sessionId: string;
  error: string;
  agentType: string;
  provider?: string | null;
  namedAgentId?: string | null;
}

/** Minimal shape of a unified session row as returned by /api/projects/:id/sessions. */
export interface FailureCandidateSession {
  id: string;
  kind: string;
  status: string;
  epicId?: string | null;
  error?: string | null;
  agentType?: string | null;
  provider?: string | null;
  namedAgentId?: string | null;
  createdAt?: string | null;
  endedAt?: string | null;
}
export function selectLatestFailures(
  sessions: FailureCandidateSession[],
  runningEpicIds: Set<string>
): Record<string, FailedSessionInfo> {
  const byEpic = new Map<string, FailureCandidateSession[]>();
  for (const session of sessions) {
    if (session.kind !== "agent_session") continue;
    if (!session.epicId) continue;
    const list = byEpic.get(session.epicId);
    if (list) list.push(session);
    else byEpic.set(session.epicId, [session]);
  }

  const failed: Record<string, FailedSessionInfo> = {};
  for (const [epicId, epicSessions] of byEpic) {
    // Registry-only active agents have no DB row yet; never badge those epics.
    if (runningEpicIds.has(epicId)) continue;

    let newest = "";
    for (const s of epicSessions) {
      if ((s.createdAt ?? "") > newest) newest = s.createdAt ?? "";
    }
    const newestGroup = epicSessions.filter((s) => (s.createdAt ?? "") === newest);

    // Same-second tie with any non-failed session → clear the badge.
    failed[epicId] = {
      sessionId: latest.id,
      error: latest.error || "Unknown error",
      agentType: latest.agentType || "build",
      provider: (latest.provider as string | null) ?? null,
      namedAgentId: (latest.namedAgentId as string | null) ?? null,
    };
  }
  return failed;
}
