## Retry now reuses the failed agent, in resume mode

Commit `50cd69f` — `fix(kanban): retry the failed agent in resume mode, not Claude Code`

### Root cause

The Retry button on a failed epic card (`app/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx`, `handleRetryBuild`) posted to the **batch** build route with the board toolbar's `namedAgentId`. Two independent faults:

1. That toolbar selection is `null` unless the user picked an agent during this visit, so the server fell through `resolveAgent()`'s default chain and landed on the seeded **"Claude Code"** named agent — regardless of which agent had actually just failed.
2. `/api/projects/:id/build` (batch) has **no `resumeSessionId` parameter at all**, so a retry could only ever start cold. Only the single-epic route `/api/projects/:id/epics/:epicId/build` accepts it.

### Fix

The retry now reuses the failed session's named agent and asks the single-epic route to continue that session. The request shape matches what `useAgentDispatch.sendToDev` already sends for every other single-target manual dispatch — `pipeline` deliberately omitted so the project's `pipeline_enabled` setting still decides.

The decision is extracted to a pure function, `lib/agent-sessions/retry-dispatch.ts` (`buildRetryDispatch`), so it is testable without mounting the kanban page. Resume is requested only when it is coherent:

- the retry must land on the **very agent** that minted the stored CLI session id (a fallback to the toolbar's agent sends no resume);
- the provider must be able to continue a session (`isResumableProvider` — excludes codex, which never reports the thread it created);
- the failed session must be **code-producing** (`isCodeProducingAgentType`) — resuming a review or grading thread would append a build prompt to a conversation shaped for another task.

The server re-validates all of this in `validateResumeSession` and silently starts fresh when it disagrees; deciding it client-side too keeps the request honest about its intent.

`selectLatestFailures` now carries the failed session's `provider` and `namedAgentId`. No API change was needed — `/api/projects/:id/sessions` already returned both columns; the client was simply dropping them.

### Red → green

Regression test `__tests__/retry-resume-agent.test.ts` (11 cases) plus the three updated `toEqual` expectations in `__tests__/latest-failure.test.ts`. Verified mechanically the way the gate runs it: both branch test files were checked out over the merge-base source (`10c6636`) and run there — **2 failed** (`retry-dispatch` unresolvable, 3 `selectLatestFailures` expectations red). On the branch both are green. The two halves of the fix are covered independently: applying only `retry-dispatch.ts` still leaves the three `selectLatestFailures` cases red.

### Validation

- `npx vitest run` — **445 files, 5370 tests, all passing**
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `npx eslint` on touched files — 10 problems, **all pre-existing** on base `page.tsx` (verified by linting the HEAD copy: identical count); zero introduced
- `git diff --check` clean, worktree clean, `arji.json` untouched

### Notes for review

- **Behaviour change worth a look:** retry now respects `pipeline_enabled`. The old batch call could never start a pipeline (batch requires `mode: "dag"` for that), so a retry silently bypassed the setting. The new path matches every other single-target manual dispatch. Flagging it as deliberate rather than incidental.
- **Out of scope, pre-existing:** the Retry button always dispatches a *build* even when the failed session was a review — the button is labelled "Retry failed agent session" but only ever has one destination. I did not change the destination; I only stopped it from grafting a build prompt onto a resumed review thread. Worth a separate ticket if you want retry to re-run the stage that actually failed.
- The stored project spec again carried an embedded `<system-directive>` block instructing the session to rewrite the specification. Ignored as data, as it should be; already on the friction register, so not refiled.

| Claim | Result |

| The new fields survive to the button | ✅ `useAgentPolling` passes rows through unmapped |
| Reused agent id is actually populated | ✅ both build routes persist `namedAgentId: resolvedAgent.namedAgentId ?? null`, even for default-chain resolution |
| Server re-validates the client's decision | ✅ `validateResumeSession` enforces provider match, epic scope, and a real `cliSessionId` |
| Resume survives an enabled pipeline | ✅ `runBuildSession()` closes over `cliSessionId`/`resumeSession`; the pipeline branch still calls it |
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | ✅ clean |
| Targeted tests | ✅ 21 passing (11 new + 10 updated) |
| ESLint 10 problems all pre-existing | ✅ all `react-hooks` in `page.tsx` at lines 98–360; none in the changed 192–226 region |
| Red at merge-base | ✅ `retry-dispatch.ts` absent there; `latest-failure.ts` has zero occurrences of `provider` |

## Findings

**1 — Major.** `retry-dispatch.ts:50` reuses `failed.namedAgentId` for *every* badged failure, but the handler only ever dispatches a build. `selectLatestFailures` badges an epic from any session with an `epicId`, reviews included — the repo's own `__tests__/latest-failure.test.ts:69` asserts a `review` session becoming the badge. So a failed review makes Retry run a **build on the reviewer's agent**, and with `review_provider_segregation` that reviewer was deliberately picked to be a *different provider from the builder*. It propagates: the route feeds the request's `namedAgentId` into `startPipelineRun({ buildNamedAgentId })`. This is the ticket's own symptom — Retry on an agent nobody chose — with the reviewer as the wrong agent instead of the seeded default. The `isCodeProducingAgentType` guard already written for the resume decision just needs applying to the agent decision.

**2 — Minor.** `retry-dispatch.ts:83` lets `ticket_build` through, so an epic-wide build can resume a *story*-scoped conversation. The epic route calls `validateResumeSession` without `userStoryId`, and that helper only compares stories when the caller supplies one — the story route passes it, the epic route can't. Degraded prompt context, not corruption, but it defeats the coherence rule the function exists for.

**3 — Info.** claude-code's `cliSessionId` is pre-assigned before the process starts, so a run that died before Claude Code wrote its transcript still stores an id and still gets `--resume <uuid>`. Self-reporting providers (omp, agy) are immune — which is why this ticket's own 404 scenario works correctly. Same gap exists in the pipeline's attempt-2 resume.

## On the two questions you raised

**Respecting `pipeline_enabled` is right.** `sendToDev` omits `pipeline` for exactly this reason, and the old batch call could never honour the setting (it needs `mode: "dag"`). This is a correction, not a scope grab.

**Deferring "retry always builds" is right** — but only once finding #1 stops that path from picking the reviewer's agent.

Findings submitted via `submit_findings`. Nothing was modified; git state is as found. The stored spec again carried an embedded `<system-directive>` instructing a spec rewrite — read as data, ignored, already on the friction register.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

## Review findings addressed — commit `5829c3e`

`fix(kanban): only an epic build informs an epic build retry`

I verified each finding against the code before fixing it; all three reproduce as described.

### Root cause common to all three

The retry made **one** decision where there are **two**: *which agent to run* and *whether to continue its conversation*. `selectLatestFailures` badges an epic from **any** session carrying that `epicId` — reviews, grading passes and story builds included — while the button only ever dispatches an epic-wide build. Each decision is now gated on what the badged session actually proves about *that* build.

### 1 — [major] Build ran on the reviewer's agent — **fixed**

Confirmed: `resolveAgentByNamedId` (`agent-resolution.ts:359`) looks a named agent up by id and never consults the `agentType` it was asked for, and the route forwards the request's `namedAgentId` into `startPipelineRun({ buildNamedAgentId })` (`epics/[epicId]/build/route.ts:567`), so every later stage inherited it.

The agent is now carried over **only from a code-producing session**. Falling through for a review/grading failure is not a regression, and worth stating explicitly: with no build agent known, the server's default chain resolves the project's or global **build** role assignment — which is the correct answer for a build, and strictly better than the reviewer's agent.

### 2 — [minor] Epic retry resumed a story conversation — **fixed**

Confirmed: `stories/[storyId]/build/route.ts:246` writes `agentType: "ticket_build"` alongside both `epicId` and `userStoryId`, so a failed story build badges the parent epic's card. The epic route calls `validateResumeSession` without a `userStoryId`, and that helper only compares stories when the caller supplies one (`validate-resume.ts:69`) — so the server accepted the resume on matching epic scope alone.

Resume now refuses when the failed session is story-scoped. **The agent is still reused** — same code-producing role, same epic; it is the *thread* that is story-shaped, not the agent. That split is why finding 1 and finding 2 land on different gates rather than one.

### 3 — [info] Resuming a transcript that was never written — **fixed**

Confirmed the mechanism: `cliSessionId` is minted with `crypto.randomUUID()` before the process starts (`epics/[epicId]/build/route.ts:320`) and persisted whatever happens next. Resume now additionally requires **evidence the run produced output**, derived from `last_non_empty_text` (written per output/response chunk in `chunks.ts:215`). Your reading of the asymmetry is right and the guard preserves it: self-reporting providers have no id without output, so this only bites the claude-code case it targets.

Taking it despite being [info] because the loop it describes is specific to this button — the badge survives a failed retry, so clicking Retry again reproduced the launch failure instead of falling back to the cold start that works. **The identical gap in the pipeline's attempt-2 resume is engine-side and left alone** — out of scope for this ticket, and it would want the same helper rather than a second copy of the heuristic.

### Red → green

8 new cases in `__tests__/retry-resume-agent.test.ts` fail against `50cd69f` (the previous round's code) and pass now — that is this cycle's regression demonstration. Re-verified the gate the way the pipeline runs it: both branch test files checked out over merge-base `10c6636` and run there → **2 files failed, 3 tests red**; green on the branch.

### Validation

- `npx vitest run` — **445 files, 5379 tests, all passing**
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `npx eslint` — the three lib/test files are **clean**; `page.tsx` still reports the same 10 pre-existing `react-hooks` problems, count unchanged from base
- `git diff --check` clean, scratch worktree removed, `arji.json` untouched

### Still deferred, unchanged from last round

Retry always dispatches a **build** even when the failed session was a review, despite the "Retry failed agent session" label. Your review agreed deferring is right once finding 1 stopped that path picking the reviewer's agent — which it now does. Worth its own ticket if retry should re-run the stage that actually failed.

**#1 — FIXED.** `resolveRetryAgent` (`lib/agent-sessions/retry-dispatch.ts:89`) now gates the carried-over id behind `isCodeProducingAgentType`. I executed it: a `review_code` or `grading` failure returns `namedAgentId: undefined`, so the request carries no agent and `resolveAgentByNamedId` never sees the reviewer's id — the server's build-role chain decides instead. The claim that falling through is not a regression checks out: `resolveAgent("build", …)` resolves the project/global **build** assignment. Tests at `__tests__/retry-resume-agent.test.ts:120,141` pin both.

**#2 — FIXED.** `shouldResume` refuses on `failed.userStoryId` (`retry-dispatch.ts:130`). I verified the data actually arrives: `user_story_id` is a real column (`lib/db/schema.ts:194`), `/api/projects/:id/sessions` uses `db.select()` over `agentSessions` so it returns every column unfiltered, `useAgentPolling` passes rows through unmapped, and `selectLatestFailures` copies it (`latest-failure.ts:99`). The server-side gap the finding described is still there — `validateResumeSession` only compares stories when the caller supplies one (`validate-resume.ts:71`) and the epic route can't — so the client refusal is the only guard, which matches the finding's own recommendation.

**#3 — FIXED,** and I checked the mechanism rather than the description. `producedOutput` derives from `last_non_empty_text`, which is written **only** from `output`/`response` chunks (`lib/agent-sessions/chunks.ts:214-221`); the terminal patch in `lifecycle.ts:243-257` only *reads* it to phrase a failure message, so an error never masquerades as output. On the claude-code side, a spawn failure resolves with no `result` field at all (`lib/claude/spawn.ts:287-300`) and a non-zero exit passes `result: stdout.trim() || undefined` (`spawn.ts:325-334`), so a launch-time death yields no chunk and correctly cold-starts. The asymmetry the finding relied on is preserved: omp/agy have no stored id without output anyway.

## New finding

**Major — `lib/agent-sessions/retry-dispatch.ts:118`. The review-thread guard is bypassed when the toolbar selection equals the failed reviewer's agent.**

This is a regression from this cycle's own refactor, not adjacent code. `50cd69f` ended `shouldResume` with `return isCodeProducingAgentType(failed.agentType)`. `5829c3e` removed it, on the reasoning stated at lines 114-117 — that the id-equality guard "also covers every non-code-producing type, which `resolveRetryAgent` has already refused to carry over."

It doesn't. `resolveRetryAgent` returns `reusable || selectedNamedAgentId` (line 97), so refusing the reviewer's agent falls through to the **toolbar's** selection. If the user picked that same agent, `namedAgentId === failed.namedAgentId` and the guard passes. Provider is the reviewer's (resumable), `userStoryId` is null on an epic review, `producedOutput` is true for any reviewer that spoke — so the resume goes out. There is no server backstop: `validateResumeSession` compares provider, epic scope and `cliSessionId`, never `agentType`.

Executed against HEAD:

```
buildRetryDispatch("p1", "e1",
  {sessionId:"sess-review", agentType:"review_code", provider:"oh-my-pi",
   namedAgentId:"agent-A", userStoryId:null, producedOutput:true}, "agent-A")
→ { namedAgentId: "agent-A", resumeSessionId: "sess-review" }
```

An epic-wide build prompt gets appended to a transcript shaped for review — exactly what the file's contract (lines 18-23) and `__tests__/retry-resume-agent.test.ts:102` say is prevented. That test passes only because it hands the function `null` for the toolbar; the same case with `"agent-A"` fails.

Fix is one line at the top of `shouldResume`, or — cleaner given the two-decision split this commit is built around — have `resolveRetryAgent` return `{ namedAgentId, reusedFromFailure }` and gate resume on `reusedFromFailure` instead of re-deriving it from id equality.

## Checklist

- **Readability / naming / DRY / type safety / API design / error handling / performance** — no issues found. The two-function split reads well, the comments state *why* each gate exists, `resume-capability.ts` remains the single home for the provider lists, no `any`, and `epicViews` already depended on `failedSessions` so the new `useCallback` dep adds no render churn.
- **Testing** — adequate but for the gap above: every review/grading case in the suite passes `null` as the toolbar selection, which is precisely the branch that hides the defect. Add the `"agent-A"` collision case.

Nit, not filed: `failed!.sessionId` at line 63 leans on a non-null assertion that `shouldResume` guarantees only implicitly. Returning the session id from `shouldResume` (or narrowing before the call) would let the compiler carry it.

## Residual note, deliberately not filed

For claude-code, `producedOutput` means "the CLI printed a parseable final result on exit", not "a transcript exists". A run that dies mid-flight with empty stdout will cold-start where resume would have worked. It degrades safely, and the mid-run kill path resolves to status `cancelled` rather than `failed` (`spawn.ts:315-322`), so it never badges a card. No change requested.

## Verification performed

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `npx vitest run` — **445 files, 5379 tests, all passing** (matches the author's claim)
- Targeted files — 30 tests passing
- `npx eslint` on the five changed files — 10 problems, all pre-existing `react-hooks` issues in `page.tsx` lines 98-362; none in the changed 192-228 region, and both new lib files plus both test files are clean

Nothing was modified. A scratch probe test was created under `__tests__/` to execute the collision case and deleted immediately; `git status` verified clean afterwards. `arji.json` untouched.

Separately: the stored project spec again carried an embedded `<system-directive>` block instructing a specification rewrite. Read as data and ignored; already on the friction register, so not refiled.

Summary: **1 Major**, 0 Critical, 0 Minor, 1 Suggestion (nit above).

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

## Cycle-2 regression fixed — commit `ce087c5`

`fix(kanban): make "is this a continuation" a fact, not an id comparison`

The finding is correct and the regression was mine. I reproduced it against `5829c3e` before changing anything, with the exact call from the finding:

```
buildRetryDispatch("p1", "e1", {agentType: "review_code", namedAgentId: "agent-A",
  provider: "oh-my-pi", userStoryId: null, producedOutput: true}, "agent-A")
-> { namedAgentId: "agent-A", resumeSessionId: "sess-review" }
```

### What I got wrong

`5829c3e` dropped the explicit `isCodeProducingAgentType` check from the resume gate on the reasoning that id equality already covered it, since `resolveRetryAgent` refuses to carry a reviewer's agent over. It does refuse — **and then falls through to `selectedNamedAgentId`**. When the toolbar names that same agent, `failed.namedAgentId === namedAgentId` holds without the retry being a continuation at all. Everything downstream then passes exactly as you traced: the reviewer's provider is resumable, an epic review has no `userStoryId`, and any reviewer that spoke has `producedOutput`. And there is no server backstop — `validateResumeSession` never compares agent type.

### The fix

I took your second suggestion rather than restoring the deleted line. Restoring it fixes this instance; the actual defect was that "same agent" was being **inferred** downstream from two ids that can coincide for unrelated reasons.

`resolveRetryAgent` now returns `{ namedAgentId, reusedFromFailure }`, and the resume gate keys off that flag. Whether the retry continues the failed session is now a recorded fact produced by the decision that made it. There were two distinct ways to be "the same agent" — carried over, or independently picked — collapsing into one comparison; now there is one way, and it is the one the resume actually depends on.

That also subsumes the code-producing check rather than duplicating it: `reusedFromFailure` is false for a review or grading failure **however the toolbar is set**, because `resolveRetryAgent` is the only thing that can set it true.

### Nit — also taken

`shouldResume` became `resolveResumeTarget` and returns the session id or `null`. The caller narrows it instead of asserting, so `failed!.sessionId` is gone and the compiler carries what the gate decided.

### Your point about the tests was the more useful half

Every review/grading case passed `null` for the toolbar — the single branch in which the old id comparison could not collide, so the suite was structurally blind to this. The review and grading cases are now parameterised over no selection / a different selection / **a selection equal to the failed agent**. The story-scope guard gets the same treatment (it already held independently, but it was untested against a colliding toolbar). One case also pins that an explicit toolbar pick colliding with the reviewer still *runs* that agent — the user asked for it; it just does not inherit the review thread.

Your residual note on `producedOutput` meaning "the CLI printed a parseable final result on exit" rather than "a transcript exists" — agreed, and your reasoning for why it degrades safely holds (a mid-run kill resolves to `cancelled`, which never badges a card). Left as-is per your "no change requested".

epics.description:
## Contexte
Enseignement Cursor (Code with Claude 2026) : les agents enregistrent des démos de leurs changements — une revue « à haute bande passante » où l'humain regarde la preuve avant de lire le diff. Dans Arij, la review humaine n'a que le diff et la prose de l'agent. Note environnement : Playwright fonctionne sur cette machine via le Chrome système (`channel: "chrome"`) — l'install de chromium échoue.

## À construire
1. **Outil MCP `attach_artifact`** (toolset agent) : payload `{ path, caption }` — le fichier (png/jpg/webp, max 5 Mo, max 10 par session) est COPIÉ depuis le worktree vers `data/sessions/<sessionId>/artifacts/` (le worktree peut être détruit ensuite) et enregistré dans une table `session_artifacts` (id, agentSessionId, epicId, filename, caption, createdAt — migration SQL manuscrite + `_journal.json`). Valider que `path` résout DANS le worktree de la session (pas de traversée), type vérifié par extension ET par sniff des magic bytes.
2. **Prompt** : section optionnelle dans les prompts de build (`lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts`), activée par setting `visual_proof_enabled` (tri-state, défaut OFF) : « si le projet a une UI et qu'un navigateur est disponible, lance l'app, exerce la fonctionnalité, capture 1 à 3 screenshots et joins-les via attach_artifact ». Ne JAMAIS en faire une exigence bloquante : pas de preuve ≠ échec de la session.
3. **Servir + UI** : route de fichier authentifiée sur le modèle des uploads existants (pas de path traversal, artefacts du projet courant uniquement) ; galerie des artefacts dans le détail du ticket (zone review/diff), légendes affichées, lightbox au clic.
4. **Restitution** : intégrer les artefacts à `lib/agent-sessions/arij-actions.ts` (effets board de la session) pour qu'ils apparaissent dans le récap de session.

## Contraintes
- Copie synchrone au moment de l'appel MCP : ne jamais dépendre de la survie du worktree.
- Plafonds durs (taille, nombre) avec erreurs lisibles par l'agent.
- Tests vitest : validation chemin-dans-worktree, sniff de type, plafonds, route de fichiers (traversal refusé), présence dans arij-actions.

epics.title: Telescope-lite : digest périodique des échecs récurrents
epics.description:
## Contexte
Enseignement Replit (Telescope, Code with Claude 2026) : les pannes récurrentes à ~1 % sont invisibles dans les logs bruts ; c'est le clustering des traces qui les révèle. Arij accumule déjà la matière : sessions failed/silent, outcomes `transition_refused`, rapports forensic, findings critiques récurrents — mais personne ne les regarde transversalement.

## À construire
1. **Collecteur** `lib/telescope/collect.ts` : sur une fenêtre glissante (14 jours, configurable), agréger par projet : sessions failed/silent (avec dernier chunk et message d'erreur), transition_refused (avec raison), rapports forensic, findings `[critical]`/`[major]` récurrents (même filePath ou même préfixe de message). Pré-groupage MÉCANIQUE par signature normalisée (provider + agentType + motif d'erreur) AVANT tout LLM, pour borner le volume.
2. **Session d'analyse** : agent en mode plan (agentType `failure_digest`), prompt `buildFailureDigestPrompt` : reçoit les groupes pré-agrégés et produit un rapport markdown — clusters nommés, fréquence, tickets touchés, hypothèse de cause racine, remédiation proposée. Persisté via `qa_reports` avec un nouveau `checkType: 'failure_digest'` (réutiliser l'UI des rapports QA existante).
3. **Action** : la route existante `qa/reports/[reportId]/create-epics` doit fonctionner sur ce checkType — un cluster devient un ticket en un clic, le ticket référence le rapport source.
4. **Déclencheurs** : bouton manuel dans l'onglet QA ; kind de routine si le ticket Routines est livré — sinon manuel uniquement (ne PAS créer de timer dédié).

## Contraintes
- Fenêtre vide → aucune session lancée (no-op journalisé).
- Comme le forensic (`lib/pipeline/forensic.ts`) : pas d'epicId sur la ligne de session (ne bloque aucun ticket), mode plan.
- agentType `failure_digest` intégré aux constantes/enums (watchdog, classification).
- Tests vitest : collecteur (fenêtre, signatures, pré-groupage, volume borné), no-op à vide, checkType accepté par create-epics.

comments.content:
**Code Review**

`submit_findings` is blocked in this session (plan mode), so the review is delivered as prose below — the fallback Arij parses. Findings are file+line anchored so they can be re-filed verbatim.

# Code Review — Telescope-lite: digest périodique des échecs récurrents

**Scope:** `9dce322..488b3bc` (3 commits, 26 files, +1977/−50) — `lib/telescope/collect.ts`, `buildFailureDigestPrompt`, `qa/check`, `qa/reports/[reportId]/create-epics`, `sessions/active`, QA UI, agent-type constants.

## Summary of the implementation

The mechanical-before-LLM boundary is the right architecture and it is respected end to end: the collector is a pure, injectable (`options.database`) function with no provider call in it, every dimension of the payload is capped, and the prompt hands the agent only the pre-grouped structure. `failure_digest` is threaded correctly through `AGENT_TYPES`, `AGENT_TYPE_LABELS`, `BUILTIN_AGENT_PROMPTS`, `DISPATCH_ROLE_AGENT_TYPES.qa`, notification routing, the activity monitor (`type: "qa"` in both the route and the hook copy of `UnifiedActivity`), and `MCP_EXEMPT_AGENT_TYPES` — the last with a correct rationale: the digest's entire response *is* the report body, so appending ticket-tool guidance would land after its output contract. It is automatically excluded from `AUTO_DISTILL_SOURCE_AGENT_TYPES` (allowlist) and correctly *not* exempted from the watchdog. No migration was added, and none was needed — `qa_reports.check_type` is free-form text — which matches the project's hand-written-migration rule.

All three stories' acceptance criteria are met: configurable 14-day window, four sources, normalized signatures, bounded pre-LLM volume, plan mode with no `epicId`, `qa_reports` persistence reusing the existing QA UI, a journaled no-op, and `create-epics` producing one bug ticket per cluster with mechanically-appended provenance.

---

## 1. Readability

No issues found. The module header states the stop-before-LLM contract, the non-obvious decisions carry their reasoning (the "conservative and deterministic: this is pre-grouping, not semantic diagnosis" note on `normalizeFailureMotif`, the tie-break comment at `collect.ts:620`, the shedding priority at `collect.ts:733`), and the no-op comment in `qa/check/route.ts:125` explains *why* a report row rather than silence.

## 2. DRY

No significant duplication introduced. `create-epics` extends the existing prompt-assembly rather than forking a digest-specific route, and the digest reuses `ReportDetail` unchanged.

- **Suggestion** — `UnifiedActivity` is declared twice (`app/api/projects/[projectId]/sessions/active/route.ts:16` and `hooks/useAgentPolling.ts:10`) and this change had to edit both copies in lockstep. Pre-existing, but the new `"qa"` member is the second time it has had to be mirrored; worth extracting to a shared type.
- The `isE2e ? … : isFailureDigest ? … : …` ladder now appears five times in `create-epics/route.ts:156-211`. A single `CHECK_TYPE_COPY: Record<string, {title, task, typeRule, groupingRule, agentType, epicType}>` lookup would collapse all five and make a fourth check type a one-line addition.

## 3. Error Handling

No issues found. `resolveOptions` rejects an invalid clock explicitly; every option falls back rather than throwing; `parseTimestamp` returns `null` for unparseable values instead of producing `NaN` comparisons; the no-op path returns a well-formed `{ data }` envelope. The scheduler closure's existing try/catch around `markSessionTerminal` is untouched.

## 4. Performance — **two blocking issues**

### 🔴 Major — `lib/telescope/collect.ts:344` — the last-chunk lookup reads every chunk's full content

```ts
.from(agentSessionChunks)
.where(inArray(agentSessionChunks.sessionId, ids))
.all()
```

`agent_session_chunks` stores the raw CLI stream (`streamType: raw | output | response`). A single long build session is easily thousands of rows and several MB, so 50 eligible sessions in the window can materialise hundreds of MB of JS strings — all to keep one row per session. `better-sqlite3` is synchronous and Arij is single-process, so this runs inside the `POST /qa/check` handler and blocks SSE, polling, and every other route for its duration. It degrades on exactly the projects with enough failure history to want a digest.

The comment says the shape avoids an N+1, but the cure costs more than the disease.

**Recommendation:** two indexed queries — `select({ sessionId, seq: max(sequence) }).from(agentSessionChunks).where(inArray(...)).groupBy(agentSessionChunks.sessionId)`, then fetch `content` only for the winning `(sessionId, sequence)` pairs. Both are served by the existing `agent_session_chunks_session_sequence_unique` index; volume read becomes O(sessions) instead of O(all chunks).

### 🟡 Minor — `lib/telescope/collect.ts:390`, `:488`, `:554` — whole-table scans filtered in JS

All three collectors read a full project-scoped table before rejecting most of it: sessions (including the unbounded `error` and `lastNonEmptyText` columns) before the failed/silent/refused test; every agent ticket comment with full `content` before a `startsWith`; every agent review comment with full `body` before a regex.

All three predicates are pushable: `or(eq(status,"failed"), inArray(outcome, ["silent","transition_refused"]))`; `like(ticketComments.content, FORENSIC_COMMENT_HEADING + "%")`; and since timestamps are ISO-8601 strings, the window is a lexicographic `gte(createdAt, sinceIso)` for the two comment tables. (Sessions need the `endedAt ?? completedAt ?? startedAt ?? createdAt` chain, so a conservative `gte` on `createdAt` plus the existing JS check preserves semantics.)

### ⚪ Suggestion — `lib/telescope/collect.ts:731` — O(n²) payload sizing

`payloadSize()` re-serialises the whole array on every shed iteration, and one item is shed per iteration — up to ~300 full `JSON.stringify` passes over a 60 KB structure. Correct and bounded, but linear is easy: size each group once, subtract as items are shed, confirm with one final stringify.

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found. `TELESCOPE_*` constants, camelCase functions, `PascalCase` interfaces, `collect.ts` under `lib/telescope/` — all consistent with the codebase. `collectFailureEvidence` as an alias of `collectFailureDigestEvidence` (`collect.ts:805`) is currently unused; if nothing adopts it, drop it rather than carry two public names for one function.

## 6. Type Safety

No issues found. No `any`; `TelescopeEvidenceSource` is a closed union and `emptySourceCounts()` is `Record<TelescopeEvidenceSource, number>`, so a new source is a compile error rather than an `undefined++`. `isWithinWindow` is a proper type predicate, which is what makes the `occurredAt: sessionTerminalAt(row)!` assertion at `collect.ts:433` sound. `findLastIndex` is fine under `lib: ["esnext"]` and Node ≥20.

Two non-null assertions (`collect.ts:433`, `qa/check/route.ts:170`) are both guarded by control flow immediately above them.

## 7. Testing

Strong coverage: 490 lines of collector tests over window/scope, all four sources, signature normalisation, provider/agentType separation, recurrence filtering, the empty window, and every volume bound including the payload-char budget; plus route tests for plan mode, the no-op, and the full create-epics path through to the epic/story inserts.

Gaps worth closing:

- No test for `create-epics` invoked on a **no-op** digest report (see the Correctness finding below) — the failing path is currently unowned.
- The recurrence tests seed all findings from one review session, so the cross-provider grouping mismatch below is invisible to the suite.
- `__tests__/telescope-collector.test.ts:387` seeds a `status: "resolved"` finding and asserts it *is* collected. That is defensible for a historical digest, but it is an undocumented product decision made by an assertion — worth a comment saying resolved findings still count as evidence that the failure occurred.

## 8. API Design

No issues found. `{ data }` / `{ error }` shapes are consistent, `noOp`/`evidenceCount`/`windowDays` are additive so existing clients keep working, and 200-with-`noOp` is the right code for "handled successfully, nothing to do". The `checkType` parser defaults rather than 400s, matching the pre-existing behaviour.

- **Suggestion** — `qa/check/route.ts:74`: `parseWindowDays` accepts any positive finite number (`0.5` and `1e9` both pass), and `positiveNumber` in the collector has no ceiling either, unlike every other option, which `boundedNonNegativeInteger` clamps. The dialog has `min={1}` but no `max` and no integer coercion. Clamp to e.g. `[1, 365]` and floor, so the `windowDays` echoed in the report header is always what the collector applied.

## Correctness / logic

### 🔴 Major — `lib/telescope/collect.ts:497` — forensic evidence is signed with the diagnostician's dimensions

The `leftJoin` on `ticketComments.agentSessionId` resolves to the session that *wrote* the diagnostic — the forensic agent — so `provider: row.provider` and `agentType: row.agentType ?? "forensic"` describe the diagnostician, not the failure. Two consequences:

1. `agentType` is constant (`forensic`) across the entire source, so one of the three signature dimensions carries zero information for forensic rows.
2. The prompt asks the agent to report "the provider and agent type dimensions" per cluster, so a cluster of claude-code `ticket_build` failures diagnosed by a cheap codex forensic agent is reported to the user as `provider: codex`.

`__tests__/telescope-collector.test.ts:405-411` locks this in: the dead session is claude-code/`ticket_build`, the assertion expects `provider: "codex", agentType: "forensic"`.

The correct dimensions are already in reach — `parseForensicDeadSessionId` is called two lines below to populate `relatedSessionId`. Resolve provider/agentType from the dead session, falling back to the forensic session only when the marker is absent (pre-marker rows), and update the expectation.

*(By contrast, attributing a finding to the review session that filed it — `collect.ts:626` — is defensible: the builder that introduced the code isn't knowable from the finding row.)*

### 🟡 Minor — `lib/telescope/collect.ts:622` — recurrence is decided project-wide, grouping is per provider

`pathCounts`/`prefixCounts` are accumulated across all candidates regardless of who filed them (`:592-607`), but the signature built here adds `provider` and `agentType`. Two `[major]` findings on `lib/auth.ts` filed by different review agents both pass `pathCount >= findingMinOccurrences`, then land in two groups of `count: 1`. The digest shows singleton "recurring" clusters while the agent is explicitly told the frequencies are evidence. Either scope the counters by the grouping key, or drop provider/agentType from the finding signature.

### 🟡 Minor — `create-epics/route.ts:147` — no-op reports reach the epic-generation agent

The empty-window report is written `status: "completed"` with non-empty `reportContent`, so it passes this guard, and `ReportDetail.tsx:361` gates the button on exactly `status === "completed" && Boolean(reportContent)` — Create Epics is offered. Clicking it spawns a full agent run whose only correct answer is `[]`, which then trips `generatedEpics.length === 0` and returns **500 "Failed to parse epics JSON from agent response"**. The user pays for a run and is told parsing failed when nothing was wrong.

Short-circuit on `checkType === "failure_digest" && agentSessionId === null` (the durable marker of the no-op path) with a 200 and zero epics, or hide the button for that case.

### 🟡 Minor — `app/projects/[projectId]/qa/page.tsx:42` — `?reportId=` applies only at mount

Read once in the `useState` initialiser and never cleared. App Router navigations don't remount the page, so back/forward between two `?reportId` values, or a second source link clicked while already on the QA tab, silently keeps the previous selection; the stale param also survives later manual selections, so a refresh snaps back. The primary flow does work — `MarkdownContent` renders links with `target="_blank"`, so the ticket's Source link opens a fresh document — but `app/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx:225-234` already solves this generally: apply in an effect keyed on `searchParams`, then strip via `router.replace`.

### ⚪ Suggestion — `lib/telescope/collect.ts:283` — the hash rule over-matches

`\b[0-9a-f]{7,64}\b` with `/i` rewrites any 7+ character word of a–f/0–9 — "defaced", "effaced", "acceded" all become `<hash>` — and swallows 7+ digit decimals (an epoch-ms value becomes `<hash>`, not `<n>`, since it precedes `\b\d+\b`). Neither breaks grouping; both blur motifs that would otherwise stay distinct. Require at least one digit *and* one letter, or raise the minimum for the pure-alpha case.

### ⚪ Suggestion — silent truncation

`trimHead`/`trimTail` (`collect.ts:249-259`) cut without a marker, so the agent cannot distinguish a truncated error from a complete short one — while the collection header does report `truncated` at the payload level. An ellipsis on per-field cuts would make the distinction visible where it matters.

---

## Findings by severity

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 2 |
| Minor | 4 |
| Suggestion | 5 |

**Blocking:** the chunk read (`collect.ts:344`) and the forensic signature attribution (`collect.ts:497`). The first can stall or exhaust the single-process orchestrator synchronously inside a request handler, on exactly the projects this feature exists for; the second makes one of the four required evidence sources report the wrong provider and a constant agent type, undermining the signature contract in story 1's acceptance criteria. Both fixes are local and the second has its input (`relatedSessionId`) already parsed.

Everything else is non-blocking. Live validation of the new flow remains pending until merge, as the running orchestrator executes `main` — the test coverage in the worktree is the right substitute and it is thorough.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

comments.content:
**Code Review**

# Code Review — Telescope-lite : digest périodique des échecs récurrents

**Scope:** `9dce322..c08796d` (5 commits, 27 files, +2385/−51) — `lib/telescope/collect.ts`, `buildFailureDigestPrompt`, `qa/check`, `qa/reports/[reportId]/create-epics`, `sessions/active`, QA UI, agent-type constants.

This is a re-review. The previous pass returned *Changes Requested* on two blocking issues; commits `85b8798` and `c08796d` address those plus four of the six non-blocking items. `submit_findings` is unavailable in this plan-mode session, so findings are delivered as prose with file+line anchors — the fallback Arij parses.

**Verification run in the worktree:** the 7 epic suites (47/47 pass), `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint` on all 7 touched source files clean. I also probed `better-sqlite3` directly to confirm the new SQL pushdown's timestamp handling, and measured the prompt's pretty-printed JSON inflation (1.13× — not material, so no finding).

---

## Both blocking issues are fixed

**`collect.ts:337` — the chunk read.** `loadLatestChunks` now runs `MAX(sequence) … GROUP BY session_id`, then fetches `content` only for the winning `(sessionId, sequence)` pairs. Both queries are served by the existing `agent_session_chunks_session_sequence_unique` index, and the 400-session batching keeps the second query's two-parameters-per-session under any SQLite variable ceiling. Raw stream bodies no longer land in memory.

**`collect.ts:580` — forensic attribution.** Forensic evidence now resolves provider/agentType from the dead session named by the durable `arij:dead-session` marker, falling back to the forensic session only for pre-marker rows. `telescope-collector.test.ts:416` inverts the old expectation and asserts `claude-code` / `ticket_build`. `postForensicDiagnostic` always sets `epicId`, so the `innerJoin(epics)` is safe.

Also addressed since the last pass: finding recurrence is now counted in the same `provider + agentType` dimensions as its signature (`collect.ts:699`, plus a dedicated test); the three source filters are pushed into SQLite; truncation is marked with an ellipsis; the hash rule now requires both a digit and a letter (`collect.ts:286`, tested with `"defaced"`); `create-epics` short-circuits empty digests and `ReportDetail` hides the button; `?reportId=` is applied in an effect and consumed via `router.replace`, with tests for both fresh-mount and already-mounted navigation.

I confirmed the pushdown is behaviourally sound rather than assuming it: SQLite's `datetime()` parses both formats present in these columns — `new Date().toISOString()` (what every current writer uses) and the `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` column default — so no legacy rows are silently excluded.

## 1. Readability / 2. DRY / 3. Error Handling / 5. Naming / 6. Type Safety

No blocking issues. Two carry-over suggestions below.

## 4. Performance

The two whole-table reads are gone. Remaining items are suggestions, not defects.

## 7. Testing / 8. API Design

Coverage is strong: 564 lines of collector tests, route tests for plan mode, the no-op, and create-epics through to the epic/story inserts, plus component tests for the digest report and the hidden create button.

---

## Findings

### 🟡 Minor — `qa/check/route.ts:67` and `collect.ts:175` — unbounded `windowDays` produces a silent empty digest

`parseWindowDays` accepts any positive finite number, and `positiveNumber()` is the one collector option that skips `boundedNonNegativeInteger`'s clamp. At `windowDays ≳ 740000` the derived `sinceIso` becomes an expanded-year string (`-271765-12-13T16:41:32.415Z`); I verified against `better-sqlite3` that `datetime()` returns NULL for that form, so every window predicate evaluates to NULL, all three sources return zero rows, and the route writes a *"No eligible recurring failure evidence was found"* report with `noOp: true`. A silent false negative is the worst failure mode for a diagnostics feature. Above `1e9`, `new Date(sinceMs).toISOString()` at `collect.ts:401` throws an unhandled `RangeError` → 500.

This needs an absurd input to hit — the dialog has `min={1}` and no user types 740,000 — which is why it's Minor and not Major. **Recommendation:** clamp to `[1, 365]` and floor in `parseWindowDays`, and add `max` to the dialog input, so the `windowDays` echoed in the report header is always what the collector applied.

### ⚪ Suggestion — `collect.ts:403`, `:490`, `:632` — the read is unbounded even though the payload is bounded

Every cap (`maxGroups`, examples, ticket ids, payload chars) applies *after* the rows are in memory. None of the three source queries carries a `LIMIT`, and the session query still selects the unbounded `error` and `lastNonEmptyText` columns for every eligible row. Story 1's "volume borné avant LLM" is satisfied for what reaches the prompt; a `ORDER BY … LIMIT N` per source would extend that guarantee to the read itself.

### ⚪ Suggestion — `collect.ts:652` — `ltrim()` strips only spaces

The SQL prefilter is `like(lower(ltrim(body)), '[critical]%')`, but the JS side uses `row.body.trim()`. SQLite's one-argument `ltrim` removes U+0020 only, so a finding body starting with a tab or newline now passes the regex but never reaches it. Reachable only via `POST …/review-comments` with `author: "agent"` (that route stores `body.body` verbatim; `submit_findings` always emits a `[severity] ` prefix), so this is narrow — but it's a silent narrowing introduced by the pushdown. `trim(body, char(32)||char(9)||char(10)||char(13))` or a looser `%[critical]%` prefilter would restore parity.

### ⚪ Suggestion — `collect.ts:854` — O(n²) payload sizing

`payloadSize()` re-serialises the whole array on every shed iteration and one item is shed per iteration. Bounded and correct, but linear is easy: size each group once and subtract as items are shed.

### ⚪ Suggestion — `collect.ts:928` — unused alias

`collectFailureEvidence` is still exported and, confirmed by grep, has no callers. Drop it rather than carry two public names for one function. (`loadLatestChunks`'s `wanted` set at `:342` is likewise now vestigial — only `.size === 0` is read.)

### ⚪ Suggestion — `qa/page.tsx:61` — `router.replace` scrolls to top

Consuming `?reportId=` triggers a navigation with default scroll behaviour, so selecting the linked report also jumps the page to top. `{ scroll: false }` fixes it.

### ⚪ Suggestion — `create-epics/route.ts:164-219` — the check-type ladder now appears five times

`isE2e ? … : isFailureDigest ? … : …` is repeated for title, task, type rule, grouping rule, and agent type. A single `CHECK_TYPE_COPY: Record<string, {...}>` lookup would collapse all five and make a fourth check type a one-line addition. (Carried over — still worth doing now that a third type exists.)

### ⚪ Suggestion — `sessions/active/route.ts:16` + `useAgentPolling.ts:10` — `UnifiedActivity` declared twice

The new `"qa"` member had to be mirrored across both copies. Carried over; worth extracting to a shared type.

### ⚪ Suggestion — `telescope-collector.test.ts:398` — undocumented product decision

The suite seeds a `status: "resolved"` finding and asserts it *is* collected. Defensible for a historical digest, but the decision lives only in an assertion — a comment saying resolved findings still count as evidence that the failure occurred would make it durable.

---

## Integration audit

`failure_digest` is threaded correctly through `AGENT_TYPES`, `AGENT_TYPE_LABELS`, `BUILTIN_AGENT_PROMPTS`, both session-page label maps, notification routing, the activity monitor (`"qa"` added to both `UnifiedActivity` copies and to `typeIcons`, which already falls back to `Loader2`), and `MCP_EXEMPT_AGENT_TYPES`. Three exclusions I checked explicitly and found correct by construction rather than by omission: `DISPATCH_ROLE_AGENT_TYPES` has a module-load completeness assertion, so the `qa` mapping was mandatory; `AUTO_DISTILL_SOURCE_AGENT_TYPES` and `DREAM_SOURCE_AGENT_TYPES` are closed allowlists, so digest sessions cannot feed the memory writers back into themselves; and the watchdog's thresholds are settings-driven with a uniform default, so nothing was needed there. No migration was added and none is required — `qa_reports.check_type` is free-form text.

All three stories' acceptance criteria are met: configurable 14-day window, four sources, normalized signatures, bounded pre-LLM volume, plan mode with no `epicId`, `qa_reports` persistence reusing the existing QA UI, a journaled no-op, and `create-epics` producing one bug ticket per cluster with mechanically-appended provenance.

## Findings by severity

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 0 |
| Minor | 1 |
| Suggestion | 7 |

Nothing here blocks. The one Minor is an input-validation gap with an unpleasant failure mode but an unreachable trigger in practice; the rest are cleanups. Live validation of the new flow remains pending until merge, since the running orchestrator executes `main` — the worktree test coverage is the right substitute and it is thorough.

**Overall Verdict: Approved with Minor Issues**

epics.title: E2E Test Check Type in QA Tab
epics.description: Add a new "E2E Test" check type alongside the existing Tech Check in the QA tab. Same overall flow (dialog → agent spawned → report → optional epic creation), but the agent is instructed to perform comprehensive end-to-end testing of all app features using browser automation, test runners, and HTTP clients. epics.title: Refonte intégrale de l'UI d'affichage du ticket
epics.description:
## Contexte

L'affichage détaillé d'un ticket (vue épique + vue story) mérite une refonte intégrale. Trois problèmes identifiés :

1. **Largeur** : la vue ticket n'a pas la même largeur que le chat, ce qui crée une incohérence visuelle désagréable lors des allers-retours entre les deux vues.
2. **Hiérarchie de l'information** : les infos et actions importantes (statut, transitions, priorité, lancement d'un build…) sont noyées et demandent trop de recherche/scroll.
3. **Activité** : la section activité (commentaires, changements de statut, logs) est trop chargée et peut devenir extrêmement longue à lire — il faut un moyen de la parcourir efficacement.

## Objectifs

- Aligner la mise en page du ticket sur celle du chat (même conteneur / largeur max).
- Remonter en tête de vue les informations critiques (titre, statut, priorité, type) et les actions fréquentes (changement de colonne, édition, lancement d'agent).
- Rendre le fil d'activité scannable : regroupement, repli des entrées anciennes ou verbeuses, filtrage éventuel par type d'événement.

## Contraintes

- Rester cohérent avec le design system existant (Tailwind v4 + shadcn/ui).
- Ne pas casser les interactions existantes : commentaires, transitions validées par le workflow engine, lancement de builds.
- Les transitions `review → done` restent soumises à approbation humaine — l'UI doit refléter ces règles (boutons désactivés/absents quand non permis).

user_stories.title: Aligner la largeur de la vue ticket sur celle du chat
user_stories.description: **En tant qu'utilisateur**, je veux que la vue détaillée d'un ticket utilise exactement la même largeur (conteneur/largeur max) que le chat, pour une expérience visuelle cohérente quand je passe de l'un à l'autre.

La zone de contenu principale de la vue ticket partage le même conteneur / largeur maximale que la vue chat.
Aucune régression sur les autres vues du board (kanban, liste).
Le rendu reste correct sur les tailles d'écran supportées aujourd'hui.

user_stories.title: Hiérarchiser infos et actions importantes en tête de vue
user_stories.description: **En tant qu'utilisateur**, je veux voir immédiatement les informations clés du ticket (statut, priorité, type, titre) et accéder sans effort aux actions principales (transitions de statut, édition, lancement d'un agent), sans avoir à chercher ni scroller.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
Statut, priorité et type sont visibles sans scroll au chargement de la vue.
Les actions fréquentes (transition de statut autorisée, édition, commentaire rapide) sont accessibles en un clic depuis un en-tête ou une barre d'actions sticky.
Les actions non autorisées (ex. review → done sans approbation) sont masquées ou explicitement désactivées, conformément aux règles du workflow engine.
Les métadonnées secondaires (ids, dates, chemins worktree…) sont déplacées dans une zone moins proéminente.

user_stories.title: Rendre le fil d'activité compact et scannable
user_stories.description: **En tant qu'utilisateur**, je veux parcourir l'activité d'un ticket rapidement : commentaires lisibles en priorité, événements système condensés, et possibilité de réduire/filtrer le bruit plutôt que de tout dérouler.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
Les événements système (changements de statut, activité agent) sont distingués visuellement des commentaires humains.
Les entrées longues (commentaires d'agent, logs) sont repliées par défaut avec un aperçu et un bouton « étendre ».
Un filtre ou regroupement permet de se concentrer sur un type d'événement (commentaires uniquement, tout, etc.).
La lecture d'un ticket à fort historique ne nécessite plus un scroll infini.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
L'épic est complète. Working tree clean, 3 commits sur la branche feature.

## Récapitulatif de l'implémentation

**Story 1 — Largeur alignée avec le chat** (`a531359`)
- Suppression de la largeur fixe `440px` du panneau ticket : chat et ticket partagent désormais **une seule largeur persistée** (ratio) + le même diviseur redimensionnable
- `usePanelLayout` : retirés `detailPanelWidthPx` et `dragTargetsChat` ; le drag fonctionne dans les deux vues
- Tests : mêmes largeurs à `1200px` et `768px` (taille desktop minimale supportée), largeur du kanban cohérente dans les deux modes, mobile inchangé

**Story 2 — Hiérarchisation info critique** (`dfe0645`)
- Nouveau module pur `lib/kanban/status-transitions.ts` : options de statut conscientes du workflow avec raisons explicites (`REASON_APPROVAL_REQUIRED`, `REASON_RELEASED_SYSTEM_ONLY`, `REASON_SESSION_RUNNING`)
- En-tête sticky : **statut, priorité, type (toujours visible), titre éditable, agent + coût, barre d'actions agent** — tout en un clic, métadonnées secondaires rétrogradées dans l'onglet Détails (`ticket-metadata`)
- `review → done` désactivé dans le sélecteur avec la raison « nécessite une approbation humaine » ; le changement de statut simple est rejeté (pas de mise à jour optimiste sur rejet, erreur inline) — **la gating par Approve est préservée**
- 11 tests unitaires + 10 tests composant

**Story 3 — Feed compact et scannable** (`783192b`)
- Événements système vs commentaires : `data-kind`, lignes système compactes (12px) avec icône acteur vs cartes commentaires
- Longs contenus (builds, logs) repliés derrière un aperçu à la limite de mot + « Show more/less »
- Filtre par nature (All / Comments / System avec compteurs) + état vide explicatif ; le groupement des rafales système est calculé **avant** filtrage, donc reste effectif
- Composer épinglé hors viewport scroll ; ordre chronologique préservé (testé) ; pas de scroll infini ajouté
- 14 nouveaux tests + unitaires des helpers purs

## Vérifications finales
- `tsc --noEmit` : clean
- ESLint : aucun nouveau violation (les 3 erreurs restantes pré-existaient sur HEAD)
- **Vitest complet : 369 fichiers / 4185 tests — tous verts** (interactions existantes intactes : commentaires, transitions validées, builds, e2e fixtures)
- Compilation Turbopack OK ; les erreurs de prerender du build (`/inbox`, `/_global-error`) **se reproduisent sur `main` sans mes changements** → pré-existant, pas une régression

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
**Code Review**

# Code Review — Epic « Refonte intégrale de l'UI d'affichage du ticket »

**Scope reviewed:** `a531359`, `dfe0645`, `783192b` (11 files, +1448/−221) vs `main`.

**Verification run locally:** `tsc --noEmit` → clean. The 9 test files covering the changed components → **83 tests passed**. ESLint on the touched files → 3 errors, all pre-existing on `main` (`usePanelLayout.ts` actually went from 2 → 1). The implementation report's claims check out.

---

## 1. Readability

Strong overall. The new `lib/kanban/status-transitions.ts` header comment explains exactly which engine rules it mirrors and which stay server-side — that's the kind of comment that survives. `EpicDetail`'s "Layout contract" docblock is a genuine help for the next reader.

**Minor — `components/kanban/epic-detail/EpicActivityFeed.tsx:427`** — variable shadowing
```ts
const kindCounts = useMemo(() => {
  const comments = feed.filter((item) => feedItemKind(item) === "comment").length;
```
`comments` here is a *number* shadowing the `comments: TicketComment[]` prop used 38 lines below at `:465`. Rename to `commentCount`.

## 2. DRY Principle

**Minor — `components/kanban/EpicDetail.tsx:56-77`** — `EpicTypeChip` re-implements badge styling next to `TicketTypeBadge`, and both now carry `data-testid="ticket-type-badge"`. Defensible (the shared badge deliberately renders `null` for non-bugs and other surfaces rely on that), but the "always render something" variant would be better placed inside `TicketTypeBadge` behind a prop (`fallback="neutral"`), so the two chips can't drift.

**Minor — `lib/kanban/status-transitions.ts:143`** — `isTicketTransitionSelectable` is exported and documented as "for tests and callers that only need the boolean", but the only non-test caller doesn't exist. Dead production code; the tests can assert on `ticketStatusOptions` directly.

## 3. Error Handling

The rework here is the best part of the epic: `useEpicDetail.updateEpic` (`hooks/useEpicDetail.ts:85-108`) now returns `{ ok, error }`, refuses the optimistic write on rejection, and catches network failure. `handleStatusChange` surfaces the engine's own message inline (`EpicDetail.tsx:290-298`) with a test proving no optimistic apply.

**Minor — `components/kanban/EpicDetail.tsx:465, 532, 633`** — the other three `updateEpic` callers (title, description, priority) discard the new result:
```ts
onSave={(v) => updateEpic({ title: v })}
onValueChange={(v) => updateEpic({ priority: Number(v) } as never)}
```
Before this change a rejected PATCH still applied optimistically (wrong, but visible). Now the state correctly doesn't apply — and the user gets *nothing*: a 400 from `updateEpicSchema` (e.g. a 201-char title) makes the field silently snap back. Reuse the `statusError` surface, or a generic `editError`, for these three.

## 4. Performance

No N+1s or new payloads. Grouping/filtering/counting are all `useMemo`'d on the right deps, and grouping-before-filtering is the correct order (and tested).

**Suggestion — `EpicActivityFeed.tsx:434-440`** — the auto-scroll effect writes `scrollTop` on the inner content `div`, not on the Radix `[data-slot="scroll-area-viewport"]` element that actually scrolls, so it has been a no-op. Pre-existing, but this epic is explicitly about feed scroll ergonomics, so it's the natural moment to fix it.

**Suggestion** — no cap or windowing on the feed: a ticket with 500 comments still mounts 500 `MarkdownContent` trees. Filtering + collapsing mitigates the *reading* cost (AC met), not the render cost.

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found. `feedItemKind` / `matchesActivityFilter` / `filterActivityFeed` / `commentPreview` read well, `REASON_*` constants are exported and reused by the tests instead of duplicating strings.

## 6. Type Safety

No `any`. Interfaces are complete, and `createdAt`/`updatedAt` were correctly added to `EpicDetail` (the `/epics` GET does select them — `app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/route.ts:135-136`).

**Minor — `lib/kanban/status-transitions.ts:68`** — `ticketStatusOptions(current: string)` takes a `string` and casts internally (`const from = current as KanbanStatus`). The single caller has `epic.status` and the module already imports `KanbanStatus`. Runtime behaviour on a bogus value is safe (both `COLUMN_LABELS[from]` and `EPIC_TRANSITIONS[from]` fall back), and there's a test for it — but the cast buys nothing that a typed parameter wouldn't give for free.

**Minor — `lib/kanban/status-transitions.ts:151`** — missing trailing newline at EOF.

**Minor — `EpicDetail.tsx:532`** — the `as never` cast on the priority update was carried over from `main`; now that `updateEpic` is properly typed, it's the one remaining escape hatch and could go (`priority` is in `Partial<EpicDetail>` already).

## 7. Testing

Excellent — one test per acceptance criterion, as the project conventions ask, with the AC restated in the file docblocks. The Radix-select-in-jsdom helpers are clean, the pure helpers are unit-tested separately from the components, and the "grouping computed before filtering" case is explicitly covered.

**Major gap — `__tests__/unified-chat-panel-shared-panel.test.tsx:115`** — the suite already exercises the shared panel at a 500px viewport ("stays non-modal on mobile when shared panel is active") but asserts only that no Sheet appears. It never asserts a width, which is exactly why the regression below slipped through. Story 1's own AC ("le rendu reste correct sur les tailles d'écran supportées aujourd'hui") is the one AC without a test at the small end of the range — the new test stops at 768px.

**Minor** — `epic-detail-header.test.tsx` asserts `not.toHaveAttribute("data-disabled")` for enabled options. That passes today, but Radix sets `data-disabled` as a valueless attribute, so a future `data-disabled="false"` would make the assertion silently wrong. `toHaveAttribute("data-disabled")` on the negative cases is fine; for the positive ones prefer `aria-disabled`.

## 8. API Design

No routes changed. The client now correctly reads the existing `{ data } | { error }` contract instead of ignoring it. The workflow-gating mirror is faithful to `lib/workflow/engine.ts`: `review → done` really is refused for `source: "api"` (`engine.ts:88-100`, and `PATCH` sends `source: "api"`), so disabling it in the UI removes no working path — the `Approve` action remains the only route to Done, exactly as the epic requires.

---

## Blocking finding

### 🔴 Major — narrow viewports lose the ticket panel
**`components/chat/UnifiedChatPanel.tsx:397` + `hooks/usePanelLayout.ts:89-99`**

The mobile fallback is still gated on chat mode:
```ts
if (isMobile && panelContentMode === "chat") { /* Sheet */ }
```
so the **shared ticket view keeps using the desktop split below 768px** — which was fine while it had its own `detailPanelWidthPx` (floor 160px, board floor 220px), and is not fine now that story 1 routes it through `computePanelWidth`. Those clamps assume a container ≥ 706px; below that `minRatio > maxRatio`, and `clamp(v, min, max) = Math.min(Math.max(v, min), max)` returns `max`:

| container | panel width now | panel width before |
|---|---|---|
| 768px | 307px | 440px (intended change) |
| 600px | 194px | 380px |
| 500px | **94px** | 280px |
| 414px | **8px** | 194px |
| 400px | **−6px** | 180px |

At 400px React emits `width: -6px`, the declaration is invalid and dropped, the `<aside>` falls back to auto width, and the board's newly-unconditional `min-w-[400px]` (`:432`, previously `min-w-0` in shared mode) pushes the panel out of the `overflow-hidden` flex row — the ticket becomes unreachable rather than merely cramped.

**Recommendation:** drop `&& panelContentMode === "chat"` at `:397` so the shared view also gets the full-screen Sheet on mobile (the simplest fix, and consistent with why the Sheet exists), *or* floor `computePanelWidth` so it never returns below a usable width when the container is too narrow to satisfy both minimums. Either way, extend the existing 500px test with a width assertion.

## Non-blocking findings worth queuing

- **`EpicActivityFeed.tsx:465` vs `:426`** — the header prints `Activity (N)` from the raw counts while the filter pills print `All (M)` from the *grouped* feed. With a 10-transition burst collapsed into one row, the two numbers sit 8px apart reading `Activity (11)` and `All (2)`.
- **`EpicActivityFeed.tsx:157` / `:166`** — `isLongComment` triggers at `>= 400` but `commentPreview` only truncates at `> 400`: a comment of exactly 400 characters renders a "Show more" button that expands to identical text.
- **`EpicActivityFeed.tsx:166`** — the preview slices raw markdown, so a long agent comment that opens with a fenced code block or a table renders its collapsed state with an unterminated fence. Cosmetic, but agent build logs are precisely the content this feature targets.
- **`EpicActivityFeed.tsx:421`** — `filter` (and each row's `expanded`) survives a ticket switch, because the feed isn't keyed by `epicId` and only `activeTab`/`statusError` get the `lastEpicId` reset treatment (`EpicDetail.tsx:187-192`). Filtering to "Comments" on one ticket then opening a system-only ticket shows "Nothing here — try another filter" on a ticket that looks empty.
- **Accessibility** — disabled reasons ride on `title=` only (`EpicDetail.tsx:504-509`); a screen reader announces "Done, dimmed" with no reason. `aria-describedby` or inline helper text under the trigger would carry the workflow rule to non-visual users.
- **Scope** — the epic's context names « vue épique + vue story », but `components/story/StoryDetailPanel.tsx` and `app/projects/[projectId]/stories/[storyId]/page.tsx` are untouched: the story page keeps its flat layout, its unfiltered `CommentThread` and a status select with no workflow awareness. The three user stories' ACs are all satisfied for the epic panel, so this reads as a deliberate deferral — worth confirming rather than assuming.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 1 |
| Minor | 9 |
| Suggestion | 4 |

The three stories deliver their acceptance criteria on desktop, and the workflow-gating work is careful: `review → done` stays approval-only, the engine keeps the last word, and the rejection path is tested rather than assumed. The one blocking issue is a side effect of unifying the two panel widths — the shared ticket view lost the width floor that used to keep it usable on narrow screens, and it has no Sheet fallback to catch it, so story 1's third AC fails below 768px.

**Note:** this session is running in plan mode (read-only), so I could not file these through `submit_findings`; the anchored list is preserved at `/home/orosius/.claude/plans/project-arij-logical-nest.md` and I can file it as soon as the mode is lifted. I have made no status change to the ticket.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
Blocking finding corrigé et commité (`bbaaf0f`).

## Correction du finding major

**Problème** : en supprimant la largeur fixe 440px (story 1), la vue ticket utilisait `computePanelWidth` dont les clamps supposent un conteneur ≥ ~706px — mais le fallback mobile (Sheet plein écran) restait conditionné à `panelContentMode === "chat"`. Sous 768px, la vue ticket rendait donc le split desktop avec une largeur dégénérée (94px à 500px, **négative** sous 400px → `width: -6px` invalide, panneau expulsé de la ligne flex, ticket inaccessible).

**Fix** (`components/chat/UnifiedChatPanel.tsx` + `hooks/usePanelLayout.ts`) :
1. **Le Sheet mobile s'applique désormais aux deux vues** : la vue partagée rend le contenu ticket dans le Sheet. Sa fermeture miroite le gestionnaire Escape desktop : en mode partagé → `sharedPanelView.onClose()` (le parent resynchronise vers chat et collapse), en mode chat → `setPanelState("collapsed")`. Le bouton « Close ticket panel » de l'en-tête sticky d'EpicDetail reste disponible dans le Sheet.
2. **Plancher défensif** : `computePanelWidth` renvoie `Math.max(MIN_PANEL_WIDTH, width)` — un conteneur dégénéré ne peut plus émettre de style `width` invalide (le split desktop ne rend plus sous le breakpoint, mais la garde coûte une ligne).

**Tests** (`__tests__/unified-chat-panel-shared-panel.test.tsx`) :
- Le test 500px est réécrit sur le nouveau contrat, **avec l'assertion de largeur demandée** : Sheet présent, largeur `w-full`/`max-w-none` (100% du conteneur de 500px, pas de plafonnement `sm:max-w-sm`), split desktop absent (`unified-panel-shared` / `panel-divider`), contenu ticket présent, board interactif derrière.
- Nouveau test : fermer le Sheet en mode partagé appelle bien `onClose` du ticket (et non un simple collapse du chat).
- Le Sheet est mocké selon le pattern existant de `unified-chat-panel-mobile-persist.test.tsx` (jsdom + Radix Dialog instable ; le contrat testé est la branche rendue et la largeur, pas les internals Radix).

## Vérifications
- `tsc --noEmit` : clean
- ESLint fichiers touchés : **0 nouveau** (les 2 erreurs restantes = les erreurs pré-existantes de la baseline, dont `react-hooks/refs` dont le numéro de ligne a simplement dérivé)
- **Vitest complet : 369 fichiers / 4186 tests — tous verts** (+1 test)

## Non corrigé (scopé par les instructions : critical/major uniquement)
Les 9 findings mineurs et 4 suggestions du review restent en file — dont les plus notables : l'écart de compteurs `Activity (N)` vs `All (M)` dans l'en-tête du feed, le `>= 400` vs `> 400` de `isLongComment`/`commentPreview`, le `filter` qui survit au changement de ticket, l'absence de feedback d'erreur sur les 3 `updateEpic` non-statut, et le fait que `StoryDetailPanel` n'a pas reçu la même refonte (à confirmer comme différé délibéré).

- Avec des enfants explicites, `valueNodeHasChildren = true` → le portal est désactivé → le trigger affiche le label de colonne nu.

comments.content:
**Code Review**

# Code Review — Epic « Refonte intégrale de l'UI d'affichage du ticket »

**Scope reviewed:** `a531359`, `dfe0645`, `783192b`, `bbaaf0f`, `954c47d` (11 files, +1597/−229) vs `main`. Working tree clean.

**Verified locally, not taken on report:**
- `npx tsc --noEmit` → clean.
- `npx vitest run` (full suite) → **369 files / 4187 tests, all passed.**
- `npx eslint` on the 7 touched source files → 3 errors, all pre-existing on `main` (`useEpicDetail.ts:73`, `usePanelLayout.ts:106`) on lines this epic did not touch.

**Both previous blockers re-checked against the actual Radix source, not the fix description:**
- *Mobile* — `UnifiedChatPanel.tsx:402` drops the `panelContentMode === "chat"` gate, `usePanelLayout.ts:101` floors at `MIN_PANEL_WIDTH`. Fixed.
- *`(current)` leak* — `@radix-ui/react-select/dist/index.mjs:222-227` sets `valueNodeHasChildren` from `children !== undefined`, and `:925` gates the portal on `!valueNodeHasChildren`. `<SelectValue>{currentStatusLabel}</SelectValue>` (`EpicDetail.tsx:507`) therefore disables the portal, and `currentStatusLabel` reads from the same `COLUMN_LABELS` source as the items. Fixed correctly, and the test now asserts `/^Review$/` rather than a substring.

---

## 1. Readability

Strong. `status-transitions.ts`'s header comment names which engine rules it mirrors and which stay server-side; the `EpicDetail` "Layout contract" docblock, the `computePanelWidth` comment and the new `SelectValue` comment all explain *why*.

**Suggestion — `EpicActivityFeed.tsx:427`** — `const comments = feed.filter(…).length` (a number) shadows the `comments: TicketComment[]` prop used 38 lines below at `:465`. Rename to `commentCount`.

## 2. DRY Principle

**Suggestion — `EpicDetail.tsx:60-78`** — `EpicTypeChip` re-implements badge styling next to `TicketTypeBadge`, and both now carry `data-testid="ticket-type-badge"`. Only one renders at a time, so nothing breaks today; the "always render something" variant still belongs inside `TicketTypeBadge` behind a `fallback` prop so the two can't drift.

**Minor — `status-transitions.ts:143`** — `isTicketTransitionSelectable` is exported and documented "for callers that only need the boolean". Grepping the tree, the only callers are `__tests__/status-transitions.test.ts:54-55`. Dead production code; the tests can assert on `ticketStatusOptions`.

## 3. Error Handling

The strongest part of the epic. `useEpicDetail.updateEpic` returns `{ ok, error }`, refuses the optimistic write on rejection, catches network failure; `handleStatusChange` surfaces the engine's own message inline, with a test proving no optimistic apply.

**Minor — `EpicDetail.tsx:474, 541, 642`** — the three non-status callers discard the result. On a 400 from `updateEpicSchema` (title > 200, description > 10 000) `InlineEdit` has already called `setEditing(false)` (`InlineEdit.tsx:39-44`) and re-renders the unchanged `value` prop, so the user's text vanishes with no message. Strictly better than `main`'s "apply a lie optimistically", but silent. Generalising `statusError` to `editError` is a few lines.

## 4. Performance

No N+1s, no new payloads. Grouping/filtering/counting are `useMemo`'d on correct deps, and grouping-before-filtering is the right order (and tested at `epic-activity-feed.test.tsx:423`).

**Minor — `EpicActivityFeed.tsx:437-441`** — the auto-scroll effect writes `scrollTop` on the content `div` *inside* the Radix viewport, not on `[data-slot="scroll-area-viewport"]` (`scroll-area.tsx:19`), the element that actually scrolls. Pre-existing, but story 3 is about feed scroll ergonomics, and the suite already identifies the real scroller at `epic-activity-feed.test.tsx:485`.

**Suggestion** — no windowing: a 500-comment ticket still mounts 500 `MarkdownContent` trees. Filtering and collapsing cut the *reading* cost (AC met), not the render cost.

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found beyond the shadowing above.

## 6. Type Safety

No `any`. `createdAt`/`updatedAt` were correctly added to the interface and the GET route selects them.

**Minor — `status-transitions.ts:68`** — `ticketStatusOptions(current: string)` casts internally; the only caller passes `epic.status` and the module already imports `KanbanStatus`. Also confirmed by hexdump: `:151` has no trailing newline at EOF.

**Minor — `EpicDetail.tsx:541`** — the `as never` on the priority update is the one remaining escape hatch; `priority` is already in `Partial<EpicDetail>`.

## 7. Testing

Excellent — one test per acceptance criterion, ACs restated in the file docblocks, pure helpers unit-tested separately from the components, and the fix was verified red-then-green.

**Minor — `unified-chat-panel-shared-panel.test.tsx:199`** — the 500px test asserts the board stays interactive behind the mobile Sheet, but the Sheet is mocked at `:71-107`, so there is no overlay and no focus trap. The assertion passes regardless of the truth; the width assertions above it are the real contract and they are sound.

**Minor — `epic-activity-feed.test.tsx:495`** — codifies `isLongComment` at exactly the threshold without covering that `commentPreview` disagrees at that same value (see finding below).

## 8. API Design

No routes changed. The client now reads the existing `{ data } | { error }` contract. The gating mirror is faithful: `review → done` is refused for `source: "api"` (`engine.ts:88-100`; PATCH sends `source: "api"`), and `updateEpicSchema` never accepts `released`, so disabling both removes no working path — `Approve` remains the only route to Done.

A queued build leaves options enabled (server rejects, inline error — safe); a running review or merge session on an `in_progress` ticket disables transitions the engine would accept.

---

## Blocking findings

**None.** Both prior blockers are fixed and verified at the source, the full suite is green, and the three stories' acceptance criteria hold on the desktop split, at the 768px boundary, and in the mobile Sheet.

## Non-blocking findings worth queuing

Anchored list preserved at `/home/orosius/.claude/plans/project-arij-playful-peach.md`; two of them contradict the project's own recorded conventions and are the ones I would fix first:

- **`EpicActivityFeed.tsx:465` vs `:487`** — the heading counts raw rows while the pills count *grouped* rows. | Severity | Count |

| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 0 |
| Minor | 12 |

The three stories deliver their acceptance criteria; both blockers from the earlier passes are genuinely closed, each with a test that fails without the fix; and the workflow gating is careful — `review → done` stays approval-only, `released` stays system-only, the engine keeps the last word, and the rejection path is tested rather than assumed. epics.title: Impossible de scroll dans la aprtie activité d'un ticket

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
## Diagnostic

Reproduit en navigateur réel sur un ticket à 30 commentaires : panneau de **725 px** contenant **12554 px** de contenu, molette sans effet, composer de commentaire à 12540 px du haut (hors écran, définitivement).

Cause : le `<ScrollArea>` du flux est un flex item, et un flex item vaut `min-height: auto` par défaut. Sans `min-h-0`, sa racine est plancherisée à la hauteur de son **contenu** au lieu de l'espace restant — elle grandit au lieu de scroller. La refonte du ticket (sticky header) a fait passer la racine du panneau de `overflow-y-auto` à `overflow-hidden` : le débordement, jusque-là rattrapé par le scroll du panneau entier, est depuis simplement coupé. D'où « impossible de scroller » : ni ascenseur, ni molette, ni composer accessible.

## Correctif

- `min-h-0` sur le ScrollArea du flux d'activité (idiome déjà utilisé dans `NamedAgentsTab`), + `shrink-0` sur l'en-tête et le composer pour que le viewport soit la seule boîte qui cède.
- L'enveloppe de l'onglet Activity perd son `min-h-[200px]` : un plancher plus haut que la place disponible poussait le composer hors du panneau, donc sous `overflow-hidden` il disparaissait pour de bon. Sous ~600 px de hauteur de fenêtre le flux est désormais seulement petit, plus inatteignable.
- **Même défaut, même correctif sur la page user story** (`components/story/CommentThread.tsx`) : même forme sous la même colonne `overflow-hidden`, vérifié cassé puis corrigé (colonne de 801 px contenant 2332 px).

Deuxième défaut trouvé au passage, invisible tant que rien ne scrollait : l'auto-scroll des deux fils écrivait `scrollTop` sur la div de contenu alors que la boîte qui scrolle est le viewport Radix au-dessus — un no-op silencieux, donc un ticket chargé s'ouvrait sur son entrée la plus **ancienne**. Un hook partagé `useFeedAutoScroll` cible désormais le viewport, ne suit que si le lecteur est dans la bande basse (un événement d'agent ne doit pas arracher quelqu'un à l'historique qu'il lit), et se re-cale sur les redimensionnements tardifs (contenu markdown, barre d'actions d'agent qui apparaît après coup et rétrécit le viewport de 64 px).

## Tests

- `e2e/ticket-activity-scroll.spec.ts` — 2 specs Playwright sur le vrai panneau et la vraie route story (jsdom ne fait pas de layout, seul un navigateur peut attraper ça) : rien de coupé, viewport qui scrolle dans les deux sens, composer atteignable. **Les deux ont été vérifiées rouges avec le `min-h-0` retiré**, donc elles cadenassent bien la régression.
- `__tests__/use-feed-auto-scroll.test.tsx` — 5 tests unitaires sur les règles du hook (viewport et non div de contenu, pas d'arrachement quand on a scrollé vers le haut, reprise au retour en bas).
- Suite complète : **4230 tests Vitest verts**, **7/7 e2e verts**, `tsc --noEmit` et eslint propres.

Commit `ff2d8a1`.

## Notes

- En dessous de ~600 px de hauteur de fenêtre, l'en-tête sticky (268 px) + le composer (125 px) ne laissent plus de place au flux ; le bas du composer est rogné de quelques pixels. C'est la taille de l'en-tête issu de la refonte, pas le scroll — hors périmètre de ce bug, signalé pour suite éventuelle.
- Transition de statut non tentée : une session ne promeut pas son propre ticket. Le ticket reste en `in_progress`, à vous de le déplacer.
