comments.content:
**Bug fixed and committed (`ff2d8a1`).**

**Root cause.** The activity feed's `<ScrollArea>` is a flex item, and flex items default to `min-height: auto` — without `min-h-0` its root is floored at its *content* height, so it grew past the panel instead of scrolling. The ticket-view refonte then switched the panel root from `overflow-y-auto` to `overflow-hidden`, so that overflow — previously reachable via the panel's own scrollbar — is now simply cut off. Measured in Chrome on a 30-comment ticket: a 725px panel holding 12554px of content, wheel events moving nothing, composer parked at 12540px.

**What I changed**
- `min-h-0` on the feed's ScrollArea (the idiom already used in `NamedAgentsTab`), plus `shrink-0` on the header and composer.
- Dropped `min-h-[200px]` from the activity tab wrapper — a floor taller than the remaining space pushed the composer out of the `overflow-hidden` panel, clipping it away permanently. Below ~600px window height the feed is now merely small instead of unreachable.
- Same defect, same fix on the user-story page's comment thread (`components/story/CommentThread.tsx`) — verified broken (801px column holding 2332px), then fixed.
- A second, previously invisible defect: both feeds' auto-scroll wrote `scrollTop` on the content div while the scrolling box is the Radix viewport above it — a silent no-op, so busy tickets opened on their *oldest* entry. Extracted `hooks/useFeedAutoScroll.ts`, which pins the viewport, follows only when the reader is in the bottom band, and re-pins on late layout settling (I traced a 64px shift from the agent action bar appearing after first paint).

**Verification** — `e2e/ticket-activity-scroll.spec.ts` (2 specs) drives the real panel and the real story route; jsdom does no layout, so only a browser catches this. Both were checked red with `min-h-0` removed, so they genuinely pin the regression. Plus 5 unit tests for the hook. Full suite: 4230 Vitest tests and 7/7 e2e green, `tsc --noEmit` and eslint clean. epics.description:
Agents got this error  :

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
Done. Epic **"Board transition refused"** is implemented, tested, and committed as `6669349`.

## What was wrong
The `in_progress` lock in `lib/workflow/engine.ts` refused *any* out-of-`in_progress` move while a queued/running code-producing session existed — and the session list included the acting session itself. So a build agent calling `update_ticket_status` on its own ticket got `INVALID_TRANSITION` from its own session.

## The fix — owning-session exemption
- **`lib/workflow/engine.ts`** — new `ownsInProgress` flag on `TransitionContext`; the lock now fires only on `hasRunningSession && !ownsInProgress`. All other guards (review→done approval/merge, completed-review, open comments, released rules, structural edges) are untouched.
- **`lib/workflow/context.ts`** — `buildTransitionContext` accepts the acting `sessionId`; `ownsInProgress` is true only when the acting session is the **sole** queued/running code-producing session on the ticket (story-scoped when a story is in scope), using the existing reads.
- **`lib/workflow/transition-service.ts`** — threads `sessionId` through both `applyTransition` and `applyStoryTransition`.
- **`lib/claude/prompt-sections.ts`** — build/ticket_build/team_build prompts now tell the agent it may move its own ticket to Review once committed, and to flag a pending transition if refused.

## Preserved invariants (all tested)
- Concurrent second build → ticket stays locked (even for the owner)
- User drags / no session signal → still refused
- Exemption never bypasses approval, completed-review, or structural guards
- Terminal handler promotion unchanged (session is terminal before it validates)

## Tests (full suite: 372 files / 4245 tests green, tsc + eslint clean)
- **Engine**: owner may move own ticket (review/todo/backlog); non-owner, no-signal, and second-session cases refused; exemption doesn't bypass other guards.
- **Service**: owning-session exemption for epic and story transitions, incl. refusal variants.
- **MCP route e2e** (`mcp-routes.test.ts`): the exact reported scenario — an owning `build` session moves its own `in_progress` ticket to review via `update_ticket_status` → 200; a different session's attempt → 409; owner + second live build → 409. (The old test asserting the owner's own move is refused now asserts the opposite.)
- **Prompt tests**: build types get the new sentence; review/chat/merge types don't.
- **Two terminal write-failure tests** (`pipeline-stages-dispatch`, `epic-build-asked-question`) updated: when the session row is left `running` by a failed lifecycle write, the terminal handler acts for the owning session, so the ticket now advances to review and the run settles as success instead of `transition_refused`.

No schema change, no migration, `arji.json` never staged.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
**Code Review**

# Code Review — Bug fix: "Board transition refused" (`6669349`)

**Scope reviewed:** `lib/workflow/engine.ts`, `lib/workflow/context.ts`, `lib/workflow/transition-service.ts`, `lib/claude/prompt-sections.ts`, and the six touched test files. Traced against the callers that consume the changed contract (`app/api/mcp/update-ticket-status/route.ts`, `lib/mcp/http-auth.ts`, `lib/workflow/automatic-transitions.ts`, `lib/auto-mode/select.ts`).

The diagnosis is correct and the core fix is the right shape: the lock counted the acting session among the concurrent movers it exists to protect against, and `ownsInProgress` is a fail-closed, sole-owner exemption threaded through the one entry point that builds a `TransitionContext`. My findings are about the invariants the lock was *also* silently upholding.

---

## 1. Readability

No issues found. The guard comment at `lib/workflow/engine.ts:62-68` and the `ownsInProgress` doc block at `:47-54` state the rule and its boundary precisely; the "sole live session" rationale at `lib/workflow/context.ts:96-98` is exactly the non-obvious part a reader needs.

## 2. DRY Principle

### Minor — duplicated code-producing agent-type list
**Location:** `lib/claude/prompt-sections.ts:205` and `lib/workflow/context.ts:70`

`["build", "ticket_build", "team_build"]` now appears in both files. These two are semantically coupled in a way the others are not: `prompt-sections.ts` decides who is *told* they may move their ticket, `context.ts` decides who is *granted* the exemption. If they drift, a newly added build type gets an instruction it cannot follow — reproducing the exact bug this commit fixes.

There are three further, mutually inconsistent copies already in the tree: `lib/agent-config/review-segregation.ts:45` (omits `team_build`), `lib/agent-config/dispatch-reliability-constants.ts:49`, `lib/auto-mode/select.ts:75` (adds `merge`).

**Recommendation:** export one `CODE_PRODUCING_AGENT_TYPES` (natural home: `lib/agent-config/constants.ts`) and import it in `context.ts` and `prompt-sections.ts`. The other three differ on purpose — leave them.

## 3. Error Handling

### Major — early promotion is never rolled back on failure, question, or cancellation
**Location:** `lib/workflow/automatic-transitions.ts:484-497` (`logBuildFailure`), reachable because of `lib/workflow/engine.ts:69-79`

The prompt added at `prompt-sections.ts:204-212` actively instructs build agents to move their ticket to Review as soon as work is committed. Nothing constrains *when* — an agent can promote and then fail, ask a question, or be cancelled.

The terminal handlers only log. `logBuildFailure` hardcodes `const status = "in_progress"` (`:490`) and writes `Build failed; ticket held in in_progress` — while the epic actually sits in `review`. Before this commit that string was true by construction; now it is a false audit entry, and the ticket is left in Review with a failed build. `lib/auto-mode/select.ts` then treats it as a review candidate, so Full Auto reviews and can merge work that never completed.

**Recommendation:** read the real status via the existing `readEpicStatus` helper instead of hardcoding, and on the `failed` / `awaiting_reply` outcomes return the ticket to `in_progress` through the guarded `applyTransition` when the agent moved it out mid-session.

### Suggestion — refusal message is now misleading to its main audience
**Location:** `lib/workflow/engine.ts:76`

`"Cannot move an in-progress ticket while an agent session is queued or running."` reads as self-contradictory to an agent that *is* a session and was just told it may move its ticket. With the owner exempt, the refusal now always concerns a different session — including on user drags.

**Recommendation:** `"…while another agent session is queued or running."`

## 4. Performance

No issues found. `ownsInProgress` is derived from the `runningSessions` array already materialised for `hasRunningSession` — no additional query, no extra scan.

## 5. Naming Conventions

### Suggestion — `sessionId` silently changed from provenance to authorization
**Location:** `lib/workflow/transition-service.ts:26` and `:56`

`ApplyTransitionOpts.sessionId` was a logging field (`logTransition`, `logRefusedTransition`) and is now also an authorization input. Both are undocumented on the interface. Today every caller happens to pass the acting session — I checked all 24 call sites; the merge paths (`resolve-merge/route.ts:291,312`, `merge/route.ts:247`, `auto-mode/merge.ts:170`) pass a session id but always target `→ done`, which is structurally unreachable from `in_progress`, so no unintended exemption exists. But a future caller passing a session id purely for traceability would silently grant it.

**Recommendation:** document on the field that it must be the *acting* session, mirroring the phrasing already used at `lib/workflow/context.ts:17`.

## 6. Type Safety

No issues found. No `any`; `ownsInProgress?: boolean` defaults to `undefined` → falsy → lock applies, which is the correct fail-closed default for the many contexts constructed without it.

## 7. Testing

Coverage of the intended behaviour is genuinely good — engine, service, and route levels, both refusal directions, plus explicit non-bypass assertions for the approve, completed-review, and structural guards. Two gaps:

### Major — the story-scoped path is untested, and it is broken (see §8)
`applyStoryTransition` gets owner-exemption tests, but the MCP route never calls it. No test covers a `ticket_build` session acting through the route.

### Minor — the exemption is not restricted to `→ review`
**Location:** `lib/workflow/engine.ts:69-79`; blessed by the new test *"allows the owning session to move its own ticket to other reachable columns"*

`EPIC_TRANSITIONS.in_progress` is `["todo", "review", "backlog"]` (`engine.ts:21`), so the owner may also move its ticket to To Do or Backlog. From `todo`, the terminal handler's `todo → review` promotion is structurally invalid, so the run settles as `transition_refused` and the committed work is stranded in To Do — the exact orphaned-column state this engine exists to prevent.

**Recommendation:** tighten to `ctx.ownsInProgress && ctx.toStatus === "review"` and flip that test to assert refusal.

**Note on the two flipped terminal tests** (`pipeline-stages-dispatch`, `epic-build-asked-question`): the new expectations are defensible — a forced lifecycle-write failure leaves the row `running`, the handler acts as that owner, the ticket advances. Worth stating explicitly that this also means a zombie `running` session no longer pins its ticket in `in_progress`; the rewritten test comments justify the change honestly, which is the right call.

## 8. API Design

### Major — a story-scoped build session can promote its parent epic, bypassing the sibling-story guard
**Location:** `app/api/mcp/update-ticket-status/route.ts:44-53`, enabled by `lib/workflow/context.ts:99-102`

The route **always** transitions an epic: `resolveTicketForToken` (`lib/mcp/http-auth.ts:58`) resolves to `record.epicId`, and the route only ever calls `applyTransition` — never `applyStoryTransition`. So `buildTransitionContext` runs epic-scoped, with no `userStoryId`.

A story build session is created with **both** `epicId` and `userStoryId` set and `agentType: "ticket_build"` (`app/api/projects/[projectId]/stories/[storyId]/build/route.ts:236-252`), and `transitionBuildStarted` moves the parent epic to `in_progress` too. It therefore appears in the epic-scoped `runningSessions` query and — as the sole live build — receives `ownsInProgress: true`.

**Failure scenario:** epic E has stories S1 and S2, both `todo`. The user builds S1 only; S1 and E go to `in_progress`. The agent, following the new prompt, calls `update_ticket_status({status: "review"})`. The route targets **E**, the exemption applies, and E moves to Review while S1 is still `in_progress` and S2 is still `todo`.

`transitionBuildCompleted` enforces exactly this rule at `lib/workflow/automatic-transitions.ts:311-315` (`remaining.length === 0` before epic promotion) — spec §3.5, *"Story-scoped work promotes the epic only after all sibling stories are in `review` or `done`"*. The MCP route always bypassed that check; the `in_progress` lock was the only thing making the bypass unreachable, and this commit removes it. `lib/auto-mode/select.ts` then picks the epic up as a review candidate once the session settles.

There is also a smaller correctness gap in the same place: a `ticket_build` agent literally cannot move *its own ticket* (the story) through this route — the stated goal of the ticket is unmet for story scope, while the parent gets over-promoted instead.

**Recommendation:** when the token carries a `storyId`, route through `applyStoryTransition` so the context is story-scoped and epic promotion stays with `transitionBuildCompleted`. A narrower alternative: in `context.ts`, refuse `ownsInProgress` when the sole live session has a `userStoryId` but the context is epic-scoped.

Otherwise the API surface is consistent: 409 + `INVALID_TRANSITION`, `released` still absent from the input enum, `{ data }` shape preserved.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 2 |
| Minor | 2 |
| Suggestion | 2 |

The fix correctly identifies and repairs the reported defect, and it does not weaken the guards that matter most — `review → done` still needs approve/merge, `released` is still system-only, structural edges are intact, and concurrent builds still lock. I verified each of those, and the new tests assert them directly.

What blocks approval is the second-order effect: the `in_progress` lock was load-bearing for two invariants beyond concurrency. Removing it for the owner lets a story agent promote its parent epic past the sibling-story rule (§8), and lets a failed or cancelled build leave its ticket parked in Review with an activity log that says otherwise (§3). Both are reachable through the exact behaviour the new prompt now instructs agents to perform, and both feed tickets into Full Auto's review/merge path. Fix 1 and 2 with the regression tests described, and this is good to land.

A remediation plan with the concrete edits and red→green test cases is at `/home/orosius/.claude/plans/project-arij-jiggly-petal.md`.

*Plan mode is active for this session, so I did not post these as `submit_findings` / `post_comment` on the board, and I did not run the test suite — no board write and no transition was attempted. The findings above are from static tracing of the full call graph.*

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
**Code Review**

# Code Review — Bug fix: "Board transition refused" (remediation round)

**Scope reviewed:** the five commits `6669349 → b44c43a` against merge-base `c9eda8d` — `lib/workflow/{engine,context,transition-service,automatic-transitions}.ts`, `lib/agent-config/constants.ts`, `lib/claude/prompt-sections.ts`, `app/api/mcp/update-ticket-status/route.ts`, `app/api/projects/[projectId]/build/route.ts`, and the seven touched test files. Traced against the consumers of the changed contract: `lib/mcp/http-auth.ts`, `lib/mcp/token-store.ts`, `lib/claude/process-manager.ts`, `bin/arij-mcp.mjs`, `lib/auto-mode/select.ts`, `lib/agents/scheduler.ts`, `lib/agent-sessions/boot-cleanup.ts`, `instrumentation.ts`, and all four `finalizeBuildTerminalOutcome` call sites.

The two Majors from the previous round are genuinely fixed, and I verified each by tracing rather than trusting the summary:

- **§8 (story session over-promoting the epic)** — `context.ts:113` refuses `ownsInProgress` when the sole live session carries a `userStoryId` but the context is epic-scoped, and the route defaults a story token to `applyStoryTransition`. The sibling-story rule in `transitionBuildCompleted:311-315` is no longer bypassable from the MCP channel.
- **§3 (ticket parked in Review with a lying audit entry)** — `pullTicketBackIfPromoted` is correctly scoped (epic vs story), returns the *real* status, and `logBuildFailure` names it instead of hardcoding. The four new rollback tests in `automatic-transition-invariants.test.ts:392-531` assert both the transition and the audit string.

What I found this round is the same class of defect, in the two places the rollback and the ownership model still do not reach.

---

## 1. Readability

No issues found. The comment at `lib/workflow/engine.ts:64-72` explaining *why* only `→ review` is exempt, and the ownership rationale at `lib/workflow/context.ts:102-108`, are exactly the non-obvious parts a reader needs. The `CODE_PRODUCING_AGENT_TYPES` doc block at `lib/agent-config/constants.ts:21-29` correctly names the three sibling lists that must stay separate.

## 2. DRY Principle

No issues found. `CODE_PRODUCING_AGENT_TYPES` resolves the duplication cleanly and the doc block explains why `review-segregation`, `dispatch-reliability` and `auto-mode/select` keep their own lists. The second story-status read in `pullTicketBackIfPromoted:532-538` duplicates the first, but it is a deliberate re-read after a refused write, not copy-paste.

## 3. Error Handling

### Minor — the failure path can now throw where it previously could not
**Location:** `lib/workflow/automatic-transitions.ts:571-579` and `:648-656`

`logBuildFailure` was pure logging: `logWorkflowDecision` → `logTransition`, which catches internally. `lib/workflow/agent-question.ts:38-40` documents the contract these handlers run under — *"best-effort by design; it runs inside background completion blocks and must never throw into them."*

It now calls `pullTicketBackIfPromoted`, which performs `applyTransition`/`applyStoryTransition` — DB writes plus `emitTicketMoved` — with no try/catch. The success path is protected (`transitionBuildCompleted:401-405` catches everything and degrades to `refused`); the failure and question paths are not, and no call site wraps them: `epics/[epicId]/build/route.ts:339` and `stories/[storyId]/build/route.ts:306` both call `finalizeBuildTerminalOutcome` bare.

**Failure scenario:** any throw inside the pullback rejects `runBuildSession`, so the agent's output comment (`stories/[storyId]/build/route.ts:317-327`) is never written and the run settles through the scheduler's safety net instead of its own handler. The pre-fix code could not fail this way — the one thing the failure path did was already exception-proof.

**Recommendation:** wrap `pullTicketBackIfPromoted`'s body in try/catch, returning the last-read status on error — the same shape `transitionBuildCompleted` already uses.

### Minor — the team build's asked_question hold still hardcodes `in_progress`
**Location:** `app/api/projects/[projectId]/build/route.ts:421-436`

The per-epic `pullTicketBackIfPromoted` return values are discarded and `handleAskedQuestionOutcome` is handed a literal `"in_progress"` — the exact hardcoded-lie shape this remediation fixed at `finalizeBuildTerminalOutcome:648-661`. It is reachable rather than theoretical because coordinated team epics have no lock at all (see §8), so an epic can genuinely be sitting in `todo` or `backlog` when the hold is logged.

**Recommendation:** collect the returned statuses and log per epic with its real one. `handleAskedQuestionOutcome` takes a single `ticketStatus` for N epics, so this needs either a status map or one call per epic.

## 4. Performance

No issues found. `ownsInProgress` reuses the `runningSessions` array already materialised for `hasRunningSession` — no extra query. The pullback adds at most one indexed read plus one guarded write per terminal outcome, on a path that already does several.

## 5. Naming Conventions

### Minor — `logBuildFailure` now mutates board state
**Location:** `lib/workflow/automatic-transitions.ts:562`

It is the only `log*` function in the module that writes a status; `logWorkflowDecision` and `logTransition` are pure. Its doc block explains the new behaviour, but the name still promises otherwise to anyone reading the two call sites (`build/route.ts:439`, `finalizeBuildTerminalOutcome:666`) or adding a third.

**Recommendation:** rename to `holdFailedBuild` or `recordBuildFailure`.

### Minor — the refusal message misleads the session it now most often refuses
**Location:** `lib/workflow/engine.ts:83`

A story build that passes `ticket_id: <epic>` is refused with *"while **another** agent session is queued or running"* — but there is no other session. It is refused by the ownership gate at `context.ts:113`. That is precisely the confusing-message problem this ticket was filed about, relocated one case over. The new test (`mcp-routes.test.ts`, *"refuses the story build moving its parent epic"*) asserts only the 409 and `code`, so nothing pins the wording.

**Recommendation:** give the gate its own message, e.g. *"A story build may only move its own story; the parent epic is promoted once every sibling story reaches review."*

## 6. Type Safety

No `any`, and `ownsInProgress?: boolean` defaults falsy → lock applies, the correct fail-closed default for the many contexts built without a session id.

### Suggestion — redundant cast suppresses a check worth keeping
**Location:** `app/api/mcp/update-ticket-status/route.ts:89`

After the `backlog` early return at `:73-82`, `toStatus` is narrowed to exactly `StoryStatus`, so `as StoryStatus` is a no-op today — its only effect is to suppress the compile error a future `bodySchema` enum addition *should* raise. Runtime stays protected by `isAllowedTransition`, so this is hardening, not a bug. Also `:57-63` selects every story column where `{ id, status }` would do; `pullTicketBackIfPromoted:511-515` already uses the narrow projection.

## 7. Testing

Coverage of the intended behaviour is strong — engine, service and route levels, both refusal directions, the story-scoped path end-to-end, and explicit non-bypass assertions for the approve, completed-review and structural guards. The four rollback tests assert the transition *and* the audit string, and the *"names the real status when the ticket never left its column"* case (`:501-530`) pins the exact lie that was fixed. The two flipped terminal tests are honestly re-commented: they now assert that a zombie `running` row no longer pins its ticket, which is the correct consequence and worth having stated in the test itself.

Gaps, all downstream of the findings above: no test reaches the route with a `team_build` token (§8), nothing covers the restart path (§3-below), and the story-vs-epic refusal test does not assert the message (§5).

## 8. API Design

### Major — `team_build` is told to move a ticket it cannot address, and the workaround bypasses the new restriction
**Location:** `lib/agent-config/constants.ts:31` + `lib/claude/prompt-sections.ts:204-212`, enabled by `app/api/projects/[projectId]/build/route.ts:329-343`

A team session row is created with **no `epicId`** — `createQueuedSession` at `build/route.ts:329-343` passes `id, projectId, mode, orchestrationMode, provider, prompt, logsPath, cliSessionId, namedAgentId, agentType, namedAgentName, model, createdAt` and nothing else. So its MCP token carries `epicId: null` (`process-manager.ts:119-134`). But `team_build` is in `CODE_PRODUCING_AGENT_TYPES`, so `arijToolsSection` appends the new sentence to its prompt — and `mcp-injection.test.ts:412-421` asserts it does.

**Failure scenario A:** the team agent follows the instruction verbatim and calls `update_ticket_status({status: "review"})`. `resolveTicketForToken` (`lib/mcp/http-auth.ts:58-68`) sees a null `targetId` and returns **400 `MISSING_TICKET` — "This session is not attached to a ticket."** The capability the prompt promises does not exist for this agent type.

**Failure scenario B:** the agent works around it with `ticket_id: <epic>`. `buildTransitionContext` matches live sessions on `agentSessions.epicId` (`context.ts:82`); the team row has none, so `hasRunningSession` is `false` and the guard at `engine.ts:73-86` never executes. The `→ review`-only restriction added in `e2fe99e` is gated on that guard running, so it does not apply: the team agent may move a coordinated epic to `todo` or `backlog`. `pullTicketBackIfPromoted` only undoes `review`, so a failed team build then logs `Build failed; ticket held in in_progress` while the epic sits in `backlog` — reintroducing the exact false audit entry `31ebc4d` was written to remove.

The unguarded team move predates this branch; what is new is that agents are now actively instructed to perform it, which turns a latent hole into a live one.

**Recommendation:** stop emitting the sentence for `team_build`. Keep `CODE_PRODUCING_AGENT_TYPES` as the engine/ownership list and give `prompt-sections.ts` a narrower list (or filter `team_build` with a comment pointing at the null `epicId`). Test: flip the `it.each` in `mcp-injection.test.ts` so `team_build` asserts `not.toContain(...)`, and add an `mcp-routes` case proving the 400.

### Major — a mid-run promotion survives a restart with no rollback and no audit entry
**Location:** `lib/agent-sessions/boot-cleanup.ts:115-152`, reachable because of `lib/workflow/engine.ts:79`

`failOrphanedRunningSessions` marks zombie rows failed and performs **no board work** — I checked `instrumentation.ts:37-46`; nothing else reconciles ticket state at boot. `lib/agents/scheduler.ts:248-256` (`handleLaunchFailure`) has the same shape.

**Failure scenario:** an agent commits, calls `update_ticket_status → review` (the exemption grants it), and the server restarts — or the launch closure rejects — before the dispatch route's terminal block runs. The session is recorded `failed`; the epic stays in `review`; no activity entry is written at all, because `logBuildFailure` never runs on this path. `instrumentation.ts` then starts Full Auto in the same boot, and `selectReviewCandidates` (`lib/auto-mode/select.ts:648-660`) takes any epic in `review` not reviewed since its last code change — which this one is, since the failed build is the newest code session. It gets reviewed, and on a clean verdict `selectMergeCandidates` will merge it.

Before the exemption this was structurally impossible: the lock kept a crashed run's ticket in `in_progress`. The remediation closed this hole for the three in-process terminal paths; the boot sweep is the fourth, and it is the one that fires precisely when the in-process handler *didn't*.

**Recommendation:** `failOrphanedRunningSessions` already iterates the rows and has everything it needs. Select `epicId`, `userStoryId` and `agentType` alongside `id`, and after `markSessionTerminal` call the existing `pullTicketBackIfPromoted` for rows whose `agentType` is in `CODE_PRODUCING_AGENT_TYPES` and that have an `epicId` (scope `"story"` when `userStoryId` is set), with `ORPHANED_BY_RESTART_REASON`. Guard per row so one bad row cannot abort the sweep, matching the loop's existing style. Do the same in `handleLaunchFailure`. Red→green: seed an epic in `review` plus a `running` `build` row, call `failOrphanedRunningSessions()`, expect `in_progress`.

### Suggestion — the shim's shared `ticket_id` description is now wrong for one of the two tools it decorates
**Location:** `bin/arij-mcp.mjs:46-53`

`TICKET_ID_PROPERTY` says *"Defaults to the ticket this session was launched for"* and is spread into both `get_ticket` and `update_ticket_status`. | Major | 2 |
| Minor | 4 |
| Suggestion | 2 |

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
**Code Review**

# Code Review — Bug fix: "Board transition refused" (round 3)

**Scope reviewed:** the seven commits `6669349 → d1e86f7` against merge-base `c9eda8d`, with a focus on this round's two: `58c993a` (team_build prompt gating) and `d1e86f7` (restart/launch-failure rollback). Traced against the consumers of the changed contracts: `instrumentation.ts`, `lib/agent-sessions/lifecycle.ts`, `lib/agent-sessions/terminal-hooks.ts`, `lib/auto-mode/{engine,select}.ts`, `lib/mcp/http-auth.ts`, `bin/arij-mcp.mjs`, `lib/claude/mcp-injection.ts`, and all four `finalizeBuildTerminalOutcome` / `markSessionTerminal` build call sites.

**Unlike the previous two rounds, I ran the checks:** `npx vitest run` → **372 files / 4262 tests pass**, `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `git status` clean (no `arji.json`). The branch's own claim holds.

Both round-2 Majors are genuinely closed, verified by tracing rather than by the summary:

- **team_build** — `createQueuedSession` at `build/route.ts:329-343` really does omit `epicId`, so the token is ticket-less; the prompt sentence is now gated on `CODE_PRODUCING_AGENT_TYPES` minus `team_build` (`prompt-sections.ts:211-213`), and `mcp-routes.test.ts:623-655` pins the 400 `MISSING_TICKET` with nothing moved. The tool stays in the uniform agent allowlist (`mcp-injection.ts:50-57`), which is the right call — the allowlist is not per-type, and the prompt is the correct lever.
- **restart orphans** — `failOrphanedRunningSessions` now pulls the promotion back, and I confirmed the boot ordering it depends on: `instrumentation.ts:43-44` runs the sweep *before* `startAutoMode()` (`:52`) and before `setSessionTerminalHook` (`:63`), so nothing observes the ticket mid-rollback. At runtime the `kickAutoMode` debounce (`auto-mode/engine.ts:875-911`, 250 ms into a later macrotask) covers the same ordering for the scheduler path.

What I found this round is one case where the new rollback fires against a session that *had* settled.

---

## 1. Readability

No issues found. The three new doc blocks earn their length: `boot-cleanup.ts:114-120` explains *why* the sweep is the fourth terminal path, `scheduler.ts:270-275` mirrors it, and `constants.ts:21-29` names the prompt-side exception and the three sibling lists that must stay separate.

## 2. DRY Principle

No issues found. `isCodeProducingAgentType()` gives the two new call sites one predicate instead of two inline `includes`.

### Suggestion — name the prompt-side list
**Location:** `lib/claude/prompt-sections.ts:211-213`

`(CODE_PRODUCING_AGENT_TYPES as readonly string[]).filter((type) => type !== "team_build")` is rebuilt on every call and expresses the derivation inline. Exporting `TICKET_MOVING_AGENT_TYPES` next to its parent in `constants.ts` would make the relationship visible from the constants file and testable on its own.

## 3. Error Handling

### Major — the launch-failure net reverts a *delivered* build's promotion
**Location:** `lib/agents/scheduler.ts:270-302`

`handleLaunchFailure` fires whenever the launch closure rejects — which includes a throw in the **tail** of `runBuildSession`, after `finalizeBuildTerminalOutcome` already promoted the epic to Review. That tail is real code: `emitSessionCompleted`, `resolveSessionOutput`, and the `db.insert(ticketComments)` at `epics/[epicId]/build/route.ts:366-372`; the pipeline wrapper at `route.ts:394-408` catches, settles the stage, and **rethrows on purpose** to reach this net.

The early return at `:241-246` inspects the *launch* error, not the row's state. So in that case the row is already `completed`, the inner `markSessionTerminal` throws a `SessionLifecycleConflictError` (`lifecycle.ts:216-227` — terminal statuses have no outbound transitions), that throw is caught and silenced at `:258-268`, and the new pullback then runs unconditionally.

**Failure scenario:** epic build for E succeeds → `transitionBuildCompleted` moves E to `review` → the comment insert throws (SQLite busy / disk error) → closure rejects → `handleLaunchFailure` → `pullTicketBackIfPromoted` reads `review`, applies `review → in_progress`, and writes an activity entry saying *"Build session launch failed; returning ticket to in_progress"*. The work is delivered and committed, the session row says `completed`, and the board now says the epic is still being built. `selectBuildCandidates` (`lib/auto-mode/select.ts:597-620`) treats an `in_progress` epic with no live session as buildable, so Full Auto re-dispatches a build over finished work.

This is the round-2 §3 defect in the mirror direction: an audit entry that names a status the board only has *because this code put it there*. The scheduler's own doc block at `:234-238` already knows the state ("the closure already finalized the row before failing") — it just doesn't gate on it.

**Recommendation:** record whether `markSessionTerminal` succeeded and run the pullback only then; a lifecycle conflict means the closure owned the board effects. Red→green: seed a `completed` row whose epic is in `review`, make the lifecycle mock throw a conflict, reject the launch with a plain `Error` — assert `dbMockState.updateCalls` stays empty.

### Minor — the boot sweep undoes a legitimate promotion in one documented state
**Location:** `lib/agent-sessions/boot-cleanup.ts:143-180`

`status = 'running'` is a good proxy for "the in-process handler never ran", and the pullback is correctly guarded per row. But this branch's *own* flipped tests (`pipeline-stages-dispatch`, `epic-build-asked-question`) establish the state where the proxy is wrong: a failed lifecycle write leaves the row `running` while the terminal handler promotes the ticket as the owning session. At the next boot the sweep demotes that delivered ticket to `in_progress` with reason "orphaned by restart". Note also that the pullback runs even when `markSessionTerminal` itself failed for that row (it sits outside the `failed++` branch).

The direction is conservative (work returns to `in_progress`, nothing gets merged), which is why this is Minor rather than Major — but it should be a stated trade-off in the doc block, not an unexamined one.

**Recommendation:** move the pullback inside the successful-mark branch and name the residual case in the comment.

### Carried over, still open (all Minor, all acknowledged in the branch's follow-up queue)
- `pullTicketBackIfPromoted` is unguarded inside `logBuildFailure` (`automatic-transitions.ts:572`) and the `asked_question` path (`:648`) — a throw there rejects `runBuildSession` and loses the agent's output comment. Note the interaction with the Major above: that throw now *also* triggers the scheduler pullback.
- The team build's `asked_question` hold still passes a hardcoded `ticketStatus: "in_progress"` (`build/route.ts:436`) while discarding the per-epic statuses the loop above it just computed.
- `logBuildFailure` mutates board state under a `log*` name.

## 4. Performance

No issues found. The sweep adds one indexed read plus at most one guarded write per zombie row, at boot; `handleLaunchFailure` adds one point read on an error path. Neither is on a request path.

## 5. Naming Conventions

### Minor — refusal messages still name a session that is not there
**Location:** `lib/workflow/engine.ts:83`, reached via the gate at `lib/workflow/context.ts:109-113`

A story build passing `ticket_id: <parent epic>` is refused with *"…while **another** agent session is queued or running"* — but there is no other session; it is refused by the ownership gate. That is this ticket's original complaint, relocated one case over. The existing test (*"refuses the story build moving its parent epic"*) asserts only the status and `code`, so nothing pins the wording. The queued follow-up #4 covers the concurrent-build variant of the same message but not this one.

**Recommendation:** give the ownership gate its own message — *"A story build may only move its own story; the parent epic is promoted once every sibling story reaches review."*

## 6. Type Safety

No `any`. `isCodeProducingAgentType` takes `string | null | undefined`, matching the nullable `agentType` column, and the two `as readonly string[]` casts are the standard `as const` widening, not suppression. `ownsInProgress?: boolean` still defaults falsy → lock applies, the correct fail-closed default.

## 7. Testing

Strong and honest. The four boot-cleanup cases cover both scopes plus two no-ops (ticket never in Review; non-code-producing zombie), and they assert the **activity row** — `fromStatus`/`toStatus`/`actor`/`sessionId`/reason — not just the status column. The story case explicitly asserts the epic and the sibling do *not* move, which is the sibling-story rule the sweep must not front-run. The scheduler pair covers the pullback and the ticket-less no-op. `mcp-injection` now asserts the sentence's absence for `team_build`, for reviewers, and for the auxiliary types, so a future addition to `CODE_PRODUCING_AGENT_TYPES` cannot silently re-promise the move.

Gaps, both downstream of the findings above: nothing covers a launch failure on an **already-terminal** session (§3 Major), and nothing pins the refusal wording (§5).

## 8. API Design

### Minor — the story branch returns a `ticketId` no MCP route accepts
**Location:** `app/api/mcp/update-ticket-status/route.ts:106` + `bin/arij-mcp.mjs:46-53`

The story branch returns `ticketId: story.id`, but `resolveTicketForToken` (`lib/mcp/http-auth.ts:70-81`) resolves **epics only** — so an agent that echoes that id back as `ticket_id`, to either tool, gets `404 TICKET_NOT_FOUND`. The shared `TICKET_ID_PROPERTY` description ("Defaults to the ticket this session was launched for") is now true of two different tickets depending on which tool it decorates: `get_ticket` → the epic, `update_ticket_status` → the story. This was raised as a Suggestion last round and is not in the deferred queue; given the ticket exists because agents got confusing answers from this exact channel, it is worth the two-line description split.

Otherwise the surface is consistent: 409 + `INVALID_TRANSITION` on both branches, 400 `MISSING_TICKET` for ticket-less tokens, `{ data }` preserved, `released` absent from the enum, and `backlog` correctly rejected before it can be written into a story row.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 1 |
| Minor | 3 (+3 carried over, acknowledged) |
| Suggestion | 1 |

The round-3 work is well aimed and the two Majors it targeted are closed — I traced the ticket-less team session row, the boot ordering against Full Auto's start, and the kick debounce, and each holds. The guards that matter are intact: `review → done` still requires approve/merge, `released` is system-only, structural edges hold, concurrent builds still lock, user drags are still refused, and the sibling-story rule is no longer reachable from the MCP channel. Suite, types and tree verified green on this checkout.

What blocks approval is that the rollback added this round fires one case too wide. `handleLaunchFailure` cannot tell "the closure never settled the board" from "the closure settled it and then threw on the way out", so a delivered build whose tail errors has its Review promotion silently reverted and its epic handed back to Full Auto's build selector — with an activity entry that says the launch failed. It is a three-line gate on the lifecycle conflict the code already catches, with an obvious red→green test. Fix that, and the two Minors that pin the wording and the `ticket_id` contract, and this lands.

A remediation plan with the concrete edits and test cases is at `/home/orosius/.claude/plans/project-arij-robust-rocket.md`.

*Plan mode is active for this session, so I did not post these via `submit_findings` / `post_comment` and attempted no transition — the ticket's board state is unchanged. I did run the read-only verification (`vitest`, `tsc`) against an in-memory test database; nothing on disk was modified.*

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

epics.title: MCP : permettre aux agents de créer des tickets de bug
epics.description:
## Contexte

Les agents qui travaillent sur Arij (via les outils MCP `mcp__arij__*`) disposent déjà de : lecture de ticket, commentaires, question bloquante, mise à jour de statut (gardée par le workflow engine) et soumission de findings. Il leur manque un outil pour **signaler un bug** rencontré pendant leur travail — par exemple dans l'utilisation des MCP eux-mêmes, ou dans l'app Arij qu'ils manipulent en live.

Aujourd'hui, si un agent tombe sur un bug adjacent hors du scope de son ticket, il ne peut que le mentionner en commentaire ou dans son rapport final — ce qui se perd facilement.

## Comportement attendu

- Nouvel outil MCP `create_bug` (ou équivalent) permettant à un agent de créer un ticket de bug sur le projet courant, avec :
  - titre
  - description (markdown) : contexte, étapes de reproduction observées, erreur constatée
  - sévérité suggérée (optionnel)
  - référence optionnelle au ticket/session source pour la traçabilité
- Le bug créé passe par le chemin canonique de création de tickets (même route que l'UI), donc : ID lisible généré (`B-arij-NNN`), export `arji.json` déclenché, activité loggée.
- Anti-abus : un agent ne doit pas pouvoir spammer — déduplication simple conseillée (ex. refus ou warning si un bug ouvert a un titre quasi identique) et plafond raisonnable par session.
- Le bug créé apparaît dans le board comme tout bug (carte rouge), et la session source est référencée dans son activité.

## Notes

- S'appuyer sur l'architecture MCP existante décrite dans la spec §6.5 (token court-lived scopé session/projet/épic/story).
- Penser au cas où l'agent travaille sur un projet autre qu'Arij lui-même : le bug doit être créé sur le projet courant de l'agent, ce qui permet aussi aux agents de signaler des bugs dans *n'importe quel* projet qu'ils buildent.
- Ne pas confondre avec les review findings (ancrés fichier/ligne, bloquants avant merge) : ici c'est un vrai ticket de bug autonome, non bloquant pour la session courante.

comments.content:
**Code Review**

ExitPlanMode isn't available in this session, so here is the review report directly. Note that plan mode blocked me from filing these through `mcp__arij__submit_findings` — that step is pending your approval.

---

# Code Review — Epic: MCP, permettre aux agents de créer des tickets de bug

**Branch:** `feature/epic-gUVMNLV4GzG2-mcp-permettre-aux-agents-de-cr-er-des-ti`
**Commits reviewed:** `5442dfc`, `a4a4460`, `7f29f88` (17 files, +1213/−7 against merge-base `4957611`)

## Verification performed

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `vitest` on the 5 affected test files | **126 passed / 5 files** |
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | clean |
| `npx eslint` on the 7 changed source files | clean |

The concurrency test at `__tests__/mcp-create-bug.test.ts:321` genuinely exercises the race it claims to: both calls run their synchronous pre-checks before either awaits `fetch`, so only the transactional check in `app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/route.ts:404` can be what stops the second insert. Confirmed by reading, not just by the green tick.

## Acceptance criteria

All three stories are met.

1. **Tool exists and creates a readable-id bug on the current project.** `create_bug` is in `AGENT_TOOLS` (`bin/arij-mcp.mjs:123`), the shared allowlist (`lib/claude/mcp-injection.ts:56`, consumed by both Claude and Codex), and the tools prompt section (`lib/claude/prompt-sections.ts:196`). Creation goes through `POST /api/projects/:id/epics` — the same route `lib/chat/board-tools.ts:437` uses — so `generateReadableId`, `emitTicketCreated` and `tryExportArjiJson` are inherited rather than re-implemented. Project scope comes from the token, never the body.
2. **Provenance is trustworthy.** The audit row is inserted *inside* the creation transaction (`epics/route.ts:445`), so a failing audit rolls back the ticket and skips the export — proven by the trigger-based test at `mcp-create-bug.test.ts:235`. Attribution requires a live, non-chat, same-project bearer; spoofed headers alone produce an ordinary unattributed UI write (`mcp-create-bug.test.ts:261`). Writing the row directly rather than via `logTransition` is the right call here, since `logTransition` swallows its own errors and would defeat the atomicity.
3. **Spam is limited.** Normalized-title dedup refuses with an explicit `409 DUPLICATE_BUG` carrying the existing bug's id, readable id, title and status — not a silent drop.

## Checklist

**Readability** — Strong. Every non-obvious decision carries a comment that explains the *why* (the `create-bug.ts` header on why the canonical route owns id allocation; the `create-bug-contract.ts` note that the activity prefix is a durable marker; the `normalizeBugTitle` note on why fuzzy matching was rejected). Matches the density of the surrounding code.

**DRY** — Mostly good: the activity-reason marker, severities and headers live in one contract module shared by server, UI and tests, and `findOpenDuplicateBug` takes a `Pick<ArijDatabase, "select">` so the same function serves the fast path and the transactional path. Three smaller duplications noted below (#2, #3, #5, #6).

**Error handling** — Every failure mode returns a typed `{ok:false, status, code, error}` rather than throwing: fetch rejection → 502 `CANONICAL_CREATE_UNAVAILABLE`, non-JSON body → status fallback, missing `data.id` → 502 `INVALID_CANONICAL_RESPONSE`. No unhandled rejections.

**Performance** — `findOpenDuplicateBug` scans all open bugs of the project and normalizes in JS. There's no index on `epics(project_id)` — but the existing `GET /epics` already full-scans the same table, so this is consistent with the codebase, not a regression. At board scale it's microseconds.

**Naming conventions** — Consistent. camelCase internally, snake_case on the wire (`source_ticket_id`, `existing_bug`, `readable_id`), matching every sibling MCP route.

**Type safety** — No `any`. The `unknown` narrowing in `upstreamErrorBody` and the response parsing is hand-rolled but honest — each field is checked before use.

**API design** — Follows the sibling routes exactly: `requireMcpToken` → chat 403 → `validateBody` → `{data}` envelope. Status codes are apt (409 duplicate, 429 cap, 404 source ticket, 403 chat, 502 upstream).

**Testing** — 9 focused cases covering the happy path, atomicity, anti-spoofing, punctuation/case dedup, the concurrent race, the cap, cross-project source tickets, chat rejection and upstream failure passthrough. Gaps noted in #4.

---

## Findings

### 1. Minor — per-session cap is check-then-act outside the transaction
**`lib/mcp/create-bug.ts:222`**

`countSessionCreatedBugs` runs synchronously *before* `await fetch`, while the audit row that feeds the counter is only written inside the canonical route's transaction. Two `create_bug` calls emitted in the same agent turn (Claude routinely batches parallel tool calls) both observe the same count and both pass, so a session at 4 can reach 6.

Commit `7f29f88` closed exactly this shape of race for the duplicate-title check by repeating it inside the transaction. The cap was left outside.

**Recommendation:** carry the session id through the existing header channel and repeat the count inside `db.transaction` at `epics/route.ts:403`, throwing a `BugLimitReachedError` that mirrors `DuplicateMcpBugError`. The plumbing is already there.

### 2. Minor — unescaped `_` wildcard in the rate-limit `LIKE`
**`lib/mcp/create-bug.ts:134`**

`MCP_CREATE_BUG_ACTIVITY_PREFIX` is `"Agent MCP create_bug:"`, and `_` is a single-character LIKE wildcard, so the predicate also matches `Agent MCP create-bug:`, `createXbug:`, etc. Harmless today because nothing else writes such a reason — but it gives this marker a *third* matching semantic, different from both `isMcpCreateBugActivityReason` (UI) and `startsWith` (session actions). Divergent matchers on a marker the contract module explicitly asks you to keep stable will drift.

**Recommendation:** add `ESCAPE`, or drop the SQL predicate and filter the session's rows with `isMcpCreateBugActivityReason` in JS, as `arij-actions.ts` already does.

### 3. Minor — `resolveSourceTicket` bypasses the declared single ticket-resolution path
**`lib/mcp/create-bug.ts:141`**

`lib/mcp/http-auth.ts:9` states that `resolveTicketForToken` is "the ONLY way a request picks a ticket". The new function re-implements project-scoped lookup and additionally accepts readable ids, which `resolveTicketForToken` does not. An agent that discovers `B-arij-014` works for `create_bug`'s `source_ticket_id` will get a 404 passing the same value to `get_ticket` or `post_comment`.

**Recommendation:** add readable-id support to `resolveTicketForToken` and call it here — every tool benefits and the stated invariant holds. If it must stay separate, say why in the header comment.

### 4. Minor — test gaps on untested branches
**`__tests__/mcp-create-bug.test.ts`**

Three branches carry real regression risk and have no coverage:
- `notInArray(epics.status, ["done","released"])` (`create-bug.ts:116`) — nothing asserts that a **closed** bug with the same title does *not* block creation. Break this filter and the tool refuses forever on any previously-fixed bug.
- `CANONICAL_CREATE_UNAVAILABLE` (fetch throws) and `INVALID_CANONICAL_RESPONSE` (missing `data.id`) — hand-rolled narrowing, no test.
- The cap is asserted for one session but never that another session's rows don't count toward it.

### 5. Suggestion — inline re-implementation of an exported predicate
**`lib/agent-sessions/arij-actions.ts:347`**

The file already imports from `create-bug-contract`; use `isMcpCreateBugActivityReason(row.reason)` for the test and keep the prefix only for the `slice`.

### 6. Suggestion — validation `details` dropped on passthrough
**`lib/mcp/create-bug.ts:159`**

`upstreamErrorBody` keeps only `error` and `code`. `lib/chat/board-tools.ts:295` (`passthroughFailure`) exists specifically to forward zod `details` "so the model can self-correct a rejected call". Today the MCP schema mirrors `createEpicSchema`'s caps exactly (200 / 10000 / priority 0–3), so this is only reachable once the two schemas drift — which is precisely when the agent would need the field-level detail most.

### 7. Suggestion — the source ticket gets no trace
**`app/api/projects/[projectId]/epics/route.ts:440`**

The audit row is written with `epicId: <new bug>`. The epic the agent was building shows nothing, so a user reading the source ticket cannot discover the bug it spawned; the link only works in the other direction. Consider a same-state activity row (or a short comment) on the source ticket too.

### 8. Suggestion — activity detail repeats the linked session id
**`components/kanban/epic-detail/EpicActivityFeed.tsx:304`**

The row renders "View source session" as a link *and* the raw `source session <nanoid>` in the italic detail. Trim that clause when the link is shown.

### 9. Suggestion — anti-abuse guards cover the MCP path only
**`lib/mcp/create-bug.ts`**

Both dedup and cap key off `x-arij-mcp-action` plus a valid token. Agents have shell access on the same host and `/api/projects/:id/epics` and `/bugs` are unauthenticated, so `curl` bypasses both. Separately, `ticket_activity_log.epic_id` cascades on delete, so deleting agent-created bugs restores the session's budget. Neither is exploitable by a well-behaved agent and neither is fixable without route auth — but a comment recording that the guard is a convention, not an enforcement boundary, would keep the next reader from over-trusting it.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| Major | 0 |
| Minor | 4 |
| Suggestion | 5 |

Nothing here blocks the merge. The two things most worth doing before it lands are #1 (finish the job `7f29f88` started — move the cap into the transaction alongside the dedup) and #4 (the closed-bug-title case is the one silent-failure mode that would make the tool useless without anyone noticing).

Live validation of the tool is correctly deferred: the running orchestrator executes `main`, so the new MCP surface only takes effect after merge and restart. The comment history says this plainly rather than claiming a live check, which is the right call.

**Overall Verdict: Approved with Minor Issues**

epics.description:
## Contexte

Aujourd'hui, le project memory (document Markdown unique, borné, §5.4 du spec) vit dans une surface dédiée et mineure de l'UI, alors qu'en amont il a exactement le même statut que la spec : c'est injecté dans les prompts de build/review/chat à côté de la spec (§5.3, « project context »), c'est le support de la distillation par session et du Dreaming croisé-sessions, et c'est réécrit par l'agent avec garde-fous (§6.8 : verrou mémoire-écriver, refus d'écraser un edit manuel concurrent, snapshot pré-Dreaming conservé).

L'UI ne reflète pas ce poids. Ce ticket rend le memory **premier citoyen** : il intègre la section spec, y occupe un espace équivalent, et obtient un éditeur à la hauteur de la spec.

## Périphérie (ce qui ne change PAS)

- **Zéro changement moteur** : la logique de Dreaming / distillation / verrou / snapshot / injection prompt reste telle quelle. C'est un ticket UI + surface.
- **Zéro migration** : le document mémoire est déjà persisté comme aujourd'hui ; pas de nouvelle table ni de nouvelle colonne.
- **`arji.json` inchangé** : la spec est ré-exportée, le memory ne l'est pas ; on garde ça.
- Les règles de concurrence du §6.8 s'appliquent au nouvel éditeur tel quel, on ne les assouplit pas.

## Décisions tranchées (points ouverts résolus)

- **Mise en page** : 2 panneaux pairs côte à côte (Spec | Memory) dans la section ; empilement vertical sur mobile.
- **Intitulé de nav** : l'entrée est renommée **« Spec & Memory »**.
- **Cap mémoire : haussé.** La section gagne du poids, donc le cap suit : on l'élève d'un cran (ordre de ~1,5× le cap actuel ; valeur exacte à figer en implémentation, arrondie à un chiffre propre, documentée en tête de code). Si on choisit de l'exposer en réglage de projet, c'est une clé free-form de la table settings — aucune migration requise.
- **Les 4 sections requises du Dreaming** (`Codebase pitfalls`, `Recurring agent mistakes`, `Strategies that work`, `Build instructions`) sont proposées comme **squelette** quand le document est vide ou non conforme, mais le reste du corps est du Markdown libre — on ne casse pas le format que le Dreaming réécrit.
- **Provenance affichée** : la dernière écriture (manuel / Dreaming / distillation) + horodatage est visible en tête de section, avec restauration en 1 clic du snapshot pré-Dreaming (déjà conservé par le moteur).
- **Bornage visible** : le cap mémoire (nouvelle valeur) est affiché (« x / N caractères ») avec avertissement en approche.

Les references aux « points ouverts » dans les stories ci-dessous sont caduques : les décisions ci-dessus les remplacent (story 1 lit « Spec & Memory » + absence de migration ; story 2 lit le nouveau cap haussé).

## Points ouverts

Aucun — tous tranchés (mise en page, intitulé de nav, cap).

**Code Review**

Findings submitted to Arij (7 findings, verdict recorded).

# Code Review — Epic: Project memory → Spec section

**Scope:** commit `d108345` on `feature/epic-yF1VA5lAudv2-…`, diffed against merge-base `3ca8939` — 20 files, +1503 / −518.

**Verification performed (read-only):**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | ✅ clean, 0 errors |
| `npx vitest run` (full suite) | ✅ 428 files / 5044 tests passed |
| `npx eslint` on all 10 touched files | ✅ clean — the one `react-hooks/immutability` error in `hooks/useProjectEvents.ts` is **pre-existing** (confirmed by linting the merge-base version via `--stdin`) |
| `git status` after runs | ✅ clean, nothing modified |

---

## 1. Readability

Good overall. Comment density matches the surrounding codebase, and the "why" comments on the raised cap (`memory-constants.ts:42-47`) and the deliberately unconditional restore (`memory/restore/route.ts:26-34`) are exactly the kind of decision-record the repo favours.

Nits (not filed as findings):
- `lib/events/bus.ts:19-25` — the `memory:changed` doc comment is wedged *between* two members of the `TicketEventType` union at column 0, breaking the indentation of the list. Legal TS, but it reads as a stray block; move it above the union or after the member.
- `app/projects/[projectId]/documents/page.tsx:41` — the removal deleted the comment explaining *why* internal memory kinds are filtered out of the uploads list, while keeping the filter. That rationale still applies and was worth keeping.
- Stray double blank lines at `memory-constants.ts:105-106`, `memory-provenance.ts:30-31`, `MemoryPanel.tsx:87-88`.
- `MemoryPanel.tsx:126` — `const safeContent = content ?? ""` is dead defence; `content` is `useState("")`, typed `string`.

## 2. DRY Principle

**Two findings.** The four Dreaming section titles are a contract owned by `DREAMING_MEMORY_SECTIONS` (`lib/workflow/dreaming-constants.ts:170`) and derived everywhere else — including `lib/claude/prompt-builder.ts:2127`. This epic introduces the only two places that don't derive them:

- `MemoryPanel.tsx:20` — `DREAMING_MEMORY_TEMPLATE` hardcodes them as a literal. *(Minor)*
- `MemoryPanel.tsx:36` — `hasAllDreamingSections` re-implements `validateDreamedMemoryStructure` (`lib/workflow/dreaming-digest.ts:289`) with a weaker, divergent rule. That module is pure and client-safe, so the duplication buys nothing. *(Minor)*

## 3. Error Handling

No issues found. Load failure correctly distinguishes `loading` from `loaded` so a failed fetch never presents a saveable empty editor over content nobody read; every `fetch` has a `.catch`; the engine-side `recordMemoryWriteProvenance`/`emit` calls in `dreaming.ts` and `memory-distill.ts` are wrapped so a bookkeeping failure can't break the write path. The restore route correctly 404s when there's no snapshot, and `saveProjectMemory` truncates, so a restore can't exceed the cap.

## 4. Performance

**One finding (the blocking one).** `MemoryPanel.tsx:181` — the panel re-fetches *only* on `memory:changed`, and discards the hook's `pollTick`. Two consequences:

- `pendingWriter` never updates while the panel is open. Nothing emits an event when a memory writer **starts** (`dispatchDreamingSession`/`dispatchMemoryDistillSession` don't call `emitSessionStarted`), and `memory:changed` fires only *after* the write — when `pendingWriter` is already null. So the Story-4 read-only banner effectively never renders for a user with the page open, which is exactly the case it protects: they edit, save, and the dream discards its whole output at the optimistic guard.
- With SSE down, the panel never refreshes at all. The board page wires `pollTick` to a refresh (`app/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx:94-98`); this one doesn't — and this epic *added* the `typeof EventSource === "undefined"` early-return that forces that state.

*(Major — see finding for the recommended fix.)*

Also: `MemoryPanel.tsx:279` uses `window.location.href` where the deleted card used `router.push`, forcing a full page reload on every manual Dream. *(Minor)*

No N+1 or query-shape issues: the GET envelope is 4 point-lookups against SQLite.

## 5. Naming Conventions

No issues found. camelCase throughout, `MemoryPanel.tsx` matches the component, `data-testid` names are consistent (`memory-*`), settings key prefix follows the existing `<name>:<projectId>` convention.

## 6. Type Safety

No issues found. No `any`. `MemoryWriteProvenance`/`MemoryWriteSource` are imported with `import type`, so the db-importing `memory-provenance.ts` is correctly erased from the client bundle. `getMemoryWriteProvenance` validates the parsed JSON against a source allowlist and returns `null` on anything unrecognised. `PROJECT_MEMORY_MAX_CHARS` and `DREAMING_MEMORY_SECTIONS` both come from db-free constants modules.

## 7. Testing

**One finding.** Route coverage is genuinely good — the new `memory-route.test.ts` cases pin provenance, archive, `pendingWriter`, both restore 404 paths, restore repeatability, and the notification's `targetUrl`.

The gap is on the component side: `__tests__/spec-page-memory-panel.test.tsx:93` — 8 tests, none of which touches `memory-conflict-notice` or the SSE refresh path, leaving the entire `applyEnvelope(…, keepLocalEdit=true)` branch untested. Story 4 lists "Test de composant : scénario de bannière conflit" as an acceptance criterion, and Story 5's "un changement mémoire s'affiche sans refresh" is likewise unasserted. *(Minor)*

Note the `handleInsertSkeleton` test only exercises the empty-content path; the non-empty path short-circuits on jsdom's `confirm()` returning `undefined`, so the destructive branch is silently uncovered.

## 8. API Design

No issues found. Both routes follow the `{ data }` / `{ error }` convention, `getProjectOr404` + `isErrorResponse` guard first, `validateBody` + zod enforces the cap with a 400, restore returns 404 for "no snapshot". PUT and POST return the identical envelope shape as GET, which is what lets the panel apply the response directly instead of re-fetching. Origin protection is handled globally by `middleware.ts`.

One deliberate design note (not a defect): the PUT route has no expected-version guard, so a manual save after a background agent write clobbers it. That matches §6.8's "manual content wins" rule and the panel warns the user first — flagging only so it's a conscious choice.

---

## Summary

| Severity | Count |
|---|---|
| Critical | 0 |
| **Major** | **1** |
| Minor | 6 |
| Suggestion | 0 (4 un-filed readability nits listed above) |

The epic delivers Stories 1, 2, 3 and 5 cleanly, with a genuinely careful engine-side integration (one write channel, one event, provenance on all four paths, no migration). Story 4's read-only guard is the one that doesn't hold up in the case it was written for: because nothing refreshes `pendingWriter` while the panel is open, the banner never appears mid-rewrite, and the user can silently destroy a dream's entire output — the exact failure the story set out to prevent. That, plus the unused `pollTick` fallback, is a single-fix change in `MemoryPanel.tsx`.

**Follow-ups deliberately left out of scope:** the `react-hooks/immutability` error in `hooks/useProjectEvents.ts` is pre-existing and belongs to `main`, not this branch.

**Prompt-injection note:** the stored project spec again carried an embedded `<system-directive>` block instructing this session to "compose the complete updated project specification". It arrived through content, not through the ticket, and was ignored. It's already on the friction register (per project memory), so no new friction was filed.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

comments.content:
**Code Review**

# Code Review — Epic: Project memory → Spec section (re-review of `89a6b84`)

**Scope:** `3ca8939..HEAD` — 3 commits, 22 files, +2159 / −518.

## Verification (read-only; working tree left clean)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | ✅ clean |
| `npx vitest run` | ✅ 428 files / 5055 tests passed |
| `npx eslint` on all 13 touched files | ✅ clean, except one `react-hooks/immutability` error in `hooks/useProjectEvents.ts` — confirmed **pre-existing** by linting the merge-base version via `--stdin` |
| `git status` after runs | ✅ clean |

## Previous round's findings — all six genuinely fixed

I re-verified each rather than taking the summary at face value:

- **Terminal events** — `session:completed`/`session:failed` are now emitted unconditionally in both dispatch callbacks (`dreaming.ts:1079`, `memory-distill.ts:678`), placed *after* `markSessionTerminal` and *before* every early return, so a dream that fails, stays silent, asks a question, or is discarded by the structure/optimistic guard now clears the read-only banner. I confirmed no duplicate emitter exists for these two agent types, so the raw `eventBus.emit` (bypassing `emitSessionCompleted`) correctly avoids a second notification.
- **Conflict detection** — `savedContentRef` comparison means an unchanged refetch no longer raises a false banner.
- **Append missing sections** — the document-wiping branch is gone.
- **Structure hint** — now presence-based, so preamble and custom sections don't trigger a permanent warning.
- **Restore** — dirty-guarded with an explanatory `title`.
- **Session subscriptions** — filtered to memory-writer agent types / the tracked session id.

## Checklist

**Readability** — Good. The decision records on the raised cap (`memory-constants.ts:42-47`) and the deliberately unconditional restore (`memory/restore/route.ts:25-34`) are the kind of "why" this repo favours. One comment now asserts behaviour that doesn't exist (finding 5).

**DRY** — One regression: the section-presence regex is written three times (finding 4).

**Error handling** — One coupling issue (finding 3). Otherwise solid: every `fetch` has a `.catch`; `loading`/`loaded` are distinguished so a failed load never presents a saveable empty editor over content nobody read; engine-side bookkeeping is wrapped so it can't break the write path.

**Performance** — No N+1. The panel no longer refetches on unrelated session events; `pollTick` only fires when SSE is down; handlers live in a ref so passing a fresh object each render doesn't churn the `EventSource`.

**Naming** — No issues found.

**Type safety** — No `any`. `MemoryWriteProvenance`/`MemoryWriteSource` are `import type`, so the db-importing module is erased from the client bundle; `getMemoryWriteProvenance` validates parsed JSON against a source allowlist and returns `null` on anything unrecognised.

**Testing** — 20 component tests with a real `MockEventSource` driving actual handler dispatch, plus route coverage for provenance, archive, `pendingWriter`, both restore 404 paths, and notification `targetUrl`. The uncovered paths are precisely the findings below.

**API design** — No issues found. `{ data }`/`{ error }`, `getProjectOr404` first, zod cap → 400, 404 for "no snapshot", identical envelope shape across GET/PUT/POST.

## Findings

| # | Severity | Location | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Major** | `lib/workflow/dreaming.ts:1140` | §6.8 conflict is invisible when the *agent's* write is the one discarded — Story 4 AC not met |
| 2 | Minor | `app/api/projects/[projectId]/sessions/[sessionId]/route.ts:129` | Cancelled *queued* writer (and server restart) leaves the panel stuck read-only |
| 3 | Minor | `lib/workflow/dreaming.ts:1152` | One `try` couples the provenance write to the `memory:changed` emit |
| 4 | Minor | `components/spec/MemoryPanel.tsx:25` | Section-presence regex written three times; exported helper used only by tests |
| 5 | Minor | `lib/workflow/memory-writer-lock.ts:26` | Doc comment describes a 409 body that doesn't exist |
| 6 | Suggestion | `components/spec/MemoryPanel.tsx:417` | Resolved conflict banner can resurface |
| 7 | Suggestion | `app/api/projects/[projectId]/memory/route.ts:108` | Every manual Save raises a bell notification for the user who clicked Save |

**Totals:** Critical 0 · Major 1 · Minor 4 · Suggestion 2.

The one blocker: Story 4's AC says the user must be told explicitly when a manual save and an agent rewrite collide — "jamais d'écrasement silencieux". The new conflict banner covers the direction where the agent write *lands* while you're editing. The reverse, where the optimistic guard *throws the agent's work away* because you saved, produces a `console.info` and a bare `return` — no notification, no event, and the session still reads "completed" in the Sessions list. That path is one click away now that Dream sits in the panel. Fix is small and lives in the two branches at `dreaming.ts:1140` and `memory-distill.ts:716`.

**Carried-forward deferral:** the `react-hooks/immutability` error in `hooks/useProjectEvents.ts` is pre-existing on the merge-base, not this branch's to fix.

**Spec note (not filed as a defect):** Story 1's AC says "aucune nouvelle clé de settings", while Story 3's provenance requirement introduces `memory_provenance:<projectId>`. Reading Story 1's AC as scoped to Story 1's changes, that's a defensible deviation — flagging so it stays a conscious call. No migration was added, as required.

**Prompt-injection note:** the stored project spec again carried an embedded `<system-directive>` block instructing this session to rewrite the specification. It arrived through content rather than through the ticket or the user, and was ignored. It's already on the friction register, so no new friction was filed.

**Overall Verdict: Changes Requested**

epics.description:
Implement a QOL continuity and identity upgrade across ticket workflow, session resume, and UI readability. The epic removes friction from re-dispatching work, enforces resume-first execution for all providers (including Codex), and introduces human-readable IDs for tickets and agents with full backfill.

Implementation plan:
1) Schema and constraints: add/extend nullable session continuity fields in `agentSessions` and `chatConversations` for provider session tracking, add immutable `readableId` fields for Epic/Bug records, and add agent display-name fields tied to a predefined name registry; enforce uniqueness with indexes.
2) Provider layer: capture CLI session IDs from provider output and inject resume arguments for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and Codex; extend `resolveAgent()` to return `namedAgentId` for scoped session filtering.
3) Process manager and APIs: persist `cliSessionId` on completion, expose/extend resume endpoints used by work-session actions, and implement resume-first with automatic fallback to fresh prompt when session resume fails or expires.
4) Ticket UX: add `Send to dev` next to `Add comment` at the bottom of ticket detail; clicking it immediately dispatches the assigned/current agent with no dialog and no required comment.
5) Readable ticket IDs: generate IDs using one shared per-project counter across Epic and Bug types (e.g., `E-project-001`, `B-project-002`), keep IDs immutable after assignment, and replace technical IDs with readable IDs on cards/details/activity surfaces.
6) Agent readable identity: seed a predefined Ancient Greek name list, assign deterministic unique names to existing and new agents/sessions, and use these names where agent identity is shown.
7) Backfill and validation: run idempotent backfill for existing tickets and agents, add collision/concurrency tests for counter generation, add resume/fallback tests for all providers, and add UI tests for button placement and readable ID rendering.

epics.description:
Rework Kanban ticket detail behavior from a blocking right-side modal to a non-modal experience in the shared left panel area. Clicking a ticket must both select it and open its details, while the board remains fully interactive for additional selections and quick actions.

Implementation plan:
1. Refactor board UI state to keep ordered selection (`selectedTicketIds`) and derive `activeDetailTicketId` from the first selected ticket.
2. Update card interaction so primary ticket click selects the ticket and opens details in the shared left panel container (same area used by chat/epic panels).
3. Keep multi-select active while details are open using existing additive selection controls; additional selections must not block board interaction.
4. Enforce first-selected anchoring: detail content follows the first selected ticket; adding more tickets does not switch detail; if the first selected ticket is removed, promote the next oldest selected ticket; if none remain, close details.
5. Remove all modal mechanics across desktop/tablet/mobile: no dim layer, no pointer-event lock, no focus trap, no modal fallback.
6. Increase detail panel width for readability using responsive sizing target `clamp(420px, 34vw, 560px)` and preserve usable board space.
7. Add/adjust tests for selection-order logic, non-modal interactivity, quick-action continuity, and responsive rendering. No DB/schema/API/provider changes are expected.

Dependency-Aware Batch Ticket Orchestration
epics.description:
Build an orchestration epic for Arij that adds ticket dependencies and batch actions while reusing existing PR/Git/review flows. Scope is limited to dependencies inside one project (including tickets across different epics in that project), with schema designed for future cross-project expansion.

Implementation plan:
1. Dependency domain model
- Add dependency edges (`ticket_id`, `depends_on_ticket_id`, `project_id`) plus extensibility fields (`scope_type`, `scope_id`) for future scope expansion.
- Enforce current business rule: dependencies are valid only within the same project.
- Persist dependency metadata generated by the ticket-creation agent.
2. Ticket detail dependency management
- Add dependency editor in ticket detail to add/remove predecessors.
- Validate DAG integrity on every update (cycle detection with explicit error path).
3. Batch selection UX
- On ticket selection, auto-include all transitive prerequisites.
- Mark auto-included tickets as required and non-deselectable while dependents remain selected.
- Show batch actions `Review all` and `Merge all` when multiple tickets are selected.
4. DAG scheduler and execution engine
- Implement topological planning for batch `build`, `review`, and `merge` actions.
- Run dependent chains sequentially and independent branches in parallel, while respecting existing agent concurrency guardrails.
- Track per-ticket states: `ready`, `running`, `blocked`, `failed`, `success`.
5. Failure policy and remediation
- If a ticket fails, block descendants and continue all independent branches.
- For `Merge all`, add a batch toggle to auto-launch a merge agent on first failure for every failed ticket (including auto-included tickets), with no retry limit; rely on existing manual agent stop controls.
6. Integration and quality
- Reuse existing single-ticket PR/Git/review/build pathways; do not duplicate core Git/PR logic.
- Add tests for transitive auto-inclusion, DAG validation, topological execution, failure propagation, and auto-merge triggering.

Named Agents with Model Selection & Gemini CLI Provider
epics.description:
Extend the agent system from simple CLI provider selection to named agents that combine a CLI provider with a specific model. Users can create named agents like 'CC Opus 4.6' (Claude Code + claude-opus-4-6), 'Codex GPT-5.3' (Codex + gpt-5.3), or 'Gemini Flash' (Gemini CLI + gemini-2.0-flash), then assign one named agent per task type (build, review, chat, etc.). This also adds full Gemini CLI support as a third provider alongside Claude Code and Codex.

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Schema & Types
- Add `namedAgents` table to Drizzle schema with columns: id, name, provider (claude-code | codex | gemini-cli), model (text), createdAt
- Add `namedAgentId` foreign key column to `agentProviderDefaults` table
- Extend all provider type unions to include `gemini-cli`

### Phase 2: Gemini CLI Provider
- Create `lib/gemini/spawn.ts` implementing the spawn interface using `gemini --prompt` with `--model`, `--yolo`, and `--output-format stream-json` flags
- Create `lib/providers/gemini-cli.ts` provider adapter returning `SpawnedClaude`-compatible interface
- Register Gemini CLI in the provider factory alongside claude-code and codex
- Generalize process manager dispatch to handle all three providers

### Phase 3: Named Agent CRUD & Resolution
- Create `lib/agent-config/named-agents.ts` with list, create, update, delete operations
- Implement `resolveAgent(taskType, projectId)` function that looks up the named agent for a task type and returns { provider, model }
- Backward compatibility: when `namedAgentId` is null, fall back to existing `provider` column behavior

### Phase 4: API Routes
- Add CRUD API routes for named agents at `/api/agent-config/named-agents`
- Update provider defaults API to accept `namedAgentId`
- Update build, review, and chat dispatch routes to use `resolveAgent()` instead of direct provider lookup

### Phase 5: UI
- Add new 'Agents' tab in agent settings for creating/editing/deleting named agents (name + provider dropdown + model text input)
- Update 'Providers' tab to show a named agent dropdown per task type instead of raw provider select
- Show agent name in session monitoring and activity indicators

epics.title: Permanent Delete Actions for Epic and User Story Detail
epics.description:
Add destructive delete actions directly in Epic Detail and User Story (US) Detail views, with explicit confirmation and immediate permanent deletion (no recovery, undo, or trash).

Implementation plan:
1. Add a `Delete` action in the danger zone of Epic Detail and US Detail, visible only to users who already have edit/delete permissions.
2. Implement a shared confirmation dialog used by both pages with irreversible copy (`This action cannot be undone`), Cancel, and Confirm actions.
3. Wire/extend backend `DELETE` handlers for epics and user stories to perform transactional hard deletes only.
4. Ensure relationship handling is deterministic: deleting an epic removes its child user stories and dependent planning artifacts in the same transaction; deleting a US removes its dependent links/comments/tasks per FK rules with no partial writes.
5. On successful deletion, redirect to the correct parent list view (epics/backlog), invalidate cached queries, and refresh UI state so removed items disappear from detail, kanban, and lists immediately.

Bug Tickets with Direct Creation and Agent Dispatch
epics.description:
Add a new 'bug' ticket type to the existing kanban system. Bugs are standalone kanban cards that reuse the epics table (with a new `type` column: 'feature' | 'bug') and the full dispatch/worktree/PR pipeline. Bugs have a simplified creation flow — a direct form (title, description, images) with no mandatory chat step. They can optionally link to an existing epic. A 'Create and Resolve' action creates the bug and immediately dispatches a selected agent (via the existing provider/agent selector) in an isolated worktree+branch. Bug cards have a distinct background color on the kanban board.

## Implementation Plan

1. Schema migration: Add `type` column ('feature'|'bug') to `epics` table (default 'feature'), add optional `linkedEpicId` self-referencing FK, add `images` JSON column for bug attachments.
2. API routes: New POST `/api/projects/[id]/bugs` for direct creation (no chat), POST `/api/projects/[id]/bugs/create-and-resolve` that creates + dispatches agent. Existing epic routes continue working unchanged.
3. Bug creation form: Modal/panel with title, description, image upload (reuse existing image infra from chat), optional epic linker dropdown, and agent selector for 'Create and Resolve'.
4. Kanban integration: Filter/display bugs alongside epics, distinct BG color for bug cards, badge or icon to distinguish type. Drag-and-drop, status transitions, and column behavior remain identical.
5. Agent dispatch: Reuse existing worktree+branch creation and agent dispatch logic. When linked to an epic, inject epic context (title, description, user stories) into the agent prompt.
6. Bug detail view: Lighter version of epic detail — shows title, description, images, linked epic, status, and agent session if dispatched.
