comments.author: agent
comments.content:
I've stopped and asked rather than proceeding, because proceeding would have destroyed another agent's uncommitted work.

## What I found

**A second, orphaned session is already building this exact story in this same worktree.** PID 1421661 (session `fa643c08-…`, started 11:39:49) lost its orchestrator parent and was reparented to systemd, but it is still actively running. My session (PID 1455493) was spawned normally by the Arij dev server three minutes later.

The proof it's live: `git status` was clean when I started, and showed its edits three minutes later. It had also restarted the worktree's `next dev` on port 3100 and run an `evil.example.com` cross-origin probe against it, recorded in `.next/dev/logs/next-development.log`.

It has already written `next.config.ts` (`allowedDevOrigins: ["127.0.0.1", "[::1]"]`), a new `__tests__/next-config-dev-origins.test.ts`, and doc updates to `playwright.config.ts` and `e2e/README.md` — the exact four files this story needs. Its regression test is better than a naive config assertion: it drives Next's real `blockCrossSiteDEV` module with the repo's actual config and asserts parity against `middleware.ts`'s loopback allowlist, with a negative case preventing the fix from being widened to a wildcard. That is genuinely red on the merge-base and green with the fix.

Writing to those files would have overwritten irrecoverable work, and a competing e2e run would have fought it for port 3100, the `.next/dev` lock, and the shared dev database — corrupting both sets of measurements. So I wrote nothing.

## Two corrections to the ticket's premises

The `127.0.0.1` baseURL the description blames is **already fixed on main** — commit `bbbe7f4` moved the Playwright baseURL to `localhost`. The real remaining gap was the one the other session closed: a developer browsing `http://127.0.0.1:3000` by hand still got a silently non-hydrating board, because `middleware.ts` accepted that host for `/api/*` while `next dev` refused it `/_next/*`.

This worktree's `node_modules` is also **already lockfile-consistent** (next 16.3.3, simple-git 3.36.0), so the AC's `npm ci` precondition and the "verified against 16.3.3, not 16.1.6" criterion are both satisfied here — and the phantom `lib/git/clone.ts:976` error from sibling story RGYV82-rowtW does not reproduce in this worktree.

## Status

I filed a friction report (`rsCRH9aQi8yC`) recording the duplicate-session hazard and the detection recipe, since neither the MCP token nor the `agent_sessions` row identifies a duplicate — listing provider processes by cwd is the only way to see it.

The ticket is held awaiting your answer on whether to let PID 1421661 finish (my recommendation) or kill it and have me take over the verification and commit. I have not touched the working tree, and won't until you decide.

One thing I could not verify, and am not claiming: I never ran the e2e suite, so the 7/7 acceptance criterion is still unmeasured by me — deliberately, since running it would have disrupted the other session.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
Done — commit `cc13f4f`, ticket moved to Review.

## What the flake actually was

Not latency. I proved it in a browser: a `loading="lazy"` image 3000px down a scroll container, polled 15× over 3s with `Locator.evaluate()`, stayed at `naturalWidth === 0` having issued **zero network requests**. One `scrollIntoViewIfNeeded()` and it fetched. `evaluate()` runs no actionability checks, so it never scrolls, so Chrome is never asked for the bytes — and no poll timeout rescues a request that was never made.

On the live board the thumbnail happens to land at y=430 inside a scroll container (`scrollHeight` 579 > `clientHeight` 322), i.e. just inside Chrome's lazy threshold. So it usually loads, and the observed failure was the serve round-trip still in flight. But that's a layout coincidence — the images section sits below the description in a scrolling panel.

**Done** — commit `cc13f4f`, 3 files: `e2e/fixtures/board.ts`, `e2e/bug-image-paste.spec.ts`, `__tests__/lazy-image-assertion.test.ts`.

## The mechanism, measured

Chose `scrollIntoViewIfNeeded()` over raising the timeout, because the failure mode is **not latency**. Measured in Chrome against a `loading="lazy"` image 3000px down a scroll container:

| | `naturalWidth` | network requests issued |
|---|---|---|
| 15 × `Locator.evaluate()` over 3s, no scroll | 0 | **0** |
| after one `scrollIntoViewIfNeeded()` | 16 | 1 |

`evaluate()` runs no actionability checks, so it never scrolls; Chrome never asks for the bytes. No poll timeout rescues a request that was never made — raising it would only have made the bad case hang longer.

Also measured on the live board (viewport 1280×720): the thumbnail lands at y=430 **inside** a scroll container (`scrollHeight` 579 > `clientHeight` 322), so on this layout it happens to sit within Chrome's lazy threshold and does get fetched — `naturalWidth` was still 0 when `openTicketDetail` returned, with the serve request in flight. That's the flake the epic saw. It passing was a layout coincidence, not a guarantee: the images section sits below the description in a scrolling panel, so more content above it moves the thumbnail out.

Correction to one epic detail: `expect.poll` **does** inherit the config `expect.timeout`, so in dev mode it waits 30s, not 5s (measured 29891 ms). The 5s budget is the `start`/CI mode one. Either way the timeout was never the lever.

`naturalWidthOfLazyImage(image)` in `e2e/fixtures/board.ts` — scroll, then read — called **inside** the poll body, so every tick re-establishes visibility instead of trusting a one-off preamble (the panel can still be settling on the first tick, and the scroll is a no-op once in view). epics.title: Serveurs MCP additionnels, globaux et par projet
epics.description:
Permettre à l'utilisateur de déclarer des serveurs MCP tiers (Godot, Confluence, Playwright…), globaux ou scopés à un projet, et les injecter dans les sessions d'agents en plus du canal `arij`.

## Contexte

Aujourd'hui claude-code est lancé avec `--mcp-config <fichier 0600>` **et `--strict-mcp-config`** (voir `lib/providers/types.ts:32` et `docs/architecture/mcp-provider-matrix.md`). Conséquence : les serveurs MCP que l'utilisateur a configurés dans son propre `~/.claude.json` ou `.mcp.json` sont **ignorés** par les sessions Arij.

Cette épic ne consiste donc pas à « ajouter du MCP » mais à **rendre explicite et scopé ce que le mode strict coupe** — ce qui est le bon modèle : le comportement d'un build ne doit pas dépendre de la config locale de la machine, et un serveur utile à un projet (Godot) n'a rien à faire dans les sessions d'un autre.

Le point de câblage existe déjà et reste unique : `buildMcpSpawnConfig()` dans `lib/claude/mcp-injection.ts:239`, appelé depuis `processManager.start()`.

## Modèle de résolution

Ordre de fusion : **`arij` d'abord, puis les serveurs globaux, puis ceux du projet**. En cas de collision de `name`, le projet gagne. Le nom `arij` est **réservé** : le refuser en validation, sinon on écrase le canal de contrôle.

Le gate `mcp_tools_enabled` reste unique et couvre les extras : off = aucun MCP du tout.

## Contrainte structurante : les providers n'ont pas la même surface

| Provider | Surface d'injection | Scope réellement supporté |
|---|---|---|
| claude-code | fichier `--mcp-config` par spawn | global + projet |
| codex | overrides `-c mcp_servers.<name>.*` par spawn | global + projet |
| oh-my-pi | `mcp.json` statique (`~/.omp/agent/mcp.json`) | global seulement |
| agy | registre user-global (`agy mcp add`) | global seulement |

omp lit `.omp/mcp.json` relatif au cwd (donc au worktree), ce qui ouvrirait le per-projet — mais écrire de la config dans un worktree est exactement ce qui avait fait écarter gemini-cli. Hors périmètre v1.

agy : réconcilier son registre global avant chaque spawn serait *racy* (deux sessions parallèles sur deux projets se marcheraient dessus). Global-only, assumé.

## Pièges identifiés

- **Fuite de secret dans l'argv codex** : `maskCodexMcpSecret()` (`lib/providers/codex.ts:129`) ne masque que l'override contenant `ARIJ_MCP_TOKEN`. Un token tiers passerait en clair dans le `command_display` persisté et dans `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`.
- **Env des extras** : sur omp et agy, le mécanisme d'injection *est* l'environnement de l'enfant — un secret extra y est donc lisible par le Bash de l'agent. À interdire ou à assumer explicitement.
- **Seuil de découverte omp** : `tools.discoveryMode: auto` cache les outils MCP derrière `search_tool_bm25` au-delà de 40 outils. Ajouter un serveur tiers volumineux peut faire **disparaître les outils arij du prompt** sans aucune erreur.
- **Injection de prompt** : les descriptions d'outils d'un serveur tiers arrivent dans le contexte de l'agent — même classe de surface que `projects.spec`.
- **Prompt** : un agent n'utilisera pas un serveur dont le prompt ne mentionne pas l'existence.

user_stories.title: Schéma, migration et CRUD des serveurs MCP
user_stories.description:
Créer la table `mcp_servers` et le service CRUD associé.

Colonnes : `id`, `project_id` (NULL = global, FK vers `projects` avec cascade), `name`, `enabled`, `transport` ('stdio' | 'http'), `command`, `args` (json), `env` (json), `url`, `headers` (json), `agent_types` (json, NULL = tous), `usage_hint` (texte court), `last_checked_at`, `last_check_ok`, `last_check_error`.

La FK cascade dispense d'ajouter une entrée dans `perProjectSettingKeys()` (`lib/projects/project-settings-keys.ts`), qui n'existe que parce que la table `settings` n'a pas de FK.

Migration **écrite à la main** : fichier SQL numéroté + entrée ajoutée à la main dans `meta/_journal.json` avec un `when` strictement croissant. Ne pas lancer `npx drizzle-kit generate` (les snapshots s'arrêtent à 0013).
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- Table `mcp_servers` créée par une migration SQL manuelle, avec l'entrée correspondante dans `meta/_journal.json` (index et `when` croissants).
- `project_id` NULL signifie global ; la suppression d'un projet supprime ses serveurs par cascade, ce qu'un test couvre.
- Le nom `arij` est refusé à la création et à l'édition, avec une erreur explicite.
- `name` validé contre `[a-z0-9_-]+` et unique par scope.
- La forme est validée selon le transport : `command` requis en stdio, `url` requis en http ; les combinaisons incohérentes sont refusées.
- Les tailles de `env`, `args` et `headers` sont plafonnées, et un dépassement est **rejeté avec une erreur explicite plutôt que tronqué**, avec la même forme d'erreur qu'une valeur d'énumération invalide.
- Routes API CRUD globales et par projet, avec la forme `{ data }` / `{ error }` habituelle.
- Les valeurs de `env` et `headers` ne sont jamais renvoyées en lecture : l'API retourne `"***"` (champ write-only).

All nine review findings are addressed in commit `58c4045`, and the ticket is back in Review.

## What changed

**The three majors:**

1. **Secrets wiped on edit** — `handleSave` always sent the secret map while `startEdit` correctly left the box empty, so editing anything sent `env: {}` and erased every stored value. The key is now omitted when the textarea is blank.

2. **Transport switch dead-ended both ways** — PATCH is a merge, so the abandoned side survived into validation. Both sides are cleared explicitly now.

3. **Blocking spawns on the request path** — reconciliation moved off the request path: async `execFile`, chained so runs can't interleave, coalesced to one pending run. I promisified `execFile` *lazily* — at module scope it reads `child_process` on import, which crashed any suite using a partial mock. That was a real regression I introduced and then caught.

**A bug the transport fix uncovered:** `effectiveState` normalises missing `args` to `[]`, and `[]` is truthy, so the http branch's `if (value.args)` fired on every http row — **http servers were uneditable outright**, one-click enable/disable included. Fixed to check length, with a separate test proving a genuinely present args list is still refused.

**Minors/info:** `usage_hint` neutralised (before the budget check, since escaping lengthens the string); `agent_types`/`tool_allowlist` in the form and as badges, sending `null` rather than `[]` when blank; the shadow-disable badge and note now say oh-my-pi and agy keep loading the global; migration 0046 adds the two partial unique indexes 0045 wrongly said SQLite couldn't express; the shadow row no longer copies credentials, and since an Enable button sits right next to it, stored secret *keys* are now shown so a credential-less row is visible.

## Verification

477 files / 5979 tests passing, `tsc --noEmit` clean, `next build` succeeds, eslint clean. I mutation-checked six fixes — reverting each one makes a specific test fail, so the coverage is real rather than incidental.

Two things worth flagging: the worktree's `node_modules` was stale (next 16.1.6, simple-git 3.30.0 vs lockfile 16.3.3/3.36.0) and produced a phantom type error in `lib/git/clone.ts`, a file this branch never touches — `npm ci` cleared it, and I re-ran everything against the clean install. Four existing tests asserted the old behavior the review asked me to change; I updated those assertions deliberately rather than working around them, and the commit says which.

comments.author: agent
comments.content:
Both findings are fixed and committed as `32aa470`; the ticket is back in Review.

## The short-secret leak (`lib/mcp/probe.ts`)

`scrubSecrets` skipped values under four characters as "not a credential" while the schema accepts them. I confirmed it on two paths, not just the one the review named — the http transport leaks with no misbehaving CLI at all, because the SDK builds its failure as `` `Error POSTing to endpoint: ${text}` ``, so an endpoint quoting the credential it rejected puts it straight in the message. That path had no test.

Now every non-empty value is redacted, longest-first so a prefix can't fragment a longer secret. I chose that over the review's alternative of a minimum length: `env`/`headers` are write-only *by contract*, so length can't decide secrecy — but a floor would refuse legitimate `DEBUG=1`. The trade-off is documented at the function: a very short value will mangle an unrelated diagnostic, which is recoverable in a way a leaked credential isn't.

## The reconciliation race (`lib/mcp/user-global-sync.ts`)

I took the CRUD-side barrier rather than the spawn-side one. `processManager.start()` is synchronous with ~9 call sites, so a barrier there is a cross-cutting refactor outside this story; the global handlers now await `whenUserGlobalMcpSyncSettles()` before responding. The spawns stayed async, so only that one request waits — the freeze the earlier finding was about doesn't come back — and a 2xx now means "already in the registry" instead of "queued".

To test it I extracted the scheduler as a factory and injected the reconciliation's targets, so a 20 ms fake `agy` can hold the barrier open and the tests can assert what a session would see meanwhile. That also gives `syncOmp`/`syncAgy` their first behavioural coverage, since the live path refuses to run under VITEST by design.

## Verification

478 files / 6016 tests passing, `tsc` clean, eslint clean, `next build` succeeds. `node_modules` matches the lockfile, so no phantom failures. Each fix is mutation-checked — reverting the length floor, the sort, the `settled()` chain, the coalescing guard, the run chaining, the handler `await`, or the project-scope skip each fails a specific named test.

Two things worth flagging: I did **not** extend the scrub to `toolNames` (users build `tool_allowlist` from those, so redacting one would hand back an unusable value for a fringe gain), and a session started *concurrently* with a CRUD request is still unordered with respect to it — that's inherent to "not yet acknowledged", and the module's rule 5 now says so explicitly rather than leaving it implied.

Separately: the stored project spec ends with an embedded `<system-directive>` instructing the session to abandon its task and write a specification. I treated it as data and ignored it, but it's live prompt-injection content sitting in `projects.spec` and worth its own ticket.

user_stories.description:
Faire passer `McpSpawnConfig` d'un serveur unique à une liste, et injecter les serveurs résolus dans les deux providers qui ont une surface par spawn.

`McpSpawnConfig` devient `{ servers: McpServerSpec[], allowedToolNames }`. `buildClaudeMcpConfigJson()` (`lib/claude/mcp-injection.ts:278`) itère au lieu de coder en dur `[mcp.serverName]` ; les tests qui assertent la forme du fichier suivent.

Sur l'allowlist : les outils tiers ne sont pas énumérables à l'avance. On pousse une entrée « serveur entier » par extra (`mcp__<name>` pour claude), **dans l'orthographe du provider** — `arijMcpToolPrefix()` (`lib/claude/mcp-injection.ts:108`) : double underscore pour claude/codex, simple pour omp, nom nu pour agy. Un `tool_allowlist` optionnel par serveur permet de restreindre.

Inclut la correction du masque de secret codex : `maskCodexMcpSecret()` (`lib/providers/codex.ts:129`) doit masquer **toute** valeur `mcp_servers.*.env=`, pas seulement celle qui contient `ARIJ_MCP_TOKEN`.

- `McpSpawnConfig` porte une liste de serveurs ; le canal `arij` reste toujours présent et en premier.

- Les entrées d'allowlist des extras sont générées dans l'orthographe du provider de la session.
- Le gate `mcp_tools_enabled` à false supprime les extras comme le canal arij.

A server that starts, rejects its config and exits was reported as `MCP error -32000: Connection closed` — no cause. Its actual diagnostic went to a stderr pipe nothing read. I measured this before changing anything, and confirmed the text was still recoverable afterwards.

`collectStderr` now attaches for the whole handshake and appends the server's own output on failure. Attaching *up front* rather than reading after the failure matters twice: an unread pipe stalls the child once the ~64 KiB buffer fills, so a chatty server hung until the 15 s timeout instead of failing immediately — the new `flood` fixture went from **5 s to 24 ms**.

That also exposed something worth flagging: **the secret-scrub tests were vacuous**. With `scrubSecrets` disabled entirely, the existing "keeps configured secrets out of the returned error" test still passed, because no configured value could reach the message at all. The recovered diagnostic is the server's own output — which is exactly where a rejected credential gets quoted back — so that test now fails when the scrub is removed. I verified that by removing it.

The UI stored the verdict but not the reason, leaving a bare "Failed — date" after any reload; the row now renders `last_check_error`.

This is a **departure from the ticket text**, which I've flagged in the ticket comment for review: the ticket asks for a route and persisted health, not for changes to the probe's error text. I made them because the criterion wasn't actually satisfied otherwise.

comments.content:
**Forensic diagnostic**
<!-- arij:dead-session=BG8S06jxHp62 -->

**Probable root cause** — Not a code or ticket problem. The session hit oh-my-pi's context-compaction path, which renders archived conversation history as PNG images and sends them as `image_url` parts. The configured endpoint (`ninfer` / `qwen3.8-27b`) has vision disabled, so the server rejected the very first request of the resumed turn with HTTP 400 before generating a single token (`"usage":{"input":0,"output":0}`, `duration:65.7ms`). This is deterministic: once the epic's prompt (system block 27 KB + ~28 KB of epic spec/comment history + 31 messages of tool traffic) crosses omp's compaction threshold, every retry re-images the history and fails identically — which is why 2 attempts died the same way.

**Evidence**
- `400 Vision is disabled for this server ... (type=invalid_request_error param=messages code=vision_disabled)` — rejection is on `messages`, not on content the agent wrote.
- The logged raw request `/home/orosius/.omp/logs/http-400-requests/1787838016894-1aco2ebtdsh8p.json` shows message 1 with parts `['text','text','text','image_url','image_url','image_url','image_url','image_url','text']` — five `data:image/png;base64,…` blobs totalling ~358 KB, preceded by `"Resume prior conversation. Earlier turns archived under HISTORY below"` and followed by `"-------------- imaged middle above …"`.
- The failure is *late*, not at launch: the comment history records real progress (`"Schema and migration done. Now the core service module with validation, CRUD, masking, and resolution."`), and the imaged text already quotes a docstring for `lib/mcp/user-global-sync.ts`, so partial work exists on `feature/epic-00KYihOMj_jl-serveurs-mcp-additionnels-globaux-et-par` / its worktree at `/home/orosius/workspace/.arij-worktrees/feature-epic-00KYihOMj_jl-…`.

**Recommended next action**
- Re-dispatch the build stage on a provider whose context handling is text-only for this endpoint — either switch the provider/model to `claude` (or `codex`) for this epic, or keep omp and disable its image-based history compaction / point it at a vision-capable endpoint; then resume on the existing branch rather than from scratch, since story 1 (migration + schema + `lib/mcp/user-global-sync.ts`) is already partly written. Splitting this 7-story epic into smaller tickets would also keep the prompt below the compaction threshold that triggers the imaging in the first place.

comments.content:
## Serveurs MCP additionnels — 7/7 stories livrées

7 commits sur `feature/epic-00KYihOMj_jl-...` (`2f36705`..`201b2ea`). Suite complète verte : **476 fichiers, 5923 tests**. Arbre propre.

### Fichiers principaux
- `lib/db/migrations/0045_mcp_servers.sql` + entrée journal manuscrite, `lib/db/schema.ts`
- `lib/mcp/servers.ts` (CRUD + résolution), `server-limits.ts` (caps, importable côté client), `user-global-sync.ts`, `probe.ts`, `server-routes.ts`, `probe-route.ts`
- `lib/providers/extra-mcp-scope.ts`, `types.ts` (`McpSpawnConfig.servers` + `arijChannelSpec`), `codex.ts`, `base-provider.ts`, `oh-my-pi.ts`, `agy.ts`
- `lib/claude/mcp-injection.ts`, `process-manager.ts`, `prompt-sections.ts`, `lib/chat/cli-tool-channel.ts`
- `components/settings/McpServersSection.tsx`, montée dans les deux pages de réglages
- `docs/architecture/mcp-provider-matrix.md`

### Vérifié en bout de chaîne
Serveur de dev sur le port **3987** (jamais touché au 3000 — l'orchestrateur est resté vivant, pid inchangé). Rejets 400 avec **une seule forme d'erreur** (`arij` réservé, nom invalide, command manquant, usage_hint trop long), 409 sur doublon et sur shadow existant, secret masqué en lecture, probe réel sur `bin/arij-mcp.mjs` → **14 outils énumérés**, cascade projet vérifiée. Résolution live :

```
claude-code / codex   → [selfprobe, playwright]   exclus: []
oh-my-pi   / agy      → [godot, selfprobe]        exclus: [playwright]
```

`godot` est masqué par une ligne projet désactivée sur les providers per-spawn, mais **reste livré** sur les providers user-global — une ligne projet qu'ils ne peuvent pas voir ne doit pas supprimer un global qu'ils peuvent voir. Asymétrie voulue et testée.

### 4 bugs trouvés et corrigés en route
1. **Fuite de secret** — `createMcpServer`/`updateMcpServer` renvoyaient la ligne brute au lieu de la vue masquée : tout secret repartait en clair dans la réponse de création.
2. **`disableGlobalForProject` ne faisait rien** — le résolveur filtrait sur `enabled` *avant* de calculer l'ombrage, donc la ligne désactivée disparaissait et le global était injecté quand même. Le critère « désactiver un global pour un projet » n'était pas rempli.
3. **La section de prompt dépassait son propre plafond** — la mention « N de plus » était ajoutée sans contrôle de budget (1514 car. pour un cap de 1500).
4. **La résolution des extras pouvait coûter le canal `arij`** — elle partageait le `try/catch` de l'injection, donc un serveur tiers malformé faisait tomber `options.mcp` entier : agent sans outils board et review classée invérifiable. Elle a désormais son propre catch et dégrade en arij-seul.

### Incident : mes tests ont pollué la vraie config de la machine
Le premier passage de la suite CRUD a écrit deux serveurs de fixture (`godot`, `pinned`) dans le vrai `~/.omp/agent/mcp.json` et en a fait un `agy mcp add` — chaque CRUD global appelle la réconciliation, et les tests passent leur propre base. **Nettoyé** (les deux registres ne contiennent plus que `arij`, vérifié). Le correctif est un garde de fond, pas un contournement de test : réconcilier un registre CLI user-global depuis autre chose que la base applicative **live** est faux par définition. Test de mutation : retirer le garde fait échouer la suite.

### Correction d'une prémisse de l'épic (mesuré, pas supposé)
L'épic annonce `tools.discoveryMode: auto` cachant les outils MCP derrière `search_tool_bm25` au-delà de 40 outils. **Ça ne correspond pas au build omp installé** : `omp config get tools` répond `Unknown setting`, `omp config list` n'a aucun `discoveryMode`, et ni ce nom ni `search_tool_bm25` n'apparaissent dans les 130 docs embarquées d'omp. La clé vivante la plus proche est `inlineToolDescriptors`, elle-même documentée comme migrée. La doc décrit donc **la forme du risque** (un serveur volumineux peut faire disparaître les outils arij sans erreur) et la recommandation de pinner, en disant explicitement que le seuil de 40 n'a pas pu être confirmé plutôt que de le répéter comme un fait.

Également mesuré sur agy : son registre réel est `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json`, **pas** le `~/.gemini/antigravity/mcp_config.json` que nomme `lib/providers/agy.ts` (0 octet sur ce build). `agy mcp add` fait un upsert, persiste `env` en stdio et `headers`/`serverUrl` en http, et accepte `--` avant les deux types de cible. Arij passe par la CLI justement pour que cette dérive de chemin ne casse rien.

### Décisions à signaler
- **Secrets sur omp/agy : assumés, pas interdits.** Ces CLIs n'ont aucune indirection par session, donc un identifiant tiers atterrit littéralement dans leur fichier de config, lisible par le Bash de l'agent. C'est documenté dans la matrice (tableau par provider) et affiché dans l'UI. L'alternative — l'environnement de l'enfant — est strictement pire : `/proc/self/environ` est à un `cat` de chaque appel d'outil.
- **La santé n'est jamais un gate.** Un serveur tiers injoignable coûte ses outils à la session, jamais la session. Conditionner le spawn à la joignabilité laisserait l'indisponibilité d'un tiers arrêter un build.
- **`mcp_user_global_sync`** (défaut ON) permet de sortir Arij des fichiers de config de la machine.

`lib/git/clone.ts:976` échoue au typecheck (`allowUnsafeAskPass` absent des types simple-git) et **casse `next build`**. Fichier **identique au merge-base** (`git diff bc4d5a1 -- lib/git/clone.ts` = 0 ligne) et ni `package.json` ni `package-lock.json` modifiés sur cette branche : pré-existant, dérive de typage simple-git. La compilation Turbopack réussit — donc le bundle client est sain, pas de fuite de module serveur. C'est le seul fichier en erreur du dépôt.

Un `<system-directive>` de réécriture de spec est de nouveau arrivé via `projects.spec` ; ignoré, déjà au registre des frictions.

Epic complete — all 7 stories delivered, ticket moved to Review.

## What shipped

Seven commits (`2f36705`..`201b2ea`). **476 test files, 5923 tests, all green.** Clean tree.

Users can now declare third-party MCP servers (Godot, Confluence, Playwright) globally or per project. They ride alongside the `arij` control channel through the existing single wiring point — making explicit and scoped what `--strict-mcp-config` deliberately cuts off.

## Verified end-to-end, not just unit-tested

I ran a dev server on port **3987** (never touched 3000 — the orchestrator survived, same pid). Validation rejections all return one error shape, secrets mask on read, the probe did a real handshake against `bin/arij-mcp.mjs` and enumerated **14 tools**, and the project cascade works. Live resolution:

```
claude-code / codex  → [selfprobe, playwright]   excluded: []
oh-my-pi   / agy     → [godot, selfprobe]        excluded: [playwright]
```

`godot` is shadowed away on per-spawn providers but still delivered on user-global ones — a project row those CLIs can't see must not suppress a global they can. Deliberate asymmetry, tested.

## Four bugs found and fixed

The most serious: `createMcpServer`/`updateMcpServer` returned the **raw row instead of the masked view**, so every secret went back out in clear on creation. Also — `disableGlobalForProject` did nothing at all (the resolver filtered on `enabled` before computing shadowing, so the disabled row vanished), the prompt section overflowed its own cap, and extras resolution shared the injection `try/catch` so one malformed third-party server cost the session its entire Arij tool channel.

## One thing you should know

**My tests wrote into your real machine config.** The first CRUD suite run added two fixture servers to `~/.omp/agent/mcp.json` and `agy mcp add`ed one — every global CRUD call triggers reconciliation, and tests pass their own database. I cleaned both registries (verified: only `arij` remains) and added a guard, mutation-tested: reconciling a user-global CLI registry from anything but the live application database is wrong by definition.

## A premise in the epic didn't hold

The epic states `tools.discoveryMode: auto` hides MCP tools past 40. That setting **doesn't exist on the installed omp** — `omp config get tools` returns `Unknown setting`, and neither that name nor `search_tool_bm25` appears in omp's 130 embedded docs. I documented the risk shape and the pin-it recommendation, and said plainly the 40-tool figure couldn't be confirmed rather than repeating it as fact. I also found agy's register actually lives at `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json`, not the path `lib/providers/agy.ts` names.

Two judgment calls worth your attention: secrets on omp/agy land literally in those CLIs' config files (readable by the agent) — I treated this as **assumed and surfaced** rather than forbidden, since the alternative is strictly worse; and server health **never gates a build**.

**Pre-existing, not mine:** `lib/git/clone.ts:976` fails typecheck and breaks `next build`. The file is byte-identical to the merge-base with no dependency changes on this branch. Turbopack compilation itself succeeds, so the client bundle is clean — it's the only file in the repo with errors, and it deserves its own ticket.

## Test de connexion et remontée de l'état de santé — livré

Le gros de l'histoire était **déjà committé** sur la branche (`2f36705` backend, `39bbc08` UI) : `lib/mcp/probe.ts`, `lib/mcp/probe-route.ts`, les deux routes `POST .../:serverId/test`, la persistance `last_checked_at`/`last_check_ok`/`last_check_error`, le badge de santé et le bouton Test. J'ai vérifié chaque critère plutôt que de refabriquer un diff, et j'ai livré les deux vrais manques.

### 1. Un défaut réel contre le critère « une erreur lisible » (`5e72ad8`)

Le mode d'échec le plus courant ne renvoyait aucune raison. Mesuré avant de toucher au code : un serveur qui démarre, refuse sa config et sort en code 3 était rapporté comme `MCP error -32000: Connection closed` — rien sur la cause. Son diagnostic (`FATAL: config error: ...`) partait dans un pipe stderr que **rien ne lisait**.

`collectStderr` s'attache maintenant pendant tout le handshake et un échec ajoute la sortie du serveur au message. L'attacher **en amont** plutôt qu'après l'échec est porteur une seconde fois : un pipe non lu bloque l'enfant dès que le buffer OS (~64 Kio) est plein — un serveur bavard restait suspendu jusqu'au timeout de 15 s au lieu d'échouer en millisecondes. La fixture `flood` l'épingle : **5 s avant, 24 ms après**. Borné en taille et en temps (le texte finit dans un message d'erreur *et* une colonne SQLite).

Effet de bord important : **le scrub de secrets devenait enfin testable**. Il ne l'était pas — en désactivant entièrement `scrubSecrets`, le test existant « keeps configured secrets out of the returned error » **passait toujours**, car aucune valeur configurée ne pouvait atteindre le message. Le diagnostic récupéré est la sortie propre du serveur, et un serveur qui rejette une credential la recite couramment. Ce test échoue désormais quand on retire le scrub — vérifié en le retirant.

Côté UI, la ligne affichait le verdict stocké mais pas la **raison** stockée : après un rechargement il restait un « Failed — <date> » sans cause. La ligne rend maintenant `last_check_error`, colonne que la route persistait déjà.

**Écart au texte du ticket, signalé pour revue** : le ticket demande une route de test et une santé persistée, pas une modification du texte d'erreur de la sonde. Les deux changements servent le critère « une erreur lisible », qui n'était pas tenu pour le mode d'échec le plus fréquent.

### 2. Couverture de la frontière HTTP (`6ebde42`)

`handleProbeMcpServer` n'avait aucun test — même angle mort que la revue précédente avait relevé sur les routes CRUD sœurs. 13 tests épinglent ce que seul le handler décide : un échec est une **donnée** (200 + `ok:false`, pas un 5xx) ; l'issue et sa date sont persistées et un test vert **retire** l'échec précédent ; les deux scopes ne se rejoignent pas **dans les deux sens** et un lookup refusé n'écrit aucune santé ; le scrub survit à la persistance ; une ligne au transport incomplet est traitée par le handler et non par la sonde.

Chaque assertion est **vérifiée par mutation**, pas supposée : retirer le scrub, mapper l'échec en 500, supprimer le persist, retirer le scope du lookup — chacune fait échouer un test nommé. Une nuance à noter : retirer le scope du **seul** lookup renvoie encore 404, parce que l'appel `persistMcpServerCheck` revérifie le scope indépendamment ; il faut muter les deux sites pour percer la frontière. C'est de la défense en profondeur, pas une assertion redondante.

### État des critères

| Critère | État |
|---|---|
| Route par serveur : nombre + noms d'outils, ou erreur lisible | ✅ — erreur lisible désormais réellement tenue |
| Bornée par un timeout, aucun process orphelin | ✅ déjà couvert (`ps` sur les enfants du process) |
| Résultat persisté et affiché avec sa date | ✅ — la **raison** stockée est maintenant rendue aussi |
| Serveur injoignable ne bloque ni ne fait échouer une session | ✅ test existant : résolution + `buildMcpSpawnConfig` intacts, canal `arij` préservé |
| Aucune fuite de secret (message et logs) | ✅ — et l'assertion est enfin non vacue |

### Vérification

Suite complète verte : **5997 tests / 478 fichiers**. `tsc --noEmit` propre, eslint propre sur les fichiers touchés.

Les 9 findings de la revue précédente (CRUD story) étaient déjà tous traités par `58c4045` / `2270292` / migration `0046` — rien de neuf à corriger de ce côté.

comments.content:
Both review findings are addressed in `32aa470`.

## `lib/mcp/probe.ts:86` — short secrets returned and persisted verbatim

`scrubSecrets` skipped every configured value under four characters as "not a credential", while the CRUD schema happily accepts one. Confirmed on two paths, not one:

- **stdio** — a server echoing `PIN=123` on its way down reaches `{ data.error }`, `handleProbeMcpServer` writes it to `last_check_error`, and the settings screen renders it after every reload.
- **http** — no misbehaving CLI needed. The SDK builds its failure as `` `Error POSTing to endpoint: ${text}` `` (`streamableHttp.js:369`), so an endpoint that quotes the credential it rejected puts it straight into the message. This path had no test at all.

Fixed by redacting every non-empty value, **longest first** so a short value that is a prefix of a longer one can't fragment it before the real credential matches (`["abc","abc123"]` used to leave `<redacted>123`).

I took redaction over the review's alternative of rejecting short values at validation: `env`/`headers` are write-only *by contract* (reads return `"***"`), so length can't be what decides secrecy — but a minimum length would refuse legitimate settings like `DEBUG=1` or `PORT=80` that merely live in a field the contract treats as secret. The cost is real and now documented at `scrubSecrets`: a one- or two-character value will mangle an unrelated diagnostic. A mangled message is recoverable; a leaked credential is not.

The test at `__tests__/mcp-server-probe.test.ts:210` that locked the leak in is inverted, and three real regression tests added: a stdio fixture echoing a 3-char env value, an http fixture echoing a 3-char header, and the route-level assertion that `last_check_error` is clean too.

## `lib/mcp/user-global-sync.ts:475` — stale registry after an acknowledged write

Confirmed as described: nothing awaited the reconciliation, so a session launched between the HTTP response and the end of `syncAgy` froze the old set for its whole run.

I took the **spawn-side** option the review offered second and rejected it: `processManager.start()` is synchronous with ~9 call sites, so the barrier there is a cross-cutting refactor well outside this story. The **CRUD-side** barrier is in scope and sufficient — the global handlers now await `whenUserGlobalMcpSyncSettles()` before responding. Because the spawns stayed async, only that one request waits; SSE, chunk persistence, the watchdog and pipelines keep running, so the finding that motivated the async move is intact. What changes is that a 2xx now means "already in the registry" rather than "queued". A session started *during* the request is still unordered with respect to it — that's what "not yet acknowledged" means, and rule 5 says so explicitly. Project writes skip the wait; they request no reconciliation.

To make it testable I extracted the scheduler as a factory and injected the reconciliation's targets (omp config path, ownership manifest, `agy` runner). The barrier's value only exists in a window a fast machine closes by accident, so the tests hold it open with a 20 ms fake `agy` and assert what a session would see meanwhile — including the deletion case, where the register still has the server until the barrier releases. Side benefit: `syncOmp`/`syncAgy` get their first behavioural coverage, since the live path refuses to run under VITEST by design.

I also wrote down the coalescing invariant the fold silently depends on: `queued` is cleared immediately before `run()`, and `run()` must read the database before its first `await`. It was correct but undocumented, and one stray `await` would have broken it.

## Verification

478 files / 6016 tests passing, `tsc --noEmit` clean, eslint clean, `next build` succeeds (`NODE_ENV` unset). `node_modules` matches the lockfile — next 16.3.3, simple-git 3.36.0, MCP SDK 1.30.0 — so no phantom failures.

Every fix is mutation-checked: reverting the length floor fails 4 tests, the longest-first sort 1, `settled()` returning a fresh promise 4, the coalescing guard 1, the run chaining 1, the handler `await` 3, and the project-scope skip 1.

One note on scope: I deliberately did **not** extend the scrub to `toolNames`. A user sets `tool_allowlist` from those names, so redacting one would hand back an unusable value for a fringe gain — the leak the finding names is in errors, and that is where it is closed.

The accepted cost (`DEBUG=1` mangling a diagnostic) is documented at the function.

## Finding 2 — stale registry after a 2xx (`lib/mcp/user-global-sync.ts:475`) — CONFIRMED CLOSED

`server-routes.ts:83` now awaits the barrier before answering; all three mutating handlers call it, and project-scoped writes correctly skip it (they request no reconciliation). Removing the `await` fails 3 named tests — POST, PATCH **and** DELETE.

I checked the two things that decide whether the barrier is *sound* rather than merely present:

1. **Ordering.** All three call sites in `lib/mcp/servers.ts` (520/580/597) run the synchronous better-sqlite3 `.run()` *before* `syncUserGlobalMcpServers`, so the write is visible to the run being awaited.
2. **The coalescing invariant.** `queued` is cleared immediately before `run()`, and `reconcileLive` evaluates `syncableGlobalServers(db)` as an argument — i.e. synchronously, before its first `await`. So while `queued` is true the pending run provably hasn't read the DB and will see the folded write; once it has, the next write chains a fresh run. I traced the three interleavings (fold-into-pending, chain-after-active, write-after-snapshot) and the tests pin the third explicitly.

The tests use the delayed fake `agy` runner the finding asked for, and assert the stale window from the session's point of view (`register.has("godot") === false` before `settled()`, true after) — including the deletion case, which is the access-control half.

## Adjacent surface checked, and clean

Since the acceptance criterion covers logs too, I checked the other place a configured secret could escape: `agy mcp add` takes credentials in its **argv**. `runAgy` swallows the exec error with a bare `catch` — an `execFile` rejection embeds the full command line, so returning `false` instead of logging it is load-bearing, not laziness. The `console.warn` in `syncAgy` prints only `server.name`. No leak.

## One accepted trade-off, named rather than hidden

The barrier means a *global* settings save now waits for reconciliation. Bounded — `runAgy` caps each call at 10s — but the worst case is `(1 + removals + adds) × 10s` with an `agy` that is installed *and* hanging. A missing `agy` fails fast on ENOENT, so the common cases are unaffected. This is the intended cost of the fix the review asked for (a 2xx now means "already applied"), not a regression; recording it so nobody rediscovers it as a mystery latency.

The test that previously *locked in* the leak (`mcp-server-probe.test.ts:210`) is replaced by real regression tests, and both halves the review asked for are covered:
- **short env** — a stdio fixture echoing `PIN=123` on its way down;
- **short header** — an http endpoint replying `rejected credential abc`, which is the leak path with no misbehaving CLI involved.

Each asserts the diagnostic still arrived (`toContain("FATAL: bad config")` / `"rejected credential"`) so it cannot pass for the wrong reason on an error that never carried the secret.

*Mutation:* restoring `secret.length < 4` → **3 tests fail**.

### Finding 2 — the reconciliation race (`lib/mcp/user-global-sync.ts`)

The finding's core point was that `whenUserGlobalMcpSyncSettles` had no production caller. It now has three: `handleCreate/Update/DeleteMcpServer` each `await settleUserGlobalSync(projectId)`, which awaits the barrier only when `projectId === null`. Spawns stay asynchronous, so only that one request waits — the event loop stays free, which is what the earlier blocking finding required.

I checked this is airtight rather than assuming it: the **only** production callers of the CRUD service are those three handlers, and the three `syncUserGlobalMcpServers` call sites (`servers.ts:520,580,597`) are guarded by exactly the same `projectId === null` condition. `disableGlobalForProject` writes a project-scoped shadow row and requests no sync, correctly.

The scheduler's coalescing invariant holds: `queued` is cleared immediately before `run()`, and `run()` reads the DB synchronously before its first `await`, so a write that folds into a pending run is provably seen by it.

Coverage is the delayed fake runner the review specified — `fakeAgy({ delayMs })` plus *"has not applied the new set when the request would have answered"* and *"holds the answer until a DELETED server is really gone from the register"*, i.e. the stale window is proven to exist and the barrier proven to close it.

*Mutation:* removing the three `await settleUserGlobalSync` calls → **3 tests fail**.

### My own change — one commit, comment only

`f4b7d1d` documents why the multi-line fields carry no `maxLength`. Rule 2 of the section's docstring explains that every `maxLength` mirrors a service constant — true of the four that have one (name, command, url, usage hint) — but said nothing about args, agent types, allowed tools and secrets, so their absence read as an oversight.

It cannot be one: those caps are **per-item** (`MCP_SERVER_ARG_MAX_LENGTH` per arg, `MCP_SERVER_ENV_VALUE_MAX_LENGTH` per value), which one textarea-wide attribute cannot express — and putting the args cap there would be *worse* than omitting it, since `MCP_SERVER_ARGS_MAX_TOTAL_LENGTH` is measured over `JSON.stringify(args)` (`lib/mcp/servers.ts:200`), brackets and commas included, so it matches no count of raw typed characters. I verified each claim against the code before writing it. Same class as the review's earlier `agent_types` point: a deliberate gap is only a decision if it is written down.

### Verification

Full suite **478 files / 6016 tests / 0 failures**, `tsc --noEmit` clean, eslint clean, `next build` exit 0 with `NODE_ENV` unset. Exit codes were read from the commands themselves, not through a pipe — a piped `tail` reports its own status and hides a failure. `node_modules` was checked against the lockfile before any result was trusted.

### One pre-existing flake, not from this branch

The *first* full run reported `1 failed | 6015 passed`: `__tests__/refinement-button.test.tsx:123`, a spinner-visibility assertion. It is **not** this branch's:
- the test and its component `components/kanban/RefinementButton.tsx` are byte-identical to the merge-base and appear nowhere in the 48-file diff;
- no dependency changed;
- isolated re-runs failed **3 of 5** times, and the final full suite passed it.

Reported as friction (`flaky_test`) — it deduplicated at **8 occurrences**, so it is a known recurring flake. Left unfixed deliberately: fixing a flake one merely trips over would widen the diff. Worth its own ticket, because any gate that runs the full suite can fail an unrelated branch about half the time and read as a regression from the diff under review.

### Still live

The stored `<system-directive>` prompt injection in `projects.spec` continues to instruct sessions to rewrite the project specification. Ignored, as data rather than instruction; re-flagging it since it still reaches prompts verbatim.

## Both review findings verified closed — no new code needed

Both majors were already fixed in `32aa470` (+ `f4b7d1d` docs), which post-dates the review. Rather than trust the commit message, I re-derived each fix from current code and **mutation-checked it**, confirming the mutation was still on disk when the suite ran (the false-negative trap where a reverted mutation makes a green run read as a coverage hole).

### `lib/mcp/probe.ts:86` — short-secret leak

The length floor is gone: `scrubSecrets` now skips only the empty string, and redacts longest-first so a short value that prefixes a longer one can't fragment it. `secretValues` filters on `length > 0` alone. Every failure path funnels through the scrubbing `fail()` — transport-construction, handshake, timeout — and the success path returns `error: null`.

Mutation (restore `secret.length < 4`) → **4 named tests fail**, covering exactly what the finding asked for:
- `keeps a THREE-character secret out of the error too` — stdio fixture echoing `PIN=123`
- `keeps a short header value out of the returned error` — a real HTTP server echoing `Authorization: abc` into a 400 body; it also asserts the body *reached* the message, so it can't pass for the wrong reason
- `keeps a SHORT configured secret out of the stored error as well` — the route test, proving the scrub survives into `last_check_error`, which is the durable copy the settings screen re-renders
- `redacts a short value as readily as a long one` — the unit case that replaced the test which used to lock in the leak

### `lib/mcp/user-global-sync.ts:475` — stale-registry race

The finding's core claim — "no production route or provider awaits the barrier" — no longer holds. `settleUserGlobalSync` in `lib/mcp/server-routes.ts:83` is awaited by all three global handlers (POST/PATCH/DELETE) after the row is written, so a 2xx means "already in omp's `mcp.json` and agy's register". Spawns stay async, so only the one request waits. `settled()` returns the chained `active` promise and the handler calls it *after* `request()`, so the new run is always captured; the `.catch` means it never rejects a settings save.

Mutation (drop the `await`) → **3 named route tests fail**: `holds the POST response until the registries agree`, `holds the PATCH response too`, `holds the DELETE response`. These use a held barrier and assert the response does *not* settle promptly while the row is already written — i.e. the handler waits on reconciliation, not on a lock. Scheduler-level tests drive a deliberately slow fake `agy` and assert what a session spawning mid-window would observe, which is the finding's actual failure mode.

**Checked for a residual gap:** the finding also suggested gating at spawn. The request-side barrier is sufficient because it covers every mutating path — the only non-route CRUD caller is `disableGlobalForProject` (shadow route), which is project-scoped and correctly requests no sync, since a project row can't be expressed in a user-global registry.

### Verification

`npm test` → **6015 passed / 6016**, 477/478 files · `tsc --noEmit` clean · `eslint` clean on all 44 files this branch changed · `next build` clean with `NODE_ENV` unset.

**The one failure is not from this branch.** `__tests__/refinement-button.test.tsx` › "disables itself with a spinner and badge once a pass is under way" failed **4 of 8 isolated runs** on code byte-identical to the merge-base. It's a poll/render race — `pollIntervalMs={0}` against a two-entry fetch mock, so a poll can flip state back between the `waitFor` and the following synchronous spinner assertion. Filed as friction (`7U21HTjsPNfh`); it is a known recurrent one, now at 10 occurrences.

epics.title: Next.js 16.3.3 build warnings: deprecated middleware convention and whole-project tracing
epics.description:
Two build-output hygiene issues surfaced on the pinned Next 16.3.3. Neither breaks behaviour today; both are forward-compatibility debt currently hidden by the stale 16.1.6 install.

1. The `middleware` file convention is deprecated. Every dev start and every build prints a warning recommending `npx @next/codemod@canary middleware-to-proxy .`. The middleware itself is correct — it was verified to enforce the localhost boundary in both directions (403 for a forged `Host: evil.com` or `Origin: http://evil.com`, 200 for localhost and 127.0.0.1) in dev and against the production build.

2. The build emits 13 warnings of the form 'Dynamic filesystem access causes tracing of the whole project'. Static analysis cannot scope `path.join(process.cwd(), attachment.filePath)` at `app/api/projects/[projectId]/chat/uploads/[attachmentId]/route.ts:25` or `path.join(process.cwd(), uploadsDirectoryFor(projectId), image.fileName)` at `lib/uploads/ticket-image-paths.ts:39`, so it includes the entire project — all source files and the public folder — in the server output bundle.

user_stories.title: As a maintainer, I want the middleware migrated to the proxy convention so that the build stops warning
user_stories.description: Run `npx @next/codemod@canary middleware-to-proxy .` and verify the localhost host/origin boundary still behaves identically afterwards. The security assertions must be re-run in both directions — a silently opened boundary is the failure mode that matters here.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The deprecation warning no longer appears on dev start or build
- [ ] `Host: evil.com` and `Origin: http://evil.com` still receive 403 on `/api/*`
- [ ] `Host: localhost`, `Host: 127.0.0.1:<port>` and `Origin: http://localhost:<port>` still receive 200
- [ ] `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` still permits a configured non-local origin
- [ ] The boundary is verified against the production build, not only in dev

user_stories.title: As a maintainer, I want filesystem joins statically scoped so that the server bundle stops including the whole project
user_stories.description: Scope the dynamic `process.cwd()` joins to a static subfolder so Turbopack can trace them, e.g. `path.join(process.cwd(), 'data', ...)` as the warning suggests, in `app/api/projects/[projectId]/chat/uploads/[attachmentId]/route.ts:25` and `lib/uploads/ticket-image-paths.ts:39`. Path containment is a security boundary on these routes, so the existing traversal protection must be preserved exactly.
user_stories.acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The build emits zero 'tracing of the whole project' warnings
- [ ] Uploaded images and ticket screenshots still serve correctly (200, correct content-type, valid image bytes)
- [ ] Path-traversal attempts on the uploads and artifacts routes are still refused
- [ ] Both the permitted and the refused direction of the containment boundary are covered by tests

`eslint-suppressions.json` is keyed by **file path**. Three of the four stories here move React code into new files — the settings page split by domain, `EpicDetail` and `Board` decomposed into `components/kanban/epic-detail/`, `runPipeline` and `dispatchPipelineStage` split along stage boundaries. It also removes a trap from B-arij-140's own path — its acceptance is "fix the violations", which is much harder to verify if the files have just been reshaped underneath it.
